name: Baratang Island (Limestone Caves)
tagline: Mangrove creek boats to limestone caves and a bubbling mud volcano

why.winter: Dec-Mar seas stay calm for the creek run to the caves and Parrot Island's dusk roost; mornings bring the day-trip convoy rush
why.summer: April still works on calm days before pre-monsoon swells; by May squalls build and boatmen start cancelling runs
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the SW monsoon means cancelled boats and a soaked convoy road; day trips routinely abort, so sit it out
why.autumn: Oct swells ease and November clears; stay the night and you reach the caves before the Port Blair convoys arrive

vibe: A jetty bazaar, basic lodges and a government guest house; day-trippers vanish by 2 pm leaving you with the fishermen
hub: From Port Blair by ATR road convoy through the Jarawa reserve (no stops or photos), then Middle Strait ferry

spots.name: Baratang Limestone Caves
spots.note: Speedboat up a mangrove creek from Nilambur jetty, then 1.2 km on foot through forest to the caves; boats stop by early afternoon.

spots.name: Parrot Island
spots.note: Mangrove islet where thousands of parakeets pour in to roost; take the boat around 4.30 pm and expect mosquitoes.

spots.name: Baratang Mud Volcano
spots.note: Cold grey mud burping out of low craters at the top of a short boardwalk; ten minutes, free, do it on the caves trip.

spots.name: Baludera Beach
spots.note: Quiet driftwood beach with a small park, the closest one to the jetty; no shops or stalls, so carry water and go before dark.

name: Diglipur (Ross & Smith Islands)
tagline: Remote North Andaman turtle beaches and twin-island sandbar

why.winter: Peak season: best Saddle Peak trekking, calm crossing to Ross & Smith, turtle nesting overlaps.
why.summer: Hot and humid (32-34C) by April-May, turtle season over, but the long haul up is still doable.
why.monsoon: The 10-12hr road-and-ferry run from Port Blair turns genuinely unreliable. Plans fall apart here.
why.autumn: Seas start settling in October, first turtle nesting begins by November. Quiet before the rush.

vibe: End-of-the-road offbeat: turtle researchers and rare travellers, no crowds at all.
hub: Weekly ferry (10-12h) or road from Port Blair via Mayabunder.

spots.name: Ross & Smith Islands
spots.note: Twin islands joined by a white sandbar you can walk at low tide; permit and boat both come from Aerial Bay.

spots.name: Kalipur Beach
spots.note: Dark sand nesting beach where four turtle species come ashore December to March; the forest camp runs night watches.

spots.name: Saddle Peak
spots.note: Highest hill in the Andamans at 732 m, roughly six hours return from Lamiya Bay; buy the forest ticket and carry two litres.

spots.name: Alfred Caves
spots.note: Narrow limestone caves full of swiftlets, an hour of jungle walking each way; you need a local guide to find them.

spots.name: Lamiya Bay
spots.note: Boulder and pebble beach under Saddle Peak where the summit trek starts; no shade and no shop, so carry water and lunch.

name: Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep)
tagline: Andaman's backpacker-diving hub with Radhanagar Beach

why.winter: Best all-round season: calm water at Radhanagar, good dive visibility, full hostel scene.
why.summer: Hot and sticky (32C+) by April-May, but seas stay calm and diving visibility can peak pre-monsoon.
why.monsoon: Ferries get cancelled without much notice, dive shops mostly shut, Radhanagar loses its calm.
why.autumn: Sea starts settling in October though still choppy early on; hostels reopen, notably quieter.

vibe: Beach hostel dorms and dive crews. Easiest island here to meet solo travellers.
hub: Fly to Port Blair, then 2-3h ferry to Havelock jetty.

spots.name: Radhanagar Beach
spots.note: The wide white beach on the west coast, best at sunset; lifeguards call swimmers in at 5 pm and transport thins after.

spots.name: Elephant Beach
spots.note: Snorkelling reef reached by boat from the jetty or a muddy 40 minute forest walk; boats run mornings only and fill up early.

spots.name: Kalapathar Beach
spots.note: Black rock and turquoise water on the sunrise side where the road ends; scooter out before 6 am for empty sand.

spots.name: Vijaynagar Beach (Beach No. 5)
spots.note: Shallow mahua fringed beach along the resort strip, easy for a swim at high tide; the No. 5 cafes are a short walk back.

spots.name: Govind Nagar Beach
spots.note: The beach along the main village road at Govind Nagar, where most of the cheap stays and cafes sit; shallow, calm, sunrise side.

name: Little Andaman (Hut Bay)
tagline: Surf breaks, waterfalls and a ferry that may not come back

why.winter: Dec-Mar is when the ferry actually sails, the sea is swimmable at Butler Bay and the White Surf falls are still running.
why.summer: April and May are the surf window, with rideable waves at Butler Bay right up until the monsoon swell turns it dangerous.
why.monsoon: June-Sep the ferry is cancelled for days on end, and being stranded here with one bank and basic lodges is a real risk.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the rains ease unevenly and sailings resume, but the schedule stays unreliable and the beaches are storm-scoured.

vibe: Six or eight basic guesthouses, a small surf crowd in April and long empty roads you cycle; power cuts are normal
hub: Government ferry Port Blair to Hut Bay, 6-8 h, three to five sailings a week; book at the DSS counter

spots.name: Butler Bay Beach
spots.note: Crescent bay with the island's surf break and a few huts; the rip current is real and there is no shop past Netaji Nagar.

spots.name: White Surf Waterfall
spots.note: Roadside fall with a shallow pool ten minutes off the Hut Bay road; fullest after the rains, leeches in monsoon.

spots.name: Whisper Wave Waterfall
spots.note: The bigger fall, a two hour jungle walk beyond the road head; take a local guide, the path vanishes in the plantation.

spots.name: Little Andaman Lighthouse
spots.note: Red and white tower at the south tip, two hundred odd steps for a view over the reef; ask the keeper, small fee.

spots.name: Netaji Nagar Beach
spots.note: Long casuarina backed beach where the cycle ride out of Hut Bay pays off; no stalls, carry water and a torch.

name: Long Island
tagline: No cars, one village, and Lalaji Bay a two-hour walk away

why.winter: Dec-Mar is the window: flat seas, the Yerrata boats running to schedule, and a two-hour forest walk over to Lalaji Bay.
why.summer: March and April stay calm and give the clearest snorkelling light of the year; by mid-May the swell builds and boats thin out.
why.monsoon: June-Sep the sea is rough, the Yerrata boat gets cancelled for days at a stretch and you can genuinely be stuck here.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the tail of the rains with the north-east monsoon still passing through, so sailings resume but stay uncertain.

vibe: One settlement, no cars, a few guesthouses and a beach-hut place; the sort of island where travellers stay a full week
hub: Government ferry Port Blair-Neil-Havelock-Long Island on set days, or the one-hour boat from Yerrata at Rangat

spots.name: Lalaji Bay Beach
spots.note: White sand bay two hours on foot through forest from the village, or twenty minutes by dinghy; no water, shade or shop.

spots.name: Merk Bay
spots.note: Sandbar beach on uninhabited North Passage Island, a boat charter from the jetty; go early, the sea roughens by noon.

spots.name: Guitar Island
spots.note: Tiny wooded island named for its shape, a short boat hop for a swim; share the charter cost through your guesthouse.

name: Mayabunder (Karmatang Beach)
tagline: Turtle beach at Karmatang with Karen villages inland on Middle Andaman
festival: Dec/Jan: Karen New Year at Webi village

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: green turtles haul out at Karmatang after dark and the sea is flat enough for the Avis Island run
why.summer: March and April are dry near 33 C and the Interview Island permit still comes through before May squalls build
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the Avis and Interview boats stop and the trunk road turns to mud; June and September are wet but passable
why.autumn: October rain thins and November brings the water back clear, with Karmatang empty and turtle season just starting

vibe: One bazaar street, a PWD guest house and two lodges; evenings are the jetty, fishing boats and a very early dinner
hub: Bus up the Andaman Trunk Road from Port Blair, about 10 hours, or 2 hours north of Rangat; ferries call at the jetty

name: Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep)
tagline: The quiet, bicycle-friendly Andaman island next door

why.winter: Calm water, good snorkeling at Bharatpur: this laid-back island is at its easiest to reach.
why.summer: Warm and humid through April-May but ferries usually still run. Fewer crowds than Havelock.
why.monsoon: Same story as the rest of the archipelago. Ferries cancel in rough seas, island quietens hard.
why.autumn: Reliable ferry schedule resumes by late October, still noticeably quieter than peak winter.

vibe: Sleepier than Havelock: a few guesthouses and the kind of quiet that invites chat.
hub: Fly to Port Blair, then 1-1.5h ferry, or hop from Havelock.

spots.name: Bharatpur Beach
spots.note: Shallow reef beach by the jetty with glass bottom boats and snorkel hire; best at high tide, skip the jet ski end.

spots.name: Laxmanpur Beach
spots.note: Long shallow sunset beach of shells and driftwood; the reef flat opens up at low tide, 20 minutes by cycle from town.

spots.name: Natural Bridge (Howrah Bridge)
spots.note: Coral rock arch past Laxmanpur, reachable only at low tide across sharp reef; check the tide chart, wear hard shoes.

spots.name: Sitapur Beach
spots.note: Sunrise beach at the east end below a low cliff; be there by 5.30 am, and the swim gets rough when the wind is up.

spots.name: Ramnagar Beach
spots.note: Quiet beach with a reef edge and almost nobody on it, decent snorkelling at high tide; the sandy track in is walkable.

name: Port Blair
tagline: Andaman capital, Cellular Jail history and island ferries

why.winter: Calm seas, dry weather: peak season, Cellular Jail and Ross Island tours run smoothly.
why.summer: April-May hot and humid (32-34C), seas still mostly calm though afternoon showers creep in by May.
why.monsoon: Rough seas and heavy rain June-September; ferries get cancelled and sightseeing is a washout.
why.autumn: October the monsoon tapers off, seas choppy early on but calm down noticeably by November.

vibe: Everyone's transit stop: swap island plans with travellers before scattering out.
hub: Fly direct from major Indian cities, or ship from Chennai.

spots.name: Cellular Jail National Memorial
spots.note: The colonial prison kept as a memorial, wings and gallows intact; open 9 to 5, with a sound and light show after dark.

spots.name: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep)
spots.note: British island headquarters swallowed by fig roots, deer everywhere; 20 minute ferry from Aberdeen jetty, last boat 4 pm.

spots.name: Anthropological Museum
spots.note: Honest state museum on the islands' Andamanese and Nicobarese peoples; an hour is enough, and it shuts on Mondays.

spots.name: Chidiya Tapu
spots.note: Sunset rocks and a mangrove trail at the island's south end; buses back stop early, so most people hire a scooter.

spots.name: Corbyn's Cove Beach
spots.note: The city beach at the end of a palm lined coast road; the water is fine, the sand is small and busy on Sundays.

spots.name: Aberdeen Bazaar
spots.note: Town crossroads for ferry tickets, permits and cheap thalis; shops close for a long lunch and again around 8 pm.

name: Rangat (Amkunj & Dhani Nallah)
tagline: Middle Andaman stopover with a mangrove boardwalk and turtle beach

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry and calm, and sea turtles come ashore to nest along the Dhani Nallah beach on the darkest nights of the month.
why.summer: March and April are hot but the reef off Amkunj is at its clearest; from mid-May the swell shuts the small beaches down.
why.monsoon: June-Sep is heavy rain and rough water: ferries and the onward Long Island boat get cancelled and Rangat is a wet wait.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov still catches the north-east rains, but the mangrove boardwalk is at its greenest and nobody else is walking it.

vibe: A functional bazaar town rather than a beach scene: basic lodges and an APWD guest house, used as a base by very few
hub: Ferry Port Blair to Rangat by sea takes 6-8 h; the road bus crosses a tribal reserve where stopping is banned

spots.name: Dhani Nallah Mangrove Boardwalk
spots.note: A 1.3 km wooden walkway over mangroves to a turtle nesting beach; nesting runs December to March, go near dusk.

spots.name: Amkunj Beach
spots.note: Driftwood eco park beach on the Rangat Bay road, built after the tsunami; shaded benches, but the current makes swimming unsafe.

spots.name: Cuthbert Bay Beach
spots.note: Turtle nesting beach with a forest department hatchery; the season is December to March and the watch happens at night.

spots.name: Yerrata Mangrove Park
spots.note: Creek side mangrove park and watchtower beside the jetty where the Long Island boat goes; ten minutes, best at high tide.

name: Ahobilam
tagline: Nine Narasimha shrines scattered up a Nallamala gorge

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the season for the 8 km climb between the lower and upper shrines, 28 C and dry gorge beds underfoot.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the Nallamala runs to 45 C and the rock gorge holds that heat, making the upper temples genuinely unsafe.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the gorge streams rise, the path to Jwala Narasimha turns slick and leech-ridden and jeeps stop running.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the forest is green, pilgrim numbers are low and the walk up to Upper Ahobilam is at its most pleasant.

vibe: Pilgrim rest houses and jeep drivers, very few tourists; fine alone, but carry water and start the climb early
hub: Nandyal railhead 65 km, Allagadda 25 km; buses to Lower Ahobilam, shared jeeps the 8 km up to the shrines

spots.name: Ahobila Narasimha Swamy Temple
spots.note: The main hill shrine at Upper Ahobilam, old and half rock cut; shared jeeps run the 8 km up, first darshan around 7 am.

spots.name: Prahlada Varada Narasimha Temple
spots.note: The big lower town temple with carved Vijayanagara mandapas, easy darshan if you skip the climb; closed midday.

spots.name: Ugra Stambham
spots.note: The cleft rock pillar above Upper Ahobilam where the legend begins; four hard hours return, start by 6 am with water.

spots.name: Jwala Narasimha Temple
spots.note: Shrine beside a red stained stream pool on the way to Ugra Stambham; an hour up a rough path, no stalls beyond it.

spots.name: Yogananda Narasimha Temple
spots.note: Small shrine on the fields below the gorge, reached on a stony track; a 30 minute walk from Lower Ahobilam, go early.

name: Araku Valley
tagline: Eastern Ghats coffee valley on a tunnel-laced toy train

why.winter: Coolest, clearest months - misty mornings, coffee harvest, best window for the toy train.
why.summer: Milder than the Andhra plains thanks to elevation, but warm and humid by May.
why.monsoon: Serious Eastern Ghats rain - dramatic falls but landslide-prone ghat road and rail.
why.autumn: October: monsoon greenery intact, waterfalls still running, far fewer crowds than winter.

vibe: Coffee estates and Adivasi villages draw nature-and-culture travelers, not a party crowd.
hub: Train/road from Visakhapatnam (3-4h), or the scenic toy train.

spots.name: Borra Caves
spots.note: Lit limestone caverns dropping 250 ft into the hillside; the Vizag train stops here, and ticket sales end by late afternoon.

spots.name: Chaparai Water Cascade
spots.note: Sheet of water sliding over flat rock where locals bathe and picnic; go after the rains, and the stalls grill bamboo chicken.

spots.name: Katiki Waterfalls
spots.note: Gorge fall below Borra, a jeep ride then a rocky 20 minute walk down; barely runs outside the monsoon months.

spots.name: Araku Tribal Museum
spots.note: Dioramas and Dhimsa dance displays on the valley's Adivasi communities; small fee, an hour, it shuts for lunch.

spots.name: Galikonda View Point
spots.note: Roadside lookout on the ghat road over folded Eastern Ghats ridges; clearest at dawn, cloud swallows it by 10 am.

spots.name: Padmapuram Botanical Garden
spots.note: Old horticulture garden with hanging tree cottages and a toy train; cheap ticket, an hour, near empty on weekdays.

name: Atapaka (Kolleru Lake)
tagline: Pelican and painted stork colony on India's biggest freshwater lake

why.winter: Dec-Feb the Atapaka grove is loud with nesting grey pelicans and painted storks; be on the bund by 7 am for the low light.
why.summer: March sees the last chicks fledge and the colony break up. By Apr-May the lake shrinks into fish ponds and the delta sits at 40 C.
why.monsoon: June and July are green and empty, but Aug-Sep floods put the bunds and the approach road under water and cut the sanctuary track.
why.autumn: October the water level settles and the first pelicans return; by November the colony is filling and the Kaikaluru paddy is gold.

vibe: Fish-pond country: basic lodges in Kaikaluru, delta fish curry for dinner, and the bund shared at dawn with net fishermen
hub: Eluru or Gudivada railhead, bus to Kaikaluru, then 8 km by auto to the Atapaka gate and watchtower

name: Baruva (Sompeta)
tagline: Coconut-backed sand where the Mahendratanaya river meets the sea

why.winter: Nov-Feb: 28 C days, a flat sea and three km of empty sand; Sankranti in January is the one week Srikakulam families turn up.
why.summer: Mar-Apr stay swimmable if you go early. May turns humid and heavy at 36 C, though the coconut shade and the river mouth still work.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the southwest monsoon puts a rip and a heavy surf on this coast, boats stay ashore and the beach road floods. Not a swimming season.
why.autumn: October clears once the depressions pass and November is the best month here: warm water, clean sand and almost nobody on it.

vibe: One state beach resort, a fishing hamlet and the Kotilingeswara temple; evenings are boats coming in and no nightlife at all
hub: Baruva halt or Sompeta station on the Howrah-Chennai line, then 8 km by auto; Visakhapatnam is 4 h by road

name: Belum Caves
tagline: India's second-longest cave system, 1.5 km of it lit and walkable

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the sane window; the tunnels still sit near 30 C inside, so carry water and skip the deepest galleries.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the surface hits 46 C and the cave air turns close despite the blowers, an hour most people cut short.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Rayalaseema plain greens briefly, but the caves are the same warm air whatever the sky does.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is comfortable above ground and the site is quiet on weekdays, with Gandikota an easy add-on.

vibe: A ticketed cave with school groups by day and nothing after dark; you sleep in Tadipatri or Nandyal, not here
hub: Tadipatri railhead 30 km, buses to Belum village; caves open 10:00-17:00, nearest beds are in Tadipatri

spots.name: Belum Buddha Statue
spots.note: A 40 ft seated Buddha on the mound above the cave mouth, the landmark you see from the road; free, five minutes.

spots.name: Bugga Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
spots.note: Vijayanagara temple by the Penna at Tadipatri, its carved gopuram left unfinished; shoes off at the gate, shuts midday.

spots.name: Chintala Venkataramana Temple
spots.note: ASI temple at Tadipatri with a stone chariot and dense pillar carving; no ticket, quiet, do it on the same auto trip.

name: Bhairavakona
tagline: Eight rock-cut shrines in a horseshoe gorge of the Veligonda hills
festival: Feb/Mar: Maha Shivaratri fair at the cave shrines

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: 28 C days, dry rock underfoot for the scramble between all eight shrines, and cold clear nights in the gorge.
why.summer: March is the last workable month. Apr-Jun bake the bare amphitheatre past 44 C, the fall is dry and there is no shade, so skip it.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep rain arrives late and thin over the Veligondas; by September the fall is running again and the last track in turns to mud.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is best. The northeast monsoon fills the waterfall, the cliff ring turns green, and even weekends stay close to empty.

vibe: A stream, a temple choultry and a few pilgrim sheds; day visitors leave by five and the gorge goes quiet except for langurs
hub: Train to Nellore or Ongole, bus to Chandrasekharapuram or Podili, then 20 km of rough forest road by jeep or auto

name: Bheemili (Bheemunipatnam)
tagline: Dutch tombs and a river mouth at the end of the beach road

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: 27 C, calm water where the Gostani meets the sea, and the Dutch cemetery quiet at 4 pm.
why.summer: Apr-Jun runs 38 C with sticky coastal humidity, and there is almost no shade on the sand or at the cemetery.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the sea is rough with a real rip and no lifeguards; treat it as a walking beach or skip it altogether.
why.autumn: Sep-Nov is fine weather for the ride up the coast road, though a Bay cyclone can close it for a day or two.

vibe: Vizag day-trippers at the weekend, fishermen and stray cows midweek; a few beach resorts and cheap town lodges
hub: City buses run out along the Vizag beach road in about an hour; last buses back to Vizag go early evening

spots.name: Bheemili Dutch Cemetery
spots.note: Seventeenth century Dutch tombs and obelisks half lost in scrub behind the town; unfenced, so go in daylight.

spots.name: Bheemili Beach
spots.note: Wide beach where the Gosthani river meets the sea, fishing boats drawn up at the mouth; the current is dangerous.

spots.name: Erra Matti Dibbalu
spots.note: Red sand ravines beside the coast road, a protected geo heritage site; best at sunset, stay off the crumbling edges.

spots.name: Thotlakonda Buddhist Complex
spots.note: Monastery ruins on a hill over the sea, stupas and rock cut cisterns; no shade at all, so go late afternoon.

name: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Boardwalks and boat creeks in India's second largest mangroves

why.winter: Nov-Feb is birding prime: painted storks and waders on the mudflats, calm creek boats, cool 25 °C boardwalk mornings.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is a sweaty 38 °C with hard glare off the water; go at the 9 am opening or skip, otters and jackals hide anyway.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep downpours and Bay depressions cancel boat rides without notice; the mangrove is greenest if you catch a dry day.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings the first migrant birds, but this coast watches cyclones in these months; check forecasts before boating.

vibe: Local families on the boardwalk, fishers and birders in the creeks; sleep in Kakinada, this is a half-day of green.
hub: Kakinada rail 18 km on NH-216, autos to the Chollangi gate; Rajahmundry airport 65 km; closed Tuesdays.

spots.name: Hope Island
spots.note: Hook shaped sandbar that shelters Kakinada bay, reached only by boat from the port; about an hour each way, no shade

spots.name: Draksharama Bhimeswara Temple
spots.note: One of the five Pancharama Shiva temples, its tall lingam worshipped from an upper gallery; shut roughly 12 to 4

spots.name: Yanam
spots.note: Former French enclave at the Godavari mouth, still Puducherry territory; clock tower, river walk and cheap bar prices

spots.name: Uppada Beach
spots.note: Eroding sand strip where the sea keeps taking the coast road; go at sunrise, not for swimming, Jamdani looms inland

spots.name: Subbayya Gari Hotel
spots.note: Kakinada's unlimited banana leaf meal, small bowls refilled until you fold the leaf; go before 1 pm, lunch is the sitting

name: Dindi (Konaseema Backwaters)
tagline: Godavari delta canals, coconut groves and toddy villages

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: 30 C, still water, coconut canals at dawn and the Antarvedi sangam an hour downstream.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the delta sits at 42 C and swamp-humid, and a slow boat under a tin roof is the worst place to be in it.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Godavari floods the delta, small ferries stop and the lanes around Razole and Malikipuram go under.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is green and empty, but this is cyclone coast and a Bay depression can shut boat movement for days.

vibe: Quiet delta villages with almost no travellers; beds are resort rooms or houseboats, so solo here costs more
hub: Palakollu railhead 25 km, or Rajahmundry 90 km by bus via Razole; boats hired at the Dindi jetty

spots.name: Antarvedi Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
spots.note: Narasimha temple at the Vasishta Godavari mouth, packed at the February kalyanam; the road loops via Sakhinetipalli

spots.name: Antarvedi Sangam
spots.note: Sand spit where the Vasishta branch meets the Bay; walk out at low tide only, the current is strong and nobody watches

spots.name: Ksheera Ramalingeswara Temple
spots.note: Pancharama Shiva temple in Palakollu with a white lingam and a big tank; closed 12 to 4, autos wait at the bus stand

name: Gandikota
tagline: 'Grand Canyon of India' - a fort above the Pennar gorge

why.winter: Coolest, clearest months - the only realistic season for a full day on the canyon rim.
why.summer: One of India's hottest regions, 43-45C - the exposed canyon edge turns genuinely dangerous.
why.monsoon: Lighter rain than the coast, but June still carries brutal heat before things cool off.
why.autumn: October: the gorge below fills a jade-green, temps dropping, great late-afternoon light.

vibe: A sparse ruin for photographers and campers - unfenced edges mean caution after dark.
hub: Fly/train to Kadapa, then 1.5h taxi to the gorge.

spots.name: Madhavaraya Temple
spots.note: Ruined Vijayanagara temple inside the fort walls, carved pillars and a half fallen gopuram; free, and best at first light

spots.name: Ranganatha Swamy Temple
spots.note: The fort's other big temple, plainer than Madhavaraya and just as empty; five minutes down the same lane, no ticket

spots.name: Jamia Masjid
spots.note: Two minaret mosque from the Qutb Shahi years standing empty inside the fort walls; five minutes, nobody charges

spots.name: Mylavaram Dam
spots.note: Reservoir on the Penna below Jammalamadugu, quiet water and a long bund road; nothing to eat there, so carry lunch

name: Horsley Hills
tagline: Rayalaseema's pocket hill station, 1250 m of gum trees and cool air

why.winter: Dec-Jan is crisp single-sweater weather with mist in the eucalyptus; weekend crowds up from Bangalore, empty midweek.
why.summer: Apr-May runs 25-32 °C, warm for a hill station but a full 10 °C kinder than the plains below; haze dulls the viewpoints.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep gets modest rain that greens the slopes without shutting anything; clouds swallow the sunset point some evenings.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov after the rains has the cleanest air of the year, long views over the Rayalaseema plains and cool walking weather.

vibe: Bangalore couples and families at the Haritha resort, zipline and viewpoint circuit; gum-tree lanes go quiet midweek.
hub: Tirupati air/rail 125 km or Madanapalle Rd railhead 30 km; buses climb from Madanapalle, thin after dark.

spots.name: Gali Bandalu
spots.note: Wind scoured boulders on the plateau edge, the one honest view here; fifteen minutes on foot, best in the last light

spots.name: Kalpavriksha
spots.note: A eucalyptus said to be over 150 years old, too wide for your arms to meet round it; signposted off the loop road

spots.name: Governor's Bungalow
spots.note: British era hill retreat on the ridge, now a state guest house; you can walk the lawns, inside depends on who is staying

spots.name: Mallamma Temple
spots.note: Small shrine to Mallamma, the woman the hill is locally named after, Yenugu Mallamma Konda; a short climb up

spots.name: Besant Theosophical College
spots.note: Madanapalle college where Tagore made the English translation of Jana Gana Mana in 1919; ask at the gate on a weekday

name: Kondaveedu Fort
tagline: Reddy kingdom capital on a ridge you have to walk up

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the only sane climbing window: 29 C, dry path, and the whole Krishna delta laid out flat from the top.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the ridge bakes past 43 C with no water and no shade on the 3 km walk up, so nobody sensible goes up.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is humid and green with water running off the gateways; start at six or not at all, and watch for snakes.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov clears after the rains, the ridge is green, and you can fit the fort and Guntur into one easy day.

vibe: Local trekking groups on a Sunday, empty midweek; no beds at the fort, so base up in Guntur or Vijayawada
hub: Guntur railhead 25 km, buses to Phirangipuram or Kondavidu village, then a 3 km walk up the ridge

spots.name: Kotappakonda (Trikoteswara Temple)
spots.note: Three peaked hill with a Shiva temple on top, a road to the summit or 700 odd steps; Shivaratri fills it with prabhalu

spots.name: Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple
spots.note: Hill shrine above Mangalagiri where the deity is fed jaggery water and half comes back; steps up, or a road to the gate

spots.name: Amaravati Mahachaitya
spots.note: Flattened base of a great Buddhist stupa with the ASI museum of its carved rail beside it; shut Fridays, allow an hour

spots.name: Undavalli Caves
spots.note: Four storey hall cut into a hillside with a reclining Vishnu on the middle floor; ASI ticket, forty minutes, hot by noon

spots.name: Guntur Mirchi Yard
spots.note: Wholesale chilli market, sacks stacked high and auctions by mid morning; weekdays only, and your eyes will sting

name: Lambasingi
tagline: The one village in Andhra where winter dawns bring frost

why.winter: Dec-Jan is the whole point: frost on the cabbage fields, single-figure dawns that can touch zero, then Vizag cars from nine.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the cold is gone, the streams dry up and the slopes go brown and dusty in the mid-30s, so there is nothing to come for.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Chintapalli ghat takes heavy Eastern Ghats rain, buses run late and the viewpoints sit inside cloud.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov cools fast and the coffee and pepper slopes are green, with a fraction of the December weekend traffic.

vibe: Family homestays and tent camps run by locals, a December weekend rush from Vizag, then nobody at all midweek
hub: Vizag 100 km: bus to Narsipatnam, then a Chintapalli bus up the ghat, about 3 h; last bus down goes early

spots.name: Thajangi Reservoir
spots.note: Small reservoir below the village where the December mist sits longest; go for sunrise, the road in is rough after rain

spots.name: Kothapalli Waterfalls
spots.note: Wide stepped falls off the Narsipatnam road, busy at weekends; the last stretch is a walk down and the rock stays slick

spots.name: Susan Garden
spots.note: Private garden at the village where apples and strawberries are grown at this altitude; fruit sold at the gate in season

spots.name: Chintapalli
spots.note: The mandal town you change buses at, ringed by coffee and pepper smallholdings; nearest ATM, pharmacy and hot meal

name: Lepakshi
tagline: Vijayanagara murals, a hanging pillar and a giant stone Nandi

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window for the murals: 28 C, low sun into the mandapa and the ceiling paintings actually readable.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the granite courtyard passes 42 C by ten and burns bare feet, so come at opening time or not at all.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is rain-shadow dry with the odd shower; the temple is fine but flat light kills the ceiling work.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings northeast monsoon bursts, still an easy two-hour run out of Bengaluru between the showers.

vibe: A one-temple village with tea stalls and day-trippers from Bengaluru; the beds are 15 km away in Hindupur
hub: Hindupur railhead 15 km, Bengaluru airport 100 km; autos from Hindupur, sleep there or back in Bengaluru

spots.name: Veerabhadra Temple
spots.note: Vijayanagara temple with painted ceilings and the pillar that clears the floor; open 6 to 6, free, and empty before 9

spots.name: Lepakshi Nandi
spots.note: Granite bull cut from a single boulder, about 4 m tall, standing alone by the village road; two minutes, no ticket

spots.name: Penukonda Fort
spots.note: Vijayanagara's second capital under a granite hill, with Gagan Mahal and a Jain temple in town; half a day, little shade

name: Mahanandi (Nava Nandi)
tagline: Glass-clear spring tanks below an old Shiva temple on the Nallamala edge
festival: Feb/Mar: Maha Shivaratri brahmotsavam

why.winter: Dec-Feb runs 28 C by day and cold at dawn; the three pushkarini tanks hold a steady 22 C and you can count coins on the bottom.
why.summer: March is fine, April touches 42 C and May goes past 45 C in Nandyal; the water stays cold but the Nava Nandi drive does not.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep greens the Nallamala scarp behind the temple and the springs run at their strongest; short heavy showers, very few pilgrims.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the sweet spot: post-monsoon green on the forest road, the tanks at their clearest, and no queue at the pool before 8 am.

vibe: Devasthanam cottages and pilgrim choultries, one bazaar street; evenings are temple bells, chai carts and people swimming in the tank
hub: Nandyal railhead 16 km, then share auto or APSRTC bus; Kurnool 2 h and Hyderabad 5 h by road

name: Manginapudi Beach (Machilipatnam)
tagline: Black-sand bay beach off the old port of Masulipatnam

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: 28 C, firm dark sand at low tide, and the old Dutch cemetery in town an easy walk away.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the delta sits at 42 C with humidity near 80 percent, and water this shallow gives no relief at all.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the sea turns muddy and rough with no lifeguards anywhere, and Bandar streets flood after a heavy night.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is pleasant between systems, but one Bay depression can shut the beach road and the buses for two days.

vibe: Sunday families and snack stalls on the sand, empty midweek; plain lodges in Machilipatnam town are the beds
hub: Machilipatnam railhead on the branch line from Vijayawada, autos 11 km out to Manginapudi through the day

spots.name: Dutch Cemetery
spots.note: Walled yard of tall Dutch tombs left from the 17th century factory port; ask in the lane for the gate, ten minutes

spots.name: Pedana Kalamkari Workshops
spots.note: Sheds where Machilipatnam kalamkari is block printed and washed at the tank; weekday mornings are when work happens

spots.name: Gilakaladindi Fishing Harbour
spots.note: Machilipatnam's harbour, boats unloading at first light and the auction right after; wear shoes you can hose down

spots.name: Ghantasala Buddhist Site
spots.note: Stupa mound and a small museum of Satavahana finds in a village; shut Fridays, half an hour, nothing to eat nearby

spots.name: Hamsaladeevi
spots.note: Sand spit where the Krishna finally meets the Bay, wide and usually empty; the road is slow, go early, no stalls

name: Maredumilli
tagline: Rain-forest pocket of the Godavari hills with tribal eco-camps

why.winter: Dec-Jan is ideal: 28 C, clear forest tracks, Amruthadhara still flowing and the camps at their most comfortable.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the streams dry out, the forest turns to tinder and the valley bakes near 43 C, which is not why you came.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the rain is heavy and leeches are everywhere; the Rampachodavaram ghat slips, but the falls run full.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the sweet spot, water still moving and the ghat road clear, and the camps take walk-ins on weekdays.

vibe: Forest-department cottages and tribal-run camps with village guides; midweek you may be the only guest there
hub: Rajahmundry 90 km by APSRTC bus via Rampachodavaram; forest camps must be booked with the range office

spots.name: Amruthadhara Waterfalls
spots.note: The bigger of the two falls here, a short walk down through leech country in the rains; best July to October

spots.name: Jalatarangini Waterfalls
spots.note: Stepped falls close to the road with a forest entry fee; the pool is shallow and the whole stop takes under an hour

spots.name: Jungle Star (Valamuru)
spots.note: Forest department camp with cottages on stilts and a guided night walk; book with the range office, no walk in beds

spots.name: Bhupathipalem Reservoir
spots.note: Reservoir ringed by hills below Rampachodavaram, boats when the water is up; the last few km are rough forest road

name: Nagarjuna Sagar (Nagarjunakonda)
tagline: Buddhist ruins moved to an island in a Krishna reservoir

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: 29 C, the reservoir high after the rains and the launch out to the island museum running.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the Krishna basin bakes at 45 C and a low reservoir can cut the island boats out altogether.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the dam is at its most dramatic with gates open, but island sailings and Ethipothala both get disrupted.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the best time for water, reservoir full and Ethipothala falls 11 km away genuinely flowing.

vibe: Dam-colony town with government guest houses and tourism rooms; boat queues at weekends, empty midweek
hub: Hyderabad 150 km by bus or Macherla railhead 25 km; island launch from the Vijayapuri South jetty

spots.name: Ethipothala Falls
spots.note: The Chandravanka drops into a gorge pool with a crocodile pen beside it; full only after the rains, August to December

spots.name: Anupu (Ikshvaku ruins)
spots.note: Monastery and a stone amphitheatre lifted above the reservoir line and rebuilt; open ground, an hour, carry water

spots.name: Buddhavanam
spots.note: Sculpture park by the reservoir retelling the Jataka tales in stone; big and shadeless, so come late in the day

spots.name: Macherla Chennakesava Temple
spots.note: Old Vishnu temple in the market town where the buses turn round; carved black pillars, shut through the afternoon

name: Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary
tagline: Pelican and stork colony nesting over a village tank

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the reason to come: spot-billed pelicans and painted storks nesting over the tank, chicks by January.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the birds have gone, the tank shrinks and the coastal plain sits at 42 C with nothing left to watch.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the dead season here; the southwest rains do little on this coast and the nesting trees stand bare.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the northeast monsoon fills the tank and the first flocks arrive, though heavy rain shuts the trail.

vibe: A forest-department watchtower, a few birders with scopes, and plain lodges 20 km away in Sullurpeta
hub: Sullurpeta railhead 20 km on the Chennai-Vijayawada line, then auto; Chennai airport is 100 km south

spots.name: Pulicat Lake
spots.note: Brackish lagoon whose north end starts below Sullurpeta; flamingos and waders in winter, boats from the fishing villages

spots.name: Satish Dhawan Space Centre
spots.note: ISRO's launch site on Sriharikota; the space museum needs prior permission and launch gallery seats are booked online

spots.name: Chengalamma Parameswari Temple
spots.note: Sullurpeta's goddess temple and the town's centre of gravity; busiest on Sundays, and the beds and buses are here too

name: Orvakal Rock Garden
tagline: Wind-carved pink quartz canyons around a green pool near Kurnool

why.winter: Nov-Feb mornings put golden light on the pink quartz, the pool sits full, and midweek you get whole canyons to yourself.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the bare rock becomes a 42 °C griddle and the lake shrinks to a puddle; Rayalaseema heat is no joke out here.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug brings short storms that refill the pool and cool the stone; ledges turn slippery but moody skies photograph well.
why.autumn: Oct after the rains has the best light-to-water ratio of the year; catch sunset from the ridge above the filled lake.

vibe: Kurnool day-trippers at the selfie points, geology nerds beyond them; APTDC Haritha rooms sit right among the rocks.
hub: Kurnool airport (IndiGo) minutes away at Orvakal; Kurnool rail 25 km; buses to village, 3 km auto to gate.

spots.name: Alampur Navabrahma Temples
spots.note: Nine Badami Chalukya temples by the Tungabhadra with the Jogulamba shrine beside them; ASI site, an hour, little shade

spots.name: Mahanandi
spots.note: Shiva temple whose three tanks run with clear spring water you can stand in; bathe first, shoes stay well outside

spots.name: Konda Reddy Fort
spots.note: Kurnool's old gate tower stranded in the middle of the traffic, lit at night; ten minutes, the inside is usually shut

spots.name: Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Grassland kept for the great Indian bustard, though blackbuck and harriers are what you see; ask the range office

name: Papikondalu (Godavari Gorge)
tagline: The Godavari squeezes between forested hills on a slow boat cruise

why.winter: Dec-Feb is prime: cool deck breeze, green gorge walls, a full river; book the Kolluru bamboo hut night ahead on weekends.
why.summer: Apr-May is a 40 °C slog on an open deck over a hazy, shrunken river; if you must, take March and carry serious sun cover.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug cruises get suspended whenever the Godavari crosses flood marks; June is a rising-river gamble, ask before booking.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov after the floods is the sweet spot: brimming river, mist on the hills, streams near Perantalapalli still running.

vibe: Telugu family groups on the boat deck, campfire nights at Kolluru bamboo huts; solos slot into package cruises easily.
hub: Rajahmundry rail/air, 1.5-2 h road to the jetty; boarding point shifts with Polavaram works, ask when booking.

spots.name: Perantalapalli
spots.note: Koya hamlet where the cruise halts for lunch, with Balananda Swamy's ashram and a cold stream behind it; boats wait about an hour.

spots.name: Kolluru
spots.note: Sandbank village on the Godavari where the bamboo huts and campfire nights are; the only place inside the gorge you can sleep.

spots.name: Pattiseema Veerabhadra Swamy Temple
spots.note: Hill temple on a Godavari island near Polavaram, reached by a short ferry; most cruises pass it on the way upstream.

spots.name: Polavaram Dam
spots.note: The unfinished Godavari barrage that keeps moving the boat jetty; the spillway is visible from the bank, ask before walking closer.

name: Penukonda
tagline: Vijayanagara's second capital: a walled town under a granite fort hill

why.winter: Nov-Feb gives 28 C days and cold mornings, the right window for the two hour climb past Gagan Mahal to the Jain temple on the hill.
why.summer: Mar-Apr work if you start at 6 am. By May the bare granite radiates past 40 C and there is no water anywhere on the way up.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep brings only thin Rayalaseema rain, enough to green the boulder fields; showers are short and the fort path stays walkable.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is clear and quiet: the haze lifts, you see the Lepakshi plain from the top, and the town's ruins have nobody in them.

vibe: A working market town with basic lodges and dhabas; the ruins stand inside the lived-in streets, so evenings are shutters and idli carts
hub: Penukonda Junction on the Bengaluru-Guntakal line, 3 h from Bengaluru; Kempegowda airport is 90 km up NH44

name: Srisailam
tagline: Jyotirlinga above the Krishna gorge inside Nallamala forest
festival: Feb/Mar: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the window: 28 C, the Krishna gorge clear from the Patalaganga ropeway and darshan queues manageable midweek.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the Nallamala road bakes near 45 C and the reservoir drops, so the gorge views go to dust and haze.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the forest is at its best and the dam often spills, but ghat buses crawl and hill mist closes the views.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the reservoir is full after the rains and the forest is green, with pilgrim numbers still manageable.

vibe: Big pilgrim town with devasthanam dorms, cheap meals and buses at all hours; easy and safe to arrive alone
hub: Road only: 210 km from Hyderabad or 180 km from Kurnool through Nallamala forest, 5-6 h by RTC bus

spots.name: Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
spots.note: The jyotirlinga and shakti peetha in one compound; the free queue can run hours, the paid darshan ticket saves most of it.

spots.name: Patala Ganga
spots.note: The Krishna river ghat below the temple where pilgrims take a dip; ropeway down, or about 500 steps back up in the heat.

spots.name: Srisailam Dam
spots.note: Big gated dam holding the Krishna inside a forested gorge; the road crosses the crest and photography on it is not allowed.

spots.name: Akkamahadevi Caves
spots.note: Limestone cave with a natural lingam up the Krishna backwaters; only reachable by launch from Patala Ganga, about 3 h return.

spots.name: Sakshi Ganapati Temple
spots.note: Small Ganesha shrine on the Hyderabad road where pilgrims record their visit; five minutes, done on the way out of town.

spots.name: Paladhara Panchadhara
spots.note: Spring channels in a rock hollow where Adi Shankara is said to have written the Sivananda Lahari; a long flight of steps down.

spots.name: Sikhareswaram Temple
spots.note: Highest point of the Srisailam hill, a plain Shiva shrine with forest falling away on all sides; late afternoon is quietest.

spots.name: Mallela Theertham
spots.note: Forest waterfall down 350 steps inside the tiger reserve; the Nallamala gate shuts by late afternoon, so leave Srisailam early.

name: Suryalanka Beach (Bapatla)
tagline: Casuarina-backed Bay of Bengal sand nine km off Bapatla

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: 29 C, firm sand, a long walk under the casuarinas and almost nobody there on a weekday.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the sand is unwalkable by ten and the humidity stays near 80 percent well after dark, so nights are rough.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the sea turns brown and rough with a real rip; there are no lifeguards, so treat it as a walking beach.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is pleasant between weather systems, but a Bay depression can shut the beach and the buses for days.

vibe: Empty weekday sand and Sunday families; the APTDC resort is the only bed, so book it before you get on the bus
hub: Bapatla railhead 9 km on the Chennai-Vijayawada main line, autos out to the beach gate through the day

spots.name: Sri Bhavanarayana Swamy Temple
spots.note: Bapatla's old Chola era temple, the one that gave the town its name; a working shrine, busiest at the evening puja, no ticket.

spots.name: Vodarevu Beach
spots.note: Wide casuarina backed beach outside Chirala with fishing boats and stalls; busier than Suryalanka on Sundays, empty otherwise.

spots.name: Nizampatnam Fishing Harbour
spots.note: Trawler harbour where the night catch is auctioned on the quay; go at first light, the road in from Bapatla takes about an hour.

spots.name: Ramapuram Beach
spots.note: The quieter Chirala beach next along from Vodarevu, casuarina and a couple of shacks; no shade after 10 am, carry water.

name: Talakona Falls
tagline: Andhra's tallest waterfall pours 82 m out of Seshachalam forest

why.winter: Dec-Jan keeps the 82 m fall alive after the northeast monsoon, cool forest walks below; log huts fill up on weekends.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the fall thins to a trickle and the Seshachalam forest bakes at 38 °C; not worth the 50 km detour from Tirupati.
why.monsoon: This is rain-shadow country: Jul-Aug stay surprisingly dry here, and only late Sept showers start feeding the stream again.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov right after the northeast monsoon bursts is peak flow, with the plunge pool and canopy walkway at their greenest.

vibe: Weekend picnic families at the falls, silence one bend upstream; forest dept log huts and a dorm sleep the few who stay.
hub: Tirupati rail/air, then 50 km road to the Nerabailu forest gate; no useful bus, take a cab or share jeep.

spots.name: Siddheswara Swamy Temple
spots.note: Small Shiva shrine at the foot of the falls where the trail starts; the pool just below it is where everyone bathes.

spots.name: Sri Venkateswara National Park
spots.note: Seshachalam forest around the falls, red sanders and slender loris country; forest gate ticket, and it closes before dusk.

spots.name: Talakona Canopy Walk
spots.note: Rope walkway strung through the forest canopy off the falls path; the forest department runs it for a small fee, shut in heavy rain.

name: Tirupati
tagline: Hilltop Venkateswara temple, one of the world's busiest
festival: Sep-Oct: Brahmotsavam, nine days of processions and Garuda Seva

why.winter: Coolest, most bearable months for the marathon darshan queues on your feet for hours.
why.summer: April-May heat makes the famously long queues genuinely punishing - heatstroke is a risk.
why.monsoon: Moderate rain, the temple runs exactly as normal year-round, Seshachalam hills turn green.
why.autumn: Sep-Oct usually brings Brahmotsavam, the year's biggest event - incredible but far busier.

vibe: A pilgrimage machine, not a social scene - solo devotees move through efficient queues.
hub: Fly/train to Tirupati, then 1-1.5h bus or the Alipiri hill footpath.

spots.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
spots.note: The hill temple itself, 22 km up a one way ghat road; book a Sarva Darshan slot online or expect a wait of many hours.

spots.name: Sri Padmavathi Ammavari Temple
spots.note: Tiruchanur shrine to Venkateswara's consort, the visit pilgrims pair with the hill; short queue, free entry, open all day.

spots.name: Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple
spots.note: Vijayanagara era temple with a towering gopuram in the middle of town, a short walk from the station; best at first light.

spots.name: Kapila Theertham
spots.note: Shiva shrine at the foot of the Tirumala hills with a waterfall dropping into its tank; worth it after rain, dry in summer.

spots.name: Alipiri Mettu
spots.note: The 3,550 step footpath up to Tirumala, 3 to 5 h; start before 6 am, and TTD carries your luggage up for free.

spots.name: Silathoranam
spots.note: Natural rock arch on Tirumala, a geological oddity beside the deer park; ten minutes off the temple circuit and free.

spots.name: Chandragiri Fort
spots.note: Vijayanagara hill fort with the Raja Mahal palace and a small museum; closed Fridays, evening sound and light show.

spots.name: Srikalahasteeswara Temple
spots.note: Vayu lingam temple known for Rahu Ketu puja, in a town of kalamkari workshops; puja slots run through the day, book on arrival.

name: Ubbalamadugu Falls (Tada)
tagline: Chennai trekkers' boulder-canyon waterfall in the Kambakkam hills

why.winter: Dec-Jan the stream runs clear over the boulder canyon and the 4 km rock-hop from the forest gate is at its best; start early.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the falls run bone dry and the boulders hit 40 °C; there is nothing here for you, wait for the northeast rains.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep southwest rains barely feed this side of the ghats; pools stay low and the trek is a hot, dry scramble.
why.autumn: Late Oct-Nov the northeast monsoon wakes the falls; flash-prone on heavy-rain days, glorious the week after a good spell.

vibe: Chennai trekking groups on winter weekends, nobody midweek; no stay at the falls, bed down in Sullurpeta or Sri City.
hub: Day trek: Chennai or Tirupati, 90 km to Tada, then 15 km to the forest checkpost; jeep for the last stretch.

spots.name: Vedanarayana Swamy Temple, Nagalapuram
spots.note: Vijayanagara temple where the sun strikes the deity for three days each March; quiet the rest of the year, and free.

spots.name: Nagalapuram Falls
spots.note: The other boulder trek in these hills, steeper and wetter than Tada; take a guide and do not attempt it after heavy rain.

spots.name: Chengalamma Temple, Sullurpeta
spots.note: Riverside goddess temple in the town where most trekkers sleep; Friday crowds are heavy, early mornings are calm.

name: Vanjangi (Paderu)
tagline: Sunrise above a sea of clouds from a grassy ridge near Paderu

why.winter: Nov-Feb dawns deliver the cloud ocean, most reliably in Jan; start the 45 min ridge climb by 4:30 am, near 5 °C up top.
why.summer: By March the cloud bed is gone and mornings are merely clear; not worth the 4 h ghat drive unless you want empty hills.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the trail is a leech-and-slush slog with the ridge socked in fog, and the ghat road from Vizag crawls in rain.
why.autumn: Oct is the gamble month: lush slopes and early cloud beds on some dawns, flat grey nothing on others; November firms up.

vibe: Telugu bikers and tent campers at dawn, tribal villages by day; sleep in a basic Paderu lodge or pre-booked ridge tent.
hub: Road only: 100 km ghat road from Visakhapatnam to Paderu, then 8 km to the base point by bike, jeep or cab.

spots.name: Tajangi Reservoir
spots.note: Small reservoir in the hills on the Paderu to Araku road, silent except for the birds; a short stop, no facilities at all.

name: Visakhapatnam (Vizag)
tagline: Port city where the Eastern Ghats meet the Bay of Bengal

why.winter: Driest, coolest, safest window on this coast - clear skies and the lowest cyclone risk.
why.summer: Hot and humid off the Bay of Bengal; beaches work early morning, sticky by midday.
why.monsoon: Heavy humid rain, sea often rough for swimming - fine for the city, not for the beach.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is peak Bay of Bengal cyclone season - Hudhud hit Vizag itself in Oct 2014.

vibe: A workaday port city - solo travelers mostly pass through en route to Araku.
hub: Direct flights and trains from all major Indian cities.

spots.name: Kailasagiri
spots.note: Hilltop park with the big Shiva and Parvati statue and a ropeway up; go for sunset over the port, skip the toy train.

spots.name: Simhachalam Temple
spots.note: Hill temple whose Narasimha idol stays caked in sandalwood all year except for one spring day; steep road, buses from the RTC complex.

spots.name: Ramakrishna Beach
spots.note: The city promenade beach, better for an evening walk past the war memorials than for swimming; the water pulls hard.

spots.name: INS Kurusura Submarine Museum
spots.note: A real Soviet built submarine beached on RK Beach and opened up inside; closed Mondays, tight ladders, bags left outside.

spots.name: Yarada Beach
spots.note: Crescent of sand behind the hills past Dolphin's Nose, the prettiest stretch here; no lifeguards and the seabed drops fast.

spots.name: Erra Matti Dibbalu
spots.note: Red laterite badlands on the Bheemili coast road, a protected geo site; go early or late, there is no shade anywhere.

name: Vizianagaram
tagline: Pusapati fort town of gate towers and Telugu music schools
festival: Oct: Pyditalli Sirimanotsavam (Tuesday after Dasara)

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the best of it: 28 C, walkable streets between the fort gate, the clock tower and the Moti Mahal.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the town runs 39 C and dusty, and there is nothing here worth walking around in that kind of heat.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is humid with heavy afternoon rain, but the fort tank fills and the town is at its greenest and quietest.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings the Sirimanotsavam crush, when a huge pole-borne procession fills the streets for one long night.

vibe: A slow district town of college musicians and tea shops; ordinary hotels near the junction, no traveller scene
hub: Vizianagaram Junction is a main-line stop 60 rail km north of Vizag, trains all day; the fort is a walk away

spots.name: Vizianagaram Fort
spots.note: The Pusapati fort in the middle of town, its gate towers and Moti Mahal now full of colleges; free to walk through by day.

spots.name: Sri Pydithalli Ammavari Temple
spots.note: The town goddess, whose Sirimanotsavam chariot festival in October fills the streets; ordinary and quiet the rest of the year.

spots.name: Ramatheertham
spots.note: Hill of Jain and Buddhist rock remains with a Rama temple below; about 20 minutes of steps, go before the sun gets high.

spots.name: Ramanarayanam
spots.note: Newer Ramayana temple and sculpture park on the edge of town, full of local families after dark; small entry fee.

spots.name: Thatipudi Reservoir
spots.note: Reservoir under the Eastern Ghats on the Vizag road, the standard Sunday picnic run; nothing to buy there, carry food.

spots.name: Bobbili Fort
spots.note: Rajah's palace and museum in the veena making town of 1757 battle fame; the veena workshops are a lane or two away.

name: Yaganti
tagline: Cave shrines and a spring-fed tank in a sandstone hollow
festival: Feb/Mar: Maha Shivaratri jatara

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the time: 29 C, the spring-fed Pushkarini cold and clear, and the cave shrines walkable even at midday.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the red sandstone hollow traps 45 C heat and the bare climb up to the caves turns genuinely unpleasant.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep brings little rain to this rain-shadow belt, so you get the heat and haze without any of the green.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the tank fills up, weekdays are thin and Belum Caves pairs neatly 45 km down the road.

vibe: Temple-town rhythm of bells and Monday crowds; sleep in Banaganapalle or Nandyal, no traveller scene at all
hub: Nandyal railhead 55 km via Banaganapalle 14 km; frequent buses, but plan to sleep in Nandyal

spots.name: Yaganti Uma Maheswara Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple built into a sandstone amphitheatre, with the Nandi locals say keeps growing; Mondays and Shivaratri are packed.

spots.name: Agastya Pushkarini
spots.note: Spring fed tank in the temple courtyard that never dries, water arriving through a Nandi mouth; pilgrims bathe before darshan.

spots.name: Venkateswara Cave
spots.note: Rock cave above the temple holding a damaged Venkateswara idol, which is why the story sends him to Tirumala; short climb.

spots.name: Veera Brahmam Cave
spots.note: Low cave where the seer Veera Brahmendra Swamy is said to have written his prophecies; you crawl the last stretch, take a torch.

spots.name: Mahanandi
spots.note: Shiva temple with three spring fed pools of glass clear water you can stand in; the usual pairing with Yaganti, allow half a day.

name: Anini (Dibang Valley)
tagline: Road-end Idu Mishmi outpost under the snows of Dibang Valley
festival: Feb: Reh, the Idu Mishmi festival (1 Feb)

why.winter: Dec-Jan is stark: snow can shut Mayudia pass for days, but clear spells hand you white ridges over empty valleys; Reh feasts open February.
why.summer: March-April is spring at its best with rhododendron up high; May's building cloud starts the road's landslide season.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is out: the 230 km Roing road is a landslide lottery and the valley disappears into cloud for weeks at a stretch.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is peak: rinsed blue skies, the snowline dropping on the Mishmi ridges, and day drives up the Dri and Mathun valleys.

vibe: Idu Mishmi homestays and a circuit house at the last town on the map; expect to be the only traveller at the viewpoint
hub: ILP online; Dibrugarh, cross to Roing, then 235 km (7-9 h) over Mayudia pass; sumos most mornings from Roing

spots.name: Mipi
spots.note: Idu Mishmi village up the Dri valley where a Tibetan settlement once stood; rough track, hire a vehicle in Anini for the day.

spots.name: Dibang Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: High forest that holds Mishmi takin and almost never sees a visitor; you need the DFO's permission in Anini and your own vehicle.

spots.name: Dri River
spots.note: The Dri meets the Mathun below town to become the Dibang; walk down to the bridge early, the water runs glacier blue in winter.

name: Basar
tagline: Galo valley of rice terraces, cane bridges and clean villages
festival: Dec: BasCon, the Basar Confluence festival (dates shift)

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry and mild at 5-22 C: cane bridges over clear streams, harvest-gold terraces and BasCon filling homestays in early December.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is green and easy for village walks; by May the Likabali approach begins slipping in pre-monsoon storms.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug regularly cuts Basar off behind landslides on the approach roads; fields flood and leeches own the field paths.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov dries the valley into harvest gold with clear skies for village walks; book homestays early if you plan to stay on for BasCon.

vibe: A cluster of Galo villages with an organised homestay network; you eat with families, walk field paths, no tourist scene
hub: ILP online; railhead Silapathar in Assam, then about 3 h by shared sumo up via the Likabali gate

spots.name: Malinithan
spots.note: Carved 10th century temple ruins on a low hill near Likabali, kept by the ASI; free, and right on the way in from Assam.

spots.name: Akashiganga
spots.note: Hill spring and pilgrim shrine above Likabali, usually paired with Malinithan on the same run; a short steep climb from the road.

name: Damro (Yamne valley)
tagline: Oldest Adi Padam village, with a 300 m cane hanging bridge over the Yamne below it

why.winter: Dec-Feb are dry with 15 C days on the ridge at 1,100 m and cold nights; the 40 min walk down to the cane bridge is easy and the Yamne runs low and clear
why.summer: Mar-May the terraces are being planted, rhododendron and orchids show in the forest above, and pre-monsoon storms roll in by late April; days reach 25 C
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Yamne rises under the bridge, the Pasighat road slips around Mariyang and leeches take the trails; the village sees no visitors. Not now
why.autumn: Oct dries slowly; November is harvest in the rice terraces, the clearest views down the valley and the season the eco lodge fills with small groups

vibe: Yamne Abor Eco Lodge's bamboo cottages and a couple of homestays; Adi Padam elders, mithun in the forest, apong by the hearth
hub: Pasighat to Damro via Mariyang, 100 km and 4-5 h by shared Sumo or hired car; Pasighat has a few flights a week. ILP needed

name: Dirang
tagline: Monpa valley with hot springs, en route to Tawang

why.winter: Cold nights but the Sangti hot springs and black-necked cranes (Dec-Jan) make it worth it.
why.summer: Best weather of the year. Apple orchards blooming, mild days, easy access.
why.monsoon: The NH13 approach is landslide-prone through this whole stretch, hours-long blocks common.
why.autumn: Clear post-monsoon skies, apple harvest, good base before continuing up to Tawang.

vibe: A quiet stopover: travellers breaking their Tawang journey, Monpa homestay hosts.
hub: Fly Tezpur, 8h drive via Bhalukpong. ILP + PAP.

spots.name: Sangti Valley
spots.note: Apple orchards along a braided river up a side valley; black necked cranes still winter here some years, best at first light.

spots.name: Dirang Dzong
spots.note: Stone walled Monpa fort village above the river, still lived in; narrow lanes, about 15 minutes on foot end to end.

spots.name: Dirang Hot Water Spring
spots.note: Sulphur pools by the river below the dzong, free and open all day; separate sheds for men and women, carry your own towel.

spots.name: Thupsung Dhargye Ling Monastery
spots.note: Large new Gelugpa monastery consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 2017; morning prayers around 6 am, shoes off at the hall.

spots.name: National Research Centre on Yak
spots.note: ICAR yak research farm on the hillside where you can see the herd; a working government centre, so ask at the gate on a weekday.

name: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary (Lama Camp & Bompu)
tagline: Birders' tented camps on a forest track up to 2,800 m, home of the Bugun liocichla

why.winter: Dec-Feb are cold at Lama Camp, frost most mornings and snow now and then on Eaglenest Pass, but skies are clear and altitude migrants come down to Bompu at 1,940 m
why.summer: Mar-May is breeding season: the Bugun liocichla sings below Lama Camp, tragopans call at dawn, and by May the pre-monsoon showers and leeches begin at Bompu
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the sanctuary is closed to visitors: the jeep track slips, the camps pack up and leeches own the forest. Come back from October
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the camps reopen as the rain stops; November gives the clearest light down the Kameng gorge and the first wintering birds, with the camps still half empty

vibe: Serious birders in the Bugun community's tented camps, hot dal by lamplight, 5 am wake-ups and no phone signal above Ramalingam
hub: Tezpur to Singchung by shared Sumo, 5 h, then a jeep 1 h up to Lama Camp, booked via the Bugun Welfare Society. ILP needed

name: Mechuka (Menchukha)
tagline: Hidden Himalayan valley near the China border

why.winter: Cold and remote with occasional snow, drive gets trickier, but very few travellers come.
why.summer: April-May is prime: apple and kiwi orchards blooming, roads at their most reliable.
why.monsoon: One of Arunachal's most landslide-prone roads. Trips get stranded for days, avoid entirely.
why.autumn: Excellent: clear valley views, the cane suspension bridge and monastery at their best.

vibe: Likely the only outsider in the guesthouse. Welcoming villages, no traveller circuit.
hub: Fly to Aalo, then 6-8h rough mountain road. ILP + PAP.

spots.name: Samten Yongcha Monastery
spots.note: 400 year old gompa on a ridge above the valley; steep 30 minute climb from the road, best light late afternoon.

spots.name: Siyom River
spots.note: The valley's cold braided river below the meadow; cross on the hanging footbridge, one person at a time, then walk the far bank.

spots.name: Dorjeeling Village
spots.note: Memba village of wooden houses across the river, about an hour on foot; ask before photographing anyone or their home.

spots.name: Guru Nanak Tapo Asthan
spots.note: Small army maintained gurudwara on the spot where Sikhs believe Guru Nanak sat; open all day, no fee, carry a head cover.

name: Namdapha National Park (Miao & Deban)
tagline: Rainforest reserve climbing from 200 m riverbank to 4,571 m peaks

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the only reliable window: dry trails to Hornbill and Bulbulia camps and hoolock gibbons calling at dawn.
why.summer: March-April brings orchids and migrant birds along with the first heavy rain, and by May the forest tracks are gone.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is relentless rain, leeches on every leaf and a Noa-Dihing in spate that cuts the Deban crossing for days.
why.autumn: October dries out slowly, but bridges and porters stay unreliable until the forest department reopens properly.

vibe: Forest rest house at Deban with no phone signal, Lisu porters, and a handful of serious birders per season
hub: ILP and park permit issued at Miao; Dibrugarh airport 160 km, 5 h; Margherita railhead 65 km, then jeep

spots.name: Noa-Dihing River
spots.note: The park's milky green river right below Deban; boatmen ferry you across to the trail head, there is no bridge upstream.

spots.name: Haldibari
spots.note: Forest camp a full day's walk in through leech country; hire a Lisu porter at Deban and carry your own food and tent.

spots.name: Hornbill Camp
spots.note: Forest clearing a few hours up the trail from Deban; hornbills and gibbon calls, turn back before the light goes.

spots.name: Bulbulia
spots.note: Sulphur mud spring bubbling in the forest, a natural salt lick animals come to; walk in from Deban with a Lisu guide.

spots.name: Choephelling Tibetan Settlement
spots.note: Tibetan refugee settlement at Miao with a monastery and a carpet centre; easy stop while your park permit is being made.

name: Nampong (Pangsau Pass)
tagline: Stilwell Road frontier village below the Pangsau Pass and Myanmar's Lake of No Return
festival: 20-22 Jan: Pangsau Pass International Festival at Nampong, with Myanmar traders and dancers

why.winter: Dec-Feb are dry, 25 C days and cool nights; the January festival brings Myanmar dancers and traders over the pass, and the lake permit from the SDO is easiest then
why.summer: Mar-May heat past 32 C at 300 m with storms from April; the pass at 1,160 m is a cooler day out and the Stilwell Road's WWII sites are still dry enough to reach
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug rain buries the pass in cloud and the 12 km road up from Nampong slips regularly, so sit those months out; September is still wet but the road reopens
why.autumn: Oct-Nov clear the cloud and the pass view over the Pangsau lake basin returns, with Namdapha 60 km away for the second half of the trip and no crowds

vibe: A tea-shop bazaar, forest and PWD rest houses, a lodge or two; Assam Rifles, Tangsa villagers and no one else outside festival week
hub: Tinsukia to Jairampur by bus or Sumo, 2-3 h via Ledo, then 13 km on to Nampong; the pass needs an SDO permit. ILP needed

name: Pasighat
tagline: Arunachal's oldest town where the Siang spreads into the plains
festival: Sep: Solung (Adi agrarian festival)

why.winter: Nov-Feb is dry at 10-26 C with clear Siang water, the only sane season for rafting and Daying Ering birding.
why.summer: March-April is warm and workable, but from May the Siang browns up and the pre-monsoon rain arrives in earnest.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug this is one of the wettest corners of India, the Siang is unraftable and the approach roads slide often.
why.autumn: September brings Solung and the first clear days; October is quietly excellent once the river drops and settles.

vibe: Relaxed Adi town with cheap lodges and a riverside promenade, a soft landing for a first Arunachal trip
hub: ILP for Indians, PAP for foreigners; small airport with Guwahati flights; Murkongselek railhead 35 km

spots.name: Siang River
spots.note: The Brahmaputra's main stem, spreading wide as it leaves the hills; rafting operators run trips upstream from November.

spots.name: Dr. Daying Ering Memorial Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Grassland river island with wild buffalo, hog deer and winter ducks; boat access only, arrange it a day ahead in town.

spots.name: Kekar Monying
spots.note: Black rock cliff where Adi fighters fought a British column in 1911; a memorial plaque and a big bend of the Siang below.

name: Roing & Mayudia Pass
tagline: Idu Mishmi valley below a 2,600 m pass that really does get snow
festival: Feb: Reh (Idu Mishmi, early February)

why.winter: Dec-Jan is when Mayudia 56 km above Roing takes real snow, and Reh in early February fills the valley with ritual.
why.summer: March is cold and clear on the pass, but from April the Dibang valley starts raining and the road surface goes.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Dibang basin is among India's wettest and landslides close the Mayudia road for days at a stretch.
why.autumn: October is drying and Mehao Lake reflects well, but the pass stays locked inside cloud most afternoons anyway.

vibe: Small Mishmi town with plain hotels, one cold hilltop lodge at Mayudia, and no other travellers outside Reh
hub: ILP for Indians; Dibrugarh airport 130 km via Bogibeel bridge, 4 h; Tinsukia railhead 110 km

spots.name: Bhismaknagar Fort
spots.note: Chutia era brick fort spread over a forested hill, walls and gateways still standing; dawn to dusk, carry water and repellent.

spots.name: Mehao Lake
spots.note: Still forest lake inside Mehao sanctuary with no boats or shops; the last stretch is a two hour walk, so leave Roing at dawn.

spots.name: Sally Lake
spots.note: Small lake in the forest just above town, a short climb from the road; families come in the evening, mornings are quieter.

spots.name: Nizamghat
spots.note: Where the Dibang comes out of the hills, boulders and a wide clear channel; a picnic and swimming spot with no facilities.

name: Shergaon
tagline: Sherdukpen pine-forest village at 2,000 m, the quiet turn-off on the Tawang road
festival: Nov/Dec: Khiksaba, the five-day Sherdukpen forest-spirit festival at Shergaon and Rupa

why.winter: Dec-Feb are frosty and clear: Khiksaba fills the village with masked dances and drums when it falls in December, then January nights drop below zero under dry sunny days
why.summer: Mar-May is orchid and rhododendron time in the pines; days reach 20 C, the forest walks are dry and the Eco Camp fills on weekends with Guwahati families
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep rain closes in most days and the Rupa-Shergaon road gets slips; the village stays reachable but the forest trails are leech-thick and views are rare
why.autumn: Oct-Nov bring the driest air of the year, harvest in the terraces below the village and clear ridge views; the best walking weeks, and homestays rarely full

vibe: A community Eco Camp of wooden cottages and a handful of homestays; evenings are wood smoke, local millet beer and an early bed
hub: Tezpur to Rupa by shared Sumo, 5-6 h via Bhalukpong, then 25 km by taxi; Tezpur is the nearest rail and airport. ILP needed

name: Tawang
tagline: Largest Indian monastery, high Himalayan passes
festival: Dec/Jan: Torgya Festival at Tawang Monastery

why.winter: Sela Pass frequently snows shut, roads get cut off for days. Real risk of being stranded.
why.summer: Prime season: April-May roads are clear, monastery and high lakes fully accessible.
why.monsoon: Landslides regularly cut the Bomdila-Tawang road. Genuinely the worst time to attempt it.
why.autumn: October is stunning, clearest mountain views of the year; November turns cold again.

vibe: Monks, army convoys, a few backpackers: quiet monastery evenings, no party scene.
hub: Guwahati + 2-day drive via Bomdila-Dirang. ILP + PAP.

spots.name: Tawang Monastery
spots.note: Galden Namgey Lhatse, founded in the 1680s and the largest in India; the morning chant starts before six, museum upstairs.

spots.name: Sela Pass
spots.note: 4,170 m pass with a lake beside the road, the gate to Tawang; cross before noon, it shuts in snow with no warning.

spots.name: Sangetsar Lake (Madhuri Lake)
spots.note: Dead tree stumps standing in a lake made by the 1950 earthquake; needs the Bum La permit from the DC office in Tawang.

spots.name: Bum La Pass
spots.note: Border post at 4,600 m where the two armies meet; Indian passport holders only, permit from the DC office and an army escort.

spots.name: Nuranang Falls
spots.note: A 100 m fall near Jang dropping straight off the cliff into a gorge; steps go down to the base, slippery after rain.

spots.name: Urgelling Monastery
spots.note: Quiet little gompa on the birth site of the sixth Dalai Lama, born 1683; usually empty, ask next door if the hall is locked.

name: Tuting (Pemako)
tagline: Road-end Memba village where the Tsangpo enters India as the Siang
festival: Feb/Mar: Losar in the Memba villages of Pemako

why.winter: Dec-Feb are the dry months: 20 C days on the river at 550 m, cold nights, the Siang running clear for expedition rafters and the Sumos from Pasighat on schedule
why.summer: Mar-May warm up fast with pre-monsoon storms by April; Losar and spring make the Memba villages lively, and the Devakota island shrine is still an easy walk
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Siang swells to a brown flood, the Yingkiong-Tuting road is cut by landslides for days at a time and Tuting is effectively out of reach. Not now
why.autumn: Oct is still wet in the upper Siang; by November the road settles, the gorges clear and you can walk to Gelling, the last village 30 km before the Tibet line

vibe: A frontier bazaar, a circuit house and two or three homestays; rafters in season, army convoys, and lamas walking the kora at Devakota
hub: Shared Sumo from Pasighat via Yingkiong, 270 km, 12-14 h; Pasighat has a few flights a week, Dibrugarh 5 h more. ILP needed

name: Wakro (Parshuram Kund & Glao Lake)
tagline: Mishmi orange village between the Lohit's holy kund and a rainforest lake trek
festival: mid Jan: Makar Sankranti mela at Parshuram Kund, a lakh pilgrims in a week

why.winter: Dec-Feb is orange harvest and trekking season: dry trails to Glao Lake, 20 C days at 430 m, and the mid-January Makar Sankranti mela at the kund, 11 km north
why.summer: Mar-May warm to 30 C with pre-monsoon storms from April; the Glao trek is still on till mid-April, and the Kamlang forest is loud with hornbills and gibbons
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Lohit and Kamlang rivers are in flood, the trek fords are impassable and the kund steps get washed; wait for the rain to stop
why.autumn: Oct is still wet; November opens the trails again, the orchards hang heavy with fruit and the Kamlang forest is at its clearest and least visited

vibe: A few family homestays among the orange orchards, a circuit house, Mishmi weavers, pilgrims only in January; early, quiet evenings
hub: Shared Sumo from Tezu, 50 km and 2 h; Tezu is 3 h from Tinsukia rail or Dibrugarh airport over the Sadiya bridge. ILP needed

name: Walong (Dong & Kibithoo)
tagline: Lohit valley outpost of the 1962 battle, with India's first sunrise at Dong

why.winter: Dec-Feb are clear and cold, 2-3 C nights and dry days; the pre-dawn climb above Dong for India's first sunrise is the reason to be here, and the road stays open
why.summer: Mar-May bring rhododendron on the Kibithoo ridges and warm days by the Lohit; hazy afternoons and short storms by May, but the Tezu Sumos still run daily
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Lohit is in flood and the Hayuliang-Walong road is cut by landslides for days; Anjaw is effectively closed to travellers. Not now
why.autumn: Oct dries slowly and by November the valley is at its best: hot spring by the river, war memorial, Kaho and Kibithoo homestays and a road with no other tourists

vibe: An army town at heart: an inspection bungalow, a few homestays, Mishmi villages and soldiers who tell the 1962 story over tea
hub: Tezu to Walong by shared Sumo, 200 km and 9-11 h via Hayuliang; Tezu is 3 h from Tinsukia rail or Dibrugarh air. ILP needed

name: Zemithang (Gorsam Chorten)
tagline: Nyamjang Chu valley beyond Tawang under a giant Bhutanese-style chorten
festival: Feb/Mar: Gorsam Kora, a three-day fair and kora around the chorten, dated by the Tibetan calendar

why.winter: Dec-Feb are dry and clear at 2,100 m, with a few black-necked cranes wintering on the Nyamjang Chu sandbars; snow on Sela Pass can shut the Tawang road for a day or two
why.summer: Mar-May bring the Gorsam Kora fair, rhododendron on the ridges and 15 C days; the valley is at its greenest before the rains and the Sumos run daily from Tawang
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep rain sits on the valley and the Lumla road slips in places; Jul-Aug are the wettest, September dries out and the terraces turn gold before the harvest
why.autumn: Oct-Nov are the clearest weeks: sharp views up the valley towards the Bhutan and Tibet ridges, harvest in the Monpa villages and cold, still nights by mid-November

vibe: Monpa homestays in Zemithang and the Pangchen villages, army trucks on the road, and evenings of butter tea by the kitchen stove
hub: Shared Sumo from Tawang via Lumla, 90 km and 3-4 h; Tawang itself is 2 days from Guwahati or Tezpur by road. ILP needed

name: Ziro Valley
tagline: Apatani tribal valley of paddy fields and music festival
festival: Late Sep: Ziro Music Festival (dates shift yearly)

why.winter: Cold and frosty at night but clear and crisp. The valley is empty of tourists.
why.summer: Lovely window: paddy fields turning green, pleasant days before the rains set in.
why.monsoon: June-Aug is a wet, leech-prone slog with landslide risk; Sept redeems it with the music festival.
why.autumn: Best all-round month: golden harvest, clearest views, valley at its most photogenic.

vibe: Apatani homestays; packed with backpackers each Sept festival, quiet otherwise.
hub: Fly Guwahati-Hollongi, 4-5h drive. ILP + PAP.

spots.name: Hong Village
spots.note: One of the largest Apatani villages, bamboo houses and log ladders; go with a local guide and ask before photographing elders.

spots.name: Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Bamboo and silver fir forest above the valley, a two day trek from Pange; permit from the DFO in Hapoli, leeches in monsoon.

spots.name: Kile Pakho
spots.note: Ridge looking over the paddy valley one way and the snow line the other; clearest just after sunrise, ten minutes from the road.

spots.name: Dolo Mando
spots.note: Hilltop above Hapoli with the whole Ziro valley below; about 40 minutes up through pine, busy with students at sunset.

spots.name: Meghna Cave Temple
spots.note: Shiva shrine inside a hillside cave, found in 1962 and now a small pilgrim stop; steps up from the road, a five minute look.

name: Bhairabkunda
