tagline: Where the Jampani leaves Bhutan and meets the Bhairabi under Arunachal's first ridge
festival: Jan: Bhairabkunda Tourism Festival by the river

why.winter: Dec-Feb the river runs clear and shallow over white stones and Bhutan's ridges stand sharp; weekend picnic parties fill the banks, weekdays are quiet
why.summer: Mar-Apr are warm and green with the planted forest full of birdsong and the river still wadeable; by May the heat passes 32 C and the storms begin
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Jampani comes down in spate, the sandbanks go under and the camp shuts; the hills vanish into cloud, so leave it for autumn
why.autumn: October dries the tracks and the eco camp reopens; November is the best of it, cool clear dawns and the river back to a swimming stream

vibe: A community eco camp with tents and a guest house in the planted forest, Bodo and Nepali villages; picnickers by day, quiet nights
hub: Train or bus to Udalguri or Tangla, then 24 km by shared sumo or taxi; from Guwahati about 4 h by road via Mangaldai

name: Chandubi Lake
tagline: Earthquake-born forest lake in Rabha country near Guwahati
festival: Jan: Chandubi festival, first week of January

why.winter: Nov-Feb is calm and clear at 10-25 C: winter ducks on the water, Rabha village walks, and the lakeside festival in early January.
why.summer: March still works for a lazy boat-and-birds day; by Apr-May it is 34 C with afternoon thunderstorms rolling off the Garo foothills.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug is a washout: Assam rain swells the lake into the forest, paths turn to mud and the far shore vanishes behind grey murk.
why.autumn: October steadies and stays green; by November the first migrants land and weekdays give you the whole lake to yourself.

vibe: Guwahati picnic families at the ghat on weekends, birders midweek; sleep at the Rabha-run jungle camp cottages
hub: 64 km from Guwahati via Mirza, about 2 h; the airport is 40 km away; no permits needed

spots.name: Kukurmara
spots.note: Sandbank on the Kulsi where Gangetic dolphins surface; hire a country boat at the ghat, best in the hour after sunrise.

spots.name: Garbhanga Reserve Forest
spots.note: Hill forest behind the lake with hoolock gibbons and an elephant corridor; go with someone local, the tracks are unmarked.

name: Dehing Patkai National Park (Jeypore)
tagline: India's easternmost rainforest: seven wild cats and gibbon song on the Burhi Dihing

why.winter: Dec-Feb mornings are misty and about 10 C under the canopy, best for hoolock gibbon calls at dawn and hornbills over the Dihing; leeches gone, trails firm
why.summer: Mar-Apr the forest is loud with breeding birds and still walkable in 28 C; May brings the first big storms and the ranges shut for the monsoon
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the park is closed: 2,500 mm of rain, the Dihing in flood and the forest roads under water, so this is not the time
why.autumn: The ranges reopen through October as the water drops; November is the sweet spot with the canopy dripping, butterflies out and almost no visitors

vibe: Forest guards and a handful of birders; sleep in the forest rest house at Jeypore or in Digboi and Duliajan hotels, nights are silent
hub: Fly or train to Dibrugarh, then 60 km by bus or taxi via Naharkatia to Jeypore (2 h); permits and a guide at the range office

name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park (Guijan Ghat)
tagline: Feral horses and river-island birding on the upper Brahmaputra

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the clean window: country boats out of Guijan, feral horses on the grass and enormous winter bird lists.
why.summer: March-April still works, but water starts rising in April and the grassland heat and horseflies wear you down.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep most of the island lies under Brahmaputra floodwater, the country boats stop and nothing is reachable.
why.autumn: October is drying out but channels stay high, so boatmen quote more and the migratory birds have not landed yet.

vibe: Homestays at Guijan and Maguri Beel, birders with scopes, no nightlife and no other travellers to speak of
hub: Tinsukia railhead 12 km to Guijan Ghat; Dibrugarh airport 55 km; boats hired at the ghat, no timetable

spots.name: Maguri Beel
spots.note: Shallow wetland famous for grassland birds, best from a poled boat at first light; hire boat and guide at Motapung.

spots.name: Bherjan-Borajan-Padumoni Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Three small forest patches near Tinsukia holding hoolock gibbons and macaques; an hour's walk, entry at the Borajan gate.

spots.name: Tilinga Mandir
spots.note: Shiva shrine at Bordubi hung with thousands of bells left by people whose wishes came true; busiest on Tuesday mornings.

spots.name: Digboi Centenary Museum
spots.note: Oil museum beside Asia's oldest working refinery, old rigs and drilling gear outside; carry photo ID, the gate is a company one.

name: Guwahati
tagline: Northeast's gateway city: Kamakhya Temple, river cruises

why.winter: Pleasant and dry, best for the Kamakhya hilltop and sunset Brahmaputra cruises.
why.summer: March-April is warm but fine; May onward turns properly hot and humid.
why.monsoon: Heavy, sustained rain and periodic urban flooding. City runs, but sightseeing suffers.
why.autumn: October still runs 31C and about 120 mm of rain with Navaratri queues at Kamakhya; November drops to 28C and under 10 mm.

vibe: Transit-hub energy: most solo travellers pass through for a night before heading on.
hub: Major airport (LGBI), direct flights nationwide. No ILP.

spots.name: Kamakhya Temple
spots.note: Shakti pitha on Nilachal hill and the state's busiest shrine; take the paid darshan slip or queue for hours, shut at midday.

spots.name: Umananda Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple on a rock island in the Brahmaputra with golden langurs; ferries from Kachari ghat until about 4 pm.

spots.name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Grassland with the densest rhino population anywhere; jeep safaris morning and afternoon, booked at the gate, shut in monsoon.

spots.name: Deepor Beel
spots.note: Ramsar wetland on the city edge with pelicans and storks in winter; the railway embankment is the easiest place to watch from.

spots.name: Assam State Museum
spots.note: Ahom and Kachari stone sculpture plus a tribal life gallery; closed Mondays, allow an hour, cameras stay at the counter.

spots.name: Fancy Bazar
spots.note: Old trading quarter of dense cloth, cane and spice lanes; late morning to evening, on foot only, keep your bag in front.

name: Haflong
tagline: Assam's only hill station, on the Lumding-Silchar hill railway

why.winter: Nov-Feb gives 8-22 C, clear ridge views over Haflong Lake and the most reliable running of the hill railway.
why.summer: March-April is warm and hazy but fine to walk; May brings the first pre-monsoon slips on the Silchar road.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Lumding-Silchar hill line and NH-27 shut for days with landslides, so do not build a plan around them.
why.autumn: October is when Jatinga 9 km away gets its foggy-night bird descent, and the hills are at their greenest all year.

vibe: Dimasa and Zeme Naga town with basic hotels, a lake to walk around, and almost no outside travellers at all
hub: New Haflong station on the Guwahati-Silchar line; Silchar 90 km, 3-4 h by shared sumo on hill road

spots.name: Jatinga
spots.note: Ridge village where migrating birds fall out of the fog on dark September nights; the watchtower is a short walk off the road.

spots.name: Haflong Lake
spots.note: The town's lake at the bottom of the bowl, about 30 minutes to walk around; pedal boats at weekends, litter the rest of the time.

spots.name: Maibang
spots.note: Old Dimasa capital on the Mahur river with a temple cut from one rock; the train from Haflong takes about an hour.

name: Hajo & Sualkuchi
tagline: Hindu, Buddhist and Muslim shrines, and a town that weaves muga silk

why.winter: Nov-Feb is dry and mild, right for the Hayagriva Madhava steps at dawn and Sualkuchi looms clattering by nine.
why.summer: March-April is warm but workable; by May it is 34 C and humid and the temple hill offers almost no shade at all.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the Brahmaputra rises over the Sualkuchi ghats and the river crossing stops, so you go the long way round.
why.autumn: October is green and empty, the river drops back, and you can watch muga silk reeled before the Bihu order rush.

vibe: Pilgrims and silk buyers by day, one small tourist lodge, best done as a slow bicycle and ferry loop
hub: Guwahati 25 km, city buses from Adabari about 1 h; Guwahati airport 30 km, railhead 22 km

spots.name: Hayagriva Madhava Temple
spots.note: Stone temple on Monikut hill, sacred to Hindus and counted a Buddha site too; steps up from the tank, elephant friezes below.

spots.name: Poa Mecca
spots.note: Hilltop dargah of Giasuddin Auliya, said to hold a quarter of Mecca's blessing; shoes off at the stairs, cover your head.

spots.name: Kedareswara Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple on Madanachal hill with a half buried monolithic lingam; quieter than Hayagriva, and the climb opens the river up.

spots.name: Madan Kamdev
spots.note: Scattered 10th century temple ruins with erotic carvings, called Assam's Khajuraho; open dawn to dusk, free, hardly visited.

name: Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary (Jorhat)
tagline: India's only ape, in a rainforest patch cut by a railway line

why.winter: Nov-Mar mornings are the ones to book: hoolock gibbons call at first light and the trails are dry and leech-free.
why.summer: April-May is humid and full of insects, but the gibbons still call by 6 am, so go early and be out by mid-morning.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the forest floor is leech soup and the tracks flood; a guide will still take you and you will regret it.
why.autumn: October is green and empty, and it pairs well with Majuli 35 km north once the Brahmaputra ferries settle down.

vibe: Half-day guided forest walk, then you sleep in Jorhat, which has cheap hotels and honest Assamese thalis
hub: Jorhat airport 25 km, Mariani railhead 5 km; autos from Jorhat 19 km, entry only with a forest guide

spots.name: Lachit Borphukan Maidam
spots.note: Burial vault of the Ahom general who beat the Mughals at Saraighat in 1671; a walled lawn off the Jorhat to Mariani road, free.

spots.name: Tocklai Tea Research Institute
spots.note: The world's oldest tea research station, working since 1911; ring the office ahead, the experimental gardens need permission.

spots.name: Dhekiakhowa Bornamghar
spots.note: Vaishnavite prayer hall founded by Madhabdev in 1528 where an earthen lamp is kept burning; bare feet, cover your legs, no fee.

spots.name: Jorhat Gymkhana Club
spots.note: Golf laid out in 1876 with an old racecourse beside it, one of Asia's oldest courses; ask at the gate, visitors pay a green fee.

name: Kaziranga National Park
tagline: One-horned rhino capital: jeep and elephant safaris

why.winter: Peak safari season: dry grass, easy rhino and elephant sightings, all safaris running.
why.summer: May is the tail end before closure. Hot, grass tall, park shuts by month's end.
why.monsoon: Fully closed: the Brahmaputra floods the park every year, no safaris run at all.
why.autumn: October reopening: grass still tall so sightings are trickier, but crowds are thin.

vibe: Resort-lodge crowd doing sunrise safaris. Easy to team up and split a jeep.
hub: 4-5h drive/bus from Guwahati airport. No ILP.

spots.name: Kohora (Central) Range
spots.note: Main gate: dawn elephant ride from Mihimukh, then a jeep loop past the beels; book the elephant a day ahead, slots go fast.

spots.name: Bagori (Western) Range
spots.note: Open grass and water on every side, the range where rhino turn up most reliably; first jeeps at sunrise, shut May to October.

spots.name: Agoratoli (Eastern) Range
spots.note: Quiet birding range around Sohola beel, pelicans and fish eagles in winter; animals sit far off, carry your own binoculars.

spots.name: Hathikuli Organic Tea Estate
spots.note: Organic garden on the highway that runs right up to the park boundary; walk the rows early, the factory takes visitors on request.

spots.name: Kaziranga National Orchid and Biodiversity Park
spots.note: Wild orchids, bamboo and an evening Bihu dance with rice beer tasting; ticketed, the obvious filler between the two safari slots.

spots.name: Kakochang Falls
spots.note: Small falls among coffee and rubber plantations near Bokakhat; go soon after the rains, by spring it is a trickle on rough road.

name: Majuli Island
tagline: World's largest river island: Vaishnavite monasteries
festival: Nov: Raas Mahotsav (Vaishnavite festival)

why.winter: Best window: dry paths between satras, reliable ferries, cool days for cycling.
why.summer: April is warm but fine; by May pre-monsoon rains start swelling the Brahmaputra.
why.monsoon: The island genuinely floods, ferries get suspended, villages relocate to higher ground.
why.autumn: October floodwaters are just receding, muddy patches but the island is reachable.

vibe: Homestays with mask-making or pottery families. Slow island pace, not a party scene.
hub: Fly to Jorhat, then 1h ferry across the Brahmaputra. No ILP.

spots.name: Uttar Kamalabari Satra
spots.note: Monks here perform Sattriya dance and drumming; turn up in the afternoon and they will usually let you sit in on practice.

spots.name: Auniati Satra
spots.note: Royal satra with a small museum of Ahom utensils and manuscripts; the dusk prayer with drums is the time to be there.

spots.name: Samaguri Satra
spots.note: Workshop where bamboo and clay masks are built for the bhaona plays; the Goswami family teaches short sessions if you ask.

spots.name: Salmora
spots.note: Riverbank potters who hand build without a wheel from Brahmaputra clay; the bank keeps eroding, ask before entering a yard.

spots.name: Dakhinpat Satra
spots.note: One of the four royal satras and the big Raas ground each November; the east road is rough, hire a scooter for the whole day.

name: Manas National Park
tagline: Grassland reserve under Bhutan with pygmy hog and golden langur

why.winter: Nov-Mar is the real season: cold mornings on the Beki, rhino and elephant on burnt grassland, very few jeeps.
why.summer: April-May stays open but runs 33 C and the grass hides everything; safaris wind down before the June closure.
why.monsoon: Gates shut Jun-Sep, the Beki runs brown with Bhutan-side rain and the Bansbari approach road becomes a swamp.
why.autumn: An October reopening depends on the rains and grass is still shoulder-high, so November is the first safe month.

vibe: Bodoland community lodges and forest bungalows, hardly any backpackers, guides who used to hunt these forests
hub: Barpeta Road railhead 22 km to Bansbari gate; Guwahati 140 km, 4 h by bus plus shared taxi

spots.name: Mathanguri
spots.note: Forest bungalows above the Manas river with Bhutan on the far bank; the drive up is the safari, beds only via the range office.

spots.name: Manas River
spots.note: Rafts float the two hour stretch from Mathanguri down to Bansbari past shingle banks; fixed at the range office, dry months.

spots.name: Bhuyanpara Range
spots.note: Eastern gate near Kahitama, better for elephant herds and open grass; far fewer jeeps, fix the vehicle the night before.

spots.name: Barpeta Satra
spots.note: The Vaishnavite centre Madhavdev built in the 1580s, huge kirtan hall; go for the evening prayer, leather stays outside.

name: Nameri National Park
tagline: Foot safaris and river rafting under the Arunachal foothills

why.winter: Nov-Feb is prime: 8 C dawns, a rafting drift down the Jia Bhoroli and a real shot at the white-winged wood duck.
why.summer: March still walks well, but the park closes through May and the foothills turn hot, wet and thick with leeches.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Jia Bhoroli is in spate, the park is shut and stretches of the Tezpur-Bhalukpong road go under water.
why.autumn: October is a gamble because gates open only late in the month and the grass is still too tall to see through.

vibe: Eco camp tents at Potasali, birders and anglers at the same dinner table, walks led by an armed forest guard
hub: Tezpur 35 km with regular buses; Rangapara North railhead 40 km; nearest working airport Guwahati

spots.name: Jia Bhoroli River
spots.note: Rafting and mahseer water along the park edge; the float from Bhalukpong down to Potasali takes a morning, cold months only.

spots.name: Bhalukpong
spots.note: Arunachal border town on the Bhoroli with riverside camps and the check post; get the inner line permit online, carry an ID.

spots.name: Tipi Orchid Research Centre
spots.note: Glasshouses of several hundred Arunachal orchid species just past Bhalukpong; it is inside Arunachal, so a permit is needed.

spots.name: Pakke Tiger Reserve
spots.note: Hornbill forest at Seijosa across the river, nest adoption scheme and a basic camp; Arunachal permit and a very early start.

name: Orang National Park (Silbori)
tagline: Mini Kaziranga on the north bank: rhino grassland, tigers and empty jeep tracks

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: short grass after the November burn, rhinos and hog deer in the open, 10 C dawns with fog off the Brahmaputra lifting by 8 am
why.summer: March and April stay open with taller grass and 30 C heat, elephants and pelicans on the beels; the park shuts on 1 May for the rains
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the park is closed: the Brahmaputra floods the grassland and the animals move to the highlands, so wait for November
why.autumn: October still shut while the tracks dry out; from 1 November the gate opens, the grass is high but fresh and the first jeeps have the park to themselves

vibe: A forest lodge and rest houses at the Silbori gate, a few eco camps on the boundary; Assamese families and birders, silent nights
hub: Tezpur airport and railhead 65 km, Guwahati 140 km; NH15 bus to Orang town, then 15 km by taxi to the Silbori gate

name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary (Mayong)
tagline: Densest rhino grassland on earth beside Mayong, Assam's village of black magic

why.winter: Dec-Feb the 38 sq km of grass and beels hold 100 plus rhinos, so a dawn elephant ride or jeep almost never misses; fog until 8 am, book beds for weekends
why.summer: Mar-Apr the grass is burnt short and rhinos and wild buffalo stand in plain view in 30 C heat; the sanctuary closes for the rains from May
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the gates are closed: the Brahmaputra floods the wetland and the rhinos shift to the Burha Mayong hills, so this is not the time
why.autumn: The sanctuary reopens in the last week of October as the water drops; November brings the first migratory ducks and the tallest grass of the year

vibe: Guwahati weekend families and a few birders; lodges and homestays sit at the gate, evenings are a village road and the magic museum
hub: From Guwahati 45 km by road, 1.5 h by taxi or a Morigaon bus to the Pobitora gate; airport and railhead both in Guwahati

name: Sivasagar
tagline: Ahom capital of oval amphitheatres and tank-side temples
festival: Jan: Me-Dam-Me-Phi (Ahom ancestor rites, 31 Jan)

why.winter: Nov-Feb is 10-25 C and dry, and Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and the Sivadol tank all fit into one long walking day.
why.summer: March-April is warm and green with Bihu in mid-April, but by May it is 35 C, sticky and full of evening squalls.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the Brahmaputra floods, feeder roads go under, and the brick monuments sit in mud and mosquitoes.
why.autumn: October drains the paddy, the light goes gold, and the Charaideo maidams 28 km away are almost empty of people.

vibe: Small tea-belt town, cycle-rickshaws between monuments, no traveller scene but easy hotels by the tank
hub: Jorhat airport 60 km; Simaluguri railhead 20 km; buses from Jorhat and Dibrugarh, 2-3 h

spots.name: Rang Ghar
spots.note: Two storey Ahom amphitheatre of the 1740s where kings watched buffalo fights; small ticket, the lawn stays open until dusk.

spots.name: Sivadol
spots.note: Ahom Shiva temple of 1734 on the bank of the great tank, about 30 m high; shoes off at the steps, walk the bund at sunset.

spots.name: Talatal Ghar
spots.note: Seven storey Ahom palace at Rangpur, the underground floors and their tunnels sealed; go early, the courtyards give no shade.

spots.name: Charaideo Maidams
spots.note: Ahom royal burial mounds, a Unesco site since 2024; shared taxis to Sonari pass the gate, allow two hours with the museum.

spots.name: Gargaon Palace
spots.note: Kareng Ghar of 1752, the Ahom court palace, with a stair up to the roof terrace; usually empty, the caretaker holds the key.

name: Son Beel (Karimganj)
tagline: Assam's largest wetland: 18 km of lake in the rains, paddy and fish traps by winter

why.winter: Dec-Feb the water drops to under half its monsoon size, the edges turn to boro paddy and fish traps and duck flocks arrive; boats still run the deep middle
why.summer: Mar-Apr the beel is at its lowest and hazy at 30 C, fields where the lake was; May storms start refilling it and the boatmen return to the ghat
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the beel is a lake of nearly 10,000 hectares between two lines of hills, fishing villages on stilts and boats for hire at about 800 rupees an hour
why.autumn: October is prime: full water, the rain gone and hyacinth in flower; by November the level drops and the eastern shore starts to show paddy again

vibe: Fishing families and Bengali day-trippers from Karimganj, almost no outsiders; sleep in a basic lodge in Karimganj or Hailakandi town
hub: Silchar airport 85 km; train to Karimganj (Sribhumi) or Badarpur, then about 25 km by bus or taxi to the lake ghat

name: Tezpur
tagline: Gupta-era stone carving on a bluff over the Brahmaputra

why.winter: Nov-Feb is clear and 10-25 C for Agnigarh at sunset, the sixth-century Da Parbatia door frame and the long bridge.
why.summer: March-April is warm, green and loud with Bihu; May turns muggy at 34 C with heavy afternoon thunderstorms daily.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the Brahmaputra is enormous and brown, ghats close and the road up to Bhalukpong washes out repeatedly.
why.autumn: October is the sweet spot, dry and empty, and Nameri 35 km upriver starts taking bookings again around then.

vibe: Easy-going riverside town of students and army families, cheap hotels, the natural first stop before Tawang
hub: Rangapara North railhead 20 km; buses to Guwahati 180 km, 5 h; Bhalukpong 60 km; no civil flights

spots.name: Agnigarh
spots.note: Legend hill with sculpture panels on a spiral path and the Brahmaputra below; small ticket, come for sunset over the bridge.

spots.name: Da Parbatia
spots.note: Gupta era carved stone doorframe, the earliest surviving sculpture in Assam, in a field of ruins; unstaffed, go in daylight.

spots.name: Mahabhairab Temple
spots.note: Hill temple over a stone lingam said to predate the town; busiest at Shivaratri, quiet at dawn, leave shoes at the stair.

spots.name: Bamuni Hills
spots.note: Ruined temple panels carved around the tenth century on a low hill; a short climb, no shade and no water, carry your own.

spots.name: Chitralekha Udyan (Cole Park)
spots.note: Town park round a pond with old carved stone pillars and boating; open into the evening, ten minutes by rickshaw from the bazar.

name: Umrangso (Kopili Reservoir)
tagline: Kopili reservoir town in Dima Hasao: hot springs, Amur falcon roosts, Panimur 33 km
festival: Nov/Dec: Falcon Festival on the Umrangso golf field

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry and cool, 8-20 C, the reservoir at its bluest and the Garampani hot spring worth the soak; Panimur runs clear but thinner than in autumn
why.summer: Mar-Apr are warm and hazy with the falls at their lowest; by May pre-monsoon storms arrive and the hill road up from Lanka starts to slip
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep Dima Hasao takes 2,000 mm plus of rain; Panimur becomes a brown roar you watch from a distance, roads cut up and leeches own the trails
why.autumn: Best window: Amur falcons roost in tens of thousands through Oct-Nov before the flight to Africa, and Panimur is at full milky width after the rains

vibe: NEEPCO staff, Dimasa and Karbi villagers and a few Guwahati weekenders; beds are the tourist lodge and basic hotels, evenings end early
hub: Train to Lanka on the Guwahati-Lumding line, then 60 km of hill road by bus or shared sumo, 2.5 h; Guwahati bus about 7 h

name: Barabar Caves
tagline: India's oldest rock-cut caves, mirror-polished by Mauryan masons

why.winter: Dec-Feb is perfect on bare granite at 10-26 C: a 25 minute stepped climb and the Lomas Rishi echo all to yourself.
why.summer: March is warm but fine; April-June bake the rock past 44 C, and this Gaya-Jehanabad belt is the hottest part of Bihar.
why.monsoon: June-September the dirt approach from Bela turns to slurry and the polished cave floors get genuinely lethal underfoot.
why.autumn: October is still hot on open rock but clear; November is dry and cool, the best month on the Barabar ridge.

vibe: No beds on the hill, just a chai stall and local pilgrims climbing to the Siddheshwar Nath shrine on top
hub: Makhdumpur station 15 km on the Patna-Gaya line; Gaya 45 km, Patna 90 km, then auto to Bela and climb

spots.name: Lomas Rishi Cave
spots.note: Mauryan cave with the carved arch facade every later chaitya hall copies; unfinished inside and often gated, ask the guard.

spots.name: Sudama Cave
spots.note: Dedicated by Ashoka in 261 BCE, the polished chamber rings for seconds if you sing in it; carry a torch, there is no lighting.

spots.name: Siddheshwar Nath Temple
spots.note: Shiva shrine on the summit up a cut rock stair; avoid Mondays in Shravan, when thousands of kanwar pilgrims climb it.

spots.name: Nagarjuni Hill Caves
spots.note: Three more polished caves cut for Dasharatha, grandson of Ashoka; a rough path over the next hill and almost nobody else.

spots.name: Kauwa Dol
spots.note: Balanced boulder hill with old Buddhist and Hindu sculpture at its foot; ask in Bela for the path, about an hour round trip.

name: Bodh Gaya
tagline: Where the Buddha attained enlightenment - Mahabodhi Temple
festival: May: Buddha Purnima

why.winter: Peak pilgrim season: cool days, and occasional Dalai Lama teachings draw international crowds.
why.summer: Apr-Jun plains heat is severe, well past 40C: early-morning temple visits only, if at all.
why.monsoon: Humid and wet, though the Mahabodhi Temple complex stays green and quieter than winter.
why.autumn: Weather turns pleasant by November, a good lead-in to the winter pilgrim season.

vibe: Monastery guesthouses fill with Buddhist pilgrims from Japan, Thailand, Tibet.
hub: Fly/train to Gaya, 15km; or 2hr drive from Patna.

spots.name: Mahabodhi Temple
spots.note: The Bodhi tree and the diamond throne, chanting from before dawn in a dozen languages; phones and bags go in lockers at the gate.

spots.name: Great Buddha Statue
spots.note: Eighty foot Buddha of 1989 beside the Daijokyo temple, disciple figures in the garden; ten minutes on foot from the Mahabodhi.

spots.name: Sujata Stupa
spots.note: Brick mound at Bakraur where the milk rice was offered, across the Falgu; walk the footbridge and add the small Sujata museum.

spots.name: Dungeshwari Cave Temples
spots.note: Hill caves where the Buddha starved before giving up austerity, gaunt Buddha inside; hire an auto to wait, then a steep climb.

spots.name: Thai Monastery (Wat Thai Buddhagaya)
spots.note: Gold roofed wat of 1957, the first foreign monastery built here; free to enter, the row of national monasteries runs on from it.

spots.name: Vishnupad Temple
spots.note: Gaya's Vishnu footprint shrine on the Falgu, ringed by pind daan priests; non Hindus are kept out of the inner sanctum.

name: Kakolat Falls
tagline: Forest waterfall with a cold bathing kund under Nawada's hills

why.winter: Dec-Feb the fall thins to a quiet ribbon over green rock; the kund stays cold and you may share it with only langurs.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is 42 °C scrub heat with feeble flow, and the mid-April Bisua fair packs the kund with thousands of bathers.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug it roars but monsoon spate shut the site for six weeks in 2025; September keeps the volume as the picnic crush eases.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the honest best: full clear flow off the plateau rim, drier steps and cool forest air around the pool.

vibe: Managed picnic scene since the 2024 revamp, bathing in the lower pool only; sleep in Nawada or day-trip from Rajgir
hub: Nawada railhead about 35 km via Thali bazar; Rajgir 60 km and Gaya 90 km make workable day trips by car

spots.name: Gunawa Ji Jain Temple
spots.note: Jain tirth outside Nawada where Gautam Swami is said to have gained omniscience; white marble by a tank, dharamshala at the gate.

spots.name: Sitamarhi Cave
spots.note: Mauryan rock cut chamber polished like Barabar, hollowed out of one boulder near Hisua; unstaffed, ask in the village, take a torch.

spots.name: Fulwaria Dam
spots.note: Irrigation reservoir in the Rajauli hills that Nawada uses as a picnic spot; over an hour by car, carry your own food and water.

name: Kanwar Lake (Kabar Taal)
tagline: Asia's largest oxbow lake, a Ramsar wetland of winter ducks near Begusarai

why.winter: Dec-Feb is what it is for: bar-headed geese, pintail, coot and marsh harriers on the open water, a fisherman's boat at dawn from Manjhaul for a few hundred rupees
why.summer: By March the ducks leave and the water shrinks to channels among wheat and makhana fields; April is thin and May bakes at 43 C over a mostly dry bed, so wait
why.monsoon: June is hot over a shrunken bed; from Jul the Burhi Gandak floods the basin back into one sheet of water, lotus and makhana in leaf, jacanas and storks, no migrants
why.autumn: Oct is warm and green with the first waders; by late Nov the migrants are in and the light is soft, a good window before winter fog shuts down mornings

vibe: Fishermen and makhana farmers, no tourist trade; a basic lodge in Manjhaul or hotels in Begusarai 22 km south, evenings very quiet
hub: Begusarai station (Patna 3h by train), then bus or shared auto 22 km north to Manjhaul; a hired car from Patna is about 3h

name: Kesaria Stupa
tagline: Hundred-foot brick stupa rising out of empty Champaran fields

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: cool, dry, and you will usually have the whole terraced mound and its niches to yourself.
why.summer: March is the last decent month; April-June push past 40 C on open ground and there is no shade at all on the mound.
why.monsoon: June-September the Gandak belt floods, village approach roads dissolve and the brick terraces stay slick and unsafe.
why.autumn: October is warm but clear over green fields; November is cool and dry, the best time to circle the terraces slowly.

vibe: Utterly untouristed: a caretaker, some goats and you. The nearest beds are in Motihari or Muzaffarpur
hub: Motihari 45 km or Muzaffarpur 70 km by road; bus to Chakia, then a shared auto out to the stupa field

spots.name: Lauriya Areraj Ashokan Pillar
spots.note: Ashokan pillar still standing where he set it, the edicts legible on the shaft; open ground, no ticket, an hour by road.

spots.name: Someshwar Nath Temple
spots.note: Big Shiva temple at Areraj beside the pillar, packed all through Shravan; the Shivaratri fair fills the bazar, go early.

spots.name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya (Motihari)
spots.note: Museum on the 1917 Champaran satyagraha, photographs and letters; free entry, the memorial pillar stands in the yard outside.

spots.name: Moti Jheel
spots.note: Long lake through the middle of Motihari with a walking bund; the evening crowd comes out along it, minutes from the museum.

name: Lauriya Nandangarh
tagline: Ashoka's best-kept lion pillar beside a 25 m brick stupa mound in Champaran

why.winter: Nov-Feb: cool, mustard in flower around the Nandangarh mound, the polished pillar shaft catching low sun; you will likely have the whole site to yourself
why.summer: March is still fine at dawn; through Apr and May the open site bakes past 42 C with no shade beyond the pillar itself, so give it a miss until October
why.monsoon: June is furnace hot; Jul-Sep rains turn the mound and the Gandak country deep green and the approach lanes to mud, the site stays open, keep your rickshaw waiting
why.autumn: Oct-Nov: clear and mild, paddy being cut around the mounds, and Chhath in late Oct or Nov jams every train into Bihar, so book that leg well ahead

vibe: A sugar-mill village: ASI chowkidar, buffaloes on the mound, a lodge or two in Lauriya, better beds 28 km back in Bettiah
hub: Bettiah on the Muzaffarpur-Narkatiaganj line is the railhead, then bus or shared auto 28 km northwest, 1h; Patna 5h by road

name: Madhubani (Mithila art villages)
tagline: Painters' courtyards at Jitwarpur and Ranti in the Mithila plain
festival: Nov: Sama-Chakeva Mithila folk festival

why.winter: Dec-Feb at 7-24 C is the time to sit in courtyards watching panels being painted, with artists home and dry.
why.summer: March is warm but fine; April-June the plain hits 40 C and long power cuts shut most painting down by midday.
why.monsoon: June-September the Kamla Balan floods this district most years, cutting the village roads for days at a stretch.
why.autumn: October is muggy but drying out; November brings Sama-Chakeva, when clay bird figures fill every Maithil courtyard.

vibe: Artist families sell straight from the house and will teach you a panel; basic hotels in Madhubani town only
hub: Darbhanga airport 35 km with Delhi and Mumbai flights; Madhubani station on the Darbhanga-Jaynagar line

spots.name: Jitwarpur
spots.note: Painters' village of Sita Devi, courtyard walls covered in Mithila line work; families sell direct, agree a price before you sit.

spots.name: Ranti
spots.note: Home of Mahasundari Devi and Dulari Devi and the kachni line school; several houses run day long lessons if you ask ahead.

spots.name: Saurath Sabha Gachhi
spots.note: Mango grove where Maithil families arranged marriages for centuries; near empty outside June, Somnath Mahadev temple beside it.

spots.name: Rajnagar Palace
spots.note: Darbhanga Raj palace wrecked by the 1934 earthquake, marble temples still standing in the ruin; open ground, go before dark.

spots.name: Uchchaith Bhagwati Temple
spots.note: Headless Durga shrine in a bamboo grove where Kalidasa is said to have been made a poet; busy at Navratri, bus via Benipatti.

name: Mandar Hill (Bounsi)
tagline: Granite churning-myth hill with a Jain summit shrine and a lotus tank below
festival: mid-Jan: Bounsi mela at Makar Sankranti

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: cool mornings for the stepped climb to the Jain shrine on the summit, and the Makar Sankranti mela in mid-Jan fills Bounsi for a week
why.summer: March still works at first light; by May the bare granite radiates 43 C by 10 am and the steps are a punishment, so leave it until the rains
why.monsoon: June still burns; from Jul the hill greens and the Papharni tank fills round its island temple, but the steps run slick and storms build by afternoon, so go up early
why.autumn: Oct-Nov bring clear post-monsoon air, the plain still green below the summit ledges, and few people outside weekend pilgrim groups

vibe: Pilgrims and local picnic groups by day; sleep in a basic Bounsi lodge or the Jain dharamshala, or go back to Bhagalpur 45 km away
hub: Train to Mandar Hill station at Bounsi (Bhagalpur 1.5h), or bus from Bhagalpur or Deoghar; autos do the last 4 km to the hill

name: Mundeshwari Hill (Kaimur)
tagline: Octagonal hilltop shrine in worship for 1400 years, Kaimur falls beyond
festival: Sep/Oct: Sharadiya Navratri fair at the temple

why.winter: Nov-Feb is cool and clear: shared autos from Bhabua, the road or the steps up the hill, and the Kaimur escarpment sharp on the southern skyline; weekend crowds only
why.summer: March is fine early in the day, then Kaimur turns into one of Bihar's hottest corners, 44 C in May-Jun with no shade on the hill; not the time
why.monsoon: Jun is the last of the heat; Jul-Sep the hill and the escarpment go green and Telhar Kund (35 km) and Karkat Falls run full, and the ghat roads turn slippery
why.autumn: Oct-Nov: post-monsoon green, Navratri crowds in early Oct, then quiet; the best window to pair the temple with a day up on the plateau at Telhar Kund

vibe: Pilgrim families and Kaimur villagers; sleep in a Bhabua hotel or the temple dharamshala, evenings are dhaba food and dark hill
hub: Bhabua Road (Mohania) station on the Delhi-Kolkata line, 22 km on by shared auto to Ramgarh and the hill; Varanasi 3h

name: Munger
tagline: Fort town on a Ganga bend and home of the Bihar School of Yoga

why.winter: Dec-Feb is best at 9-25 C: fog off the river at dawn, empty fort ramparts and Sitakund's hot spring finally welcome.
why.summer: March is fine, then April-June sit at 40-43 C with hot river wind blowing straight over the exposed fort walls.
why.monsoon: June-September the Ganga swells hard against the fort wall, the ghats go under and humidity stays brutal all day.
why.autumn: October cools off as the river drops; November is clear and dry, good for walking the entire riverfront in a morning.

vibe: Yoga students at Ganga Darshan and a busy river-town bazaar; simple lodges and almost no other travellers
hub: Jamalpur Junction 8 km is the reliable railhead, small station in town; Patna 180 km by road or rail

spots.name: Munger Fort
spots.note: Crumbling walled fort right on the Ganga bend, free and always open; enter by Lal Darwaza and walk the rampart at sunset.

spots.name: Ganga Darshan (Bihar School of Yoga)
spots.note: Hilltop ashram of the Bihar School of Yoga above the river; casual visitors need permission, courses book out months ahead.

spots.name: Sita Kund
spots.note: Hot spring tank linked to Sita's fire ordeal, warm all year round; walled bathing enclosures, come early before the queues.

spots.name: Chandika Sthan
spots.note: Shakti Peetha where Sati's eye is said to have fallen, so it draws people seeking eye cures; heaving right through Navratri.

spots.name: Kashtaharini Ghat
spots.note: The town's main Ganga ghat below the fort wall, best at first light when the boats and bathers are out; steps stay slippery.

name: Rajgir (with Nalanda)
tagline: Ancient hills and hot springs, Nalanda ruins 12km away

why.winter: Cool, comfortable weather for walking between the hills and the Nalanda ruins. Best months by far.
why.summer: Severe plains heat makes the hilltop ropeway and open ruins uncomfortable by mid-morning.
why.monsoon: Humid and wet; the hot springs feel a lot less appealing when it's already sticky outside.
why.autumn: October keeps the tail of the rains and the mugginess; November turns cool and dry, enough to pair the peace pagoda with the zoo safari.

vibe: A pilgrim/history stop more than a backpacker hub - quiet, early evenings.
hub: Rajgir has its own station; 1.5hr from Patna by road/rail.

spots.name: Nalanda Mahavihara
spots.note: Red brick ruins of the great monastic university, ASI ticket, allow two hours; the site museum across the road holds the finds.

spots.name: Vishwa Shanti Stupa
spots.note: White peace stupa on Ratnagiri hill, reached by the ropeway from the base; last ride up is around 5 pm, keep the return ticket.

spots.name: Griddhakuta (Vulture's Peak)
spots.note: Rock terrace where the Buddha taught, a 20 minute climb off the road; go at dawn for the valley haze and empty stone seats.

spots.name: Brahmakund
spots.note: Hottest of the Rajgir hot springs at the foot of Vaibhagiri hill; men and women bathe apart, crowded and slippery after 9 am.

spots.name: Son Bhandar Caves
spots.note: Two rock cut chambers under Vaibhargiri with a polished wall and a hidden treasure legend; five minutes, carry a torch.

name: Sasaram & Rohtasgarh Fort
tagline: Sher Shah's tomb on a lake, and a lost fort up on the plateau

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the only sane window for the fort: 9-25 C, dry limestone steps and clear views off the Kaimur scarp.
why.summer: March is hot but doable; April-June hit 44 C on bare rock and the 2000-step limestone climb becomes dangerous.
why.monsoon: June-September the Kaimur streams run hard, the fort track washes out and snakes and leeches make the climb a bad idea.
why.autumn: October is warm and very green after the rains; November is dry and cool, the best month on the whole Rohtas plateau.

vibe: Basic hotels by Sasaram Junction and no other travellers; the fort day is you, a local guide and hill hamlets
hub: Sasaram Junction on the Delhi-Howrah grand chord; Rohtasgarh is 2 h by road then a 1.5 h stepped climb

spots.name: Sher Shah Suri Tomb
spots.note: Octagonal sandstone mausoleum on a causeway in the middle of a tank, ASI ticket; the light is best from the east bank at dusk.

spots.name: Rohtasgarh Fort
spots.note: Ruined plateau fort with Man Singh's palace and old gateways; drive to Rohtas village, then a 1.5 hour stepped climb, start by 7 am.

spots.name: Tarachandi Temple
spots.note: Rock cut Shakti shrine under a Kaimur cliff with an old inscription; empty on weekdays, a slow queue right through Navratri.

spots.name: Dhuan Kund
spots.note: Fall dropping into a gorge on the Kaimur edge, worth it only from July to October; the wet rock lip is genuinely dangerous.

spots.name: Hasan Khan Sur Tomb
spots.note: Tomb of Sher Shah's father, the earlier trial run for the great mausoleum; ASI protected, free, ten minutes off the highway.

name: Vaishali
tagline: Ashokan lion pillar standing where the Buddha last preached

why.winter: Dec-Feb is ideal at 8-25 C, with the Kolhua pillar and the relic stupa near-empty and Patna only 1.5 h away.
why.summer: March still works, then April and May bake the open mounds at 40 C with no shade and dust off the bare fields.
why.monsoon: June-September the Gandak floods these fields, approach roads go under water and the excavated mounds turn to mud.
why.autumn: October clears up over green paddy; November is quiet, cool and the best month to walk between the two sites.

vibe: A working village of mango orchards rather than a tourist town; sleep in Hajipur or Muzaffarpur, not here
hub: Hajipur 30 km, Muzaffarpur 36 km, Patna 55 km over Gandhi Setu; shared autos from Lalganj crossing

spots.name: Ashokan Pillar at Kolhua
spots.note: Polished lion pillar of Ashoka beside a brick stupa and the monkey tank, ASI ticket; mornings are cool and nearly empty.

spots.name: Relic Stupa
spots.note: Low brick mound under a shed where a share of the Buddha's ashes was dug up; ten minutes, pair it with the museum.

spots.name: Vaishali Museum
spots.note: Small ASI museum of Licchavi era terracottas and seals from the mounds nearby; closed Fridays, tickets stop before 5 pm.

spots.name: Vishwa Shanti Stupa
spots.note: Japanese built peace pagoda beside the Abhishek Pushkarini coronation tank; free, dawn to dusk, a short walk from the stupa.

spots.name: Raja Vishal ka Garh
spots.note: Grassy earth mound held to be the Licchavi assembly ground, free and unfenced; five minutes to walk right round the rampart.

name: Valmiki Nagar (Valmiki Tiger Reserve)
tagline: Bihar's only tiger reserve, on the Gandak at the Nepal border

why.winter: Dec-Feb is prime at 8-26 C: sal forest safaris, gharials on the Gandak and the Someshwar ridge clear to the north.
why.summer: March gives good waterhole sightings; April-June push 42 C in west Champaran and an open jeep becomes an ordeal.
why.monsoon: Safaris shut roughly 1 July to 30 September, the Gandak floods and Valmiki Nagar turns into a dead end for visitors.
why.autumn: Gates usually reopen in October into wet green forest with poor visibility; from November the sightings get good.

vibe: Forest eco-huts and Tharu village homestays, a handful of Indian birders and absolutely no nightlife
hub: Valmiki Nagar station on the Narkatiaganj line, Bagaha 40 km; permits at the gate, Gorakhpur 130 km

spots.name: Gandak Barrage (Bhainsalotan)
spots.note: Long barrage over the Gandak with Nepal on the far bank; it is a border post, so carry ID and do not photograph the gates.

spots.name: Valmiki Ashram
spots.note: Riverside Valmiki temple that gave the town its name, where Sita is said to have raised Lav and Kush; busiest at Ram Navami.

spots.name: Triveni Sangam
spots.note: Confluence of the Gandak and its hill streams just above the barrage on the Nepal border; ten minutes down from the road.

name: Vikramshila (Antichak)
tagline: Excavated Pala monastic university above the dolphin Ganga

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season at 10-25 C over the cruciform stupa, with the best odds of Gangetic dolphins off Kahalgaon.
why.summer: March is workable; April-June the open excavation has zero shade and Bhagalpur runs 40-43 C under a dust haze.
why.monsoon: June-September the Ganga floods the Kahalgaon diara, dolphin boats stop running and the brickwork stays waterlogged.
why.autumn: October is warm and green with the river still high; November is dry and cool, ideal for both the ruins and the river.

vibe: One ASI site museum, no cafes and no travellers; base in Bhagalpur and come out for a long half day
hub: Bikramshila halt 3 km, Kahalgaon 13 km, Bhagalpur 40 km; autos from Kahalgaon, dolphin boats from the ghat

spots.name: Vikramshila Site Museum
spots.note: ASI museum at the excavation holding Pala bronzes and stone panels from the monastery; closed Fridays, small ticket.

spots.name: Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary
spots.note: Protected Ganga stretch where river dolphins surface; hire a boat at Kahalgaon ghat soon after sunrise, an hour is enough.

spots.name: Bateshwar Sthan (Patharghatta)
spots.note: Rock spur above the Ganga near Kahalgaon with old rock cut carvings and a Shiva shrine; unsigned, take a driver who knows it.

name: Chandigarh
tagline: India's planned modernist city, orderly and green
festival: Feb: Chandigarh Rose Festival

why.winter: Crisp and clear: the best season to walk Sukhna Lake and the Rock Garden.
why.summer: Dry heat past 40C by May; the city's wide open plazas offer little shade.
why.monsoon: July and August drop about 275 mm each and hold 34C with 27C nights; rain-fed Sukhna refills and its floodgates open.
why.autumn: Mild and clear: a comfortable time to explore the sector grid on foot.

vibe: Safe and easy alone, but more a comfortable stopover than a place to linger.
hub: Fly into Chandigarh (IXC) or 4h train/bus from Delhi

spots.name: Rock Garden of Nek Chand
spots.note: Nek Chand's secret city of sculpture built from broken bangles, tiles and waste; allow 90 minutes and go on a weekday morning.

spots.name: Capitol Complex
spots.note: Le Corbusier's High Court, Assembly and Open Hand, a UNESCO site; free guided tours at 10, 12 and 3, carry photo ID.

spots.name: Sukhna Lake
spots.note: Man made lake with a 2 km promenade under the Shivaliks; boats from 9 am, but sunrise before the joggers is the good hour.

spots.name: Government Museum and Art Gallery
spots.note: Gandhara Buddhas and Pahari miniatures that came here when Lahore's collection was split in 1947; closed Mondays.

spots.name: Sector 17 Plaza
spots.note: The city's pedestrian concrete heart of shops, bookstalls and a fountain; it only fills up after 6 pm, quiet by 9.30.

spots.name: Zakir Hussain Rose Garden
spots.note: Asia's largest rose garden in Sector 16, free and open dawn to dusk; the beds are only in flower from February to March.

name: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve (Maikal Hills)
tagline: Hilly sal forest and Baiga hamlets on the road to Amarkantak

why.winter: Dec to Feb the Maikal nights drop under 8C and the morning jeep from Achanakmar gate runs through mist; sightings are slow, the forest is the point.
why.summer: March stays cool at dawn and April pulls gaur and sloth bear to the waterholes; by May the ridge bakes past 42C and dust hangs over the track.
why.monsoon: June still has the gates open to the 30th but runs past 43C with dust on the track; Jul to Sep they shut for the breeding season and the Maniyari crossings wash out.
why.autumn: October reopens a green, leech free forest and November is the pick: cold mornings, clear air, and the Amarkantak road drive at its best.

vibe: Forest rest houses and two or three resorts near the gate; jeeps are shared with whoever turns up, and evenings are pitch dark
hub: Bilaspur railhead, then 55 km by bus on the Amarkantak road to the gate; Pendra Road station is closer from the north

name: Barnawapara Sanctuary
tagline: Sal forest of gaur and sloth bears an easy hop from Raipur

why.winter: Nov-Feb is 10-28 C with misty sal-forest drives, gaur herds in the glades and machan evenings at the Hareli eco resort.
why.summer: Mar-May pushes past 42 C but waterholes bunch the gaur and chital; drive at dawn and sleep through the white afternoons.
why.monsoon: Closed for safaris 1 July to 31 October; the sal canopy shuts over flooded tracks and the resort all but winds down.
why.autumn: October is still shut, so aim at the 1 November reopening: fresh-washed forest and Siddhakhol's falls still flowing.

vibe: CG Tourism's Hareli eco resort by the forest plus basic gate rooms; couples, birders and no crowds at all
hub: Raipur airport-railhead 100 km: NH-53 to Pithora then 40 min north; book resort and safari jeep ahead

spots.name: Turturiya
spots.note: Old temple site by a forest stream, held to be Valmiki's ashram where Lav and Kush were born; forest road in, carry water.

spots.name: Girodpuri Dham
spots.note: Satnami pilgrimage centre of Guru Ghasidas under a huge white Jaitkhamb pillar; a half day out, go before the noon heat.

name: Barsur
tagline: Eleventh century Naga temples in a Bastar village of ponds

why.winter: Dec to Feb mornings sit near 12C, good for walking between the Mama Bhanja and Battisa temples and the two big tanks with nobody about.
why.summer: March is dry and bearable; April climbs hard and May holds 43C over open stone with no shade at the ruins, which is why it is blocked.
why.monsoon: The Indravati fills and the paddy around the temple tanks turns green; Aug and Sep are fine, though June and July storms cut the Geedam road.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov give the best light of the year here, warm days, dry lanes, and Chitrakote still running full 34 km up the river.

vibe: A quiet village of tanks and loose stone; sleep at Geedam or Dantewada, since Barsur has a rest house and tea shops and no more
hub: Geedam is the junction, 24 km short of Barsur on the Indravati road; Dantewada railhead sits on the Kirandul line

name: Bhoramdeo (Kawardha)
tagline: Carved 11th-century Nagara temple below the Maikal hills

why.winter: Dec-Feb is 10-28 C and the stone carving reads best in low sun; add Madwa Mahal and Cherki Mahal on foot.
why.summer: Apr-Jun runs 43 C on the Kawardha plain and the temple courtyard has almost no shade by mid-morning.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the Maikal ridge behind the temple disappears into cloud; the site is lovely and empty, roads are patchy.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the easy season - warm days, Baiga hamlets in the hills above, and the temple tank actually full.

vibe: Very few visitors midweek; one jungle retreat by the temple and simple lodges in Kawardha 18 km away
hub: No railhead: Kawardha 18 km has buses from Raipur (3 h) and Bilaspur, then a shared jeep

spots.name: Madwa Mahal
spots.note: Shiva temple built as a stone wedding pavilion, its plinth ringed with erotic carving; a five minute walk off the main road.

spots.name: Sarodha Dadar
spots.note: Hilltop meadow in the Maikal range above the Chilphi ghat road, cool even in May; CG Tourism cottages if you stay the night.

spots.name: Kawardha Palace
spots.note: White 1930s palace of the Kawardha royals, now a heritage hotel; non guests can usually see the grounds if you ask at the gate.

spots.name: Cherki Mahal
spots.note: Small ruined stone shrine in the fields past Madwa Mahal, nobody around; keep the same driver waiting and keep it short.

spots.name: Bhoramdeo Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Sal and bamboo forest reaching towards Kanha, gaur and sloth bear country; drive the Chilphi road at dawn, sightings are luck.

name: Chitrakote Falls (Bastar)
tagline: India's widest waterfall in the heart of tribal Bastar
festival: Aug-Oct: Bastar Dussehra, a 75-day tribal festival.

why.winter: Falls thin to a scenic curtain, but easiest season for Kanger Valley caves and tribal haats.
why.summer: Indravati runs low, falls reduce to a trickle over bare rock. Hot, dusty, skip unless for markets.
why.monsoon: Chitrakote's real fame: Indravati floods the 300m ledge into a genuine roar; roads turn muddy though.
why.autumn: Falls still strong from the monsoon, Bastar's weeks-long Dussehra usually falls now. Best time to come.

vibe: Remote tribal heartland: expect local guides and market-goers, barely any tourists.
hub: Fly/train to Jagdalpur via Raipur (7-8h), then local taxi.

spots.name: Narayanpal Temple
spots.note: Eleventh century Vishnu temple on the Indravati bank with nobody else there; ask around for the caretaker to open it.

spots.name: Mendri Ghumar Falls
spots.note: Narrow fall into a wooded gorge off the Jagdalpur road, with a viewing deck; only worth the stop while the monsoon water lasts.

spots.name: Tamda Ghumar Falls
spots.note: Tall thin fall in the forest close to Mendri Ghumar, down a steep stepped path; the steps are slippery, do not go alone.

spots.name: Chitradhara Falls
spots.note: Small curtain fall on the road towards Jagdalpur, easy to reach and shallow; a quick monsoon stop, dry by February.

name: Gangrel Dam (Ravishankar Sagar)
tagline: Mahanadi mega-reservoir with a beach strip and water sports

why.winter: Nov-Feb is 13-29 C with jet skis and kayaks off the Mini Goa strip and rafts of migratory ducks on the open water.
why.summer: Apr-Jun runs 43 C while the water recedes off hot mudflats; sports pause and the treeless banks give you no shelter.
why.monsoon: Aug-Sep after heavy Mahanadi rain the spillway gates open to a roar and half of Dhamtari arrives; check flow, then go.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the reservoir sits brim-full against green hills; midweek the CG Tourism cottages by the water are yours.

vibe: Raipur weekenders, picnic families and anglers at the jetty; lakeside CG Tourism cottages make the overnight
hub: Raipur 90 km (2 h on NH-30) via Dhamtari, then 15 km to the dam; buses to Dhamtari, autos or taxi beyond

spots.name: Rudreshwar Mahadev Temple (Rudri)
spots.note: Old Shiva temple beside the Rudri barrage where the Mahanadi is held for canals; a calm evening stop just out of Dhamtari.

spots.name: Maa Angarmoti Mandir
spots.note: Village goddess of the valley the reservoir drowned, shifted up when the water rose; a short marked detour on the dam road.

spots.name: Bilai Mata Mandir
spots.note: Dhamtari's own goddess temple, walked to by the whole town through Navratri; ten minutes, and the bazaar is right there.

spots.name: Murumsilli Dam
spots.note: Asia's first siphon spillway dam, finished in 1923 and still green and empty; a picnic drive, nothing sold on site.

name: Jagdalpur (Bastar)
tagline: Bastar's tribal capital, weekly haats and bell-metal workshops
festival: Oct: Bastar Dussehra, the Danteshwari rath procession at Jagdalpur

why.winter: Nov-Feb is 12-30 C, the season for village haats, the anthropological museum and day trips out to Chitrakote.
why.summer: March is still fine, but Apr-May the Bastar plateau sits at 42 C and the haats thin out by mid-morning.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep delivers most of Jagdalpur's 1,500 mm of rain; interior roads wash out and you should not drive them after dark.
why.autumn: October is the peak - the Dussehra rath is dragged through town, Danteshwari's rituals run for days, book beds early.

vibe: Small, friendly market town; stick to the main circuit, sleep in town, and let a local guide take you to the haats
hub: Jagdalpur airport has flights via Raipur; the Kirandul-Visakhapatnam line is a 12 h ride through the Ghats

spots.name: Bastar Palace
spots.note: Low plain palace of the Bastar rajas in the middle of town, offices now; only the outside is open, and it anchors Dussehra.

spots.name: Danteshwari Temple
spots.note: The rajas' goddess temple beside the palace and the heart of the 75 day Bastar Dussehra; shoes off at the gate, no photos.

spots.name: Tirathgarh Falls
spots.note: Wide stepped falls in Kanger Valley park, hundreds of steps to the base; buy the park ticket at the gate, closed in monsoon.

spots.name: Kutumsar Caves
spots.note: Long limestone cave with stalactites and blind fish, seen with a guide; open only in the dry season, expect to wait a batch.

spots.name: Dalpat Sagar
spots.note: Big old tank on the town edge, dug by a Kakatiya raja; the walk round it at sunset is what locals actually do here.

spots.name: Anthropological Museum
spots.note: Government museum of Bastar tribal tools, masks and bell metal, good before the haats; closed Mondays, tiny fee.

name: Jogimara Caves (Ramgarh Hill)
tagline: Rock cut theatre and a painted cave on a Sarguja hill

why.winter: Dec to Feb the Sarguja plateau drops near 6C at night and the climb to Sitabenga is dry and clear; carry water, there is nothing on the hill.
why.summer: March is the last comfortable month; April and May put 40C on an open rock face with a 45 minute climb and no shade or shop at the top.
why.monsoon: Jul to Sep the hill goes green and the Meghaduta story starts to make sense, but the rock steps turn slick and the leeches are real.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov are the pick: dry rock underfoot, long views over Sarguja paddy, and Ambikapur close enough to drive back the same evening.

vibe: No village at the caves, just a caretaker and goats; sleep at Udaipur town 5 km off or in Ambikapur, and eat where the bus stops
hub: Ambikapur is the base, 50 km by bus to Udaipur on the Raigarh road, then a jeep and a 45 minute climb to the caves

name: Mainpat
tagline: Chhattisgarh's misty plateau hill station and mini-Tibet

why.winter: Genuinely cool hill air, near-frost mornings: best season for Tiger Point and the monastery.
why.summer: Warms into low-mid 30s by April-May. Mild by plains standards, but falls run at their thinnest.
why.monsoon: Waterfalls run full and the plateau turns lush green. A hidden-gem season if roads stay dry enough.
why.autumn: Rains taper through October, falls still flowing, quieter than the Dec-Jan domestic rush.

vibe: A little-visited plateau: you'll likely be the only outside traveller around.
hub: Reach Ambikapur via Bilaspur/Raipur, then 1h taxi up.

spots.name: Tibetan Camp, Kamleshwarpur
spots.note: Tibetan refugee settlement of 1962 with a small monastery and carpet looms; ask before photographing houses.

spots.name: Tiger Point
spots.note: A stream drops off the plateau edge into a wooded gorge; only full from July to October, last stretch is a rough track.

spots.name: Mehta Point
spots.note: The plateau rim looking down over the Surguja plains, the standard sunset stop; cloud swallows it through the monsoon.

spots.name: Jaljali
spots.note: A few acres of spongy peat where the ground bounces underfoot; no signs or railings, take someone local to find it.

spots.name: Ulta Pani
spots.note: Roadside stream that appears to run uphill, an optical illusion of the slope; worth ten minutes if you are passing.

name: Rajim
tagline: Three-river sangam with an 8th-century temple in the riverbed
festival: Feb: Rajim Kumbh Kalp at the Triveni Sangam

why.winter: Dec-Feb is 12-29 C, you can walk the dry riverbed to Kuleshwar Mahadev, and February brings the Kumbh crowds.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the Mahanadi bed is baked white sand at 44 C, the ghats are empty and there is no shade at the sangam.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the three rivers rise and the island temple is cut off or half under water - the sangam walk is impossible.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the water drops again, the Rajivlochan temple courtyard is calm, and evening aarti draws a small local crowd.

vibe: A pilgrim town for a fortnight and a sleepy one the rest of the year; basic lodges, most day-trip from Raipur
hub: 45 km south of Raipur on the NH-30 Jagdalpur road, hourly buses take 1.5 h; Raipur is the working railhead

spots.name: Rajivlochan Temple
spots.note: The 8th century Vishnu temple at the centre of town, carved pillars in the mandap; open early, shoes off at the gate.

spots.name: Kuleshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Stone shivalaya on a plinth out in the riverbed at the sangam; you walk across sand to it once the Mahanadi drops.

spots.name: Triveni Sangam
spots.note: Where the Mahanadi, Pairi and Sondur meet; the ghats fill for the Magh mela in February and are empty otherwise.

spots.name: Champaran
spots.note: Birthplace of Vallabhacharya, a walled temple compound out in the fields; Vaishnav crowds in February, quiet otherwise.

name: Ratanpur (Mahamaya)
tagline: Kalachuri capital of tanks, fort ruins and a Mahamaya shrine
festival: Sep/Oct: Navratri manas singing at the Mahamaya temple

why.winter: Dec to Feb is when the tanks hold the fort wall at dawn and the temple lanes stay cool; an easy day of walking, then Bilaspur for dinner.
why.summer: March still works before the plains turn; May sits at 45C with black rock underfoot around Ratanpur fort, so the month is blocked outright.
why.monsoon: June is dry and near 43C until the rain lands; Jul to Sep the old tanks brim, Khutaghat dam runs over and the Maikal foothills go green with almost nobody about.
why.autumn: Navratri in Oct packs the Mahamaya temple with all night manas singing, then November empties out and the fort ruins are yours alone.

vibe: A temple town of pilgrims rather than tourists; dharamshalas and small lodges here, proper hotels 25 km down the road in Bilaspur
hub: Bilaspur junction is 25 km, buses every 20 minutes on the Amarkantak road; Raipur airport is 145 km

name: Sirpur
tagline: Brick temples and Buddhist viharas of a lost Kosala capital

why.winter: Dec-Feb is 12-29 C and ideal - the 7th-century Laxman brick temple, Surang Tila and the viharas in one flat walk.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the Mahanadi plain runs 44 C with no shade over the excavations; there is nowhere here to escape it.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the site is green and empty but the mounds are muddy and buses from Raipur run late in heavy rain.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is dry and clear, the Mahanadi still full behind Gandheshwar temple, and you will likely be alone there.

vibe: An excavated village rather than a town; beds are basic, so most people come and go from Raipur in a day
hub: 78 km east of Raipur on NH-53 via Arang, about 2 h by bus, then an auto out to the temple field

spots.name: Laxman Temple
spots.note: The 7th century brick temple, doorway carved with Vishnu avatars, still on its plinth; ASI ticket, gates shut at sunset.

spots.name: Surang Tila
spots.note: Stepped stone temple platform dug out in 2007, its staircase left skewed by an old earthquake; climb up to read the layout.

spots.name: Anand Prabhu Kuti Vihar
spots.note: Excavated Buddhist monastery, monk cells around a courtyard and a seated Buddha; ten minutes on foot from the Laxman temple.

spots.name: Gandheshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Living temple on the Mahanadi bank built from carved fragments of the ruined city; busiest at Mahashivratri.

spots.name: Sirpur Museum
spots.note: Small ASI collection of sculpture lifted from the mounds, bronzes and door jambs; half an hour, ask at the gate if it looks shut.

name: Tatapani (Balrampur)
tagline: Sulphur hot springs steaming beside a Sarguja river bed
festival: Jan: Tatapani Mahotsav at Makar Sankranti

why.winter: Dec to Feb is the whole point: 6C mornings and water rising out of the sand hot enough to scald, plus the Sankranti mela in mid January.
why.summer: March is still fine before 9 am; by May Balrampur runs at 44C and standing over a hot spring in that is pointless, so it is blocked.
why.monsoon: Jul and Aug the river rises and swallows the spring pools while the Ramanujganj road floods; September drains slowly and June is just hot.
why.autumn: October dries the banks and the springs surface again; by November the nights are cold enough for the steam to show, and nobody is there.

vibe: A tourism resort of huts and a couple of dhabas by the mela ground; outside January you may be the only guest and evenings end early
hub: Ambikapur is the railhead, then about 90 km by bus on the Ramanujganj road; Balrampur town is 3 km short of the springs

name: Tirathgarh Falls (Kanger Valley)
tagline: Terraced falls and limestone caves inside Kanger Valley park

why.winter: Nov to Feb is the run: cool sal forest mornings, the gate open by 8, and Kotumsar's cave floor dry enough for the guided crawl.
why.summer: March is still pleasant and quiet; by late April Bastar pushes past 40C and the falls thin to a few white threads over the ledges.
why.monsoon: Jul to Sep the park gate stays shut and Kotumsar floods, so the falls run at their fullest with nobody let in; June access ends mid month.
why.autumn: The gate reopens around 1 November with the Kanger river still loud and the sal forest washed green, so October is a waiting game.

vibe: Log huts and a forest rest house at the falls, plus Jagdalpur hotels 35 km back; evenings are dark and loud with cicadas
hub: Jagdalpur, 35 km by taxi or shared jeep on the Sukma road; the Kirandul line from Visakhapatnam stops at Jagdalpur

name: Daman
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
tagline: Portuguese forts, dark-sand beaches and legal bars

why.winter: Nov-Feb at 15-30 °C is the time for the Moti Daman fort walls, the old churches and a walk on dark sand.
why.summer: Apr-May is a muggy 35 °C and the tide pulls out a kilometre at Jampore, leaving hot grey mud to wade.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep dumps most of a 1,900 mm year, the sea runs brown and rough and the beaches are simply unusable.
why.autumn: October dries out and by November the light is clean; weekends stay loud with drinkers, weekdays are calm.

vibe: Weekend drinkers escaping dry Gujarat, plus quiet Portuguese lanes and cheap seafood if you come midweek
hub: Vapi station on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad line 12 km, then auto; Surat 100 km, Mumbai 180 km by road

spots.name: Moti Daman Fort
spots.note: Sixteenth century Portuguese walls around the old quarter, offices and a lighthouse inside; walk the ramparts at sunset.

spots.name: Bom Jesus Church
spots.note: Church of 1603 inside Moti Daman fort, gilded carved wood altar and painted ceiling; open around morning mass.

spots.name: Nani Daman Fort (St Jerome)
spots.note: Smaller 17th century fort on the north bank with a big carved gateway; the fishing wharf below it is the real show.

spots.name: Jampore Beach
spots.note: Dark sand south of Moti Daman, water muddy and swimming poor; come for the long walk, the shacks and the cold beer.

spots.name: Devka Beach
spots.note: Rocky black shore north of town with a promenade and food stalls; not for swimming, best at dusk when the lights go on.

spots.name: Dominican Monastery ruins
spots.note: Roofless seminary inside Moti Daman fort, arches and a carved pulpit still standing; free and open all day, no shade.

name: Diu
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
tagline: Portuguese-era island enclave with forts and beer
festival: Feb: Diu Carnival (Portuguese-Goan-style street parade)

why.winter: Best weather - warm days, cool evenings, forts and empty beaches at their most pleasant.
why.summer: Hot and increasingly humid, still swimmable but the town feels sleepier and sweatier.
why.monsoon: Sea turns rough and unsafe for swimming, though the fort and old town keep quiet charm.
why.autumn: October cools down fast, a good early-season alternative before winter crowds arrive.

vibe: Slow island town - the easy legal beer stop next to dry Gujarat, mellow backpacker trickle
hub: Fly direct to Diu (DIU) or drive/bus 2h from Una/Veraval; no train

spots.name: Diu Fort
spots.note: Sea-girt Portuguese fort of 1535 with cannons, a lighthouse and an old jail wing; free, closes near 6 pm, no shade at all.

spots.name: Naida Caves
spots.note: Quarry chambers outside the city wall where the Portuguese cut building stone; go 9 to 11 am for the shafts of light.

spots.name: Nagoa Beach
spots.note: Horseshoe bay lined with hoka palms, the one properly swimmable beach on the island; quiet and tout-free before 9 am.

spots.name: St Paul's Church
spots.note: Jesuit church of 1610 still in use, with a huge carved wooden altar; open through the day, mass on Sunday morning.

spots.name: Gangeshwar Temple
spots.note: Five shivlings in a rock cleft at Fudam that the sea washes over; check the tide, spray reaches the steps at high water.

name: Dudhni Lake
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
tagline: Shikara rides on the Madhuban backwaters under Warli hills

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the season: glassy water at 15-30 C, shikaras and kayaks running, and Warli villages walkable along the shoreline.
why.summer: Apr-May bakes at 38 C while the reservoir drops to mudbanks; water sports wind down and there is little reason to come.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Damanganga catchment turns deep green and the lake refills; boating pauses in heavy spells but the drives are lovely.
why.autumn: Oct is the sweet spot: a brim-full lake, freshly washed hills and weekday emptiness before winter weekenders find the jetty.

vibe: Tourism-department lakeside cottages; Gujarati and Mumbai weekend families, Warli hamlets, weekday solitude
hub: Vapi railhead 60 km via Silvassa and Khanvel; taxi is realistic, buses to Dudhani are rare, go before dark

spots.name: Madhuban Dam
spots.note: The dam on the Damanganga whose backwaters make this lake; a detour off the Silvassa road, fullest just after the rains.

spots.name: Khanvel
spots.note: The small town on the road in, with a garden, a few eating places and the last ATMs before the lake; fill up here.

spots.name: Satmaliya Deer Park
spots.note: Fenced forest enclosure of spotted deer and blackbuck on the Silvassa road; a short drive-through loop, best early.

name: Silvassa
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
tagline: Warli country and boat rides on the Dudhni backwaters

why.winter: Dec-Feb at 14-30 °C is the pleasant window for the Dudhni backwaters, the tribal museum and Vanganga garden.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is a sticky 40 °C, the reservoir drops and there is little reason to be here beyond the hotel bars.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep greens the Sahyadri edge and gets the streams running, but Mumbai weekend traffic clogs every viewpoint.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the best value of the year: full reservoir, green hills and no crowd outside the Diwali rush.

vibe: Honest picnic territory: Gujarati and Mumbai weekenders, hotel bars, and Warli villages just outside town
hub: Vapi railhead 18 km by auto or shared jeep; Dudhni Lake is 40 km east, Daman 25 km west

spots.name: Tribal Cultural Museum
spots.note: Warli masks, fish traps and wedding gear from the hill hamlets in one room; an hour, pair it with the Vanganga garden.

spots.name: Vanganga Lake Garden
spots.note: Japanese-style island garden with a boating lake at Dadra, built by the tourism office; evenings and weekends get busy.

spots.name: Vasona Lion Safari Park
spots.note: Caged-bus circuit through a lion enclosure in the Vasona forest; short and zoo-like, check it is running before you go.

spots.name: Satmaliya Deer Park
spots.note: Fenced deer and blackbuck enclosure on the Khanvel road; early morning is the only time the animals are out grazing.

spots.name: Our Lady of Piety Church
spots.note: Whitewashed Portuguese-era parish church in the old quarter, the one colonial relic left in town; quiet outside mass.

name: Delhi
tagline: Mughal monuments and India's transit hub
festival: Jan: Republic Day Parade

why.winter: Pleasant days but dense smog and cold nights, especially December-January: carry a mask.
why.summer: Dry heat regularly crosses 42C; plan sightseeing for early morning and AC malls by afternoon.
why.monsoon: Humid with sudden waterlogging, but a welcome break from summer's heat all the same.
why.autumn: The best window: clearer skies and mild temperatures before winter smog sets back in.

vibe: Huge hostel scene in Paharganj and Hauz Khas; stay street-smart after dark.
hub: International/domestic airport (DEL) or major rail hub

spots.name: Humayun's Tomb
spots.note: The 1570 Mughal garden tomb the Taj Mahal was modelled on, red sandstone and marble; ASI ticket, late afternoon light.

spots.name: Jama Masjid
spots.note: Shah Jahan's 1656 mosque above Old Delhi; climb the south minaret for the rooftop view, visitors are out at prayer times.

spots.name: Chandni Chowk
spots.note: Old Delhi's bazaar lanes: silver, spice at Khari Baoli, paratha at Paranthe Wali Gali; most shops shut on Sunday.

spots.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
spots.note: Shah Jahan's walled palace of 1648, marble halls and museums in the barracks; closed Mondays, entry at Lahori Gate.

spots.name: Qutub Minar
spots.note: Twelfth century victory tower and the rustless iron pillar in the Quwwat-ul-Islam ruins; yellow line to Qutab Minar.

spots.name: Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah
spots.note: Sufi shrine down a crowded market lane; qawwali after sunset on Thursday, cover your head, leave shoes at a stall.

spots.name: Lodhi Gardens
spots.note: Fifteenth century tombs scattered through a landscaped park, free and open dawn to dusk; the best morning walk in town.

spots.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
spots.note: Stepwell dropping a hundred steps into the ground between office towers off Hailey Road; free, and quietest before 10 am.

name: Anjuna-Vagator
tagline: North Goa's flea-market, trance-party, hostel strip
festival: Dec: Sunburn Festival (nearby Vagator)

why.winter: Peak season - every shack, hostel and trance party is open, beaches packed with travellers.
why.summer: Pre-monsoon swelter and rising humidity - only budget shacks and locals stick around.
why.monsoon: Shacks dismantled, sea too rough to swim - this is Goa's quiet, empty off-season.
why.autumn: Shacks rebuild through October; by November the season is back in full swing.

vibe: Hostel-hopping party strip - flea markets, sunset parties, easiest place to meet people
hub: Fly into Goa (Dabolim/Manohar), taxi or bus 40min to Anjuna

spots.name: Chapora Fort
spots.note: Ruined Portuguese fort on the headland above Vagator, sunset over the river mouth; ten minute climb, no shade or water.

spots.name: Anjuna Flea Market
spots.note: The Wednesday market by the beach, roughly November to April; get there before noon and treat every price as an opening bid.

spots.name: Ozran Beach (Little Vagator)
spots.note: Cove under the cliffs with the carved Shiva face in the rock; steep path down, calmer than the Anjuna shack strip.

spots.name: Hilltop, Vagator
spots.note: Open-air trance venue in a coconut grove, survivor of the old party scene; season only, outdoor sound stops at 10 pm.

spots.name: Saturday Night Market, Arpora
spots.note: Lit-up night bazaar at Arpora on Saturdays in season, live music and food stalls; tourist prices, easy first night out.

spots.name: Mapusa Friday Market
spots.note: The market Goans actually use, Friday mornings: produce, chourico sausage, feni; it is over by early afternoon.

spots.name: Assagao
spots.note: Inland village of Portuguese houses turned into cafes and boutiques; leafy, walkable, where the Anjuna crowd eats.

name: Arambol & Mandrem
tagline: North Goa's hippie tail end, drum circles and cheap huts

why.winter: Dec-Feb is peak: 31 °C days, calm sea, the sunset drum circle at the north end, and huts from about 800 rupees.
why.summer: Mar-May empties out as the huts shut and humidity climbs past 80 percent; still swimmable, but the scene has left.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the huts are dismantled, lifeguards fly red flags all day, and the sweet water lake path turns to mud.
why.autumn: Oct is rebuilding season with half the huts up; by mid-November everything is open and the sea has settled.

vibe: Long-stay hippie crowd, yoga and jam sessions, easy to arrive alone and be eating with strangers by day two
hub: Mopa airport 30 km or Dabolim 65 km; Thivim railhead 30 km, then a bus to Arambol via Mandrem

spots.name: Sweet Water Lake
spots.note: Freshwater lagoon behind the rocks north of Arambol beach, warm and shallow; twenty minutes on foot round the headland.

spots.name: The Banyan Tree
spots.note: Huge banyan up the jungle path past the lake, a long-running hangout for sadhus and drummers; carry water, no shops.

spots.name: Keri Beach (Querim)
spots.note: Wide empty sand backed by casuarinas at the Tiracol river mouth; the flat ferry across runs free every half hour.

spots.name: Terekhol Fort
spots.note: Small Portuguese fort across the river, now a hotel, with a chapel and a view back down the coast; take the Keri ferry.

spots.name: Ashwem Beach
spots.note: Quieter sand south of Mandrem with shacks spaced far apart; walkable from Mandrem at low tide, otherwise take the road.

spots.name: Morjim Beach
spots.note: Olive ridley turtles nest here from November to February, nests roped off with a forest hut; wide, flat and windy.

name: Betul (Cabo de Rama coast)
tagline: Fishing village at the Sal river mouth under the Cabo de Rama cliffs

why.winter: Nov-Feb the sea lies flat, trawlers unload at the jetty at first light and the cliff track south towards Kakolem is walkable; shacks open, never full.
why.summer: March keeps a sea breeze. April and May run 33 C with heavy humidity, the water is bathwater warm and most small places shut by the middle of May.
why.monsoon: Jun-Jul the fishing ban keeps the trawlers in harbour, boats to Kakolem stop and lifeguards red-flag the water; by Aug and Sep the cliffs turn green.
why.autumn: Oct is quiet and rinsed clean, the Sal river runs high and the walk up to Cabo de Rama fort is all green; November brings back the boats and the shacks.

vibe: Fishermen, a lighthouse hill and a few family guest houses; evenings are harbour lights and one bar, with no music scene at all.
hub: Madgaon railhead 30 km or Dabolim 45 km, then a Cuncolim bus to Betul; a scooter is the only way on south to Cabo de Rama.

name: Chandor & Loutolim
tagline: Indo-Portuguese mansions in the Salcete hinterland

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the time to walk Chandor and Loutolim: 30 °C, dry, and cool enough to cross between the mansions.
why.summer: Apr-May is 35 °C on shadeless village roads; the houses stay open but you will be wrung out between any two.
why.monsoon: Jun-Jul is relentless rain with no shelter between houses; Aug-Sep eases and the paddy behind Braganza House greens up.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is close to perfect, warm and clear, with the mansions almost to yourself before the December crowd.

vibe: Almost no traveller infrastructure, a few heritage homestays; you knock, pay a fee and the family shows you round
hub: Margao railhead 12 km, then a local bus or auto; Dabolim airport 30 km, Palolem 35 km south

spots.name: Braganza House
spots.note: The long mansion facing Chandor's square, split into two family wings; ring the bell, each side asks its own donation.

spots.name: Fernandes House
spots.note: Older house with a hidden basement bunker the family used during raids; visits by appointment, ask around the village.

spots.name: Our Lady of Bethlehem Church
spots.note: Chandor's parish church; the Three Kings feast on 6 January brings boys on horseback in from the neighbouring wards.

spots.name: Ancestral Goa (Big Foot)
spots.note: Open-air model of an old Goan village at Loutolim with a laterite Mirabai carving; small entry fee, an hour at most.

spots.name: Casa Araujo Alvares
spots.note: Loutolim mansion shown as a guided audio tour of one family's rooms; ticketed with Ancestral Goa just across the road.

name: Chorla Ghat
tagline: Cloud-forest edge of Goa above the Vazra Sakla waterfall
