vibe: A few Rohru families running Larot homestays, shepherds on the ridge, a rest house at Dodra; evenings are a bukhari and no phone signal
hub: Shimla-Rohru bus (5 h), Rohru-Larot bus or taxi 35 km, then a shared jeep 30 km over the pass to Dodra

name: Chitkul
tagline: Last inhabited village toward the Indo-Tibet border

why.winter: Heavy snow often blocks the Sangla-Chitkul road and most homestays shut for the season - genuinely closed.
why.summer: May-Jun bring the best access window before monsoon, clear Baspa river views, open homestays.
why.monsoon: Jun holds up; Jul-Aug bring rockfall-prone stretches on the Karcham-Sangla road, a real risk.
why.autumn: Sep-Oct are stunning and stable - golden poplars, clear peaks, before the road turns treacherous again.

vibe: A handful of homestays and ITBP soldiers - beautiful solitude, not a crowd of travellers.
hub: Fly/train to Shimla, 9-10h via Kinnaur (Reckong Peo, Sangla).

spots.name: Mathi Devi Temple
spots.note: Three wooden shrines to the village goddess with carved deodar panels; the inner room is shut, look from the yard

spots.name: Hindustan Ka Aakhri Dhaba
spots.note: The last dhaba sign everyone photographs, rajma chawal and chai above the Baspa; open only through the summer season

spots.name: Baspa River
spots.note: Meadow and boulder bank below the village where the camps sit; the water is glacial, no swimming, evenings turn cold fast

spots.name: Nagasti ITBP Post
spots.note: Track upstream from the village to the last army post, two easy hours return; ask at the barrier, you cannot pass it

spots.name: Lamkhaga Pass Trek
spots.note: Hard week long crossing to Harsil over a 5280 m pass, starting here; needs a guide, permits and real mountain experience

name: Churdhar (via Nohradhar)
tagline: Sirmaur's 3,647 m Shiva summit above a sea of foothills

why.winter: December-March bury the trail and the temple sarai shuts; this becomes serious snow terrain, not a casual yatra, stay away.
why.summer: Snow patches linger into April; May-June is prime, an 18 km one-way climb from Nohradhar through deodar and rhododendron.
why.monsoon: June holds dry; July-August is a slippery viewless slog on clay tracks, and September clears into a superb climbing window.
why.autumn: October gives the big clear-sky payoff, plains shimmering one way and snow ridges the other; November is cold and crystalline.

vibe: Pilgrim-trekker mix: langar meals and dorm blankets at the summit sarai, weekend groups up from Chandigarh.
hub: Buses from Solan or Nahan reach the Nohradhar trailhead in about 3 h; Chandigarh air and rail are 4 h out

spots.name: Chureshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Shiva shrine on the summit rocks with a sarai and langar; nights freeze even in June, so carry warm layers up

spots.name: Nohradhar
spots.note: Trail head village where you register at the forest post before climbing; last shops, and buses from Solan or Nahan

spots.name: Teesri
spots.note: Midway halt on the Nohradhar climb with a dhaba and water at the treeline; most people break here before the rocks

spots.name: Habban Valley
spots.note: Apple and stone fruit valley below Nohradhar with a few homestays; a slow day off after the climb, buses are rare

name: Dalhousie
tagline: Raj-era pine hill town with colonial churches

why.winter: Dec can bring snow and holiday crowds; Jan-Feb are colder, much quieter, good for a calm visit.
why.summer: Apr-May are the classic season - pleasant 15-25C days pull crowds fleeing Punjab and Delhi heat.
why.monsoon: Jun is manageable; Jul-Aug bring heavy rain, view-hiding mist, and landslide-prone approach roads.
why.autumn: Clear and calm - pine forests at their best, comfortable temperatures, fewer tourists.

vibe: More honeymoon couples and families than backpackers - pleasant, no crowd scene.
hub: Fly Gaggal (2.5h) or Delhi-Pathankot train, then 3h taxi in.

spots.name: St. John's Church
spots.note: Dalhousie's oldest church, built 1863, standing where the two mall roads meet at Gandhi Chowk; stone walls and stained glass

spots.name: Dainkund Peak
spots.note: Ridge top at 2745 m with the Pholani Devi shrine; 1.5 km walk up from the air force gate, which closes in the evening

spots.name: Kalatop Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Deodar and oak forest on the Khajjiar road, a level track to the old rest house; buy the ticket at the Lakkarmandi gate

spots.name: Panchpula
spots.note: Stream pools and Ajit Singh's samadhi in a deodar hollow below town; the walk down is easy, the climb back is not

spots.name: Garam Sadak
spots.note: The sunny half of the ring road between Gandhi Chowk and Subhash Chowk, 2 km level; the whole town walks it at dusk

spots.name: Satdhara Falls
spots.note: Seven mica rich springs on the path towards Panchpula, a 20 minute detour; thin by May, best right after rain

name: Dhankar
tagline: Cliff-edge fort monastery above the Spiti-Pin confluence

why.winter: November-March the 8 km link road up from Sichling is snowbound and the old village is effectively shut; skip it entirely.
why.summer: May-June works at 3-20C, and the one-hour climb to Dhankar Lake at 4100 m is doable once the last snow patches go.
why.monsoon: Rain shadow keeps Dhankar dry through July-August, but the crumbling conglomerate cliffs shed rock after any real shower.
why.autumn: September-October is the shot everyone comes for: the fort on its spur with the Spiti and Pin rivers meeting far below.

vibe: A monastery guesthouse and a couple of homestays in a tiny cliff-top village; the nights are silent and very cold
hub: Turn off at Sichling on the Spiti road, 8 km up by shared taxi; 32 km from Kaza, no bus to the village

spots.name: Dhankar Monastery
spots.note: Mud and timber gompa wedged on the crag above the Spiti and Pin confluence; small ticket at the door, no photos inside

spots.name: Dhankar Lake
spots.note: Green pool at 4140 m, an hour of steep switchbacks above the village; carry water, there is no shade and no shop up there

spots.name: Lhalung Monastery
spots.note: The Golden Temple of the Lingti valley, clay figures on gilt walls; the caretaker holds the key, ask in the village

name: Janjehli (Shikari Devi)
tagline: Seraj valley trailhead for the Shikari Devi summit temple

why.winter: Deep snow shuts the Shikari Devi top; the valley itself stays reachable and very quiet, with cold clear days and basic rooms.
why.summer: April-June is ideal for the 16 km forest trek to Shikari Devi's roofless hilltop temple, through oak, deodar and open meadow.
why.monsoon: July-August turn the trails slippery and leech-ridden and the Chailchowk road slips in bursts; September dries out fast.
why.autumn: October is the sweet spot, sharp views from the 3,332 m ridge over half of Himachal; November gets properly cold.

vibe: Farm valley with basic guesthouses and a forest rest house; pilgrims and shepherds, rarely another tourist.
hub: From Mandi, buses via Chailchowk take 3-4 h; no railhead near, and Bhuntar airport is half a day away

spots.name: Shikari Devi Temple
spots.note: Roofless stone shrine on a 3359 m summit; 6 km climb from the village or a rough jeep track to within 3 km of the top

spots.name: Shikari Devi Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Deodar and oak forest on the way up to the temple, monal and musk deer country; walk it early, the tracks are unmarked

spots.name: Thunag
spots.note: The nearest proper bazaar and bus junction on the Mandi road, with the last ATM; Janjehli's own shops shut by dark

name: Jibhi
tagline: Pine-forest hideout near Jalori Pass, quieter than Manali

why.winter: Snow dusts the pines and Jalori Pass often closes, but Jibhi itself stays open and cosy.
why.summer: Prime season - Mar-May bring mild days, waterfalls in full flow, Serolsar Lake trek reopening.
why.monsoon: Jun is fine; Jul-Aug make the narrow Aut-Jibhi road landslide-prone and swell the streams.
why.autumn: Crisp, clear and quiet - the best forest light of the year, well before winter cold arrives.

vibe: Homestay bonfires draw more couples on weekend escapes than big backpacker groups.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (2h drive) or Delhi-Aut bus (10h), 1h taxi to Jibhi.

spots.name: Jalori Pass
spots.note: 3120 m pass with tea dhabas and a Mahakali shrine at the top; snow closes the road about January to March, taxis turn back at Shoja

spots.name: Serolsar Lake
spots.note: Forest lake a 5 km walk east of Jalori Pass with the Budhi Nagin temple beside it; locals say birds keep it free of leaves

spots.name: Jibhi Waterfall
spots.note: Short fall in a mossy gorge ten minutes off the main road, wooden bridge over it; crowded from noon, go early

spots.name: Chehni Kothi
spots.note: Tall dry stone tower house at Chehni village, entered by a ladder to the upper floor; 1 km of steep steps from the road

spots.name: Raghupur Fort
spots.note: Ruined wall on a meadow ridge 3 km west of Jalori Pass, Dhauladhar view; about an hour up, no water on the trail

spots.name: Shringa Rishi Temple
spots.note: Banjar valley's presiding deity at Baggi village, carved wood and slate roofs; the palanquin travels to fairs, so it can be shut

name: Jispa (Bhaga Valley)
tagline: Bhaga riverside village on the Leh road, base for Baralacha La and Suraj Tal

why.winter: Dec-Mar not now: the Leh road is shut at Baralacha, the camps and lodges are boarded up and snow cuts the Keylong-Darcha stretch for days
why.summer: March is still snowbound; April thaws the village; by late May the Keylong-Darcha buses run again, though Baralacha La usually opens only in June
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the season: Baralacha La and Suraj Tal a 2 h drive up, Deepak Tal 8 km on, Manali-Leh buses and bikers passing through; rain rarely reaches this far
why.autumn: October is clear and cold, gold poplars by the Bhaga and empty roads before Baralacha shuts in November; by then the camps are packed away and lodges close

vibe: Leh-road bikers and Zanskar trekkers in riverside camps and a few lodges; evenings are cold, quiet and loud with the Bhaga
hub: Manali-Keylong bus via the Atal Tunnel (4 h), then Keylong-Darcha bus 40 min; the HRTC Manali-Leh bus stops here Jul-Sep

name: Kafnu (Bhabha Valley)
tagline: Road-end trailhead for the Pin-Bhabha trek, deodar and meadows above the Sutlej

why.winter: Dec-Feb snow closes the 20 km road from Wangtu for days at a time and the two or three guest houses barely open; the valley is lovely but you may be stuck in it
why.summer: March is cold with snow still lying above the village; April is wet; May is the start, blossom below and the day walk to the Mulling meadow at 3,200 m open again
why.monsoon: June is the best Pin-Bhabha crossing month; Jul-Aug bring slides on NH5 around Wangtu and leeches in the lower forest, Sep dries out and the meadows are still green
why.autumn: Oct is peak: gold birch on the ridges, the pass still crossable in the first half, the Kinnaur road settled; November is cold, clear and empty before the first snow

vibe: A hydro-project village with a PWD rest house and two family guest houses; trekkers and their mules pass through, evenings are early
hub: Shimla-Reckong Peo buses drop you at Wangtu on NH5 (7 h), then a daily bus or shared jeep 20 km up to Kafnu

name: Kalpa
tagline: Old Kinnaur capital facing sacred Kinnaur Kailash

why.winter: Cold but genuinely rewarding - snow-capped Kinnaur Kailash views draw photographers year after year.
why.summer: May-Jun bring warm days, blossoming orchards and the best light on the Kinnaur Kailash range.
why.monsoon: Jun is fine; Jul-Aug bring rockfall risk on the Karcham-Wangtu approach, a genuine hazard.
why.autumn: Sep-Oct are ideal - apple harvest, clear peak views, comfortable temperatures before winter.

vibe: Old Kinnauri wood houses and orchard homestays - peaceful, few solo travellers.
hub: Fly/train to Shimla, 7-8h drive via Reckong Peo, Kinnaur.

spots.name: Suicide Point
spots.note: Sheer drop into the Sutlej gorge by Roghi village, apple terraces on the way out; no fencing, keep off the lip

spots.name: Narayan-Nagini Temple
spots.note: Carved stone and wood temple in old Kalpa with a Buddhist gompa sharing the courtyard; leave shoes and leather outside

spots.name: Chandika Devi Temple
spots.note: Kothi village's silver faced goddess in a tiered pagoda temple below Kalpa; the inner shrine stays closed to visitors

spots.name: Brelengi Gompa
spots.note: Large seated Buddha above Reckong Peo, built for the 1992 Kalachakra; quiet at midday, walk up through the orchards

spots.name: Reckong Peo
spots.note: District town below Kalpa for ATMs, buses and the inner line permit foreigners need beyond Jangi; the office shuts by 5 pm

name: Karsog Valley
tagline: Apple valley of ancient pagoda temples off the Shimla grid

why.winter: Cold, quiet and occasionally snow-dusted; you get temple courtyards to yourself and woodsmoke evenings in village homestays.
why.summer: March-April spread apple and plum blossom across the orchards; May stays mild at 1,470 m while the plains below cook.
why.monsoon: July-August rain slips the Tattapani approach road with depressing regularity and turns orchard lanes to mud; wait it out.
why.autumn: October-November bring harvest-end light on the pagoda roofs of Mamleshwar and Kamaksha and sharp ridgelines all around.

vibe: Orchard villages and thousand-year-old wood temples; homestays around Mamel and Chindi host the odd quiet traveller.
hub: Buses from Shimla via Tattapani or from Mandi, both about 4 h; air and rail links are all far

spots.name: Mamleshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Wooden Shiva temple at Mamel said to be Pandava built; the drum and the giant wheat grain are kept inside, ask the pujari

spots.name: Kamaksha Devi Temple
spots.note: Pagoda temple at Kao village under dense wood carving, the valley's own goddess; the last kilometre of road is narrow

spots.name: Mahunag Temple
spots.note: Temple at Chindi where Karna is worshipped as the naga Mahunag; Chindi has the HPTDC hotel, the easiest bed in the valley

spots.name: Pangna Fort
spots.note: Tall stone and timber keep of the old Suket capital at Pangna, houses packed around it; reached on foot through the lanes

spots.name: Tattapani
spots.note: Sulphur springs on the Sutlej, mostly drowned when the Kol dam filled; a few pools remain by the bridge, resorts pipe the water

name: Kasauli
tagline: Cantonment pines, colonial bakeries and a Sunset Point ridge

why.winter: December-February drops to 2-12C with the odd snow flurry, log fires in the old hotels and almost no day-trippers about.
why.summer: April-June is why Kasauli exists: 18-28C under deodar while Chandigarh below sits at 42C, but weekends are fully booked.
why.monsoon: July-August is fog, leeches on the Gilbert Trail and washed-out views; the Kalka road stays open but there is little to do.
why.autumn: October-November is the clearest window, when you can watch the Chandigarh grid light up from Sunset Point after dark.

vibe: A quiet army cantonment where walking is the whole point; Chandigarh weekenders, old-school hotels, no hostel scene
hub: Kalka railhead 24 km on the Delhi line, Chandigarh airport 60 km; shared taxis up from Dharampur on NH-5

spots.name: Monkey Point
spots.note: Hanuman temple on the highest hill, inside an air force base; photo ID needed, no phones or cameras past the gate

spots.name: Christ Church
spots.note: 1853 church on the Mall with stained glass and horse chestnuts in the yard; open through the day, service on Sunday

spots.name: Gilbert Nature Trail
spots.note: Level 1.5 km ledge path cut into the hillside near the air force gate; go at first light for birds and clear plains

spots.name: Sunset Point
spots.note: Railed ridge at the end of Upper Mall looking over the Punjab plains; on a clear night you can pick out Chandigarh's lights

spots.name: Dagshai Jail Museum
spots.note: 1849 cellular jail down the hill in Dagshai cantonment, cells that held the Connaught Rangers mutineers; small ticket at the gate

name: Kasol
tagline: Parvati valley's trance-backpacker hub, gateway to treks

why.winter: Cold, quiet and cheap - cafes stay open, snow dusts the ridgelines, a mellow off-season pick.
why.summer: Prime season - Mar-May bring warm days, full guesthouses and a steady flow of backpackers.
why.monsoon: Jun is manageable; Jul-Aug swell the Parvati river and repeatedly shut the Bhuntar-Kasol road.
why.autumn: The busiest, best window of the year - clear valley views, trance parties, easy trekking weather.

vibe: German bakeries and trance beats - the easiest place in India to join strangers by lunch.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (30 min) or overnight Delhi bus (11h), then 1h to Kasol.

spots.name: Manikaran Sahib
spots.note: Gurudwara over boiling springs, langar rice cooked in the water; free baths, the deep pools scald, cover your head

spots.name: Chalal
spots.note: Cafe hamlet across the Parvati, twenty minutes over the footbridge; cheaper beds than Kasol and no ATM up there

spots.name: Grahan Village
spots.note: Slate roofed village up a side nallah, 4 to 5 hours each way, the easiest overnight trek here; carry your own water

spots.name: Rasol
spots.note: Four hard hours up from Chalal to a village that keeps to itself; ask before photographing anyone or entering houses

spots.name: Ram Mandir, Manikaran
spots.note: Seventeenth century stone temple beside the gurudwara, images said to come from Ayodhya; steam fogs the courtyard

name: Kaza (Spiti)
tagline: Spiti's cold-desert capital - monasteries and moonscapes
festival: Aug: Ladarcha trade fair

why.winter: Brutally cold (-15 to -25C), most stays shut, but Shimla-Kinnaur road stays open for snow-leopard trips.
why.summer: The Manali-Kaza road via Kunzum Pass opens by late May/Jun, ending isolation, starting the season.
why.monsoon: Spiti's real peak - a rain-shadow desert, so this is HP's warmest, driest, greenest window.
why.autumn: Kunzum shuts by late Oct, cutting the Manali shortcut, but harvest and clear light reward Kinnaur route.

vibe: Shared taxis and Zostel Spiti gather a small rotating cast of overlanders.
hub: Fly Bhuntar, 10-12h via Kunzum (Jun-Oct) or the Shimla-Kinnaur road.

spots.name: Key Monastery
spots.note: Spiti's largest gompa stacked up a hillock above the river; morning prayers around 6 am, butter tea if you sit in

spots.name: Chicham Bridge
spots.note: Deep gorge crossing between Kibber and Chicham, claimed as Asia's highest bridge; walk across, the wind funnels hard after noon

spots.name: Langza
spots.note: Village at 4400 m under a large seated Buddha, known for the ammonites in its shale; homestays only, no shop or ATM

spots.name: Komic
spots.note: Tangyud monastery at 4587 m in one of the highest villages with a road; the cafe shuts by October, go slow up here

spots.name: Hikkim
spots.note: The world's highest post office, where the postmaster stamps and sends your card; carry change, delivery takes weeks

spots.name: Kibber
spots.note: Stone village above a limestone canyon, the base for snow leopard tracking in winter; sanctuary trails start behind it

name: Khajjiar
tagline: Saucer meadow and lake nicknamed 'Mini Switzerland'

why.winter: Dec-Jan can bring snowfall on the meadow, popular for a day trip; otherwise cold, thin on facilities.
why.summer: Apr-May bring the meadow to its greenest, with pony rides and paragliding in full swing.
why.monsoon: Jun is fine; Jul-Aug turn the meadow to mud and the Dalhousie-Khajjiar road landslide-prone.
why.autumn: Clear skies and cool air make Oct-Nov ideal for photos without summer's day-tripper crowds.

vibe: A day-trip stop for Dalhousie tourists, not really a solo base.
hub: Reach via Dalhousie (24km, ~45 min taxi); base in Dalhousie.

spots.name: Khajji Nag Temple
spots.note: Twelfth century Nag shrine with a golden dome at the meadow's edge, carved Pandava figures inside; shoes off at the porch

spots.name: Kalatop Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Deodar sanctuary between here and Dalhousie, a level 3 km track to the rest house; buy the ticket at the Lakkarmandi gate

spots.name: Dainkund Peak
spots.note: 2745 m ridge on the Dalhousie road with the Pholani Devi shrine on top; the last stretch is on foot, the gate shuts by evening

name: Kheerganga
tagline: Hot-spring trek camp, a backpacker rite of passage

why.winter: A genuine snow trek for those with proper gear - magical frozen campsite, not for casual solo hikers.
why.summer: May-Jun bring the clearest trail after snowmelt and the most reliable weather for the climb.
why.monsoon: Jun holds up; Jul-Aug bring leeches, slick rock sections and real flash-flood risk on the river.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov are the classic window - dry trail, clear ridgeline views, hot spring feels best in the cold.

vibe: Communal tent camps and a shared hot spring make it easy to bond with fellow trekkers.
hub: Fly Bhuntar, drive to Barshaini (1.5h), then trek 9-10km/5-6h.

spots.name: Parvati Kund
spots.note: Hot spring tank at the top of the meadow, the point of the whole trek; there is a screened section for women, no soap in the water

spots.name: Rudra Nag
spots.note: Snake shaped fall beside the trail about 4 km below the meadow; the last dhabas before the steep final climb

spots.name: Nakthan Village
spots.note: Old Parvati village on the lower trail with taps and rooms; the Kalga route skips it, this way is longer but gentler

spots.name: Kalga
spots.note: Orchard village above the Barshaini roadhead where most trekkers sleep before or after; the nearest ATM is back at Kasol

spots.name: Mantalai Lake
spots.note: Source of the Parvati, two hard days on from the meadow; go with a guide, the Pin Parvati pass beyond needs a permit

name: Kibber (Spiti)
tagline: Whitewashed village at 4,270 m, India's best chance of seeing a snow leopard

why.winter: Dec-Feb is snow leopard season: minus 25 C nights, bukhari-heated homestays and village trackers on the gorge ridges; the Kinnaur road can shut for days
why.summer: March still has leopards and hard snow; Apr-May the thaw turns lanes to mud and Kunzum stays closed, so it is a long haul in from Shimla, but the village is empty
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is easy Spiti: Kunzum open from Manali, the Chicham bridge 3 km on, the Kibber sanctuary walks, blue sheep on the slopes; hardly any rain this deep in
why.autumn: October is gold and cold with the clearest skies of the year and Kunzum open until early Nov; November empties the homestays as snow starts and only the Kinnaur road stays

vibe: Homestay families, wildlife photographers in winter and Kaza day-trippers in summer; evenings are butter tea, thukpa and stars
hub: Manali-Kaza bus via Kunzum (Jun-Oct, 10 h) or year-round via Shimla and Kinnaur (2 days); Kaza-Kibber bus daily, 20 km

name: Kugti (Budhil Valley)
tagline: Last Gaddi village under the 5,040 m Kugti Pass, slate roofs and a Kartik shrine

why.winter: Dec-Mar not now: two metres of snow, the Hadsar-Kugti track buried and most Gaddi families gone down to Kangra with the flocks, so there is nobody left to host you
why.summer: April is thaw and mud with the pass firmly shut; by May the families are back, the terraces are green and the 4 h walk up from Hadsar is through flowering rhododendron
why.monsoon: Jun is clear and the pass crossing to Lahaul opens; Jul-Aug are wet with slippery slate paths and Manimahesh yatra crowds at Hadsar; Sep clears and the Gaddis start moving
why.autumn: Oct is the finest: dry paths, snow on the Kugti Pass ridge, brown bear sightings in the sanctuary meadows before the flocks head down; Nov is cold and the village thins out

vibe: Gaddi families who take you in for a few hundred rupees, a forest rest house and no real shop; nights are the Budhil and a wood fire
hub: Pathankot rail, then bus to Chamba (5 h) and Bharmour (2.5 h); Bharmour-Hadsar bus 13 km, then 12 km by jeep or on foot

name: Kullu
tagline: Dussehra town where 200 village gods gather on Dhalpur maidan
festival: Oct: Kullu Dussehra, seven days (dates shift yearly)

why.winter: December-February is 0-15C with wet grey spells and most people push straight through to Manali, which is why rooms are cheap.
why.summer: April-June is 18-32C and green, the Beas runs hard, and the Manali highway through town is one long queue of tourist cars.
why.monsoon: July-August is the wrong call: cloudbursts, Beas flooding and NH-3 landslides have cut Kullu off for days in recent years.
why.autumn: October is the reason to come, when 200 palanquin deities converge on Dhalpur for Dussehra; book a room a month ahead.

vibe: Most travellers only change buses here; stay and you get Nati dancing, shawl looms and no backpacker scene at all
hub: Bhuntar airport 10 km with Delhi flights; HRTC and Volvo buses from Delhi in 12 h, Chandigarh in 8 h

spots.name: Bijli Mahadev
spots.note: Ridge temple at 2460 m where lightning is said to shatter the lingam; drive to Chansari, then a 3 km climb of about an hour

spots.name: Raghunath Temple
spots.note: Seat of Kullu's ruling deity at Sultanpur, the image brought from Ayodhya in 1651; open mornings and evenings only

spots.name: Basheshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Ancient stone shikhara temple at Bajaura on the highway, carved Vishnu, Ganesh and Durga panels outside; ASI site, no ticket

spots.name: Jagannathi Devi Temple
spots.note: Bhekhli village shrine up a steep 30 minute climb with the whole valley below; go at sunrise, the path is unlit

spots.name: Dhalpur Maidan
spots.note: The ground where the Dussehra rath is pulled each October and village deities camp; an ordinary field the rest of the year

spots.name: Pirdi
spots.note: Beas rafting start below town, 14 km of grade 2 and 3 down to Jhiri; the river shuts through the monsoon, best April to June

name: Malana
tagline: Isolated village with its own ancient customs and laws

why.winter: Snow can cut off the approach trail entirely; a hard, cold visit best left to experienced trekkers.
why.summer: Mar-May bring the clearest trail conditions and the best light on Malana's steep valley slopes.
why.monsoon: Jun is workable; Jul-Aug bring landslide risk on the Jari approach and a slick, risky final trek.
why.autumn: Stable, dry trail conditions and clear views make Oct-Nov the easiest window to visit respectfully.

vibe: Strict local customs (no touching villagers/homes) - observe, don't socialise.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (1h to Jari), then 3km/1.5h uphill trek, no road in.

spots.name: Jamlu Devta Temple
spots.note: Wooden temple of Jamlu, the village deity; outsiders may look but must never touch it, its walls or the offerings.

spots.name: Malana Dam
spots.note: Hydel project dam at the road head below the village; park here, the climb up takes about an hour with a pack.

spots.name: Chanderkhani Pass
spots.note: 3,660 m ridge pass on the old shepherd route over to Naggar; a 7 hour day from the village, snow free June to October.

spots.name: Rashol
spots.note: Small village over the 3,300 m Rashol Pass, about 5 hours on foot; homestays are basic and the trail fades in mist.

name: Manali
tagline: Himalayan backpacker basecamp for treks and easy adventure
festival: Jan: Manali Winter Carnival

why.winter: Dec brings snow and NYE crowds; Jan-Feb are colder, calmer, still fine for Solang snow trips.
why.summer: Peak escape-the-heat season - Apr-May are warm, green and busiest, book Old Manali stays ahead.
why.monsoon: Jun is still decent; Jul-Aug bring the Kullu-Manali highway's worst landslides, best avoided; Sep clears fast.
why.autumn: The best weather of the year - clear skies, apple harvest, cool nights, fewer crowds than summer.

vibe: Old Manali's cafe strip makes it easy to fall into a group of travellers by dinner.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (50 min) or overnight Volvo from Delhi (12-14h) to Manali.

spots.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
spots.note: Cedar wood pagoda of 1553 standing in a deodar grove above town; go before 9 am, tour buses fill the yard by ten.

spots.name: Vashisht Hot Springs
spots.note: Free sulphur baths beside the Vashisht temple, separate tanks for men and women; the water is scalding, go early.

spots.name: Old Manali
spots.note: The cafe strip up the hill past Manu Temple, easiest place to eat alone; most kitchens shut from November to March.

spots.name: Jogini Falls
spots.note: Two tier fall above Vashisht, a 45 minute climb past apple orchards; the rocks at the top stay slippery all day.

spots.name: Solang Valley
spots.note: Meadow below the glacier with paragliding, zip line and the Atal ropeway; book at the base counters, not from touts.

spots.name: Rohtang Pass
spots.note: 3,978 m pass holding snow into June; permits are online and capped daily, and the road shuts every Tuesday.

spots.name: Bhrigu Lake
spots.note: Lake at 4,240 m reached from Gulaba, two days with a night at Rola Kholi; tents and guides hire in Old Manali.

name: Mandi
tagline: Choti Kashi: eighty stone temples along the Beas ghats
festival: Feb/Mar: International Mandi Shivratri fair

why.winter: December-February runs 4-18C with cold, clear mornings on the ghats, and the seven-day Shivratri fair fills every lodge in town.
why.summer: March is warm and green, but by May the valley floor hits 36C and the stone temples are bearable only at dawn and dusk.
why.monsoon: Mandi takes some of Himachal's heaviest rain; July-August brings NH-3 landslides and a brown, dangerous Beas below the ghats.
why.autumn: October-November is the cleanest air of the year at 10-25C, with the ghats quiet, rooms cheap and every onward bus running.

vibe: A working hill town, not a resort: temple priests, college students, bus-stand chaos and cheap lodges near the Chowk
hub: Bhuntar airport 70 km; only railhead is Joginder Nagar narrow gauge, 55 km; all Delhi-Manali buses halt here

spots.name: Bhutnath Temple
spots.note: The 1520s Shiva temple on the Beas ghat at the centre of town; the week long Shivratri fair starts from here.

spots.name: Panchvaktra Temple
spots.note: Five faced Shiva in stone where the Suketi joins the Beas; cross the old suspension bridge and come at sunset.

spots.name: Triloknath Temple
spots.note: Shikhara temple of 1520 in Purani Mandi on the right bank of the Beas, far quieter than Bhutnath; open all day.

spots.name: Tarna Devi Temple
spots.note: Hilltop Shyama Kali shrine above the bus stand; 15 minutes up the steps buys the best view over town and river.

spots.name: Chauhatta Bazaar
spots.note: Old market lanes around Seri Manch square, good for cheap thalis and hill caps; most shutters are down by 8 pm.

spots.name: Pandoh Dam
spots.note: Beas dam with a turquoise reservoir on the Kullu highway; you may stop on the road above, photography is barred.

name: Masroor & Pong Lake
tagline: Eighth-century rock-cut temples above a Ramsar lake of a hundred thousand geese

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: cool 18 C days, the Dhauladhar white behind the shrines and bar-headed geese in the tens of thousands on the Pong shallows at Nagrota Surian
why.summer: March is still pleasant with the flocks leaving; Apr-May climb past 38 C on the bare Masroor ridge, so see the temples at dawn and skip the lake shore
why.monsoon: June is the hottest and haziest; Jul-Aug rain fills Pong, drowns the winter mudflats and greens the Kangra hills, Sep clears with the reservoir at its widest
why.autumn: Oct is warm and quiet with the water high; by mid-November the first geese and pochards come in and the Dhauladhar snow reappears behind the temples

vibe: A temple ridge visited by almost nobody, a forest rest house at Nagrota Surian and Kangra homestays; evenings are birds, not bars
hub: Fly Gaggal (35 km) or the Pathankot narrow gauge to Kangra Mandir; Kangra-Lunj-Masroor buses take 1.5 h

name: McLeod Ganj
tagline: Dalai Lama's home-in-exile - Tibetan culture hub
festival: Feb/Mar: Losar (Tibetan New Year) at the main temple

why.winter: Cold with occasional snow; a real niche season for the snow trek up to Triund, otherwise quiet and cheap.
why.summer: Peak season - Mar-May bring warm days, packed meditation courses and full Dharamkot guesthouses.
why.monsoon: Jun holds up; Jul-Aug make this one of HP's wettest towns, with trail leeches and frequent rockfall.
why.autumn: Best weather of the year - sharp Dhauladhar views, comfortable trekking temps, thinner crowds.

vibe: Meditation courses by day, guitar circles and momos by night - an easy solo scene to join.
hub: Fly Gaggal (20 min) or overnight Volvo from Delhi (10-12h).

spots.name: Tsuglagkhang Complex
spots.note: The Dalai Lama's temple, Namgyal monastery and the Tibet Museum in one yard; free, but no bags during teachings.

spots.name: Bhagsu Falls
spots.note: Fall above Bhagsunag temple, 20 minutes on foot from Bhagsu village; a trickle in May, full right after the rains.

spots.name: Triund
spots.note: Ridge camp at 2,850 m under the Dhauladhar, 4 hours up from Gallu; fine as a day walk, tents at the top cost more.

spots.name: Dharamkot
spots.note: Uphill village of yoga courses, Tushita and the Vipassana centre; courses fill months ahead, walk ins are rare.

spots.name: St John in the Wilderness
spots.note: 1852 stone church in a deodar grove at Forsyth Ganj with Lord Elgin's grave; usually open mornings only.

spots.name: Norbulingka Institute
spots.note: Tibetan arts campus at Sidhpur with thangka and woodcarving studios and a garden cafe; workshops idle on Sundays.

spots.name: Gyuto Monastery
spots.note: The Karmapa's seat at Sidhbari, a big gompa facing the Dhauladhar; the prayer hall is open to visitors, shoes off.

spots.name: Kangra Fort
spots.note: Katoch stronghold above the Banganga, wrecked by the 1905 quake; audio guide at the gate, allow two hours.

name: Miyar Valley (Urgos)
tagline: Lahaul's glacier-headed side valley of July wildflower meadows

why.winter: Snowbound and shut: homestays close, the road above Udaipur turns unreliable and nobody attempts it from November to May.
why.summer: Mar-May the valley is still snowed in, homestays shut and the road above Udaipur unreliable; hold out for the late-June opening.
why.monsoon: July-September is peak and largely rain-shadowed: wildflower meadows, blue-sheep slopes and day walks toward the Miyar glacier.
why.autumn: Early October turns the willows gold under freshly whitened peaks; by late October homestays wind down and real cold arrives.

vibe: A handful of trekkers and climbers; village homestays in Urgos and Khanjar, long silences, shared-kitchen dinners.
hub: Manali to Udaipur via the Atal tunnel takes 5-6 h; from Udaipur a daily-ish bus or shared jeep runs to Urgos

spots.name: Khanjar
spots.note: Last village with homestays before the trail up the valley; stock up here, there is no shop beyond and no signal.

spots.name: Kang La
spots.note: 5,450 m pass at the head of the valley crossing into Zanskar; six days from Urgos over glacier, guide essential.

spots.name: Mrikula Devi Temple
spots.note: Wood carved 11th century temple at Udaipur, the road junction for the valley; take a torch for the ceiling panels.

spots.name: Triloknath Temple
spots.note: White marble Avalokiteshvara revered by Hindus and Buddhists alike above Udaipur; the August Pauri fair fills it.

name: Naggar
tagline: Former Kullu capital with a 500-year-old castle

why.winter: Quiet and cold with occasional snow, but the castle and galleries stay open for an off-season visit.
why.summer: Mar-May bring pleasant days and orchard blossom, quieter than Manali just across the valley.
why.monsoon: Jun holds up; Jul-Aug bring flood risk along the Beas and landslide-prone approach road stretches.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov bring the clearest Kullu valley views of the year and a calmer pace than Manali.

vibe: A history-and-art crowd rather than a party one - easy chat over a castle-view coffee.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (30 min) or bus to Manali, 30 min taxi to Naggar.

spots.name: Naggar Castle
spots.note: Stone and cedar castle of the Kullu rajas, now an HPTDC hotel; small entry fee, the courtyard cafe holds the view.

spots.name: Nicholas Roerich Art Gallery
spots.note: The painter's house and studio above the village with his Himalayan canvases; shut Mondays, ticket covers Urusvati.

spots.name: Gauri Shankar Temple
spots.note: Small stone shikhara temple of the 11th century just below the castle, still in daily use; two minutes off the road.

spots.name: Tripura Sundari Temple
spots.note: Three tier pagoda in a cedar clearing above the castle, the village deity; the May fair is the time to be here.

spots.name: Jana Waterfall
spots.note: Fall at the end of the Jana road with dhabas serving siddu and local food; the last stretch is rough, taxis charge more.

spots.name: Chanderkhani Pass
spots.note: 3,660 m pass on the shepherd route across to Malana; a hard 7 hour climb, only clear of snow from June to October.

name: Nako
tagline: Mud-brick village round a high lake in the Hangrang valley

why.winter: November-March the Hangrang valley drops past -20C, homestays shut, and snow at Malling Nallah blocks the road for days.
why.summer: May-June is when Nako reopens for the season at 5-20C, willows greening round the lake and homestays taking guests again.
why.monsoon: Nako itself sits in rain shadow, but July-August slides in the Sutlej gorge below Pooh regularly strand buses for a day.
why.autumn: September-October is the best of it: bone-dry air, gold poplars around the lake and the whole Spiti road wide open.

vibe: Four or five family homestays in a mud-brick maze; a Spiti-road halt where most people stay exactly one night
hub: Off NH-505 in Hangrang: Reckong Peo 103 km, Tabo 65 km; one bus a day; foreigners need an inner line permit

spots.name: Nako Lake
spots.note: Willow ringed pond the mud village is built around; walk the ten minute loop at dawn, no swimming, it is sacred.

spots.name: Nako Monastery
spots.note: Four mud brick chapels of about 1025 with faded Rinchen Zangpo era murals; ask next door for whoever has the keys.

spots.name: Khab Sangam
spots.note: Bridge where the green Spiti meets the grey Sutlej far below the road; a standard photo halt, best light early.

spots.name: Gue Monastery
spots.note: Glass case holding the mummified monk Sangha Tenzin, sat upright some 500 years; a rough spur road off the highway.

name: Narkanda & Thanedar
tagline: Apple country ridge with Hatu Peak and a one-slope ski hill

why.winter: January-February brings real snow and a small ski slope, though NH-5 above Kufri shuts for hours after any heavy fall.
why.summer: April-May is orchard blossom at 8-20C, and the two-hour walk up Hatu Peak gives an unbroken Himalayan skyline to the north.
why.monsoon: July-August is when NH-5 slides between Shimla and Rampur; the orchards are green and the view is cloud, all day long.
why.autumn: September-October is apple harvest and the sharpest air of the year, with old Stokes orchards at Thanedar running homestays.

vibe: Orchard homestays and truck-stop dhabas on NH-5: apple pickers in autumn, Delhi skiers in February, no backpackers
hub: 60 km and 2 h from Shimla on NH-5 with frequent HRTC buses; Kalka-Shimla toy train, then a bus

spots.name: Hatu Peak
spots.note: 3,400 m summit with a wooden Hatu Mata temple and a wide Himalaya view; 8 km of hairpins up, closed under snow.

spots.name: Tannu Jubbar Lake
spots.note: Small forest pond with a wooden temple on the Kotgarh road; quiet on weekdays, carry food, there are no stalls.

spots.name: Stokes Farm
spots.note: Orchard where Satyanand Stokes planted India's first Red Delicious apples; the family homestay takes visitors.

spots.name: St Mary's Church, Kotgarh
spots.note: 1872 stone church among the Kotgarh orchards, still used on Sundays; the graveyard tells the missionary story.

spots.name: Narkanda Ski Slope
spots.note: HPTDC's single slope with skis and an instructor for hire; it only runs in January and February, grass otherwise.

name: Nirmand (Srikhand Mahadev)
tagline: Parshuram's stone village above the Sutlej, trailhead for 5,155 m Srikhand Mahadev
festival: Jul: Srikhand Mahadev yatra, about two weeks from Jaon village

why.winter: Dec-Feb are cold, clear and quiet at 1,450 m with snow on the ridges above and the Srikhand trail closed; the temples and lanes are yours
why.summer: Mar-May is ideal for the village itself: apple and apricot blossom, the Parshuram and Ambika temples, the ancient stone lanes, and warm walks to Jaon before the yatra
why.monsoon: July is the fortnight of the Srikhand yatra from Jaon, hard and crowded, with rain on the lower trail; Aug is wet, Sep dries and the meadows on the trail turn gold
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the best trekking weather to Bhim Dwari and Srikhand before the snow, the village harvesting apples, cool nights and empty homestays

vibe: Village homestays, a PWD rest house and a temple dharamshala; farmers and priests, evenings of woodsmoke and a Sutlej gorge far below
hub: Shimla-Rampur bus 5 h, then Rampur-Nirmand bus 1 h up the hill; Jaon, the trek start, is 8 km on

name: Palampur & Andretta
tagline: Tea gardens under the Dhauladhar and a potters village at Andretta

why.winter: December-February is 2-16C and often wet, but a clear morning after rain puts the entire Dhauladhar wall right in your face.
why.summer: March-May is tea-plucking season at 15-30C, with the Andretta pottery studio and Sobha Singh gallery both open and quiet.
why.monsoon: Palampur is one of Himachal's wettest towns; July-August means 700 mm months, leeches, and no mountain visible for days.
why.autumn: October-November is the clean window at 10-25C, when the Neugal khud runs clear and Bir's paragliders fill the sky nearby.

vibe: Tea-estate homestays and a small artist crowd at Andretta; quieter and far less backpackery than Bir, 19 km east
hub: Kangra airport 40 km; Palampur sits on the Kangra Valley narrow-gauge line; Andretta 13 km by bus or taxi

spots.name: Wah Tea Estate
spots.note: Working Kangra tea garden with a factory walk and a tasting; plucking runs May to October, book the tour ahead.

spots.name: Andretta Pottery
spots.note: Slipware studio in the potters village, wheels turning most days; short courses run in summer, book by phone.

spots.name: Sobha Singh Art Gallery
spots.note: The painter's Andretta studio with his Sohni Mahiwal canvases and a walled garden; closed Mondays, small entry fee.

spots.name: Chamunda Devi Temple
spots.note: Busy Shakti temple on the Baner river with a bathing ghat below; leave phones and shoes at the counter first.

spots.name: Neugal Khad
spots.note: Gorge where the Bundla stream cuts below the tea gardens with the Dhauladhar right above; a cafe sits on the edge.

spots.name: Baijnath Temple
spots.note: Nagara stone temple of 1204 to Shiva the healer, unbroken by any quake; open all day, come for the dusk arti.

name: Pangi Valley (Killar)
tagline: Himachal's remotest inhabited valley over the 4,400 m Sach Pass

why.winter: Cut off completely: Sach Pass and the Killar-Tandi road both close under snow by November and the valley hibernates till June.
why.summer: March-May the passes are still buried and nothing moves; Sach opens around late June, and the HRTC bus from Chamba runs July to October.
why.monsoon: July-September is the season, the valley half in rain shadow; rain still makes the cliff-cut approach roads genuinely scary.
why.autumn: Early October is gold and clear, the last safe window; do not cut it fine, snow can shut both exits within a day or two.

vibe: Bikers and the odd hardened backpacker; PWD rest houses and homestays in Killar and the Bhatori villages.
hub: In season one HRTC bus from Chamba crosses Sach Pass (10-12 h); the other way in is via Keylong and Udaipur

spots.name: Mindhal Vasini Temple
spots.note: Wooden temple of Pangi's chief goddess above Mindhal village; a steep 30 minute climb, shoes off at the gate.

spots.name: Sural Bhatori
spots.note: Buddhist village at the head of the Sural nala with a small gompa; jeeps from Killar are irregular, ask a day ahead.

spots.name: Hudan Bhatori
spots.note: Green side valley village under the glacier; the last stretch is on foot, homestay food only and no phone signal.

spots.name: Sach Pass
spots.note: 4,420 m pass on the road in from Chamba with snow walls into July; open roughly June to October, one bus a day.

name: Parashar Lake
tagline: Floating-island lake with a pagoda temple, camping spot

why.winter: Jan-Feb often bring heavy snow that closes the road; Dec is cold but usually still reachable.
why.summer: Apr-Jun are prime camping season - clear skies, warm days, the lake at its most photogenic.
why.monsoon: Jun is fine; Jul-Aug turn the approach road muddy and landslide-prone, with fog hiding the views.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov bring crisp, star-clear nights - one of the best camping windows near Mandi.

vibe: A popular Delhi/Chandigarh weekend camping spot - easy to join a bonfire with campers.
hub: Fly Bhuntar, 2h drive to Baggi village, then a 5km trek to the lake.

spots.name: Rishi Parashar Temple
spots.note: Three tier cedar pagoda beside the water, built for the sage Parashar; no leather inside, and the island drifts.

spots.name: Baggi
spots.note: Road head hamlet where the walk up to the lake begins; the last shop and parking, plus a homestay if you arrive late.

spots.name: Pandoh Dam
spots.note: Beas dam and its turquoise reservoir on the way back to the highway; stop on the road above, photography is barred.

name: Pin Valley (Mudh)
tagline: Road-end village in the snow leopard valley below Pin-Parvati

why.winter: November-March Mudh is cut off by snow with -25C nights; the Pin is snow leopard country then, not traveller country.
why.summer: March-April still has the Pin link road under snow; May opens it at 0-18C with barley going in and nights below freezing.
why.monsoon: July-August is the valley's best month, dry in the rain shadow, with the Pin-Bhaba and Pin-Parvati crossings both open.
why.autumn: September-October is clear and cold, but by mid-October the homestays start shutting and the last buses stop running.

vibe: Homestays in a small village at road end: trekkers on an acclimatisation day, herders, and almost no shops
hub: Turn off the Spiti road at Attargu, 33 km to Mudh; one HRTC bus from Kaza most summer days, else shared jeep

spots.name: Kungri Monastery
spots.note: Nyingma gompa of about 1330, the valley's oldest, with old masks and murals; ask a monk to unlock the upper hall.

spots.name: Pin Valley National Park
spots.note: Ibex and blue sheep country beyond the village with resident snow leopards; winter tracking needs a local spotter.

spots.name: Sagnam
spots.note: Largest Pin village, where the Parahio joins the Pin; the shops and health post are here and the Kaza bus stops.

spots.name: Pin Parvati Pass
spots.note: 5,319 m crossing from Mudh over glacier into the Parvati valley; a guide and rope are essential, no bail out.

name: Pragpur & Garli
tagline: India's first notified heritage village, cobbled lanes and Kangra-style mansions

why.winter: Dec-Feb is ideal: sunny 20 C days for walking the cobbled lanes, the village Taal and Garli's brick havelis, cold clear nights with the Dhauladhar snow in view
why.summer: March is still fine; Apr-May cross 38 C in the low Kangra hills, so mornings only, siestas in a thick-walled haveli and the Beas bank at Dehra for evenings
why.monsoon: Jun is hot and dusty; Jul-Aug rain turns the terraces green, the tanks fill and the mansions drip, humid but atmospheric; September clears and cools
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the best light, harvest in the fields, warm days and cool nights, Jwalamukhi's flame temple 15 km away without the summer queue

vibe: Older Indian couples and architecture nerds in a heritage court hotel and village homestays; evenings are a stroll and an early dinner
hub: Fly Gaggal (50 km) or the Kangra narrow gauge to Guler, 15 km; buses from Dharamshala via Ranital and Dehra take 2 h

name: Rakcham
tagline: Willow-lined hamlet in the Baspa valley, Kinnaur

why.winter: Cold and snowy with limited guesthouses open, but the Baspa valley is starkly beautiful in snow.
why.summer: May-Jun bring the willows in full leaf and the river running clear before the rains arrive.
why.monsoon: Jun holds up; Jul-Aug bring rockfall risk on the Karcham-Sangla road, a genuine hazard.
why.autumn: Sep-Oct bring golden willows and stable weather, the most reliable window to base here.

vibe: A tiny cluster of guesthouses on the Baspa - you'll likely have the valley to yourself.
hub: Fly/train to Shimla, 9h via Sangla; shared taxis run from there.

spots.name: Batseri
spots.note: Kath-kuni houses and a carved village temple in a deodar grove down the Baspa; leave leather outside the courtyard.

spots.name: Baspa River
spots.note: Snow-fed trout water right below the hamlet; the willow flats are where camps pitch, and it stays icy even in June.

spots.name: Rakchham Chhitkul Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: High Baspa reserve of blue sheep and brown bear above the village; ask the forest guard before walking in, no marked trails.

name: Renuka Lake (Renuka Ji)
tagline: Himachal's largest natural lake, ringed by a leafy parikrama
festival: Nov: Renuka Ji fair (five days around Kartik Ekadashi)

why.winter: December-February is the season proper: about 20 °C days, morning mist on the water and the lakeside parikrama at its calmest.
why.summer: March is still pleasant at 650 m; by May-June the foothills push past 38 °C and the lake shrinks, start at dawn or skip it.
why.monsoon: July-September is humid and intensely green with the lake brimming; cloudbursts occasionally cut the Nahan road for hours.
why.autumn: October cools quickly; the five-day Renuka Ji fair in November packs the lakeshore, the liveliest and busiest week by far.

vibe: Pilgrims, picnicking families and birders on the lake loop; HPTDC's lakeside hotel is the solo default.
hub: Buses from Nahan (45 km, 1.5 h) or Paonta Sahib; Chandigarh airport is about 3 h via Nahan

spots.name: Shri Renuka Ji Temple
spots.note: Lakeside shrine to Renuka, mother of Parshuram; the November Renuka fair fills the whole shore for five days.

spots.name: Renuka Lake Parikrama
spots.note: Shaded loop of about 3 km round the water under sal trees; walk it at first light for langurs and still water.

spots.name: Parshuram Tal
spots.note: The smaller round lake next door with the Parshuram temple; a rath procession links the two at fair time.

spots.name: Renuka Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Lion safari enclosure plus deer and blackbuck on the far shore; small ticket, go before the midday heat.

name: Rewalsar (Tso Pema)
tagline: Tso Pema, one small lake sacred to Hindus, Sikhs and Tibetans

why.winter: December-February is chilly at 1350 m but clear, with butter lamps in the gompas and the lakeside path almost entirely to yourself.
why.summer: March-May is the sweet spot at 15-28C, before plains heat pushes weekend traffic up from Mandi and Bilaspur.
why.monsoon: July-August rain is heavy here and the hill road up from Mandi turns greasy; the lake looks fine but nothing else works.
why.autumn: October-November gives the sharpest light on the floating reed islands and the gompas above, with guesthouses near empty.

vibe: Monastery guesthouses and a gurudwara sarai, Tibetan monks and Punjabi pilgrims, no bars and no nightlife at all
hub: 24 km from Mandi bus stand by bus or shared taxi, 45 min; Bhuntar airport 80 km, no railhead near

spots.name: Tso Pema Nyingmapa Gompa
spots.note: Main gompa on the lake shore, drums and horns at dawn; shoes off at the door, then walk the lake clockwise.

spots.name: Guru Padmasambhava Statue
spots.note: The 37 m gilded Guru Rinpoche on the hill above the lake, visible for miles; road up or a 20 minute stair climb.

spots.name: Padmasambhava Caves
spots.note: Meditation caves in the cliff above town, still used by retreatants; 3 km climb on foot or taxi via Naina Devi.

spots.name: Naina Devi Temple
spots.note: Ridge-top shrine over Rewalsar with the Mandi valley laid out below; share taxis go up, few of them after dark.

spots.name: Gurudwara Rewalsar Sahib
spots.note: Built by the Mandi raja where Guru Gobind Singh camped; sarai beds and langar, cover your head at the door.

name: Sangla
tagline: Baspa valley base camp with the old Kamru Fort

why.winter: Cold with occasional heavy snow, but the valley stays more accessible than Chitkul further up-road.
why.summer: May-Jun bring warm days, apple blossoms and the clearest views of the Baspa valley's peaks.
why.monsoon: Jun is fine; Jul-Aug bring serious rockfall risk on the Karcham-Wangtu stretch, avoid driving in.
why.autumn: Sep-Oct are excellent - apple harvest, clear skies, the most comfortable base for exploring Kinnaur.

vibe: A small guesthouse cluster where trekkers heading to Chitkul and Rakcham cross paths.
hub: Fly/train to Shimla, 8h drive via Reckong Peo into the Baspa valley.

spots.name: Kamru Fort
spots.note: Timber tower fort of the old Bushahr rajas above the village; you are handed a cap and sash to wear at the gate.

spots.name: Bering Nag Temple
spots.note: Wood and slate Kinnauri temple in the village itself; the Phulaich flower festival takes it over in August.

spots.name: Sangla Kanda
spots.note: High meadow and small lake above the village, 3 to 4 hours up through forest; shepherd camps, carry your own water.

spots.name: Batseri
spots.note: Old kath-kuni houses, orchards and a carved deity temple on the Baspa; flat walk or a shared taxi up valley.

spots.name: Baspa River
spots.note: Trout water running past the village; the willow flats hold the camps and evening light hits the peaks upstream.

name: Sarahan (Bhimakali)
tagline: Slate-and-timber Bhimakali temple facing Srikhand Mahadev

why.winter: December-February can snow at 2165 m; the temple courtyard is empty and beautiful, but rooms are cold and buses thin right out.
why.summer: April-May is the best of it at 10-24C, apple blossom below and the Srikhand Mahadev massif clear across the Sutlej gorge.
why.monsoon: July-August is landslide season on NH-5 through the Sutlej gorge, and Jeori to Sarahan is a slide-prone 17 km climb.
why.autumn: September-October is dry and sharp, the temple's pheasant aviary is active and the Kinnaur road onward is at its best.

vibe: You sleep in the temple's own guesthouse inside the complex; pilgrims, a few Kinnaur-bound travellers, and nothing else
hub: 175 km from Shimla on NH-5, 7 h by bus to Jeori, then a 17 km shared-taxi climb; no airport or railhead near

spots.name: Bhimakali Temple
spots.note: Slate and timber tower temple facing Srikhand Mahadev; leather and cameras into the locker, cap on at the gate.

spots.name: Sarahan Pheasant Breeding Centre
spots.note: Aviaries breeding western tragopan and monal below the temple; small ticket, the birds are active early.

spots.name: Bashal Peak
spots.note: Meadow ridge above Sarahan for the Srikhand Mahadev line, about 3 hours up through fir; no water on the ridge.

name: Shangarh (Sainj Valley)
tagline: Sacred meadow village at the quiet gate of the Great Himalayan NP

why.winter: Snow dusts the meadow between clear cold spells; homestays stay open, paths ice over and the Sainj road can block for a day after a dump.
why.summer: April-June is prime: the great meadow at its greenest, GHNP day hikes toward Barshangarh falls, and nights that still want a fleece.
why.monsoon: July-August bring landslide-prone Sainj roads, leeches and a sodden meadow; June and late September are the workable edges.
why.autumn: October-November mean crisp air, amber grass and the fewest visitors of the year; carry proper layers for cold nights.

vibe: Wood-temple meadow scene: family homestays, a couple of cafes and slow travellers swapping GHNP trail notes.
hub: Bhuntar airport 2 h; bus to Sainj via Aut and Larji, then a 12 km taxi or local bus up to Shangarh

spots.name: Shangchul Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Wooden deity temple at the meadow's edge; leave leather, shoes and meat outside, the whole maidan counts as shrine.

spots.name: Barshangarh Waterfall
spots.note: Big fall in the forest below Shangarh, 20 minutes down from the road; rocks stay slick, best just after the rains.

spots.name: Pundrik Rishi Lake
spots.note: Small green lake and temple down in Sainj, ringed by deodar; ten minutes off the road, quiet except on fair days.

spots.name: Great Himalayan National Park
spots.note: The UNESCO park's quiet Sainj gate; permit and a guide from the range office, then a day walk in to Shakti.

name: Shimla
tagline: Colonial hill capital with Mall Road and a toy train
festival: May: Shimla Summer Festival

why.winter: Dec often brings snow around Christmas/New Year and huge crowds; Jan-Feb are colder and calmer.
why.summer: Classic plains-heat escape - Apr-May bring 20-25C days and the town at its busiest, priciest.
why.monsoon: Jun holds up reasonably; Jul-Aug bring heavy rain and periodic landslides on the Kalka-Shimla highway.
why.autumn: Clear, cool and comfortable with thinner crowds than summer - arguably the nicest weather window.

vibe: More honeymooners and families on Mall Road than backpackers, but easy to spend time solo.
hub: Fly Jubbarhatti, or Kalka-Shimla toy train / 7h Volvo from Delhi.

spots.name: Christ Church
spots.note: Neo-Gothic 1857 church on the Ridge, the postcard of Shimla; stained glass reads best late afternoon, free entry.

spots.name: Jakhoo Temple
spots.note: Hanuman temple on the top ridge under a 33 m statue; 40 minute climb from the Mall, monkeys take glasses and food.

spots.name: Mall Road
spots.note: The pedestrian spine of Shimla, no cars allowed at all; walk it after 6 pm with everyone else, shops shut by nine.

spots.name: Viceregal Lodge
spots.note: 1888 Raj summer seat on Observatory Hill where the 1945 Simla Conference met; the inside is a ticketed guided tour only.

spots.name: Gaiety Theatre
spots.note: Restored 1887 Victorian theatre on the Mall; cheap tour of the auditorium, often with a rehearsal running.

spots.name: Indian Coffee House
spots.note: Time capsule cafe on the Mall with turbaned waiters; cold coffee and cutlets for small money, queue at lunch.

spots.name: Chadwick Falls
spots.note: 86 m fall in deodar forest below Summer Hill; worth the walk only during and just after the monsoon, dry by April.

spots.name: Himalayan Nature Park, Kufri
spots.note: Hillside enclosures of monal, musk deer and leopard at Kufri; walk up from the taxi stand and skip the pony touts.

name: Sujanpur Tira
tagline: Katoch fort hill above the Beas with Kangra-school murals and a huge Holi chaugan
festival: Mar: Holi fair, three days on the chaugan, the biggest in Himachal

why.winter: Dec-Feb mild 20 C days for the fort climb, the Narbadeshwar temple murals and the riverside; the Beas runs clear and green and nights are cold enough for a shawl
why.summer: March has the Holi fair, when the three-day mela fills the chaugan; Apr-May climb past 38 C on the bare Tira hill, so go at dawn or wait for autumn
why.monsoon: June is hot; Jul-Aug the Beas swells brown, the fort ruins turn green and the temples are quiet; September is humid but the town is at its lushest
why.autumn: Oct-Nov clear and warm, the best time for the ridge walk from the fort to the Gauri Shankar temple and a Beas sunset without the Holi crowds

vibe: A sleepy town of temple keepers and boys playing cricket on the chaugan; a few basic hotels and an HPTDC lodge, evenings on the river
hub: Fly Gaggal (60 km, 2 h); buses from Hamirpur (22 km, 45 min) or Palampur (40 km, 1.5 h); nearest rail Una, 3 h

name: Tabo
tagline: Thousand-year-old mud monastery with intact Indo-Tibetan murals

why.winter: December-March hits -25C at night; the Kinnaur road often stays open, but water lines freeze and most guesthouses shut.
why.summer: May-June is when Tabo opens up, 5-25C by day, and the caretaker will unlock the pitch-dark thousand-year-old assembly hall.
why.monsoon: Tabo sits in rain shadow and stays dry, but July-August landslides in the Kinnaur gorge below can add a full day to the drive.
why.autumn: September-October is the clear, dust-free peak: cold nights, warm sun, and the mud stupas glowing gold around 5 pm.

vibe: Monastery guesthouse and a handful of homestays; Spiti-circuit travellers, monks and the odd art historian, no party
hub: 47 km from Kaza, 190 km from Reckong Peo; one HRTC bus daily each way plus shared taxis in season

spots.name: Tabo Monastery
spots.note: 996 CE mud gompa holding the oldest intact Indo-Tibetan murals in India; no photos inside, carry a torch, opens 9 am.

spots.name: Tabo Caves
spots.note: Meditation caves cut into the cliff above the village, still used for retreat; ten minute scramble, go at sunset.

spots.name: Gue Monastery
spots.note: Glass shrine holding a 500 year old self-mummified monk, up a side road off the Sumdo highway; taxi only, no bus.

name: Tirthan Valley (Gushaini)
tagline: Trout-river valley on the edge of Great Himalayan NP

why.winter: Cold and sleepy, some guesthouses shut for lack of guests, but the river valley stays starkly beautiful.
why.summer: Best season - Mar-May bring clear river water, blooming forest and prime trout season.
why.monsoon: Jun is workable; Jul-Aug bring flash-flood risk on the river and landslides on the Aut-Gushaini road.
why.autumn: Quiet and golden - GHNP trails run driest, river levels drop, ideal for birdwatching walks.

vibe: Riverside guesthouses run by trout-farming families - solitude and nature, not a crowd.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (1.5h) or Delhi-Aut bus (10h), 1h taxi via Larji.

spots.name: Great Himalayan National Park
spots.note: UNESCO park gate at Sai Ropa; permit and a guide from the range office, then the trail up the Tirthan to Rolla.

spots.name: Tirthan River
spots.note: Brown trout water past every guesthouse; angling permit from the fisheries office at Banjar, catch and release.

spots.name: Chhoi Waterfall
spots.note: Forest fall above Nagini, 30 minutes up from the road over a footbridge; empty on weekdays, slippery after rain.

spots.name: Shringa Rishi Temple
spots.note: Carved cedar seat of the Banjar valley's ruling deity at Bagi; the god travels, so ask before photographing.

name: Tosh
tagline: Last-village hippie hangout above Kasol's Parvati valley

why.winter: Snow often closes the last stretch from Barshaini; beautiful but genuinely cut-off and sparse.
why.summer: Mar-May bring blossoming orchards, mild days and the valley's easiest trekking conditions.
why.monsoon: Jun is fine; Jul-Aug bring landslide risk on the Kasol-Barshaini road and a swollen Parvati river.
why.autumn: Dry trails and golden light make Oct-Nov the best window, before the first snow closes access.

vibe: Cliffside cafes draw the Kasol crowd who hiked up for cheaper stays.
hub: Fly Bhuntar (1.5h to Barshaini), 30-45 min uphill walk to Tosh.

spots.name: Kutla
spots.note: Cliff hamlet an hour's climb above Tosh with a few cafes and camps; no road up, carry a torch for the walk back.

spots.name: Kalga
spots.note: Old wooden village across the Parvati with orchard guesthouses; the Fairy Forest walk starts from Pulga next door.

spots.name: Manikaran Sahib
spots.note: Gurudwara built over boiling springs down the valley; langar rice is cooked in the spring, hot baths, head covered.

spots.name: Barshaini
spots.note: Road head below Tosh where the Kheerganga trail and the Kalga bridge start; last shops before the walk, no ATM.

name: Trilokinath (Udaipur, Lahaul)
tagline: Cliff-top shrine on the Chandrabhaga where Hindus and Buddhists share one deity
festival: Aug: Pauri fair, three days of Lahauli song and dance at the temple

why.winter: Dec-Feb the Keylong-Udaipur road along the Chenab stays open more often than not, but the village is under snow, nights are minus 20 C and almost nothing is open
why.summer: March and April are still frozen and the road can close after a storm; by mid-May the buses from Keylong run daily and the first pilgrims of the year arrive
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the window: mild days, Pattan valley fields green, Udaipur's 11th-century Mrikula Devi wood carvings 6 km down; the Pauri fair in August fills every bed
why.autumn: October is crisp and clear with the willows turning and the shrine nearly empty; by November snow returns and the homestays start closing for winter

vibe: Pilgrims, Lahauli families running homestays, the temple sarai and a PWD rest house in Udaipur; nights are silent apart from the river
hub: Manali-Keylong bus via the Atal Tunnel (4 h), Keylong-Udaipur bus 2.5 h, then a taxi or 6 km walk up to the temple

name: Aharbal Falls
tagline: The Veshaw crashes 25 m through a pine gorge, Kashmir's Niagara

why.winter: Dec-Feb the fall shrinks to an icy ribbon between snowy pines; the Kulgam road usually stays open, check after big dumps.
why.summer: Apr-Jun snowmelt is peak thunder: the Veshaw explodes through the notch and spray soaks the lower ledge, go early on weekends.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep rain keeps the fall fat and the walk up to Kungwattan meadow green; short showers, slick steps, local day-trippers.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the flow thins but the gorge is crisp and empty; JKTDC huts are easy to book and nights start touching zero.

vibe: Picnic families at the railing till mid-afternoon; stay in the JKTDC hut and the gorge and trout stream go quiet.
hub: Srinagar 70 km via Kulgam, 2.5 h; buses reach Kulgam, the last 17 km is taxi or hitching territory.

spots.name: Kousarnag Lake
spots.note: Alpine lake under the Kousarnag ridge, the classic two day walk from here; guide and tent needed, July to September.

spots.name: Kongwattan
spots.note: Fir and pine meadow up the Veshaw above the falls, about two hours of forest walking; shepherd huts, carry food.

spots.name: Veshaw River
spots.note: Trout stream below the gorge, one of Kashmir's better beats; day permit from the fisheries office at Kulgam.

name: Bangus Valley (Bungus)
tagline: Fir-ringed grass bowl behind Kupwara, only tents and Bakarwal dohkas

why.winter: Dec-Feb the bowl lies under deep snow and the jeep track from Mawar is shut; there is no village up there to shelter in, so it is off.
why.summer: March and April stay snowbound at 2,900 m. Late May the track dries out, the grass greens and the first Bakarwal flocks walk in.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the season: flowers, herder dohkas, streams you step across. Kashmir rain is light here, but one storm turns the dirt track greasy.
why.autumn: October is cold, clear and empty once the herders drop down; by November first snow closes the track and the army post stops letting jeeps up.

vibe: Bakarwal dohkas, a handful of Srinagar campers at weekends, and whatever tent you carried or booked with a Handwara operator.
hub: Srinagar to Handwara by bus (3h), then a hired jeep 40 km through Mawar and Zachaldara; ID checked at the army post.

name: Bani (Sarthal Devi)
tagline: Deodar bowl under Chattergala Pass, the back way into Bhaderwah

why.winter: Dec-Feb bring frost, the odd snowfall in the deodars and white on Sarthal Devi; the Basohli road stays open, but nothing here is heated.
why.summer: March is still cold with snow on Chattergala and little open; April and May are Bani at its best, 25 C days and rhododendron on the climb to Sarthal.
why.monsoon: June is warm and clear and the Chattergala road over to Bhaderwah usually opens; Jul-Aug the Ujh valley takes slips and the ridges sit in cloud. September dries out.
why.autumn: October is clear and cool, maize on the roofs and walnut coming down; November nights bite and Chattergala shuts with the first snow.

vibe: One bazaar street, a tourist rest house and rooms above shops; evenings are shopfront tea with forest staff and Gujjar herders.
hub: Bus from Jammu to Basohli (4h), then a shared sumo 55 km up the Ujh valley to Bani; jeeps carry on to Sarthal in summer.

name: Basohli
tagline: Birthplace of Pahari miniature painting above Ranjit Sagar lake

why.winter: Dec-Feb is prime: 18-22 C days, glassy reflections of the Atal Setu cable bridge and unhurried painting ateliers.
why.summer: Apr-Jun cooks past 38 C in these low Shivalik foothills; the lake glares, the town naps, save it for the cool months.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is sticky with rain bursts, though the reservoir brims and the hills green up; workable if you tolerate humidity.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings clean light on the water, boating below the bridge and comfortable walking through the old bazaar.

vibe: A drowsy heritage town: miniature-painting ateliers, an evening stroll to the bridge viewpoint, a couple of guesthouses.
hub: Pathankot station 45 km, 1.5 h by bus or taxi; from Jammu 130 km via Kathua, about 3.5 h.

spots.name: Vasuki Nag Temple
spots.note: Town temple to the serpent god Vasuki, the one time Basohli fills is its annual mela; quiet and open the rest of the year.

spots.name: Ranjit Sagar Lake
spots.note: Reservoir behind Thein dam on the Ravi with hills on every side; boats run from the Basohli shore when water is high.

spots.name: Atal Setu
spots.note: Cable-stayed bridge over the Ravi arm to Dunera and the town's evening walk; best light an hour before sunset.

spots.name: Basohli Fort
spots.note: Ruined seat of the Pal rajas who paid for Basohli miniature painting; walls and terraces only, go for the lake view.

name: Bhaderwah
tagline: Chenab-valley bowl of lavender fields and Nag temples
festival: Jul/Aug: Mela Patt at the Nag temples (Naga Panchami)

why.winter: Dec-Feb snows the Padri road shut and drops nights below zero; guesthouses are unheated and the buses thin right out.
why.summer: Mar is still cold and grey; Apr-May is why locals call it Chhota Kashmir, 20-28 C with the meadows above town greening.
why.monsoon: June turns the lavender fields purple; Jul-Aug rain loosens the Batote-Doda road, then Sep clears for the maize harvest.
why.autumn: Oct is the clean window with walnut trees turning and the Neeru running low; Nov gets cold and homestays start closing.

vibe: Almost no outside tourists - Gujjar shepherds, local college kids, a handful of homestays and one JKTDC hut block.
hub: Jammu railhead 200 km; bus to Batote then a shared sumo up the Neeru valley, about 6-7 h in all.

spots.name: Vasuki Nag Temple
spots.note: Bhaderwah's main Nag shrine in the old town, stone and deodar wood; the Kailash Kund yatra sets off from here in late summer.

spots.name: Padri Top
spots.note: Grassy 3000 m pass on the Bhaderwah Chamba road, snow lying into May; nothing up there but a chai shack, so carry food.

spots.name: Jai Valley
spots.note: Shepherd meadow above town with Gujjar dhoks; the last stretch is a rough jeep track, carry lunch, there are no stalls.

spots.name: Gupt Ganga Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple on the Neeru bank in town where the river is said to run hidden; packed on Shivratri, shoes off at the steps.

spots.name: Lavender Farm, Lehrian
spots.note: CSIR aromatic farm whose lavender rows bloom mid June, when the district runs its festival; ask the staff before walking in.

name: Doodhpathri
tagline: Milky Shaliganga meadows under pine, Kashmir's gentler Gulmarg

why.winter: Dec-Feb snow buries the meadow and the road past Khansahib shuts for days after each dump; huts close, go only as a cleared-road day trip.
why.summer: Mar is slush and brown turf; by May the Shaliganga runs milk-white through knee-high grass and days sit at 15-22 C.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is green and warm rather than wet, but weekend picnic crowds and pony touts peak; Jun and Sep are the quiet wins.
why.autumn: Oct frosts the turf gold and empties the meadow by dusk; November turns raw, stalls pack up and the huts start closing.

vibe: Day-trip picnic scene till 4 pm, then just JKTDC hut guests, Gujjar herders and a few chai stalls by the river.
hub: Srinagar 42 km via Khansahib, 1.5-2 h; shared taxi to Khansahib then local cab, no evening bus back.

spots.name: Shaliganga River
spots.note: The milky stream the meadow is named for; wade at the wooden bridge, the water is icy and the far bank has fewer stalls.

spots.name: Palmaidan
spots.note: Upper meadow about 40 minutes on foot or by pony above the huts; wide view over the bowl and far fewer picnic parties.

spots.name: Diskhal
spots.note: Grass and pine hollow a short walk up from the main meadow; no stalls anywhere near it, carry your own water and lunch.

spots.name: Mujpathri
spots.note: Gujjar grazing meadow just beyond Doodhpathri, reached on foot or by pony; take your own food, there is nothing to buy there.

name: Gulmarg
tagline: India's top ski resort - Gondola to 3,979m, real powder

why.winter: Peak Gulmarg - reliable powder, Gondola to Apharwat Peak, India's best skiing and snowboarding scene.
why.summer: March can still have late-season snow; by May meadows green up for golf and short hikes.
why.monsoon: June is a nice green window, but Jul-Aug often bring cloud and mist that blank out mountain views.
why.autumn: October still has clear hiking weather; November is a dead patch - too early for snow, too muddy.

vibe: International ski crowd in winter, easy to team up at lodges; summer is quiet and empty.
hub: Fly to Srinagar, then 1-1.5h taxi to Gulmarg (56km)

spots.name: Gulmarg Gondola
spots.note: Two stage cable car to Kongdoori and on to Apharwat at close to 4000 m; book phase 2 online early, it shuts in high wind.

spots.name: Apharwat Peak
spots.note: Snow ridge at the top of gondola phase 2, Nanga Parbat visible on a clear morning; no shade, take sunglasses and a windproof.

spots.name: Khilanmarg
spots.note: Meadow an hour on foot above the gondola base, best at sunrise; ponywallahs quote high, fix the price before you start.

spots.name: Alpather Lake
spots.note: Lake under Apharwat, a 4 km walk from Kongdoori over scree; the ice usually breaks up only by mid June.

spots.name: St Mary's Church
spots.note: Small 1902 stone church with a shingled roof in the middle of the bowl; opens when the caretaker is around, lawn is free.

spots.name: Baba Reshi Shrine
spots.note: Wooden 15th century Sufi ziarat below Gulmarg on the Tangmarg road; cover your head, men and women enter by separate doors.

spots.name: Gulmarg Golf Course
spots.note: One of the world's highest 18 hole courses, playable roughly May to October; clubs and a caddy on hire at the clubhouse.

name: Gurez Valley (Dawar)
tagline: Dard-Shin log-house valley on the Kishanganga behind Razdan Pass

why.winter: Dec-Feb Razdan Pass is buried and Dawar is cut off; the valley is shut to outsiders for roughly six months a year.
why.summer: Mar-Apr the pass is still shut; it usually clears in May, but late snow and slides make the first sumos a real gamble.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is Gurez at its best: 8-22 C, dry-ish, Habba Khatoon peak lit at dusk, and every homestay in Dawar open.
why.autumn: Early Oct is gold and empty, then snow starts closing Razdan through November and the last sumos out get nervous.

vibe: Wooden-house homestays in Dawar and Tulail, no hostels, patchy signal, and soldiers outnumbering travellers.
hub: Srinagar 123 km via Bandipora and Razdan Pass, 5-6 h by shared sumo; carry original photo ID for checkposts.

spots.name: Habba Khatoon Peak
spots.note: Pyramid peak above Dawar named for the poet queen; no climb needed, the light is best from the river bridge in the evening.

spots.name: Tulail Valley
spots.note: String of Dard log house villages up the valley east of Dawar; transport is a few shared sumos, carry photo ID for the posts.

spots.name: Razdan Pass
spots.note: 3300 m pass on the road in from Bandipora, open roughly May to November; no signal on the climb, fill fuel in Bandipora.

spots.name: Kishanganga River
spots.note: Green trout river through Dawar; the wooden footbridge is the evening walk, do not swim, the current is fast and freezing.

name: Katra (Vaishno Devi)
tagline: Base town for the year-round Vaishno Devi pilgrimage climb
festival: Oct: Sharad Navratri peak pilgrimage rush

why.winter: Cold but manageable, genuinely a good time - cool trekking weather, thinner crowds outside New Year.
why.summer: March-April brings Navratri crowds in good weather; by May plains heat climbs toward 40C.
why.monsoon: Worst window - brutal heat plus monsoon rain that can trigger landslides and track closures.
why.autumn: October's Sharad Navratri is peak pilgrim season with huge crowds but excellent weather; Nov calmer.

vibe: A pilgrimage crowd, not backpackers, but solo-safe - easy to join a group on the climb.
hub: Fly/train to Jammu, then train/taxi to Katra (~2h)

spots.name: Vaishno Devi Bhawan
spots.note: The cave shrine itself, a 13 km paved climb from Banganga; collect the free yatra slip in Katra first, ponies wait at the start.

spots.name: Ardhkuwari
spots.note: Halfway cave where the goddess is said to have hidden; the crawl through Garbha Joon runs on called out group numbers.

spots.name: Bhairavnath Temple
spots.note: A 2.5 km climb above the Bhawan that completes the yatra; the short ropeway saves the legs and stops before dark.

spots.name: Himkoti
spots.note: Garden and cafeteria on the newer track with a view back over Katra; that route is longer but much less crowded.

spots.name: Bhimgarh Fort
spots.note: Hill fort above Reasi with restored ramparts and a long stair up; half day by shared cab from Katra, go in the morning.

spots.name: Baba Dhansar
spots.note: Spring bursting out of rock into a stream with a Shiva shrine under an old banyan; shaded all day, packed on Shivratri.

spots.name: Shiv Khori
spots.note: Long natural cave with a self formed lingam near Ransoo; a full day by shared taxi, low crawl sections and a slow queue.

name: Kokernag & Verinag
tagline: Verinag's Mughal spring tank and Kokernag's trout gardens

why.winter: Dec is bare and cold, then Jan-Feb sits near freezing with most JKTDC huts shut; only Verinag's spring keeps running.
why.summer: Mar is thin and grey; Apr-May is blossom season across the Kokernag gardens at 18-26 C with the trout farm running.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug is Kashmir's warm stretch near 30 C by noon with weekend picnic crowds; Sep cools down and empties out again.
why.autumn: Oct is the pick: chinars turning over Verinag's octagonal tank and walnut harvest on; Nov goes cold and huts shut.

vibe: Local families picnicking, JKTDC huts at both ends and trout-and-rice lunches; no backpacker scene at all here.
hub: Anantnag railhead 25 km; buses to both run all day, and the two springs are 20 km apart by the Jammu road.

spots.name: Kokernag Botanical Garden
spots.note: Terraced garden round the Papashudan Nag spring with a trout hatchery beside it; small ticket, open till dusk.

spots.name: Verinag Spring
spots.note: Jahangir's octagonal stone tank over the source of the Jhelum, deep blue and full of fish; ticketed, buses from Anantnag.

spots.name: Daksum
spots.note: Pine hamlet where the Bringi drops out of the forest, a few huts and a trout beat; last shop before Sinthan, stock up here.

spots.name: Sinthan Top
spots.note: 3800 m pass on the Kishtwar road, snow into June; taxis go from Daksum, no fuel or food beyond it, be back before dark.

spots.name: Achabal Mughal Garden
spots.note: Nur Jahan's terraced garden where a spring drives the cascades under old chinars; small ticket, quiet on weekday mornings.

name: Lolab Valley (Sogam)
tagline: Walnut-and-paddy valley behind Kupwara with the Kalaroos caves

why.winter: Dec-Feb is snowy and stark with homestay bukharis working overtime; the Kupwara road usually stays open but services are thin.
why.summer: Apr-May is the sweet spot: fruit blossom, paddy transplanting and the Kalaroos caves an easy side trip up the valley.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is humid green with light Kashmir rain, fine for orchard walks; army checkposts add time, carry original photo ID.
