why.autumn: Sep-Oct is golden harvest and woodsmoke, the valley at its most photogenic; nights turn cold fast after mid-Oct.

vibe: No traveller scene: family homestays and eco-huts around Sogam and Chandigam, orchard walks, soldiers at the road posts.
hub: Srinagar 100 km via Sopore and Kupwara, 3.5-4 h; bus to Kupwara then shared cab to Sogam, carry photo ID.

spots.name: Kalaroos Caves
spots.note: Caves in the ridge above Madmadav that villagers say tunnel all the way to Russia; take a local guide, a torch and grip shoes.

spots.name: Satbaran
spots.note: One rock cut block with seven doorways near the caves, nobody agrees on its date; five minutes off the road, no ticket.

spots.name: Bangus Valley
spots.note: Wide alpine meadow bowl beyond Rajwar with Gujjar flocks and no buildings; jeep only, June to September, ID at the army post.

spots.name: Chandigam
spots.note: Walnut and paddy village with an eco park and a few homestays; the orchard lanes are the best flat walk in the valley.

name: Loran Valley (Poonch)
tagline: Maize terraces and pine in the old Lohara kings' valley

why.winter: Dec-Feb snow shuts the upper hamlets and the sumos stop whenever it falls; the valley goes quiet on firewood smoke, so pick a clear spell.
why.summer: March is cold and grey with snow still on the upper hamlets; April and May are the green months, maize going in and the walnut leafing out.
why.monsoon: June is warm and clear, good for the shepherd tracks toward the Nandansar lakes; Jul-Aug the Poonch side takes proper rain with slips on the Mandi road. September is dry.
why.autumn: October and November are cold and clear: gold terraces, ruined fort walls on the spur above, everyone out stacking winter fodder.

vibe: Pahari farmhouses and a one-row bazaar, no hotels: you ask around for a room or day-trip it from Poonch, and evenings end early.
hub: Poonch to Loran is 30 km by shared sumo via Mandi; Poonch itself is 8h by bus from Jammu through Rajouri.

name: Machail (Paddar)
tagline: Glacier-head village above Paddar, end of the Machail Mata walk
festival: Jul/Aug: Machail Mata yatra from Gulabgarh

why.winter: Dec-Feb Machail is snowed in and the Paddar road is shut by avalanche; families move down to Gulabgarh and nothing is open up here.
why.summer: March and April are slush and a blocked road. From late May the jeep track above Gulabgarh reopens and the sapphire villages stir.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the whole season. Jul-Aug bring the yatra crowd, langars and tent rows; by September it empties and the glacier views clear.
why.autumn: October is gold, cold and quiet with the last jeeps running down; November snow shuts the road and the village packs up for winter.

vibe: Stone and timber houses round the temple, dharamshala beds and August langars; outside the yatra you may be the only outsider.
hub: Jammu to Kishtwar by bus (8h), sumo on to Gulabgarh, then a shared jeep or a 30 km walk up to Machail.

name: Manasbal Lake
tagline: Lotus-choked lake under Nur Jahan's Jarokha Bagh terrace

why.winter: Dec is grey and Jan-Feb sits near freezing with nothing warm on the shore; only birders bother, for the wintering duck.
why.summer: Mar-May is clear and cool with the Jarokha Bagh beds replanted, though the lotus is only just breaking the surface.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is peak lotus, solid pink across the north shore; Jun and Sep are quieter but still worth the shikara hour.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov gives mirror water with Harmukh reflected at dawn and the first migratory duck in from late October.

vibe: Fishermen, lotus-stem harvesters and a couple of JKTDC huts; a day-trip from Srinagar unless you want silence.
hub: Srinagar 30 km via Ganderbal; buses to Safapora all day, then a 2 km walk to the Jarokha Bagh terrace.

spots.name: Jarokha Bagh
spots.note: Nur Jahan's small terraced garden on the south bank, its arched wall looking straight down the water; best at sunrise.

spots.name: Kheer Bhawani Temple
spots.note: Kashmiri Pandit shrine at Tulmul around a spring said to change colour; vast crowds on Jyeshtha Ashtami in May or June.

spots.name: Wular Lake
spots.note: India's largest freshwater lake, open water and reed beds north of Manasbal; go from the Bandipora bund, windy after noon.

spots.name: Andarkote
spots.note: Village on the mound of Jayapida's 8th century capital Jayapura; almost nothing stands, ask locals for the old ramparts.

name: Mansar Lake
tagline: Forest-ringed Shivalik lake with a Sheshnag shrine and turtles

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season - 8-20 C, migratory duck on the water and the Sheshnag parikrama walk done in cool air.
why.summer: Mar is still fine and Apr warms fast, but by May these Shivalik foothills push 40 C with an hour of usable sal shade.
why.monsoon: Skip Jun-Sep: June is a 40 C furnace, then Jul-Sep runs 33 C and sticky with the forest circuit path a mud slog.
why.autumn: Oct dries out and cools, then Nov is properly good: wetland birds arriving at Surinsar-Mansar and boating back on.

vibe: Jammu picnic families and mundan parties at the shrine; JKTDC huts on the bank and no traveller scene at all.
hub: Jammu 60 km, Udhampur 40 km; Jammu-Udhampur road buses drop at Mansar chowk, about 1.5 h from Jammu.

spots.name: Sheshnag Temple
spots.note: Snake god shrine on the east bank where families come for a child's first haircut; the vow is three circuits of the lake.

spots.name: Mansar Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Forest belt round the lake with a fenced spotted deer and neelgai enclosure; small ticket, go early or late for sightings.

spots.name: Surinsar Lake
spots.note: Smaller twin lake in the same sanctuary, ringed by forest and far quieter; direct road across, no shops at the bank.

spots.name: Umapati Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Old stone Shiva temple a short walk from the bank, plain slabs and usually empty; fold it into the lake circuit walk.

name: Martand Sun Temple (Mattan)
tagline: Lalitaditya's ruined 8th-century sun temple on a karewa plateau

why.winter: Dec-Feb the snowed colonnade is the best photograph in the valley, but it is near 0 C and the site empties by 4 pm.
why.summer: Mar is still bare and grey; Apr-May is ideal at 18-25 C with almond and mustard on the karewas and the lawn to yourself.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug is warm and hazy rather than wet, near 30 C by midday on the open plateau; Sep cools and the light goes hard.
why.autumn: Oct is the best all-round month with paddy turning gold below the plateau; Nov is cold and the site shuts earlier.

vibe: An ASI ticket, a caretaker and usually nobody else; sleep at Anantnag or Pahalgam, there are no beds at Mattan.
hub: Anantnag railhead 9 km, Srinagar 60 km; buses to Mattan run all day, then a 15-minute walk up the plateau.

spots.name: Mattan Temple
spots.note: Spring fed tank of sacred fish beside the bazaar, a Kashmiri Pandit pilgrimage stop; shoes off at the tank, fish feed on sale.

spots.name: Aishmuqam Ziarat
spots.note: Cave shrine of Zain ud din Wali built into a cliff on the Pahalgam road; steep steps up, huge torch procession at Zool.

spots.name: Padshahi Bagh, Bijbehara
spots.note: Mughal chinar garden on the Jhelum at Bijbehara, the old town's shaded riverfront; free, and full of school groups by noon.

spots.name: Achabal Mughal Garden
spots.note: Terraced garden whose spring drives the cascades down three levels; small ticket, come on a weekday for the chinar shade.

name: Naranag
tagline: Ruined 8th-century Shiva temples at the Gangabal trailhead
festival: Aug/Sep: Harmukh-Gangabal yatra from the temple

why.winter: Dec-Feb the Wangath spur ices over and Gangabal lies frozen under deep snow; the trek is off and every homestay is shut.
why.summer: Mar is still snowbound up top; Apr-May the ruins and village are fine but Gangabal stays patchy with snow above 3,500 m.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the trekking window: two days up to Gangabal under Harmukh, with guides and ponies hired in the village.
why.autumn: Early Oct is cold, clear and empty at the lakes; by November the shepherds are gone and the homestays have closed.

vibe: A trek-start village - Kashmiri guides, a few homestays and a campsite, plus Pandit pilgrims in yatra week.
hub: Srinagar 50 km via Ganderbal and Kangan, 2 h by bus plus a shared taxi up the Wangath side road.

spots.name: Naranag Temple Complex
spots.note: Two 8th century Shiva temple groups in huge grey blocks by the Wangath nallah; unfenced, no ticket, best light early.

spots.name: Gangabal Lake
spots.note: Alpine lake under Harmukh, a hard 13 km climb from the village; camp up there or start at first light, take a guide.

spots.name: Nundkol Lake
spots.note: Second lake just below Gangabal at the foot of Harmukh, joined by a short stream; the usual campsite, trout in the outflow.

spots.name: Kangan
spots.note: Sind valley road town below Naranag, the last ATM, shops and pharmacy; shared taxis up the Wangath road until about 5 pm.

name: Noori Chamb (Behramgala)
tagline: Mughal Road waterfall where Nur Jahan is said to have kept a mirror

why.winter: Dec-Feb the Mughal Road is shut at Peer ki Gali, so the only way in is up from Poonch, with snow on the path and the fall half frozen.
why.summer: March melt makes it loud while the pass above stays closed; April is green and quiet, and by May the road is open right through to Shopian at 25 C.
why.monsoon: June is warm with the fall still full and the road open both ways; Jul-Aug the Pir Panjal south face takes real rain, slick steps and landslide holdups. September is best.
why.autumn: October is clear and thin of people, with maple colour above Behramgala; by late November snow starts closing the pass again.

vibe: Dhabas, army camps and a couple of guest houses at Behramgala; Sundays bring Poonch families with picnic pots, weekdays nobody.
hub: Behramgala is 40 km from Poonch by shared sumo via Surankote; from the Kashmir side only while the Mughal Road is open.

name: Pahalgam
tagline: Pine-forested valley base for Amarnath Yatra and easy treks
festival: Jul-Aug: Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage transits through Pahalgam

why.winter: December can be pleasant with light snow; Jan-Feb turn properly cold, glacier routes snowbound.
why.summer: March is quiet and cool; April-May the valley blooms - a great window before Yatra crowds.
why.monsoon: June is lovely, but Jul-Aug bring Amarnath Yatra convoys and traffic curbs; September calms again.
why.autumn: October keeps the good weather with fewer crowds; November turns cold and grey into winter.

vibe: Amarnath pilgrims in season plus trekkers for Kolahoi Glacier or Tarsar-Marsar treks.
hub: Fly to Srinagar, then ~2h taxi or shared sumo to Pahalgam (95km)

spots.name: Betaab Valley
spots.note: Fenced meadow valley on the Chandanwari road, named after the film shot there; entry ticket, and it is packed by noon.

spots.name: Aru Valley
spots.note: Roadhead hamlet up the Lidder, base for the Kolahoi and Tarsar treks; shared cabs run till evening, beds cost less here.

spots.name: Baisaran
spots.note: Pine ringed meadow above town, 40 minutes on foot or by pony; check locally that it is open before you pay for a horse.

spots.name: Chandanwari
spots.note: Road end at the Amarnath yatra start, with a snow bridge over the Lidder into early summer; cabs run a fixed circuit.

spots.name: Mamleshwar Temple
spots.note: Small old stone Shiva temple with a spring tank across the river from the market; a 15 minute walk, no ticket, rarely busy.

spots.name: Tulian Lake
spots.note: Glacier lake at about 3350 m, a long day hike up past Baisaran and back; guide and an early start, snow closes it till June.

spots.name: Kolahoi Glacier
spots.note: Two to three day trek from Aru through Lidderwat to the glacier snout; guide, tent and food all arranged in Aru village.

name: Patnitop
tagline: Deodar ridge on the Jammu-Srinagar highway under Nathatop snow

why.winter: Dec-Feb brings knee-deep snow at Nathatop and sledging crowds up from Jammu; NH44 can shut for hours after a fall.
why.summer: Mar is raw and still patchy with snow; Apr-May is the sweet spot at 15-25 C under the deodars while Jammu bakes at 42 C.
why.monsoon: June is clear and green, but Jul-Aug is Ramban landslide season on NH44 with six-hour halts; Sep drains off slowly.
why.autumn: Oct is clear, empty and cold at night; by Nov it turns raw and most roadside dhabas start pulling their shutters.

vibe: Jammu weekenders and army families; JKTDC huts and budget hotels on the old road, almost no foreign backpackers.
hub: Udhampur railhead 50 km, Jammu 112 km; the new tunnel bypasses Patnitop, so take the old highway.

spots.name: Nathatop
spots.note: Bare ridge above Patnitop with the Pir Panjal laid out; the last stretch is a rough jeep track, snowbound Jan to Mar.

spots.name: Sanasar
spots.note: Cup shaped meadow with a small lake and a golf course; paragliding runs Apr to Jun, taxis charge a return fare from Patnitop.

spots.name: Skyview Patnitop Gondola
spots.note: Cable car from Sanasar over the deodar slopes; tickets are timed, book ahead on weekends, it shuts in high wind.

spots.name: Sudh Mahadev
spots.note: Shiva shrine holding an old broken trident worn smooth by pilgrims; quiet on weekdays, packed through the summer mela.

spots.name: Mantalai
spots.note: Deodar forest and a Shiva temple above Sudh Mahadev; an hour of easy walking is enough, no food past the gate.

spots.name: Kud
spots.note: Highway town whose shops sell patisa, a flaky gram flour sweet; sold by weight, buy from a shop that is turning it over.

name: Sonamarg
tagline: Meadow of Gold below Zoji La, base for the Great Lakes trek

why.winter: Buried in snow and largely cut off - Zoji La beyond is closed; not a viable visit outside a rare heli trip.
why.summer: March-April still heavily snowbound; by May the town reopens and Thajiwas Glacier draws visitors.
why.monsoon: Prime season - the Kashmir Great Lakes Trek runs Jul-Sep and the road onward to Ladakh is fully open.
why.autumn: October still has good trekking weather and autumn colour; November sees snow return, season shuts fast.

vibe: Day-trippers for glacier views and pony rides; trek camps fill with backpackers Jul-Sep.
hub: Fly to Srinagar, then ~2h taxi to Sonamarg (80km)

spots.name: Thajiwas Glacier
spots.note: Ice snout up a side valley from the meadow; about 90 minutes on foot each way, or a pony, agree the rate before you start.

spots.name: Zoji La
spots.note: Pass at 3528 m where Kashmir green ends and Ladakh rock starts; go early for convoy traffic, it shuts with the first snow.

spots.name: Baltal
spots.note: Meadow camp at the base of the short Amarnath route; a tent city in Jul and Aug, empty and windy the rest of the year.

spots.name: Nilagrad River
spots.note: Red tinted stream meeting the Sindh near Sarbal; locals bathe in it for its supposed cure, the water is glacier cold.

name: Srinagar
tagline: Houseboats on Dal Lake, Mughal gardens, J&K's summer capital
festival: Apr: Tulip Festival at Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden

why.winter: Cold - highs near 7C, sub-zero nights, gardens bare - but this is snow season, with the Gulmarg ski runs an hour away.
why.summer: March is cool; by April the Tulip Garden blooms and May weather is close to perfect.
why.monsoon: June stays lovely; Jul-Aug bring Amarnath Yatra convoys, checkpoints and higher prices, easing by Sep.
why.autumn: October is the best month - Chinars turn gold and crowds thin; November colder but still gorgeous.

vibe: Houseboat stays feel like a floating community, easy to link up for Gulmarg or Pahalgam.
hub: Fly direct from Delhi (~1.5h); well-connected from most metros

spots.name: Dal Lake Floating Vegetable Market
spots.note: Growers trade lotus stem and greens boat to boat at first light; be in a shikara by 5 am, it is over within the hour.

spots.name: Jamia Masjid, Nowhatta
spots.note: Wooden hall on hundreds of deodar pillars in the old city; visit outside prayer times, Friday noon is packed, cover your head.

spots.name: Shankaracharya Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple on the hill over the lake, up a couple of hundred steps; phones are barred at the top, go late afternoon.

spots.name: Nishat Bagh
spots.note: Twelve Mughal terraces rising from the Dal under old chinars; small ticket, quietest before 9 am when the buses arrive.

spots.name: Shalimar Bagh
spots.note: Jahangir's garden of water channels and chinar shade at the top of the lake; ticketed, the channels run only some hours.

spots.name: Pari Mahal
spots.note: Terraced Mughal school ruin on the Zabarwan slope above Chashme Shahi; taxi up for sunset, the whole lake lies below.

spots.name: Hazratbal Shrine
spots.note: White marble shrine on the Dal shore holding a relic of the Prophet; separate entrance for women, avoid Friday crowds.

spots.name: Nigeen Lake
spots.note: Quieter arm of the Dal with older houseboats and cleaner water; people swim here, shikaras cost less than on the Boulevard.

name: Teetwal (Tithwal)
tagline: Border village on the Kishanganga with a new Sharada Devi temple

why.winter: Dec-Feb the 3,100 m Sadhna Pass closes with every snowfall and Karnah is cut off for days at a time; you can be stuck either side.
why.summer: March is still a gamble on the pass. From April the road clears and the river runs full; May afternoons already touch 30 C by the water.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug is warm, hazy and thundery by late afternoon; September brings the maize and walnut in and the ridges sharpen up again.
why.autumn: October and early November are the pick: cold nights, clean light on the far bank, and the temple courtyard to yourself.

vibe: One street of Pahari houses, a temple and gurdwara compound with rooms, soldiers everywhere; nights are just the river.
hub: Kupwara to Tangdhar by shared sumo over the Sadhna Pass (3h), then 12 km down to Teetwal; carry ID for the checkposts.

name: Tulail Valley (Badugam)
tagline: Upper Kishanganga: log-and-stone Dard hamlets 40 km past Gurez

why.winter: Dec-Feb Razdan Pass is shut and Tulail lives off stored rice and firewood; nothing moves in or out but the army, so it is not a trip.
why.summer: March and April the pass is still buried. It usually opens late May, when the Kishanganga is loud with melt and the barley goes in.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is the window: warm days, cold nights, potato and rajma fields, and the rough 40 km run east of Dawar to Badugam and Chakwali.
why.autumn: October turns the poplars gold and empties the road; once November snow lands the pass closes and Tulail is on its own until spring.

vibe: Log-and-stone houses, a few new homestays and no hotels; evenings are noon chai and the last shop shutting with the light.
hub: Srinagar to Bandipora, shared sumo over Razdan Pass to Dawar (5h), then 40 km further east up the valley to Badugam.

name: Warwan Valley (Inshan)
tagline: Glacier-green valley over Margan Top that tourism never reached

why.winter: Dec-Feb Margan Top is buried and Inshan is cut off for months; villagers stock up in autumn and no outsider gets in.
why.summer: Mar-May the pass is still snowbound; late May sometimes opens to 4x4s but count on June at the earliest for shared cabs.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is the window: barley-green villages, the icy Warwan river and day walks toward Sukhnai under light valley rain.
why.autumn: Early Oct is gold and crystal but a gamble: one storm can shut Margan for the season, keep your return date loose.

vibe: Often the only outsider here: wood-smoke homestay kitchens in Inshan and Sukhnai, shepherds, no cafes, barely a signal.
hub: Srinagar via Kokernag and Margan Top, 6-7 h; seasonal shared cabs from Anantnag, none after snowfall.

spots.name: Margan Top
spots.note: The pass on the only road in, snowbound until about May; cabs stop at the top for chai and the whole valley opens below.

spots.name: Sukhnai
spots.note: Timber village upstream and the trailhead for the walk over Lomvilad Gali to Suru; homestay food only, carry your own gear.

spots.name: Marusudar River
spots.note: Glacier fed river running the length of the valley to the Chenab; cold and fast, cross only on bridges, trout in the pools.

name: Wular Lake (Watlab)
tagline: India's largest freshwater lake, seen from the Watlab orchard shore

why.winter: Dec-Feb is waterfowl season, coot and pochard in thousands on the shallows; fog holds till mid-morning and the boatmen start late.
why.summer: Mar-May the willows leaf out and snowmelt lifts the water. Mornings are flat calm for a shikara, afternoons hazy with a lake wind.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Jhelum runs brown into the lake and weed thickens along the shore; September clears the air and the evening light returns.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the clean window: still water, poplar colour on the Bandipora shore, Harmukh sharp from the shrine hill above Watlab.

vibe: Fishermen poling out before dawn, a tourist hut and a few Sopore homestays; evenings are tea on the shrine steps and little else.
hub: Sopore is 10 km off, an hour by bus or train from Srinagar, then a shared auto or sumo down to the Watlab shore.

name: Yusmarg
tagline: Pine-rimmed shepherd meadow and the walk to Nilnag lake

why.winter: Dec-Feb the meadow sits under snow and the Charar-i-Sharief road ices over; the JKTDC huts shut and taxis refuse it.
why.summer: Mar is mud and melt; Apr thaws it out and by May the meadow is at its best, 12-22 C, with Gujjar flocks moving up behind.
why.monsoon: Jun and Sep are the quiet good months; Jul-Aug is warm rather than wet but fills with Srinagar day-trippers and pony touts.
why.autumn: Oct empties out with frost on the grass and the Doodhganga running clear; Nov turns raw and the huts start shutting.

vibe: Day-trippers gone by 4 pm, then it is you, the JKTDC huts and two shepherd dhabas serving noon chai and rice.
hub: Srinagar 47 km; bus or shared taxi via Chadoora and Charar-i-Sharief, 2 h, last one back mid-afternoon.

spots.name: Nilnag Lake
spots.note: Small green lake in the pines above the meadow; about an hour up on foot or by pony, no stalls there, carry water.

spots.name: Doodh Ganga
spots.note: Frothy white stream below the meadow, boulders and pine banks; ten minutes down from the huts, people picnic on the rocks.

spots.name: Charar-i-Sharief
spots.note: Shrine of Sheikh Noor ud din Noorani, rebuilt in wood after the 1995 fire; on the road back to Srinagar, cover your head.

spots.name: Sang-e-Safed
spots.note: White rock bowl above the meadow where snow lingers into summer; about three hours out on foot, ponywallahs quote a return rate.

name: Betla National Park
tagline: Elephants and sal forest around two forgotten Palamu forts

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the core season at 8-27 C: 6 am jeep safaris, elephant herds on the Betla grassland and hard dry tracks.
why.summer: March still delivers sightings; April-June bake Palamu at 44 C in an open jeep and only the hardest wildlifers bother.
why.monsoon: The park shuts roughly 1 July to 30 September; the Koel rises, forest roads vanish and the gates simply do not open.
why.autumn: October reopening is lush but the grass is tall and visibility poor; November is when sightings and weather line up.

vibe: Forest rest houses and a state tourism lodge at the gate; a few Indian wildlife regulars, no backpacker scene
hub: Daltonganj (Medininagar) railhead 25 km, Ranchi 170 km by road; jeep safaris booked at the Betla gate

spots.name: Palamu Forts
spots.note: Two Chero forts crumbling into sal forest above the Auranga; walk in from the road, tell the forest post, no lights inside.

spots.name: Mirchaiya Falls
spots.note: Stream drop inside the park, worth the detour only after the rains; you need the park ticket and a vehicle, dry by March.

spots.name: Kechki Sangam
spots.note: Where the Koel and Auranga meet under sal, a picnic and fishing spot; a forest rest house sits above, empty on weekdays.

name: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: 900 m elephant-country summit looking over the Subarnarekha valley

why.winter: Peak: cool dawn treks from Makulakocha gate to the 900 m summit shrine, with hazy-blue views over the Subarnarekha valley.
why.summer: March-April improve elephant odds at shrinking waterholes, but by May the open climb is a 42 °C slog; start at first light.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the ghat track is slick red mud under sitting cloud; views vanish and the trails belong to leeches.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the forest is washed and green, the track dries out and weekend trekkers from Jamshedpur come back.

vibe: Forest rest house and bamboo huts at Makulakocha gate, weekend trekkers from Jamshedpur, nobody after sundown
hub: Makulakocha gate on the Ranchi-Jamshedpur highway, about 30 km from Tatanagar Jn; jeep track to the summit

spots.name: Dalma Top Shiva Temple
spots.note: Summit shrine that fills for the Shivratri fair; the jeep track up from Makulakocha gate takes an hour, walking it takes three.

spots.name: Pindrabera
spots.note: Waterhole and watchtower below the summit, the best chance of elephants or deer; sit still near dusk, arrange the stop at the gate.

spots.name: Dimna Lake
spots.note: Reservoir at the foot of the Dalma range with boating and a long dam wall; busy Sundays with Jamshedpur, quiet at dawn.

spots.name: Chandil Dam
spots.note: Subarnarekha reservoir with wooded islands below the Dalma range; on the Ranchi highway, sunset is the reason to go.

name: Dassam Falls
tagline: The Kanchi river's clean 44 m curtain drop near Taimara village

why.winter: Dec-Feb the Kanchi narrows to thin clean ribbons and the rock amphitheatre is calm; easy footing and few weekday visitors.
why.summer: Apr-May the flow nearly dies over hot black rock at 42 °C on the plateau; not worth the hour's drive out of Ranchi.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the 44 m curtain is thunderous and strictly no-swim water: drownings happen most years, stay behind the railings.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is best: post-monsoon volume with drier, safer steps and soft light through the Taimara valley forest.

vibe: Ranchi day-trip picnic scene with chowmein stalls at the rim; back to city hotels or basic Bundu lodges by dark
hub: 40 km from Ranchi on the Jamshedpur highway, then 2 km in; shared jeeps to Taimara mor, autos from Bundu

spots.name: Deori Mandir
spots.note: Sixteen armed Durga in a small stone shrine at Tamar on the Jamshedpur highway; any bus stops at the gate, shoes off outside.

spots.name: Jonha Falls
spots.note: Also called Gautam Dhara, a long drop reached by several hundred steps; the pool below drowns people, do not swim.

spots.name: Sita Falls
spots.note: Quieter fall in forest near Jonha, down a rough path from the road; needs your own vehicle, thin water after March.

name: Deoghar (Baidyanath Dham)
tagline: Jyotirlinga at the end of the 105 km Sultanganj kanwar walk
festival: Jul/Aug: Shravani Mela kanwar pilgrimage

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the calm season at 8-26 C: short darshan queues, time to climb Trikut on foot and reach Basukinath.
why.summer: March is fine; April-June the Santhal Parganas hit 42 C and the temple courtyard stone is too hot to stand on.
why.monsoon: July-August is Shravani Mela, when millions of kanwariyas arrive: hours-long queues, no rooms, a spectacle not a rest.
why.autumn: October and November are dry, mild and quiet after the mela, easily the best time for an unhurried darshan.

vibe: Pilgrim town of dharamshalas, peda shops and pandas; easy to be alone in, but you are always in somebody's queue
hub: Jasidih Junction 7 km on the Howrah-Delhi main line; Deoghar airport 12 km with Delhi and Kolkata flights

spots.name: Naulakha Mandir
spots.note: Tall white tower modelled on Belur Math, built by a Bengali rani; open through the day and far calmer than the main queue.

spots.name: Basukinath Temple
spots.note: Shiva's court, where pilgrims finish what they begin at Deoghar; buses run all day, the evening arti is the crowded hour.

spots.name: Trikut Pahar
spots.note: Three peaked hill with a ropeway and a shrine on top; check the ropeway is actually running before you make the trip.

spots.name: Tapovan Hills
spots.note: Rock hill with a Shiva cave and an old ashram at the foot; twenty minutes up bare rock, go early, no shade or water.

spots.name: Satsang Ashram
spots.note: Anukul Thakur's ashram quarter of presses and dispensaries; Bengali pilgrims fill it, visitors may walk most of the grounds.

spots.name: Nandan Pahar
spots.note: Hilltop park with a small zoo, boating and the town spread below; entry ticket, come for sunset, it closes by evening.

name: Ghatshila
tagline: Subarnarekha river town of Bengali holiday lodges, Burudih lake and Dharagiri falls

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the classic Bengali winter break: 12C dawns on Phuldungri hill, picnics by Burudih lake and Bibhutibhushan's house at Dahigora open for a look
why.summer: March is already 38C; Apr-May the Subarnarekha shrinks to sand and the town hits 44C with no shade on the hill roads, so not now
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep rains bring Dharagiri falls 13 km north to life and the Subarnarekha runs full and red-brown; humid, but the lodges empty out and the sal forest is green
why.autumn: Oct is warm and washed clean, Durga Puja fills the lodges with Kolkata families; Nov cools, the river clears and the Galudih barrage reflects the hills

vibe: Kolkata couples and families in cottage lodges around Dahigora; evenings are the riverbank, the Rankini temple lane and early dinners
hub: Ghatshila station on the Howrah-Tatanagar line: 3.5 h from Howrah by Steel Express, 40 min from Tatanagar; autos to Burudih

name: Hundru Falls
tagline: Subarnarekha drops 98 m of basalt, 740 steps below the road

why.winter: Dec-Feb the flow drops to a single clean ribbon and the pool is calm, with 740 steps down in 12 C morning air.
why.summer: Apr-May the Subarnarekha is a trickle over hot black rock at 42 C on the plateau, and there is nothing to see.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep it is at full roar and genuinely dangerous - people drown here most years, so stay off the wet rock.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the best of both: heavy post-monsoon flow, drier footing on the steps and 10 C plateau mornings.

vibe: A day trip, not a stay: Ranchi students and families, chai stalls at the top, everyone back in town by dark
hub: 45 km east of Ranchi via the Sikidiri ghat road; buses and shared jeeps from Ranchi, then 740 steps down

spots.name: Getalsud Dam
spots.note: Subarnarekha reservoir upstream of the falls, also called Rukka; the road runs along the water, best light at sunrise.

spots.name: Jonha Falls
spots.note: Gautam Dhara, a gorge fall down several hundred steps; pairs with Hundru in one day, the pool below has taken lives.

spots.name: Sita Falls
spots.note: Small fall in forest near Jonha off the Purulia road; you need your own vehicle and it is worth it only after the rains.

name: Kiriburu (Saranda Forest)
tagline: Iron-ore plateau township with a sunset ledge over Saranda's seven hundred sal hills

why.winter: Dec-Feb mornings drop to 8-10C on the plateau, the sunset point shows ridge after ridge of blue sal, and forest permits for the Thalkobad road are easiest to get
why.summer: Mar-Apr the sal sheds and flowers, dust haze thins the views and Barbil below hits 42C; May is harsh, though 880 m keeps the nights bearable
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep Saranda turns deep green with the Koina river in spate, but the forest tracks close, leeches rule and the mine haul roads become red mud
why.autumn: Oct clears the post-rain haze and the streams still run; Nov is the pick, cool 12C dawns, dry tracks to Thalkobad and Karampada, and ridges visible to the horizon

vibe: SAIL township with a guest house; evenings are the sunset ledge, a chai stall and ore trucks; Thalkobad forest rest house by permit
hub: Barbil railhead 20 km, Jan Shatabdi 7 h from Howrah; 3.5 h by road from Tatanagar via Chaibasa; Bara Jamda halt 12 km

name: Maluti
tagline: Seventy-two terracotta temples in a forgotten Jharkhand village

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the time to read the terracotta panels: 9-26 C, low raking sun on the brickwork and the lanes to yourself.
why.summer: March is warm but fine; April-June the Santhal Parganas run 42 C and there is no shade among the temple clusters.
why.monsoon: June-September rain darkens and erodes the exposed brick, the village lanes turn to mud and the panels photograph badly.
why.autumn: October is humid with green paddy all around; November is dry and cool, with the best light on the carved facades.

vibe: No stay in Maluti itself; sleep at Rampurhat or Tarapith and come for a half day among priests, goats and ruins
hub: Rampurhat station 16 km in West Bengal, then auto or the Dumka bus; Dumka 55 km, Tarapith 18 km for beds

spots.name: Mauliksha Mandir
spots.note: The living temple among the 72, goddess of the old Maluti rajas and tied to Bamakhepa; the priest opens it on request.

spots.name: Tarapith
spots.note: Tantric Tara temple and its cremation ground over in Bengal; this is where the beds and food are, dawn is the calm hour.

spots.name: Massanjore Dam
spots.note: Long dam on the Mayurakshi with a rest house above the water; about an hour by car, nothing to eat there, carry lunch.

name: McCluskieganj
tagline: Fading Anglo-Indian settlement of bungalows in sal forest

why.winter: Cool veranda weather to cycle between colonial-era bungalows, the Dugadugi stream and sal forest; nights dip near 8 °C.
why.summer: Apr-May is a dusty 40 °C on the plateau; lanes empty by mid-morning and the ganj's faded charm wilts in the heat.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep rain turns the forest lush and the Dugadugi full, but lanes go muddy and homestay days get slow and damp.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings washed green forest and the year's best walking light along the estate lanes and weekly haats.

vibe: Anglo-Indian family homestays with home cooking and long stories; Bengali nostalgia tourists at Christmas, else quiet
hub: McCluskieganj station on the Ranchi-Daltonganj line; about 65 km by road from Ranchi, autos for estate lanes

spots.name: Anglo-Indian Cemetery
spots.note: Settler graves from the 1930s colony under the sal, English names on them; the gate is usually open, ask a neighbour if not.

spots.name: Degadegi River
spots.note: Shallow forest stream a walk from the bungalow lanes where villagers wash and fish; only worth seeing after the rains.

spots.name: Ratu Palace
spots.note: Nagvanshi maharaja's palace on the Ranchi road, part Mughal part Rajput; still a family home, so you see it from outside.

name: Netarhat
tagline: Queen of Chotanagpur - pine forest sunrise/sunset points

why.winter: Cold, clear mornings: the best conditions for the sunrise/sunset points it's known for.
why.summer: Warmer but still cooler than the Jharkhand plains; hazier skies dull the famous viewpoints.
why.monsoon: Thick fog and cloud block the sunrise/sunset views entirely, and forest roads get slick.
why.autumn: Skies clear up nicely by November, matching the winter peak in quality.

vibe: State guesthouses and little else after dark - this is solitude, not a scene.
hub: 4hr drive from Ranchi; own vehicle recommended, buses are sparse.

spots.name: Magnolia Point
spots.note: Cliff edge sunset point named for an English girl in the local legend; be there by 4.30 pm, the road back is unlit

spots.name: Netarhat Sunrise Point
spots.note: Ridge above the plateau where the sal country turns pink at dawn; walk out by 5 am, mornings stay cold even in April

spots.name: Lodh Falls
spots.note: Jharkhand's highest fall, 143 m of the Burha river dropping in stages; 2 hr each way on rough road, do not leave it late

spots.name: Upper Ghaghri Falls
spots.note: Small stepped fall in sal forest below the plateau rim, ten minutes down a stone path; best just after the monsoon

spots.name: Lower Ghaghri Falls
spots.note: Bigger drop on the same stream, reached by a forest track off the Ranchi road; carry water, there are no shops

name: Parasnath Hill (Shikharji)
tagline: Jharkhand's highest hill and Jainism's holiest summit walk

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season for the 27 km round trip: 5-22 C, dry paving and 3 am starts under a properly cold sky.
why.summer: March is warm but walkable; April-June bake the lower 9 km at 40 C and the climb turns into a heatstroke risk.
why.monsoon: Mid-June to September the paved track runs with water, leeches are constant and the summit sits inside cloud all day.
why.autumn: October is humid with lingering cloud; November is superb, cold at dawn with the Chota Nagpur plateau spread below.

vibe: Jain dharamshalas at Madhuban feed and house you for very little; pilgrims of every age, doli bearers, no nightlife
hub: Parasnath station on the grand chord, then 25 km by shared jeep to Madhuban; 9 km climb, start by 3 am

spots.name: Parasnath Tonk
spots.note: Summit shrine where Parshvanatha is held to have reached moksha, the high point of the climb; leave Madhuban by 3 am

spots.name: Madhuban
spots.note: Base village of Jain temples and dharamshalas where the climb starts; the dharamshalas take walk-ins and serve a fixed thali

spots.name: Bhomiyaji Mandir
spots.note: Trailhead shrine at Madhuban where pilgrims bow before the 9 km climb; doli bearers and torch sellers wait from 2 am

spots.name: Gandharva Nala
spots.note: Stream and rest stop about a third of the way up from Madhuban; pilgrims refill water here before the long ridge of tonks

spots.name: Topchanchi Lake
spots.note: British era reservoir ringed by a small sanctuary on the Dhanbad road; an easy half day, quietest on weekday mornings

name: Patratu Valley
tagline: Hairpin ghat road dropping to a blue dam lake in Chotanagpur sal hills

why.winter: Peak: crisp 10 °C mornings, still water at the boat jetty and clear light down the hairpins; Sundays bring Ranchi convoys.
why.summer: Apr-May the plateau hazes over at 40 °C and the lake pulls back off red laterite banks; the drive loses its drama.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the valley turns rainforest green with cloud spilling over the ridge; views come and go and drizzle owns the jetty.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is prime: the reservoir sits brimful after the rains, skies rinse clean and midweek rooms are easy to get.

vibe: JTDC's lakeside rooms and dorm plus boat rides; weekends are Ranchi picnic crowds, weekdays nearly private
hub: Ranchi 40 km via the Pithoria ghat hairpins; Patratu station and shared autos from town, last leg by auto

spots.name: Patratu Dam
spots.note: The blue reservoir the valley road drops to, with a boating jetty and JTDC rooms; boats stop running around 5 pm

spots.name: Patratu Valley View Point
spots.note: Layby on the ghat where the hairpins stack up below you; come late afternoon, morning fog hides the whole valley

spots.name: Rajrappa Chhinnamasta Temple
spots.note: Tantric shrine to the headless goddess where the Bhairavi meets the Damodar; goat sacrifice happens, go via Ramgarh and start early

spots.name: Tuti Jharna Mandir
spots.note: Ramgarh shivling with a spring that drips onto it all year; five minutes off the Ranchi road, no fee, no crowds

name: Rajmahal (Sahibganj)
tagline: Mughal Bengal's lost capital on the Ganga: Akbari mosques, a river baradari, dolphins

why.winter: Nov-Feb is dry and 10-25C: walk the Jami Masjid at Hadaf, Singhi Dalan on the Ganga bank and the Baradari, then take a boat at dawn for the Gangetic dolphins
why.summer: March is still workable early in the day; Apr-May the Ganga plain hits 44C with hot loo winds through the ruins, so not now
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Ganga swells to the horizon and floods the low ghats; humid, boats stop in spate, but the Rajmahal hills behind turn green and Moti Jharna runs
why.autumn: Oct is warm and wet-green with the river still high; Nov cools, dolphin boats resume and the Mandro fossil park and Udhwa lake birds come into season

vibe: No tourists to speak of; a Sahibganj hotel or a basic Rajmahal lodge, chai at the ghat and curious locals walking you to the ruins
hub: Sahibganj station on the loop line, 6 h from Howrah, 5 h from Patna; Rajmahal 30 km / 1 h by bus or auto, or the branch train

name: Agumbe
tagline: Rainforest village known as South India's Cherrapunji

why.winter: Waterfalls still running from the tail of monsoon, forest lush, no leeches - underrated.
why.summer: The rainforest without rain is just a forest - falls reduce to a trickle, skip it.
why.monsoon: This is the season - 700cm+ of rain, roaring falls, king cobras out, but leeches everywhere.
why.autumn: Monsoon runoff still feeding the falls, canopy dripping green, sunset point visible again.

vibe: A handful of naturalists and photographers - homestay dinners are the social hub.
hub: Fly Mangalore, 3h drive; a rental car is close to essential.

spots.name: Agumbe Sunset Point
spots.note: Ghat edge platform looking over the coastal plain to the sea; only clear from November to February, monsoon is cloud

spots.name: Doddamane
spots.note: The old tiled house used for the Malgudi Days shoot, still a family home; visitors are let in during daylight hours

spots.name: Onake Abbi Falls
spots.note: Deep forest fall about an hour's walk off the ghat road; forest office permission needed and the path shuts in the rains

spots.name: Jogigundi Falls
spots.note: Small fall beside a cave shrine, twenty minutes on a leech heavy path; carry salt and socks in the wet months

spots.name: Barkana Falls Viewpoint
spots.note: Roadside lookout across the valley to a fall of about 250 m; it runs June to October only, binoculars help

name: Badami-Aihole-Pattadakal
tagline: Chalukya cave temples and sandstone shrine cluster
festival: Jan: Pattadakal Dance Festival amid the ancient temples

why.winter: Cool enough to scramble the cave temples at midday - best season for the full cluster.
why.summer: North Karnataka turns brutal, 40C+ on exposed sandstone - bearable only at sunrise.
why.monsoon: Rain here is moderate, not heavy - the Agastya lake fills nicely without landslide risk.
why.autumn: Post-monsoon light on the red sandstone is gorgeous, temps dropping - great for photos.

vibe: Quiet, independent-traveler territory - easy to chat with the handful of other visitors.
hub: Fly Hubli, 2h drive; Aihole/Pattadakal a further taxi loop.

spots.name: Bhutanatha Temples
spots.note: Sandstone shrines standing in Agastya lake below the caves; come at sunrise for the light and the empty steps

spots.name: Badami Fort
spots.note: Steps up the north cliff to Upper Shivalaya and cannon points over the town; an hour's climb with no shade at midday

spots.name: Banashankari Temple
spots.note: Living temple to Banashankari with a big stepped tank in front, still in daily use; the January jatre fills the village for days

spots.name: Mahakuta Temple Complex
spots.note: Cluster of small 7th century shrines round a spring fed tank people still bathe in; a quiet half hour by auto from Badami

spots.name: Sidlaphadi
spots.note: Natural rock bridge and prehistoric shelter in the hills behind Badami; take a local guide, the path is unmarked

name: Bandipur National Park
tagline: Deccan teak and elephant country on the Mysuru-Ooty road

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the comfortable window: 28 °C, good light, and herds of gaur and elephant out in the open teak blocks.
why.summer: Mar-May is hot at 36 °C but gives the best odds on tiger and leopard as animals crowd the last water holes.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the park stays open but heavy south-west rain and thick undergrowth cut sightings to almost nothing.
why.autumn: October greens up and the safari calendar restarts properly; November is excellent, cool and uncrowded.

vibe: Forest department jeep seats are cheap and shared; homestays at Melukamanahalli, no traveller scene beyond them
hub: Mysuru railhead 80 km, then a 2 h bus on NH-766; the highway is shut to traffic 9 pm to 6 am

spots.name: Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta
spots.note: Misty 1450 m hilltop temple inside the reserve; private cars stop at the base and a forest bus runs up till 4 pm

spots.name: Melukamanahalli
spots.note: Roadside hamlet on NH-766 holding most of the Bandipur homestays and their small eateries; about 5 km from the safari counter

spots.name: Gundlupet
spots.note: Market town on the Mysuru road ringed by marigold and sunflower fields; ask locally which fields are in bloom before driving out

name: Belur-Halebidu
tagline: Twin Hoysala temple towns carved in soapstone

why.winter: Cool, comfortable temps for lingering over the soapstone carvings - best photo light.
why.summer: Properly hot with little shade in the temple courtyards - visit early or skip it.
why.monsoon: Rain is moderate here, not a deluge; the Yagachi river fills, temples still work wet.
why.autumn: October-November mixes post-monsoon greenery with easing heat - underrated, low season.

vibe: A quiet day-trip stop for architecture fans - almost no traveler social scene here.
hub: 3h train/bus from Bengaluru to Hassan, then 30-40min to Belur.

spots.name: Veera Narayana Temple, Belavadi
spots.note: Hoysala three shrine temple in a farming village, usually empty; the Venugopala idol is the one to see, no ticket

spots.name: Parshvanatha Basadi, Halebidu
spots.note: Jain basadi with lathe turned pillars polished like mirrors; the caretaker unlocks it and expects a small tip

spots.name: Kedareshwara Temple, Halebidu
spots.note: Half ruined Hoysala temple a short walk from Hoysaleswara, usually empty; the ASI enclosure is open through daylight hours

spots.name: Doddagaddavalli Lakshmi Devi Temple
spots.note: 1114 CE four shrine temple with stone towers and demon guardians, off the Hassan road; the caretaker opens it on request

spots.name: Yagachi Dam
spots.note: Reservoir on the Hassan road with speedboats and a windy bund; the water sports counter shuts around 5 pm

name: Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Muthodi)
tagline: Teak and shola tiger reserve with a rest house at the gate

why.winter: Dec-Feb dawn safaris run at 10 C through teak and bamboo; gaur and elephant are near certain, the tigers stay a rumour.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is the sighting season as the forest dries and everything walks to the Bhadra backwater; May hits 35 C with evening storms.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the Muthodi road floods, safaris stop for days at a time and the leeches are serious; wait it out.
why.autumn: October reopens onto washed green forest and full streams, and November is the quietest good month before the winter bookings start.

vibe: A forest rest house, a state-run tented camp and two homestays; dinner at a fixed hour, then generator off and bed
hub: Train to Kadur or Birur, bus on to Chikkamagaluru, then a 1h taxi over the last 30 km to the Muthodi gate

name: Bidar
tagline: Bahmani fort, a ruined madrasa and Bidriware workshops

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the window: 27 °C, dry laterite light on the fort walls, and the tomb complexes empty on weekdays.
why.summer: Apr-Jun runs to 42 °C on the open plateau; the fort has no shade at all and the Bahmani tombs even less.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is mild by Deccan standards and green, with the old karez water channels flowing and no crowds at all.
why.autumn: October is still warm but the dust settles; by November the Mahmud Gawan madrasa is worth the trip on its own.

vibe: Very few travellers and a handful of plain hotels near the bus stand; Bidriware workshops welcome walk-ins
hub: Bidar airport has Star Air to Bengaluru; railhead in town, Hyderabad airport 170 km by road

spots.name: Bidar Fort
spots.note: Bahmani citadel on a laterite plateau with triple moats and the Rangin Mahal tilework; free entry, allow two hours

spots.name: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa
spots.note: Ruined 1472 college in the old town with one minaret of Persian tiles still standing; best light late afternoon

spots.name: Bahmani Tombs, Ashtur
spots.note: Row of domed sultan tombs in open fields; Ahmad Shah Wali's has painted interiors, the guard opens it on request

spots.name: Gurudwara Nanak Jhira Sahib
spots.note: Marble gurudwara over the spring Guru Nanak is said to have opened; free langar at midday, cover your head inside

spots.name: Narasimha Jhira Cave Temple
spots.note: You wade 300 m of chest deep water into a hill to reach the idol; leave phone and wallet in the lockers, no shoes

name: BR Hills (Biligiri Ranganatha)
tagline: Soliga tribal hills where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the sweet spot: 26 °C days, cold nights at 1,200 m, and elephant and gaur out on the K Gudi road.
why.summer: March is dry and excellent for sightings; by May it is 34 °C at the base and the hill air turns smoky.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the sanctuary road up from Yelandur runs with water, safaris are patchy and the temple track gets slippery.
why.autumn: October is still wet and quiet; November is superb, green, cool in the mornings and free of weekend traffic.

vibe: Only the JLR camp at K Gudi and a couple of Soliga-run homestays; you will not meet other solo travellers here
hub: Chamarajanagar railhead 50 km or Mysuru 90 km, then a hill bus; the last bus up leaves early afternoon

spots.name: Biligiri Ranganathaswamy Temple
spots.note: Cliff top Vishnu shrine the hills are named for, with a giant leather chappal offering; the ghat road shuts at 6 pm

spots.name: K Gudi
spots.note: Forest hamlet with the JLR camp and the safari zone; jeep drives leave about 6.30 am and 3.30 pm, book at the camp

spots.name: Dodda Sampige Mara
spots.note: Giant champak tree the Soligas worship as an ancestor, beside a stream; a rough forest road, ask at K Gudi first

spots.name: Honnametti
spots.note: Open ridge above coffee slopes with the plains laid out below; the view goes early, cloud builds through the afternoon

spots.name: Gaurishvara Temple, Yelandur
spots.note: Vijayanagara era stone temple in the market town below the hills; an easy stop on the way down, no ticket

name: Chikmagalur
tagline: Coffee-hill base for Karnataka's highest peak

why.winter: Crisp air, clear summit views from Mullayanagiri, coffee harvest in full swing.
why.summer: Warmer but still cooler than the plains; mornings are great before the heat builds.
why.monsoon: Kudremukh gets drenched, trails turn to landslide-prone mud, clouds erase the views.
why.autumn: October-November: waterfalls roaring, forests soaked green, air crystal clear.

vibe: Trekking base camps and estate homestays draw Bengaluru weekenders - easy to join a hike.
hub: Fly Mangalore or Bengaluru, 4-5h drive; nearest train Kadur (1h).

spots.name: Mullayanagiri
spots.note: Karnataka's highest peak at 1930 m with a small Shiva shrine on top; the road runs to the base, then about 250 steps up

spots.name: Baba Budangiri
spots.note: Cave shrine of a Sufi saint and Dattatreya revered by both faiths; the ridge road is narrow, go before afternoon

spots.name: Manikyadhara Falls
spots.note: Thin cold shower below Baba Budangiri that pilgrims stand under; steps down past stalls, slippery in the monsoon

spots.name: Hirekolale Lake
spots.note: Irrigation lake under the Mullayanagiri ridge, good for an evening hour; the last stretch of road is rough

spots.name: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Muthodi range jeep safaris for gaur, elephant and the odd tiger; book the 6 am drive at the Muthodi gate a day ahead

spots.name: Ayyanakere
spots.note: One of the state's oldest big tanks below Baba Budangiri, with a bund to walk; no shade and no shops, carry water

name: Chitradurga
tagline: Seven-walled hill fort spread over granite boulders

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the time to climb it: 28 °C, dry rock, and three hours of gates and bastions without heat stroke.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the granite radiates and the fort passes 40 °C by 10 am; the climb becomes a real health risk.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is rain-shadow drizzle rather than a downpour, cool enough to walk, though the smooth rock gets slippery.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is best: boulders washed clean, the tank inside the fort full, and weekday crowds down to almost nil.

vibe: Highway town with plain hotels; day-trippers from Bengaluru at weekends and near silence on a Tuesday
hub: Chitradurga station 4 km from the fort; NH-48 buses from Bengaluru 200 km and Hubballi 200 km

spots.name: Chitradurga Fort
spots.note: Seven walls of granite across a boulder hill, with Obavva's narrow gap inside; three hours minimum, start by 8 am

spots.name: Chandravalli Caves
spots.note: Lamp lit passages under Ankali Math where monks once meditated; a guide leads you in, expect to crouch and crawl

spots.name: Jogimatti
spots.note: Forest ridge and old rest house above the plain, the district's cool corner; the gate shuts at 5.30 pm, no food up top

spots.name: Adumalleshwara Temple
spots.note: Rock cut Shiva shrine where a spring pours from a stone Nandi, with a small deer park; mornings are quietest

spots.name: Vani Vilas Sagar
spots.note: 1907 masonry dam across the Vedavathi in dry hills, older than KRS; the reservoir is low outside the monsoon months

name: Coorg (Madikeri)
tagline: Misty coffee-estate hills of the Kodava heartland
festival: Nov-Dec: Puthari, the Kodava rice harvest festival

why.winter: Cool misty mornings, coffee harvest underway, waterfalls still flowing - classic Coorg.
why.summer: Warm and dry, but March-April brings the coffee blossom - hillsides turn white overnight.
why.monsoon: Some of Karnataka's heaviest rain - landslide-prone roads, leeches, zero-visibility mist.
why.autumn: October-November: monsoon just ended, everything green, waterfalls at their fullest.

vibe: More honeymoon resorts than hostels, but homestays and trekking groups work fine solo.
hub: Fly Mangalore/Bengaluru, 5-6h drive; nearest train Mysuru (3h).

spots.name: Raja's Seat
spots.note: Garden ledge where the Kodagu kings watched sunset over the valleys; small fee, be there by 5.30 pm for a seat

spots.name: Abbey Falls
spots.note: Fall inside a coffee and pepper estate, seen from a hanging bridge; full only in the rains, entry closes about 5.30 pm

spots.name: Madikeri Fort
spots.note: Town centre fort holding the old palace, a church museum and stone tortoises; the museum is shut on Mondays

spots.name: Omkareshwara Temple
spots.note: 1820 Shiva temple built with a dome and minarets round a fish filled tank; five minutes on foot from the fort

spots.name: Mandalpatti
spots.note: Grass hills at 1600 m up the track past Abbey Falls; the last 8 km need a hired jeep, go for sunrise or skip it

spots.name: Talakaveri
spots.note: Tank at the source of the Kaveri on Brahmagiri, with 350 steps to the summit; cold, and in cloud most afternoons

spots.name: Bhagamandala
spots.note: Triveni sangama where three rivers meet, with a Kerala style tiled temple; pilgrims bathe here before Talakaveri

spots.name: Dubare Elephant Camp
spots.note: Forest camp across the Kaveri where the morning elephant session runs; cross on the boat at the counter, slots end near 11 am

name: Dandeli
tagline: White-water rafting base on the Kali river

why.winter: Peak season for rafting on the Kali river plus jeep safaris for hornbills and panthers.
why.summer: Warmer and drier, river runs milder, but good for birding and canopy ziplining.
why.monsoon: The Kali floods and rafting is suspended for safety; trails turn muddy and leech-ridden.
why.autumn: October reopens the rafting season - controlled river levels, forest freshly green.

vibe: River-camp hostels and group rafting trips make solo travel easy here.
hub: Fly Goa (2.5h) or Hubli; overnight bus from Bengaluru (7-8h).

spots.name: Syntheri Rocks
spots.note: Sheer granite monolith above the Kaneri river inside the sanctuary; forest gate permit at Ambikanagar, gates shut by 5 pm.

spots.name: Kavala Caves
spots.note: Limestone cave with a natural Shivalinga, about 375 steps down through forest; carry a torch, shut in heavy monsoon.

spots.name: Sykes Point
spots.note: Cliff lookout over the Kali valley and unbroken canopy; best in the hour before sunset, no railing and no shop, carry water.

spots.name: Supa Dam
spots.note: Kali river dam above Ganeshgudi; releases from it set the water in the rafting stretch, and you see it from the road side only.

spots.name: Old Magazine House
spots.note: Birding lodge at Ganeshgudi with a hide over the water drip; hornbills and trogons at first light, day visits need booking.

spots.name: Kulgi Nature Camp
spots.note: Forest department camp at the sanctuary edge, base for the morning nature trail and jeep safari; book at the Dandeli range office.

name: Gokak Falls
tagline: Horseshoe cataract with a century-old hanging bridge at its crest

why.winter: Dec-Feb the Ghataprabha thins to streaks down the red horseshoe cliff; pleasant 29 °C walking weather, but you came for water.
why.summer: Mar-May is bare rock in 40 °C north Karnataka heat, the falls dry unless Hidkal dam releases upstream; skip it.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is the event: a curtain nearly 170 m wide in full roar; the hanging bridge often shuts at peak flow, so you watch from the banks
why.autumn: October usually still carries dam-fed flow, with softer light on the Chalukyan temple at the brink; November is a gamble.

vibe: Local families and photographers in season, nobody after; sleep in Gokak town 6 km away or day-trip from Belagavi.
hub: Ghataprabha railhead 12 km, Belagavi airport 70 km; buses to Gokak town, then an auto 6 km out to the falls.

spots.name: Godachinamalaki Falls
spots.note: Two step fall on the Markandeya river, a 400 step climb down from the village; full only in monsoon, the rock at the pool is slick.

spots.name: Mahalingeshwara Temple
spots.note: Old stone temple on the ledge above the cataract with carved pillars and a river view; open dawn to dusk, no ticket.

spots.name: Dhupdal Dam
spots.note: Low masonry dam and canal head on the Ghataprabha upstream; a calm evening walk in the months the falls run dry, free.

spots.name: Hidkal Dam
spots.note: Big Ghataprabha reservoir with a garden below the dam wall; a half day out from Gokak, best late afternoon when the heat drops.

spots.name: Saundatti Yellamma Temple
spots.note: Renuka Yellamma hill temple above Saundatti, packed on full moon days; road or steps to the top, shoes stay at the bottom.

name: Gokarna
tagline: Temple town turned backpacker beach-hopping strip
festival: Feb/Mar: Shivaratri car festival at Mahabaleshwar Temple

why.winter: Calm sea, full shack scene across Om, Kudle and Paradise beaches, best weather of the year.
why.summer: Hot and humid, sea still swimmable but the shoulder-season charm is gone.
why.monsoon: Sea turns rough and brown, most shacks shut, rip currents make swimming dangerous.
why.autumn: October's a hidden gem - cliffs still green, sea calming, a fraction of the December crowd.

vibe: Backpacker beach-hop scene close to Goa's energy but mellower - easy to find a crew.
hub: Train to Gokarna Rd, or fly Goa/Hubli then 2-3h taxi.

spots.name: Mahabaleshwar Temple
spots.note: The Atmalinga temple the town grew around; men enter bare chested, no phones or cameras, morning darshan is the calmest.

spots.name: Kudle Beach
spots.note: First beach south of town, about 20 minutes over the headland on foot; shacks and yoga decks, strong rips through the monsoon.

spots.name: Om Beach
spots.note: Two bays shaped like an om and the busiest of the strip; auto from town or the cliff path from Kudle, seafood shacks at sunset.

spots.name: Half Moon Beach
spots.note: Small cove past Om reached by a 30 minute cliff path or a boat; a handful of huts, carry cash, there is no ATM past town.

spots.name: Paradise Beach
spots.note: Last cove on the trail, clear water between rocks; camping was cleared out years ago, come for the day and boat back before dark.

spots.name: Mirjan Fort
spots.note: Laterite fort with a moat and overgrown stairways off the Kumta road; quiet on weekday mornings, any Kumta bus drops you at the turn.

spots.name: Koti Tirtha
spots.note: Temple tank in the middle of town where pilgrims perform rites for the dead; watch from the steps, no swimming, best light early.

name: Hampi
tagline: Vijayanagara ruins amid giant granite boulders
festival: Feb/Mar: Hampi Utsav (Vijaya Utsav) cultural festival

why.winter: Peak season - cool mornings for ruin-hopping, coracle rides, and Hampi Utsav some years in Feb.
why.summer: Skip it - 38-40C mean highs with 45C spikes, radiating off bare granite, and ruin-hopping here is a full day on foot.
why.monsoon: Tungabhadra river fills up, boulders turn green, fewer tourists, still hot but humid.
why.autumn: Post-monsoon green fading to gold, cool temps arriving - genuinely the sweet spot of the year.

vibe: Hippie Island guesthouses draw a laid-back backpacker crowd for sunset boulder views.
hub: Train to Hospet Jn, 15min auto; overnight bus from Bengaluru.

spots.name: Virupaksha Temple
spots.note: The living temple at the head of Hampi Bazaar, still in daily worship; token entry fee, the sanctum shuts for a long midday break.

spots.name: Vittala Temple
spots.note: Stone chariot and the ringing pillars, the finest of the ruins; one ASI ticket covers this and the Zenana enclosure the same day.

spots.name: Matanga Hill
spots.note: Steep 30 minute climb to the high point over the whole ruin field; sunrise is the reason, go in a group, thefts happen in the dark.

spots.name: Hemakuta Hill
spots.note: Cluster of small early shrines on bare rock right above Virupaksha; free, five minutes from the bazaar, come for sunset.

spots.name: Royal Enclosure
spots.note: Mahanavami Dibba platform and the stepped tank on open ground; no shade at all, come early and carry water, no ticket needed.

spots.name: Anjanadri Hill
spots.note: Around 570 steps up to the Hanuman temple across the river; ferry across or the long road loop via Kampli, monkeys grab food.

spots.name: Sanapur Lake
spots.note: Green reservoir among boulders past Anegundi with coracle rides; no lifeguards and deep water, people have drowned jumping in.

spots.name: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary
spots.note: Scrub hills where sloth bears come out to a rock face at dusk; the afternoon slot only, ticket at the gate, bring binoculars.

name: Honnemaradu
tagline: Island-studded Sharavathi backwater for kayak and coracle camping

why.winter: Dec-Feb is glass-water season: mist lifting off the reservoir at dawn, cold swims and proper darkness for a sky full of stars.
why.summer: March mornings still work; by May the water drops, red banks widen and 35 °C afternoons shrink paddling to the early hours.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the camps shut: squalls sweep the open reservoir, the catchment takes 4,000 mm plus and paddling is off the table.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the reservoir sits brim-full from the monsoon, the islands turn emerald and the first camps of the season feel private.

vibe: A tented camp and a couple of homestays, no shops or bars; you share coracles, campfires and chores with a small group.
hub: Talaguppa railhead 7 km (overnight train from Bengaluru); book the camp ahead, Jog Falls is 15 km further on.

spots.name: Linganamakki Dam
spots.note: The dam that holds back the Sharavathi and makes the backwater you paddle; drive out for the reservoir view in the last light.

spots.name: Sigandur Chowdeshwari Temple
spots.note: Sharavathi backwater goddess whose stickers ride on lorry cabs across the state; a half day trip from here, go in the morning.

spots.name: Ikkeri Aghoreshwara Temple
spots.note: Keladi Nayaka capital temple in dark stone with a deeply carved Nandi; quiet and free, 3 km south of Sagara town.

spots.name: Keladi Rameshwara Temple
spots.note: The dynasty's first capital, a carved wooden ceiling and a small museum beside it; buses run from Sagara, allow an hour.

name: Iruppu Falls (Kurchi)
tagline: Lakshmana Tirtha drop at the Brahmagiri trek gate
festival: Feb/Mar: Shivaratri bathing in the Lakshmana Tirtha

why.winter: Dec-Jan the falls still come down hard off the Brahmagiri and the ridge trek to Narimale runs on a permit; February starts to thin it out.
why.summer: Mar-May the drop shrinks to a trickle and Kodagu warms up, but the sanctuary path stays open until the first rain and the forest is silent.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug the sanctuary gate shuts, the Kutta road slips and leeches take the steps; June and late September are the only honest windows.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the best of it: full flow, mist in the evergreen forest and Nagarhole's Kutta gate close enough for a dawn safari.

vibe: Coffee and pepper homestays around Srimangala and Kurchi; evenings are frog noise and one shared dinner table
hub: Bus from Gonikoppal to Srimangala, then 8 km by auto to the gate; Mysuru is 120 km and about 3h30 out

name: Jog Falls
tagline: India's second-highest plunge waterfall on the Sharavathi

why.winter: Usually reduced to a trickle - water's held back at the Linganamakki dam upstream.
why.summer: Skip it - 95 percent of the Sharavathi's rain falls Jun-Sep, so Mar-May is bare cliff unless the dam happens to release.
why.monsoon: The real deal - July-September the Sharavathi thunders down in full four-channel force.
why.autumn: October-November still carries good residual flow, with far fewer crowds than July.

vibe: A viewpoint stop for photographers and day-trippers, not really a place to linger solo.
hub: Nearest hub Shimoga (2.5h drive) or fly Mangalore (3.5h).

spots.name: Linganamakki Dam
spots.note: The reservoir upstream that decides how much water reaches the falls; gates open only in a full monsoon, the drive out is short.

spots.name: Dabbe Falls
spots.note: White cascade down a rock face in Sharavathi forest; jeep from Hosagadde then a steep path, leeches after rain, dry by March.

spots.name: Sigandur Chowdeshwari Temple
spots.note: Backwater goddess across the Sharavathi whose stickers ride on lorry cabs; a half day out from the falls, go in the morning.

spots.name: Keladi Rameshwara Temple
spots.note: Keladi Nayaka temple with a carved wooden ceiling and a small dynasty museum beside it; buses run from Sagara town.

spots.name: Gerusoppa Chaturmukha Basadi
spots.note: Four faced Jain basadi in forest downstream, built by the pepper queen Chennabhairadevi; the last stretch is a rough track.

name: Kabini
tagline: Backwater safari base beside Nagarhole National Park

why.winter: Cool safaris, and this is when the famous Kabini elephant herds gather on exposed banks.
why.summer: Brutally hot, but excellent for tiger and leopard sightings near the shrinking waterholes.
why.monsoon: Safaris still run, Nagarhole does not shut - but the forest closes in, animals scatter and sightings drop; rates drop too.
why.autumn: October is the transition - first herds return to the drying banks, fewer safari jeeps.

vibe: Small-group safaris are naturally social, but the resort-lodge format runs pricey.
hub: Drive from Mysuru (1.5-2h) or Bengaluru (5-6h) via road.

spots.name: Nagarhole National Park
spots.note: Kabini zone jeep safaris leave the reception at 6:30 am and 3 pm; book ahead, the park shuts to visitors on heavy monsoon days.

spots.name: Kabini Backwater Boat Safari
spots.note: Flat boat along the reservoir edge in the afternoon; best odds on elephant herds in March to May, book it through your lodge.

spots.name: Kabini Dam
spots.note: Beechanahalli dam that floods the grassland the herds graze each summer; short drive for the reservoir view, no access on the wall.

name: Kalaburagi (Gulbarga)
tagline: Bahmani fort mosque and the Bande Nawaz dargah

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the only easy time: 28 °C, dry, and the fort's fully covered Jama Masjid cool enough to sit in.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is one of the hottest corners of Karnataka at 43 °C; the fort is bare rock with no shade anywhere.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep gets patchy Deccan rain and stays near 32 °C, muggy but workable, with the dargah busy all year.
why.autumn: October is still hot at 34 °C; wait for November, when the Haft Gumbaz tombs sit well in the low light.

vibe: A working Deccan city with no traveller scene; business hotels near the station and a permanent dargah crowd
hub: Kalaburagi airport 12 km, Star Air to Bengaluru only; railhead in town on the Mumbai-Chennai line

spots.name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah
spots.note: Sufi shrine that keeps the old city busy day and night; head covered and shoes off at the gate, the annual urs fills the lanes.

spots.name: Jama Masjid, Gulbarga Fort
spots.note: Bahmani mosque roofed right across with domed bays and no open courtyard; inside the moated fort, visit outside prayer times.

spots.name: Haft Gumbaz
spots.note: Seven Bahmani royal tombs in a walled compound east of the city; the caretaker opens the doors, no ticket, go before the heat.

spots.name: Sharana Basaveshwara Temple
spots.note: The city's own Lingayat shrine with a big tank beside it; the evening queue is steady, shoes come off well before the gate.

spots.name: Buddha Vihar
spots.note: Modern white vihara with four Sanchi style gateways on the city edge; free, open till evening, ten minutes by auto from the station.

spots.name: Ganagapur Dattatreya Temple
spots.note: Dattatreya shrine on the Bhima that draws people seeking cures; pilgrims bathe at the sangama first, buses run all day from town.

name: Karkala (Gomateshwara)
tagline: A 42 ft Bahubali on a rock hill and Jain basadis in the ghat foothills

why.winter: Nov-Feb is dry and about 30 C: the Bahubali rock at dawn, the Chaturmukha basadi late afternoon and empty laterite lanes between them.
why.summer: Mar-May turns sticky at 35 C with coastal humidity; climb the rock before 8 am and sit out the middle of the day in a basadi.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the ghats behind the town take four metres of rain, the streets run red and the tanks fill; you get the monuments to yourself.
why.autumn: October dries out and November is the pick of the year: gold paddy in the fields and a clear line to Kudremukh from the top of Gomata Betta.

vibe: One main road of small hotels and Jain lodgings; most mornings you are the only person on the monolith hill
hub: Bus about 40 km from Udupi or 50 km from Mangaluru; nearest railhead Udupi on the Konkan line, 1h out

name: Karwar (Devbagh & Kurumgad)
tagline: Kali river mouth, island beaches and a naval town's coast

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: a flat sea, boats running to Devbagh and Kurumgad, and 31 °C days with little humidity.
why.summer: Mar-May is still swimmable but the town sits at 34 °C and estuary haze kills the Sahyadri view behind it.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the boat operators shut down, the Kali runs brown into a red-flag sea, and the beaches are off limits.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings back the boats and the clearest water of the year, with Gokarna's crowds still 60 km away.

vibe: Quiet naval town, not a backpacker scene; a few beach camps out on Devbagh and cheap lodges back in town
hub: Karwar station on the Konkan line; Dabolim airport 100 km north, Gokarna 60 km south by bus

spots.name: Rabindranath Tagore Beach
spots.note: Town beach where Tagore stayed in 1882, lit and busy every evening; swimming is poor, come for the walk and the fried fish stalls.

spots.name: Warship Museum INS Chapal
spots.note: A decommissioned missile boat hauled up on the beach and opened inside; small ticket, hot by midday, an hour covers it.

spots.name: Sadashivgad Fort
spots.note: Ruined hill fort with a Durga temple above the Kali river bridge; ten minute climb, the estuary at sunset is the reason to go.

spots.name: Tilmati Beach
spots.note: Cove of dark sesame coloured sand south of town under the naval road; no shade or shops, access is closed off at times, ask first.

name: Kemmangundi
tagline: Raj-era garden hill station with the Z Point cliff walk and Hebbe Falls

why.winter: Dec-Feb is crisp at 1,400 m: gardens in bloom, Z Point sunrises over a cloud sea and shared jeeps running out to Hebbe Falls.
why.summer: March is fine, Apr-May warm and hazy; Hebbe thins to a stream but the ridge stays far cooler than the plains below.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the ghat road up turns slippery and landslide-prone, mist erases Z Point and the Hebbe jeep track closes when flooded.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the reward: falls at full flow, gardens rinsed green and clear mornings before the December weekend rush.

vibe: Horticulture department guesthouses and a few Kalhatti homestays; weekend families, almost no backpackers.
hub: Tarikere railhead 35 km, then taxi up the ghat; Chikmagalur 55 km via Lingadahalli, last stretch rough.

spots.name: Z Point
spots.note: Cliff nose about 30 minutes on foot from the guesthouses; go at first light, mist often closes the view later, no railing at the end.

spots.name: Hebbe Falls
spots.note: Two stage fall below the hill in coffee estate country; the last 8 km is jeep track only, then a short wade to the pool.

spots.name: Kalhatti Falls
spots.note: Water drops over the rock behind a Veerabhadra temple on the ghat road; steps up from the road, thin outside the monsoon.

spots.name: Kemmangundi Rose Garden
spots.note: Terraced horticulture garden below the guesthouses, laid out in the Raj era; small ticket, blooms November to February.

spots.name: Shanti Falls
spots.note: Small stream fall in the woods off the Z Point path; five minutes each way, a cool stop rather than a sight, rocks stay slippery.

spots.name: Amrutheshwara Temple
spots.note: Hoysala temple of 1196 at Amruthapura with a carved frieze right round the wall; 10 km past Tarikere, quiet, no ticket.

name: Kodachadri (Kollur base)
tagline: Sharp Western Ghats summit above the Mookambika forest
festival: Sep/Oct: Mookambika Navaratri at Kollur

why.winter: Dec-Feb gives dry grass slopes, a clear Arabian Sea line from the summit and genuinely cold nights up top.
why.summer: Mar-May the trail is dust at 34 °C down at the base, and haze usually erases the coastline view you climbed for.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Hidlumane falls route is a leech-covered scramble under 5,000 mm of rain and the summit jeeps stop.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the reward: grass at its greenest, streams still flowing, and Navaratri filling Kollur down below.

vibe: Weekend trek groups out of Bengaluru; basic rooms at Bhattara Mane near the top, proper hotels in Kollur
hub: Kollur is the base for jeeps and beds, buses from Udupi 80 km; forest check post permit before the climb

spots.name: Mookambika Temple
spots.note: The Kollur temple the whole base town serves; queues start before dawn, dress code is enforced, free meals at noon and night.

spots.name: Sarvajna Peetha
spots.note: Small stone mandapa on the summit where Shankara is said to have sat; sunrise above the cloud line, no shelter from the wind.

spots.name: Hidlumane Falls
spots.note: Stepped fall on the old walking route up from Nittur; a rock scramble beside the water, slippery in monsoon, leeches after rain.

spots.name: Chitramoola Cave
spots.note: Cave in the cliff below the summit reached by a rough scramble; take someone from Bhattara Mane who knows it, skip it in the wet.

spots.name: Souparnika River
spots.note: Pilgrims bathe here before Mookambika darshan; steps at the Kollur ghat, shallow and clear in winter, busiest at dawn.

name: Kokkare Bellur
tagline: Village where pelicans nest in the trees above the houses

why.winter: Dec-Feb the colony is full: spot-billed pelicans and painted storks on nests over the street, and villagers who count the mess as luck.
why.summer: March and April are the loudest weeks, fledglings on every branch; by May the trees empty and the Deccan sun gets to 36 C.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the birds have gone and this is simply a farming village; there is nothing to come for until they drift back in October.
why.autumn: October brings the first pelicans back to last year's nests; November is cool and quiet, good for watching them rebuild without a crowd.

vibe: One street of tiled houses under nesting trees, a community homestay and a village volunteer who walks you round
hub: On the Bengaluru to Mysuru line: train or bus to Maddur, then 12 km by auto into the village

name: Kudremukh
tagline: Horse-face peak above rolling grass ridges of Kudremukh National Park

why.winter: Dec-Jan is prime trekking: dry trail, cold Mullodi mornings, and the 1,894 m summit line clear before the haze builds.
why.summer: March still works at a push; Apr-May the shola grass goes brown, streams shrink and heat haze flattens the famous ridge views.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the forest office often suspends permits: swollen stream crossings, relentless leeches, zero-view mist; Sept reopens green.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the classic window: meadows at their greenest, trailside streams still alive and washed post-rain skies.

vibe: Mullodi homestays feed trekkers at one long table; weekend groups from Bengaluru, near silence midweek.
hub: Overnight bus Bengaluru to Kalasa, then jeep up the rough track to Mullodi; trek permits are online-only now

spots.name: Hanuman Gundi Falls
spots.note: Forest fall off the Karkala road inside the park, roughly 400 steps down to the pool; ticket at the gate, shut in heavy monsoon.

spots.name: Kadambi Falls
spots.note: Roadside fall on the Kalasa to Karkala highway, seen from the bend with no walk; full in monsoon, a trickle by February.

spots.name: Lakya Dam
spots.note: Tailings dam left by the closed iron ore mine, still water under bare red slopes; you pass a forest check post, nothing to buy there.

spots.name: Kalaseshwara Temple
spots.note: Old Shiva temple above the Bhadra at Kalasa, the town every trek here starts from; tirthas on the rock below, open dawn to dusk.

spots.name: Horanadu Annapoorneshwari Temple
spots.note: Temple that feeds every visitor free at noon and night; queues run long on weekends, shoulders and knees covered inside.

spots.name: Kurinjal Peak
spots.note: Grass ridge trek from Bhagavathi Nature Camp, about 5 hours return; online permit only, a guide is compulsory, start by 7 am.

name: Kukke Subramanya (Kumara Parvatha)
tagline: Serpent temple at the foot of the Kumara Parvatha climb
festival: Nov/Dec: Champa Shashti car festival at the temple

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the trek window: about 20 C in the village before dawn, near 12 C on the ridge at Mantapa, and the longest darshan queues around Shashti.
why.summer: Mar-May the climb is open and dry but every stream on the ridge fails, so carry four litres and be past Bhattara Mane by 9 am.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the forest department shuts the Kumara Parvatha gate, leeches own the trail and the Ghat rain barely stops. Temple only.
why.autumn: The gate reopens in October onto green grass ridges and full streams; November gives the cleanest views of the whole year.

vibe: Pilgrim lodges and homestays along one street, trekkers filling up on rice plates before a 4 am start
hub: Train to Subrahmanya Road on the Mangaluru ghat line, 8 km out, then an auto; buses from Mangaluru take 3h

name: Lakkundi (Gadag)
tagline: Fifty Chalukyan temples and stepwells in one village

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the season: 28 °C, dry, and enough soft low light to make the Kashivishvanatha carving readable.
why.summer: Apr-Jun hits 41 °C on the open Deccan and the village has no cafe, no shade and no reason to be there.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is mild here, under 700 mm for the year, and the stepwells actually hold water for once.
why.autumn: October is warm but manageable; November is ideal, and pairs with Gadag's Trikuteshwara temple 12 km away.

vibe: No stay in the village itself; sleep in Gadag or Hubballi and come out by bus or auto for a half day
hub: Gadag railhead 12 km, Hubballi airport 70 km; frequent buses and autos from Gadag bus stand

spots.name: Kasivisvesvara Temple
spots.note: The best carved of Lakkundi's temples, its shrine facing a small Surya shrine; ASI site, sunrise to sunset, free

spots.name: Brahma Jinalaya
