spots.note: The village's largest Jain basadi, built about 1007 by Attimabbe; ask the ASI man to open the dark inner shrine

spots.name: Manikesvara Temple and Musukina Bavi
spots.note: Temple beside a roofed stepwell, one of the many bavis here; mid morning is when light reaches down the steps

spots.name: Lakkundi Archaeological Museum
spots.note: One room of Chalukyan sculpture and hero stones gathered from the fields; closed Fridays, ticket a few rupees

spots.name: Trikuteshwara Temple, Gadag
spots.note: Gadag's Chalukyan complex, with lathe turned pillars in the Saraswati shrine; 20 minutes by auto from Lakkundi

name: Madhugiri
tagline: Rock-cut stairs up a monolith fort with seven gateways

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the climb: cool rock, seven gateways to the summit in about ninety minutes and a clear line of hills back towards Nandi.
why.summer: Apr-May the bare rock is at 38 C by ten in the morning; go up at six with two litres and be down before the granite starts radiating.
why.monsoon: This is dry Tumakuru country, so Jun-Sep means passing showers rather than washouts; the rock is slick when wet but the scrub greens up.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the sweetest window, clean air after the late rains and the whole fort staircase to yourself on any weekday.

vibe: A market town with basic lodges and no tourism at all; climb at dawn, then idlis at the bus stand afterwards
hub: Bus from Bengaluru in 3h or Tumakuru in 1h15; nearest railhead Tumakuru, 45 km, then a town auto to the fort gate

name: Maravanthe
tagline: NH-66 ribbon with surf on one side, the Souparnika river on the other

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: calm sea, empty sand past the highway pull-off and sunsets that light water on both sides of the road.
why.summer: Mar-May turns humid at 34 °C and hazy by noon, but the sea stays swimmable and beach resort rates drop before the rains.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the surf eats the beach, red flags go up and spray blows across the highway; a dramatic drive, a pointless stay.
why.autumn: October reopens the beach with the Souparnika backwater green and full; by November the settled blue-sky sea is back.

vibe: Sunset selfie traffic on the highway shoulder, then quiet; a couple of beach resorts at Trasi, homestays in Kundapura.
hub: Kundapura railhead 15 km on the Konkan line; Udupi-Bhatkal buses stop at Maravanthe, Mangaluru airport 100 km.

spots.name: Kodi Beach
spots.note: Sandspit at Kundapura where the Panchagangavali turns into the sea; the ferry to Gangolli crosses the river mouth

spots.name: Anegudde Vinayaka Temple
spots.note: Hill Ganapati temple at Kumbashi, one of the seven mukti sthalas; free prasada lunch served around 1 pm

spots.name: Gangolli Fishing Harbour
spots.note: Trawler port at the river mouth, the catch landed early morning; the ferry to Kodi leaves from the same jetty

spots.name: Hattiangadi Siddhi Vinayaka Temple
spots.note: Old Ganapati temple on the Varahi river near Kundapura, empty on weekdays; morning puja is over by 12.30

spots.name: Trasi Beach
spots.note: The quieter end of the same sand, where the resorts sit; no lifeguards and a hard undertow, so wade only

name: Maski
tagline: The rock edict where Ashoka was first named in stone

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the time to climb Durgada-gudda: 29 C, clean low light on the Brahmi letters and dry granite underfoot.
why.summer: Apr-Jun hits 44 C on bare rock and the edict shelter throws no shade; locals do not go up before six in the evening.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the scrub greens up and the Maski river runs, but the granite slabs turn slick and the light goes flat.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is easy walking weather, fields still green, and the Neolithic ground around the hill worth an extra hour.

vibe: A working market town with no tourists and no hotel worth the name; ride out from Raichur or Sindhanur for the day
hub: Raichur railhead 80 km; buses on the Kalaburagi-Bengaluru road, the edict hill is a walk from the bus stand

spots.name: Maski Ashokan Rock Edict
spots.note: Minor edict cut into granite, the first stone to name Ashoka himself; caged shelter, ten minutes up from town

spots.name: Durgada Gudda
spots.note: The boulder hill the edict sits on, old wall lines near the top and the whole town below; climb before 8 am

spots.name: Jaladurga
spots.note: Ruined fort on a rock island in the Krishna, boatmen take you across; a long half day by road via Lingsugur

name: Melukote
tagline: Hilltop Vaishnava town of stepped tanks and Ramanuja
festival: Mar/Apr: Vairamudi Brahmotsava

why.winter: Dec-Feb is ideal: 27 °C, clean light on the Kalyani tanks, and the hill temple climb comfortable at any hour.
why.summer: Apr-May is 36 °C on bare rock with almost no shade between the two temples; only Vairamudi justifies the heat.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is light rain rather than a washout here, greenish and very quiet, though the rock steps get slippery.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the other good stretch: warm, dry, harvest colour on the plateau and no crowd beyond local pilgrims.

vibe: A working temple town rather than a tourist one; a couple of basic lodges, and most people come out from Mysuru
hub: Mysuru railhead 50 km or Mandya railhead 35 km, then frequent KSRTC buses up the hill

spots.name: Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple
spots.note: The town's Vaishnava temple, Ramanuja's own seat; it shuts about 1 pm and reopens near 5, so plan around that

spots.name: Yoganarasimha Temple
spots.note: Hilltop shrine reached by a few hundred steps full of monkeys; best air and light in the hour after sunrise

spots.name: Raya Gopura
spots.note: Unfinished stone gateway standing alone on the ridge, the sunset spot; last stretch is a walk over bare rock

spots.name: Kalyani (stepped tank)
spots.note: Deep stepped tank below the temple that film crews keep using; the lower steps stay green and slippery

spots.name: Thonnur Lake
spots.note: Big old tank ringed by rock hills, birds on it at dawn; half an hour by bus down the hill, no food stalls

name: Mudgal
tagline: Moated frontier fort the Bahmanis and Vijayanagara fought over

why.winter: Dec-Feb runs about 30 C by day and cold at dawn; the moat still holds water and you can walk the full rampart circuit.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the doab is a furnace at 43-45 C with no shade anywhere on the bastions and the moat dries to cracked mud.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep brings modest rain and green thorn scrub over the walls, but the citadel steps get slick and nobody is around.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the pick: tanks full, black soil green, and Lingsugur buses running through the day in decent light.

vibe: You will likely be the only visitor; there is no hotel in Mudgal, so this is a day out from Raichur or Lingsugur
hub: Raichur railhead 100 km; bus to Lingsugur, then 20 km local bus into Mudgal; go early and return the same day

spots.name: Mudgal Fort
spots.note: Moated frontier fort with double walls and gate bends still standing; no ticket, no guide, carry your water

spots.name: Jaladurga
spots.note: Fort on a rock island in the Krishna beyond Lingsugur, crossed by boat; start early, it fills the whole day

name: Murudeshwar
tagline: Giant Shiva on a headland and scuba boats to Netrani
festival: Feb/Mar: Maha Shivaratri

why.winter: Dec-Jan is peak: 15-20 m visibility out at Netrani, calm boats, and the statue lit up over an empty beach at dusk.
why.summer: Mar-May the sea stays diveable into early May, but the headland is 34 °C and the town has almost no shade.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep every Netrani boat stops, the beach is closed to swimmers and the temple town shrinks back to its bus stand.
why.autumn: October reopens the dive season once the swell drops, but visibility only settles properly by late November.

vibe: A pilgrim town more than a beach scene; budget hotels by the temple, dive shops the only other travellers
hub: Murdeshwar station on the Konkan line, temple 2 km; Gokarna 60 km north, Udupi 100 km south

spots.name: Murudeshwar Beach
spots.note: Grey sand under the statue with fishing boats at one end; the shelf drops away fast, so stay near the shore

spots.name: Netrani Island
spots.note: Heart shaped rock 19 km offshore, the clearest diving on this coast; boats run October to May, book a day ahead

spots.name: Idagunji Mahaganapati Temple
spots.note: Busy Ganapati shrine inland from Honnavar; the queue is shortest before 9 am, share autos run from Honnavar

spots.name: Apsarakonda Falls
spots.note: Short falls into a pool with a cliff viewpoint over the sea just below; only worth it once the rains start

spots.name: Chandranatha Basadi, Bhatkal
spots.note: Jain basadi from Bhatkal's port years with a tall manasthambha; the old stone mosques are the same walk

spots.name: Sharavathi backwaters, Honnavar
spots.note: Mangrove creeks where the Sharavathi meets the sea; boatmen wait at the Honnavar jetty, go on a rising tide

name: Mysuru
tagline: Palace city that peaks during Dasara in October
festival: Oct: Mysuru Dasara - ten days of processions and palace illumination

why.winter: Cool and clear, palace lit up nightly, Dasara processions if dates align in October.
why.summer: Dry heat climbs to 36-38C by April-May; sightseeing is fine but midday is rough.
why.monsoon: A rain-shadow pocket keeps monsoon mild here - overcast, green, none of the coastal chaos.
why.autumn: Dasara runs through October - elephants, illuminated palace, huge crowds but unmissable.

vibe: Walkable heritage core with a small hostel scene and plenty of Bengaluru daytrippers.
hub: 3h train or bus from Bengaluru, frequent departures.

spots.name: Mysore Palace
spots.note: Amba Vilas, the Wodeyar seat; shoes off at the gate, and the whole facade is lit 7 to 7.45 pm on Sundays

spots.name: Chamundi Hill
spots.note: Chamundeshwari temple above the city, 1008 steps past the monolithic Nandi; city buses run up all day

spots.name: Devaraja Market
spots.note: Old covered rows of flowers, bananas and kumkum cones; go before 10 am and expect the first price to halve

spots.name: Srirangapatna
spots.note: Tipu's island capital: Ranganathaswamy temple, Daria Daulat and the Gumbaz; any Bengaluru bus drops you there

spots.name: Brindavan Gardens
spots.note: Terraced gardens below the KRS dam with a musical fountain at 7 pm; weekends are packed and buses back fill

spots.name: St Philomena's Cathedral
spots.note: Neo Gothic twin spires, one of the tallest churches in India; the crypt below is open and quiet after lunch

spots.name: Vinayaka Mylari
spots.note: Butter soft masale dose at a few tables on Nazarbad main road; mornings and evenings only, queue moves fast

name: Nandi Hills
tagline: Sunrise fort above the Bengaluru plain at 1478 metres

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the reason people come: 12 C at dawn, a cloud sea below the ramparts, and a long queue of cars behind you.
why.summer: Mar-May the hilltop stays maybe 8 C cooler than Bengaluru, but the plain below is hazy and the cloud sea does not form.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the hill sits inside the cloud rather than above it: green, cool, and some mornings you see fifty metres.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is quietly the best value, clear air after the rains and thinner weekday crowds than you get in December.

vibe: Sunrise crowds, cyclists grinding up the ghat, couples on the ramparts; a state-run hotel lets you sleep up top
hub: Chikkaballapur railhead 10 km below, autos up the ghat road; weekend vehicle quotas make a weekday far easier

spots.name: Tipu's Drop
spots.note: Cliff edge on the summit with a 600 m fall past the railing; be there before 6 am for the cloud sea below

spots.name: Bhoga Nandishwara Temple
spots.note: Ninth century temple at the foot of the hill with a stone Kalyani tank; opens 6 am and stays far quieter

spots.name: Yoga Nandeeshwara Temple
spots.note: Small Shiva shrine inside the summit fort walls, cool and shaded; two minutes on foot from the top car park

spots.name: Amrutha Sarovara
spots.note: Spring fed tank on the summit that never dries out; the path around it is the only quiet corner up top

spots.name: Skandagiri
spots.note: Night climb to a ruined fort for sunrise over cloud; forest department permits and a guide are now compulsory

spots.name: Visvesvaraya Museum, Muddenahalli
spots.note: The engineer's birth house and his notebooks and medals, below the ghat road; small fee, half an hour is enough

name: Ramanagara (Ramadevarabetta)
tagline: Sholay granite domes and the first vulture sanctuary in India

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the climbing season: 27 C, dry granite, and the best odds of a long-billed vulture off the cliff face.
why.summer: Apr-May the rock is over 40 C by nine and the stepped climb up Ramadevarabetta is punishing after mid-morning.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep rain here is patchy, but lichen makes the domes greasy, so it turns into a walking and birdwatching trip.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is clear and green after the rains, and the morning silk cocoon market is worth an hour before you climb.

vibe: Bengaluru boulderers at weekends, temple walkers on the hill, empty midweek; plain lodges in town if you stay
hub: Ramanagara railhead on the Bengaluru-Mysuru line 50 km out; autos 5 km to the Ramadevarabetta gate

spots.name: Government Silk Cocoon Market
spots.note: Sacks of yellow cocoons weighed and auctioned, the biggest such market in Asia; trading is done by noon, free

spots.name: Janapada Loka
spots.note: Folk museum of masks, leather puppets and Yakshagana costume on the Mysuru road; allow two hours, small fee

spots.name: Savandurga
spots.note: One of Asia's largest monoliths, two hours up bare rock from the temple at the base; no shade, start by 7 am

spots.name: Revanasiddeshwara Betta
spots.note: Boulder hill with a cave shrine on top, steps most of the way; monkeys take anything left unzipped

spots.name: Kanva Reservoir
spots.note: Quiet backwater under the granite hills, good for birds and an hour of nothing; no boats, no food, carry lunch

name: Sakleshpur
tagline: Estate-trekking base for the Bisle Ghat viewpoint

why.winter: Cool and green from the tailing monsoon - best window for Bisle Ghat and estate trails.
why.summer: Warming up but shaded by estate canopy; waterfalls are thin this time of year.
why.monsoon: The famous abandoned-railway 'Green Route' trek turns lethal here - landslides, floods, leeches.
why.autumn: October-November: waterfalls full, mist over the ghats, comfortably cool - the best month.

vibe: Weekend trekking crowd from Bengaluru and estate homestays - decent for meeting people.
hub: 4-5h drive from Bengaluru, or overnight train to Sakleshpur Jn.

spots.name: Manjarabad Fort
spots.note: Tipu's star shaped fort on the ridge at Donigal, a ten minute climb off NH 75; small ticket, clear days best

spots.name: Bisle Ghat Viewpoint
spots.note: Balcony over the Pushpagiri forest and the Kumara Parvatha ridge; mist swallows it by 11 am in the monsoon

spots.name: Sakleshwara Temple
spots.note: The town's namesake Shiva temple in the old bazaar lanes; five minutes from the bus stand, busiest on Mondays

spots.name: Kadamane Tea Estate
spots.note: Steep tea rows high on the Bisle road with the ghat falling away below; ask at the estate office before wandering

spots.name: Manjehalli Waterfalls
spots.note: Wide falls down an estate track east of town, full only after the rains; the last stretch is a walk in slush

name: Sandur (Kumaraswamy Temple)
tagline: Green valley in ore country under a Chalukyan hill temple

why.winter: Nov-Feb the valley is 15 C at dawn: the Kumaraswamy temple up in the hills, Lambani embroidery workshops in town and no other visitors.
why.summer: Apr-May Ballari district is an oven at 42 C with hot wind off the ore roads and no shade in the hills. Nothing here is worth that.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Sandur hills actually turn green and the Narihalla fills, but ore trucks churn the wet ghat road into red slurry.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the pick: green ridges, clear evenings and the hill road up to the temple free of dust for a few weeks.

vibe: A quiet former princely town with two lodges and a crafts centre; evenings amount to the bus stand and a dosa
hub: Train to Toranagallu or Ballari, then a 25 to 40 km bus into the valley; Hosapete and Hampi are 40 km north

name: Sannati & Kanaganahalli
tagline: Buddhist maha stupa with a stone relief labelled Raya Asoko

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: 30 C, the black-soil track in stays firm and a caretaker is usually there to open the shed.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the Kalaburagi plain runs 43-45 C with zero shade over the stupa mound and the Bhima shrinks back to sand.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the Bhima runs high and the last few km of black-cotton road turn to grease, so skip it after heavy rain.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the easiest run out from Kalaburagi, green fields all the way and the Chandralamba ghat busy at dusk.

vibe: Farmers, an ASI caretaker and nobody else; sleep in Kalaburagi, because there is nothing to book at Sannati
hub: Kalaburagi railhead 65 km, bus to Chitapur then a share auto; from Raichur about 3 h by road via Shahabad

spots.name: Chandralamba Parameshwari Temple
spots.note: Working Shakti temple by the Bhima, where Ashokan edict slabs turned up reused as temple stone; open early

spots.name: Kanaganahalli Maha Stupa
spots.note: Excavated stupa drum with the panel labelled Raya Asoko; the ASI caretaker holds the key, so arrive before 4 pm

spots.name: Malkhed Fort
spots.note: Manyakheta, the Rashtrakuta capital, crumbling walls above the Kagina and a Jain math in the village below

name: Sasihitlu Beach
tagline: Sandbar where two rivers meet the sea, Karnataka's surf beach

why.winter: Dec-Feb has the cleanest, flattest water of the year: gentle beginner surf, warm evenings and a sandbar you can walk right around.
why.summer: Mar-May is humid at 34 C with a sea like bathwater; May brings the first real swell and the pre-monsoon contests down at Mulki.
why.monsoon: Jun-Jul the Shambhavi comes down brown and fast, rips run at the mouth and lessons stop; late Aug and Sep clean up for surfers who know how.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the rain quits, the river runs clear again and the beach empties; the best weeks of the year to learn without an audience.

vibe: A fishing hamlet, a surf school with dorm beds and one tea shack; sunset on the sandbar with maybe ten other people
hub: Train to Mulki on the Konkan line, then 6 km by auto; Mangaluru airport is 25 km down the coast road

name: Shivanasamudra Falls
tagline: Twin Kaveri cataracts in full thunder after the rains

why.winter: Dec-Jan carries decent leftover flow with easy 28 °C weather; by February the curtains narrow to ribbons on the rock face.
why.summer: Mar-May is a trickle over bare basalt at 36 °C on the open Deccan; not worth the drive unless the dams release upstream.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is the spectacle: Gaganachukki becomes a churning wall of whitewater and the viewing rails pack out on weekends.
why.autumn: October is the sweet spot, full falls and washed air; November stays good, and coracles start running below Bharachukki.

vibe: Weekend day-trippers from Bengaluru and Mysuru at the railings; sleep in Malavalli or a farmstay, not at the falls.
hub: Buses from Mysuru 75 km or Bengaluru 130 km to Malavalli, then a local bus or auto 15 km to the viewpoints.

spots.name: Barachukki Falls
spots.note: The eastern cataract, steps down to the spray and coracles when the flow drops; 20 minutes round by road

spots.name: Talakadu
spots.note: Shiva temples dug out of the Kaveri sand dunes, walked barefoot; go early or after 4 pm, the sand burns

spots.name: Chennakeshava Temple, Somanathapura
spots.note: The most complete of the three Hoysala star plan temples; ASI ticket, gates shut 5.30 pm, no puja inside

spots.name: Dargah Hazrat Mardane Ghaib
spots.note: Cliff top dargah beside the Gaganachukki gorge with the falls roaring below; shoes off and heads covered

spots.name: Shivanasamudra Power House
spots.note: Asia's first hydroelectric station, generating since 1902; a working plant, so you see it from the road only

spots.name: Bheemeshwari
spots.note: Kaveri camp in the Cauvery sanctuary, coracles, otters and river birds; day entry needs a call ahead

name: Sirsi & Sahasralinga
tagline: Malnad temple town with lingas carved into a river bed

why.winter: Dec-Jan is dry and cool at 600 m, with the Shalmala river low enough to walk out over the carved lingas.
why.summer: Mar-May the river bed is bare rock at 35 °C and Unchalli falls thins out; the temple town is all that is left.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the Shalmala buries the carvings completely and the Unchalli approach path is closed by mud and leeches.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the pick: Unchalli and Burude falls at full roar, arecanut harvest under way, the lingas re-emerging.

vibe: An ordinary Malnad market town with cheap lodges; the biennial Marikamba jatra is the one genuinely busy time
hub: Hubballi airport 110 km, Kumta railhead 60 km; frequent buses from Hubballi and Karwar

spots.name: Sri Marikamba Temple
spots.note: Sirsi's 1688 goddess temple with a huge painted wooden ratha; the jatra fills the town for nine days every second year.

spots.name: Madhukeshwara Temple, Banavasi
spots.note: The Kadamba capital's old Shiva temple with a carved stone cot and lathe-turned pillars; buses run via the Siddapur road.

spots.name: Unchalli Falls (Lushington Falls)
spots.note: The Aghanashini drops into deep forest here; about 1 km of steps down from the car park, and it is loudest after the rains.

spots.name: Sonda Vadiraja Mutt
spots.note: Madhva monastery at Swadi with Vadiraja's brindavana and its tiger legend; a free midday meal is served, dress modestly.

spots.name: Shivaganga Falls
spots.note: A broad sheet of water falling into a pool near Sonda; short slippery walk down, and it thins right out by February.

name: Sringeri
tagline: Adi Shankara's first matha on a fish-filled bend of the Tunga
festival: Sep/Oct: Sharada Sharannavaratri at the matha

why.winter: Dec-Feb is ideal: cool riverside mornings, soft light on the Vidyashankara temple's zodiac pillars, Sirimane Falls 12 km away.
why.summer: Mar-May is humid Malnad heat around 34 °C; darshan queues stay short and the ghat by the Tunga is still pleasant early.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep brings roughly 4,000 mm of rain: the Tunga runs brown and fast, umbrellas barely cope, but the matha rhythm never stops.
why.autumn: October is lush and quiet after the rains, and Sharannavaratri (late Sep or Oct) fills the temple town with music.

vibe: Pilgrims and Sanskrit students rather than tourists; matha guest blocks take solo travellers, lodges line the bazaar.
hub: Buses from Chikmagalur (2.5 h), Mangaluru (4 h) and Udupi over the Agumbe ghat; no useful railhead nearby.

spots.name: Sri Sharadamba Temple
spots.note: The matha's main shrine with a Sanskrit school around it; darshan pauses over midday and phones stay outside.

spots.name: Vidyashankara Temple
spots.note: 14th century temple in the same courtyard, 12 zodiac pillars lit by the sun month by month; ask a priest to show you.

spots.name: Tunga Hanging Bridge
spots.note: Footbridge below the matha where protected mahseer shoal for puffed rice sold on the bank; free, busiest after evening puja.

spots.name: Sirimane Falls
spots.note: Stepped falls in coffee country past Kigga, shallow enough to stand under; small entry fee, fullest July to October.

spots.name: Rishyashringeshwara Temple, Kigga
spots.note: Village temple said to bring rain when the deity is bathed; quiet, 10 km uphill and easy on a hired scooter.

spots.name: Horanadu Annapoorneshwari Temple
spots.note: Temple that feeds every visitor free; lunch from about 12.30, and the bus takes 1.5 h through coffee ghats.

name: Udupi-Malpe & St Marys Island
tagline: Temple town beside a basalt-column island
festival: Jan: Paryaya, biennial handover festival at Krishna Matha

why.winter: Calm sea, boats to St Marys Island running smoothly - the best window by far.
why.summer: Hot and sticky by April-May, but boats to St Marys run right up to the monsoon - start early and be off the sand by noon.
why.monsoon: Boats to St Marys do not run Jun-Sep and the sea is rough - the island, which is the entire point of coming, is unreachable.
why.autumn: October: boats resume, sea calming, temple town far quieter than winter.

vibe: A pilgrim-and-daytrip crowd rather than backpackers, but easy enough to wander solo.
hub: Fly Mangalore, 1h to Udupi/Malpe; also on the Konkan Railway line.

spots.name: Sri Krishna Matha
spots.note: 13th century Madhva matha where Krishna is seen through the nine-holed Kanakana Kindi; free meals at the dining hall.

spots.name: Malpe Beach
spots.note: Town beach beside a working fishing harbour; the island boats leave from the jetty here and the last one is back by 5 pm.

spots.name: Mitra Samaj
spots.note: Old canteen on Car Street by the matha for goli baje and biscuit roti; snacks only, cash only, and a queue at teatime.

spots.name: End Point, Manipal
spots.note: Landscaped cliff edge above the Swarna river valley in Manipal, the student sunset spot; free, and autos back to Udupi are easy.

spots.name: Hasta Shilpa Heritage Village
spots.note: Coastal timber houses rescued and rebuilt on one campus in Manipal; guided entry only, closed Mondays, allow two hours.

spots.name: Kaup Beach and Lighthouse
spots.note: Rocky shore under a 1901 lighthouse you can climb for a few rupees; the tower opens late afternoon and the surf is rough.

name: Vijayapura (Bijapur)
tagline: Gol Gumbaz and the Adil Shahi capital of the Deccan

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the only comfortable season: 29 °C, dry, and the Gol Gumbaz whispering gallery quiet before 9 am.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is 42 °C on open stone with no shade in the Ibrahim Rauza gardens; genuinely dangerous by midday.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep gets modest Deccan rain, around 600 mm for the whole year, so it stays workable and the monuments empty.
why.autumn: October is still 34 °C but drying; from mid-November the light is superb and the city is at its most walkable.

vibe: Cheap lodges near the bus stand and autos that know every tomb; a serious monument city with no tourist gloss
hub: Vijayapura railhead in town, direct trains from Bengaluru, Solapur and Hubballi; Kalaburagi 160 km

spots.name: Gol Gumbaz
spots.note: Adil Shahi tomb under a 44 m dome; climb the stair turret to the whispering gallery before 9 am, later it is bedlam.

spots.name: Ibrahim Rauza
spots.note: Tomb and mosque sharing one plinth, the finer building of the two; late afternoon light picks out the stone tracery.

spots.name: Bara Kaman
spots.note: Twelve unfinished arches over Ali Adil Shah II's grave, roofless and open to the sky; free, and best in the last light.

spots.name: Jama Masjid
spots.note: Adil Shahi mosque with 2250 prayer squares marked on the floor; visit outside prayer times and cover your head.

spots.name: Malik-e-Maidan
spots.note: A 55 tonne bronze cannon on the Sherza Burj bastion, said to stay cool even at noon; free, five minutes off the ring road.

spots.name: Gagan Mahal
spots.note: Roofless ruin of the Adil Shahi durbar hall with one huge arch still standing; open ground, no ticket, quiet at dusk.

name: Yana Rocks
tagline: Two black karst monoliths in deep Uttara Kannada forest

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the clean window: dry steps up to the Bhairaveshwara monolith, no leeches, and cool forest walking.
why.summer: Mar-May the forest is dry at 35 °C, the stream at the base disappears, and the black rock radiates heat by noon.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the last 500 m of trail is leech country and the rock face runs wet; the forest road also washes out in spells.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the best of both: the forest still soaked green, the path drying out, and almost nobody on the steps.

vibe: No stay at the rocks themselves; sleep in Kumta or Sirsi, and expect pilgrims rather than trekkers on the path
hub: Kumta railhead 25 km or Sirsi 40 km, then a jeep; the last stretch is narrow forest road with sparse buses

spots.name: Vibhooti Falls
spots.note: Limestone-tiered falls in the same forest belt, about 1 km on foot from the road; only worth it in the monsoon months.

spots.name: Devimane Ghat View Point
spots.note: Hairpin lookout where the Malnad plateau falls away to the coastal plain; buses pull in for tea, mornings are clearest.

spots.name: Mirjan Fort
spots.note: Laterite fort on the Aghanashini with intact bastions and stepped wells; free, unshaded, and the gate shuts by evening.

name: Yellapur (Sathodi & Magod Falls)
tagline: Malnad forest town ringed by the Sathodi and Magod waterfalls

why.winter: Dec-Feb both falls still run on perennial rivers: January mornings are cold and clear and the forest tracks at their driest.
why.summer: Mar-Apr the flow thins as heat builds to 35 °C; Magod's gorge stays worth it, Sathodi barely; May is empty for a reason.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the streams across the Sathodi track run axle-deep and mist swallows Magod's gorge; wait for the rain to ease.
why.autumn: Sep-Nov is the show: Magod's two-step plunge of nearly 200 m in full force, Sathodi's curtain pounding its pool, roads passable again

vibe: Arecanut farmstays and plain town lodges; you share the falls with langurs and a few Karnataka road-trippers.
hub: Hubballi airport and railhead 70 km; buses from Sirsi and Hubballi, then hired jeep or scooter to the falls.

spots.name: Jenukallu Gudda
spots.note: Cliff platform over the Bedthi valley named for the honey collectors who climbed it; last stretch is rough, go early.

spots.name: Kavadikere
spots.note: The town lake with a walking path and a small park where Yellapur comes out at dusk; five minutes from the bus stand.

spots.name: Kavala Caves
spots.note: Limestone cave with a natural linga inside the tiger reserve; forest gate permission, a torch and a steep 1 km descent.

spots.name: Kodasalli Dam
spots.note: Kali river reservoir where boatmen run trips up the still backwater; ask at the dam gate, and there is no shade waiting.

name: Agasthyakoodam (Athirumala)
tagline: Kerala's permit-only peak, two days up through Agasthyavanam forest

why.winter: Jan-Feb is the only real window: the Bonacaud gate opens around mid January on a capped daily permit, the ridge is dry and Athirumala camp drops to 10 C.
why.summer: Early March closes the season, usually around the 10th; after that the gate shuts and the whole Agasthyavanam sanctuary is off limits to walkers.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the sanctuary is closed outright, the Karamana streams run chest deep and the Bonacaud road is a landslide track. Nothing to do here.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the gate stays shut through the second rains, so this is when you book the January slot online, not when you travel to it.

vibe: Forest tents and a dorm shed at Athirumala, no shop and no signal; you walk with a Kani guide and eat what the camp kitchen cooks
hub: Bus from Thiruvananthapuram to Vithura and on to the Bonacaud gate, about 2h, then 14 km on foot to Athirumala

name: Alleppey (Alappuzha) Backwaters
tagline: Venice of the East - houseboats through the backwaters
festival: Aug: Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race

why.winter: Peak season - calm water, cool evenings on the houseboat deck, book weeks ahead for holidays
why.summer: Hot and sticky (32-35C); houseboat naps under the AC are the only way through April-May
why.monsoon: June-July rain is relentless and humid; August's snake boat races light up the backwaters instead
why.autumn: October is gorgeous - lush paddy fields, comfortable temps, thinning crowds before winter rush

vibe: Houseboats cost more solo, but homestays and kayak tours make it easy to meet people
hub: Fly to Cochin, 1.5h taxi/bus to the Alleppey houseboat jetty

spots.name: Punnamada Kayal
spots.note: The wide lake where the Nehru Trophy snake boats race on the second Saturday of August; shikaras go out from the jetties.

spots.name: Alappuzha Beach
spots.note: Grey sand and a ruined iron pier walking out to sea; the beach road fills after 5 pm with fried fish and chai carts.

spots.name: Alappuzha Lighthouse
spots.note: Red and white 1862 tower behind the beach, climbable for a view over the coconut coast; afternoons only, small fee.

spots.name: Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple
spots.note: Known for its palpayasam, ladled to a queue each afternoon; men enter bare chested in a mundu and tokens run out early.

spots.name: Champakulam St Mary's Church
spots.note: One of Kerala's oldest Syrian Christian parishes, on the Pamba where the Moolam boat race starts; go by canal boat if you can.

spots.name: Karumadikuttan
spots.note: Black granite Buddha with its left side broken away, sitting beside a canal at Karumadi; free, and a five minute stop.

spots.name: Revi Karunakaran Museum
spots.note: A coir trader's house of Belgian glass, ivory and Tanjore paintings; guided rounds only, closed Mondays, about an hour.

name: Aranmula
tagline: Snake-boat village on the Pamba that still casts metal mirrors
festival: Aug/Sep: Aranmula Uthrattathi snake boat race

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry at 22-33°C: the Parthasarathy temple at dawn, the mirror workshops open to visitors and the Pamba low and clear.
why.summer: Mar-May pushes 36°C and the Pamba shrinks to sandbanks, leaving the metal-mirror and Vastuvidya workshops as the only reason to come.
why.monsoon: Rain is constant through June and July, but four days after Thiruvonam the Pamba carries dozens of snake boats and the village fills.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov brings north-east monsoon evenings; mornings stay clear, the paddy is green and there is nobody else around.

vibe: A working temple village of boat-club sheds and mirror-makers; homestays only here, hotels 10 km away in Chengannur
hub: Chengannur station 10 km on the main line, then an auto; Kochi airport 100 km, Trivandrum airport 110 km

spots.name: Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple
spots.note: Riverside Vishnu temple of the Uthrattathi snake boat race each Onam season; men enter bare chested in a mundu, no shorts.

spots.name: Aranmula Kannadi workshops
spots.note: Family sheds still casting the polished metal mirror by hand; even a small one runs to thousands, ask before filming.

spots.name: Parumala Church
spots.note: Orthodox church built around St Gregorios' tomb, busiest for the feast on 2 November; open all day, cover your shoulders.

spots.name: Thrikkakudi Cave Temple, Kaviyoor
spots.note: Rock-cut Shiva shrine with carved guardian figures on a low hill; a short climb, usually empty, and no ticket.

spots.name: Chengannur Mahadeva Temple
spots.note: Round-roofed Shiva and Parvati temple known for the Thriputharattu ritual; near the station, shut in the middle of the day.

name: Athirappilly Falls
tagline: An 80ft waterfall curtain at its thundering best in monsoon

why.winter: Dec-Jan the falls still run decently with cooler trekking weather, but well past monsoon peak
why.summer: Skip if the waterfall is the point - by April-May it's reduced to a thin trickle over bare rock
why.monsoon: This is peak season here - the falls roar at full width; stick to viewing platforms, rocks are lethal
why.autumn: October-November still has strong flow with clearer skies than the monsoon months

vibe: Mostly a day-trip crowd of families and photographers; better as a stop than a base
hub: Fly to Cochin, 1.5-2h taxi/bus into the Sholayar forest range

spots.name: Vazhachal Falls
spots.note: Wide rapids on the same river 5 km up the road, calmer and less crowded; a separate ticket, and the forest starts here.

spots.name: Charpa Falls
spots.note: Cascade that pours across the road between the two big falls; alive only in the monsoon, and the tarmac stays slick.

spots.name: Thumboormuzhi Dam
spots.note: Garden and hanging bridge over the Chalakudy river with a butterfly park; small fee, shuts around 5 pm, good picnic stop.

spots.name: Sholayar Dam
spots.note: Reservoir up the Malakkappara road with forest on every side; the roadside view is open, the dam itself needs permission.

spots.name: Ezhattumugham
spots.note: Sandbanked stretch of the Chalakudy where streams meet, shallow enough to wade; local families fill it on Sunday afternoons.

name: Bekal
tagline: A fort above a quiet, uncrowded north Kerala coastline

why.winter: Peak season - cool sea breeze off the ramparts, calm water, far fewer tourists than the southern beaches
why.summer: Hot and humid; the fort's laterite walls give little shade so midday visits get rough by April-May
why.monsoon: Rough Arabian Sea swell and heavy rain batter the coast; the fort stays open but beach time is a write-off
why.autumn: October is decent once the monsoon tail ends, and November onward is genuinely pleasant

vibe: Sleepy and uncrowded - the ramparts to yourself, but little backpacker scene
hub: Nearest airport Mangalore; or train to Kanhangad, taxi to fort

spots.name: Bekal Fort
spots.note: Kerala's largest fort, a laterite keyhole on the sea with an observation tower over the surf; 8 am to 5.30 pm, small ticket.

spots.name: Kappil Beach
spots.note: Empty sand under the Kodi cliff looking back at the fort; no shacks or lifeguards, so carry water and watch the current.

spots.name: Chandragiri Fort
spots.note: Ikkeri-era ruin on a bluff where the Chandragiri river meets the sea; free, best at sunset, boats run below the walls.

spots.name: Ananthapura Lake Temple
spots.note: Kerala's only temple set in the middle of a lake, reached by a causeway; morning darshan, and it closes over midday.

spots.name: Madhur Temple
spots.note: Gabled Ganesha temple above the Madhuvahini river, copper roof and carved wood; no photography once you are inside.

name: Beypore
tagline: Estuary port where Kerala still hand builds wooden dhows

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the run: 30 C, a flat evening sea, the uru yard working all day and the 2 km rubble jetty walkable to its far end at sunset.
why.summer: Mar-May sit muggy at 34 C with a breeze only after 5 pm; the shipwrights stop by early afternoon, so see the yard in the morning.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Arabian Sea comes in hard and the jetty is closed off, Chaliyar boat rides stop until late September, but the uru yard works under its sheds.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the sea settles and the estuary clears; the fishing harbour is at full noise before dawn and the light on the water is the year's best.

vibe: A few homestays by the estuary and cheap hotels 10 km up in Kozhikode; evenings are halwa, fish fry and the whole town on the jetty
hub: Kozhikode railhead 10 km by bus or auto, Karipur airport 30 km inland

name: Champakulam (Kuttanad)
tagline: Kuttanad canal village of snake boats and paddy below sea level
festival: Jun/Jul: Champakulam Moolam Vallamkali, the oldest snake boat race

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the dry window: 30 C days, a punt boat through the canals at dawn and paddy being cut a metre below sea level behind the bunds.
why.summer: Mar-May turn humid and the canals drop; the Thanneermukkom barrage holds the salt back, so the water still works if you go out before 8 am.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the fields flood, race crews train at dusk and the village smells of wet paddy; in a bad year Kuttanad goes under and the buses stop.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the fields drain, the light turns clean and canal traffic goes back to being purely local once the Onam race season is over.

vibe: Homestays on the bund and country boat families who take you out; evenings are toddy shops, church bells and no houseboat music
hub: Alappuzha 16 km by bus or about 2h on the state ferry up the Pamba, Kottayam railhead 30 km east

name: Fort Kochi
tagline: Colonial port town of fishing nets, spice lanes and art
festival: Dec: Kochi-Muziris Biennale (biennial art festival)

why.winter: Best months - cool enough for long heritage walks, cafes buzzing, biennale years draw an art crowd
why.summer: Hot and humid, worsening into May; fine for a short stop if you stick to early morning and evening walks
why.monsoon: Narrow lanes flood and harbour breeze turns to driving rain; atmospheric but many boat cruises pause
why.autumn: October-November is a sweet spot - monsoon clears, temperatures drop, not yet at winter-peak crowds

vibe: Compact and walkable with a steady cafe crowd - easy to chat at a heritage guesthouse
hub: Fly into Cochin International Airport, 45min taxi/bus to Fort Kochi

spots.name: Chinese Fishing Nets
spots.note: Cantilevered shore nets worked by teams along Vasco da Gama Square; watch a dip at dawn, and a tip is expected if you help.

spots.name: Mattancherry Palace
spots.note: Portuguese-built palace lined with Ramayana murals in vegetable dye; closed Fridays, no cameras, an hour is plenty.

spots.name: Paradesi Synagogue
spots.note: 1568 synagogue floored with hand-painted Cantonese tiles under glass lamps; shut Friday afternoon and Saturday, shoes off.

spots.name: St Francis Church
spots.note: Oldest European church in India, where Vasco da Gama lay buried until 1539; free, quiet, punkah cloths still hang overhead.

spots.name: Jew Town
spots.note: One lane of spice godowns turned antique shops and tea rooms behind the synagogue; haggle hard, and it is shut on Saturday.

spots.name: Santa Cruz Basilica
spots.note: Painted Indo-Gothic interior on a 16th century Portuguese foundation; open through the day and quiet between the masses.

spots.name: Cherai Beach
spots.note: Long shallow beach on Vypeen island with backwater on the other side of the road; ferry across, then a bus or scooter north.

name: Gavi
tagline: Cardamom-forest eco camp deep inside Periyar tiger country

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the window: cool lake mornings, hornbills and gaur on guided walks, clear ridgelines; KFDC beds sell out, book ahead.
why.summer: March-May is warm but shaded at 1,150 m; wildlife pulls in to the waterholes and plantation tracks stay walkable before the rains.
why.monsoon: June-Aug the reserve gets hammered: leeches on every trail, forest roads slither and the camp sits socked in cloud; wait it out.
why.autumn: Sep is still dripping; October turns lush and misty, the lake brims and midweek you can have the whole camp to yourself.

vibe: KFDC swiss tents and the Green Mansions lodge; a handful of guests, forest staff for company, elephants heard after dark
hub: Entry on a KFDC booking: jeep from Vandiperiyar (28 km) or the dawn Pathanamthitta-Kumily KSRTC bus

spots.name: Gavi Lake
spots.note: The camp's own reservoir; boating is part of the KFDC package and the shore at first light is where the herds come down.

spots.name: Kakki Reservoir
spots.note: Sabarigiri project dam ringed by cardamom forest on the Angamoozhy road; jeeps pull up at the view, no swimming allowed.

spots.name: Moozhiyar Dam
spots.note: Reservoir on the long descent to Angamoozhy with a powerhouse below; single track road, so time the drive against the jeeps.

name: Guruvayur
tagline: Kerala's busiest Krishna temple and its elephant yard
festival: Nov/Dec: Guruvayur Ekadasi

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry at 24-32°C and the wedding season peaks: queues form before dawn and the elephants stand at Punnathur Kotta.
why.summer: Mar-May is 35°C and airless, though the ten-day Utsavam in Feb-Mar is the last big draw before the heat properly sets in.
why.monsoon: June-Aug is heavy rain and the queue shuffles under dripping sheds; Chavakkad beach 4 km away is unswimmable anyway.
why.autumn: Oct still rains most afternoons; November turns dry and cool and builds towards Ekadasi, the temple's single biggest day.

vibe: Pure pilgrim town: dawn queues, brass-lamp shops, cheap devaswom lodges and a strict dress code, with no other scene
hub: Guruvayur has its own station off the Thrissur line; note that non-Hindus are not admitted inside the temple

spots.name: Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple
spots.note: The Krishna shrine the whole town exists for; nirmalyam darshan starts at 3 am, mundu or sari only, no phones, Hindus only.

spots.name: Punnathur Kotta
spots.note: Devaswom elephant yard inside a ruined chieftain's fort, dozens of temple elephants; small ticket at the gate, mornings are bath time.

spots.name: Mammiyoor Mahadeva Temple
spots.note: The Shiva temple pilgrims pair with Guruvayur; locals say the darshan is incomplete without it, five minutes on foot west.

spots.name: Palayur St Thomas Church
spots.note: One of the seven churches St Thomas is held to have founded in 52 AD; quiet on weekday mornings, small museum by the pond.

spots.name: Chavakkad Beach
spots.note: Where Guruvayur empties out at sunset, wide grey sand at the harbour mouth; no shacks, tea and fried fish come off carts.

spots.name: Thriprayar Sree Ramaswami Temple
spots.note: Old Rama temple on the Karuvannur river, first stop of the Nalambalam circuit; get there before 11 am, then it shuts.

spots.name: Snehatheeram Beach
spots.note: Groomed DTPC beach south along the coast road, casuarina shade and a boat park; entry ticket, packed on Sunday evenings.

name: Ilaveezhapoonchira
tagline: Treeless grass hills above Melukavu, climbed for sunrise and camping

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the whole point: 14 C at 4 am, a clear line along the Ghats and a few tents on the ridge waiting for the sun; February hazes up by late month.
why.summer: March keeps the dawn view before the haze thickens; Apr-May afternoons are hot and dusty on the bare tops, so come for the 6 pm light, not for noon.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the hills are green and sitting inside cloud, camping is suspended in heavy spells and the last 3 km of road turns slick and rutted.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov the rain stops, the grass is high, the three ponds are full and the sunrise finally clears. Book the tent early for a weekend.

vibe: Tents on the ridge and homestays at Melukavu; Kottayam students on weekends, silence midweek, and no shop past the last village
hub: Kottayam railhead 55 km, bus to Melukavu or Kadanad, then 6 km up by jeep or an hour on foot

name: Kakkayam
tagline: Mist-locked dam valley and waterfalls above Kozhikode

why.winter: Dec-Feb is calm and cool over a full reservoir, mist lifting off the water at dawn and easy walks out to the Urakkuzhi chute.
why.summer: March still works at dawn; April-May the valley turns hot and hazy at 730 m and the falls thin, wait for the monsoon to break.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the ghat road takes landslips and the forest gates shut in heavy rain; by September the valley reopens, wild and loud.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is prime: waterfalls at full throat, leeches receding, deep green ridges; weekends bring Kozhikode day-trip crowds.

vibe: Kozhikode day-trip country: rocky river at Kariyathumpara, tent camps and farm stays around Koorachundu if you linger
hub: 45 km from Kozhikode via Balussery; buses to Koorachundu, jeep onward; tickets at the forest checkpost

spots.name: Urakkuzhi Waterfalls
spots.note: Rock chute falls below the reservoir inside the sanctuary; forest ticket and a guide at the checkpost, gates shut by 5 pm.

spots.name: Kariyathumpara
spots.note: Flat rock riverbed on the Koorachundu road where the day trip stops to swim; lethal after rain, no shops past the turn off.

spots.name: Koorachundu
spots.note: Last village on the climb, arecanut and pepper farms, the homestays and the last shops; jeeps up to the dam start here.

spots.name: Peruvannamuzhi Dam
spots.note: Bigger reservoir down at Perambra with speedboats to a wooded islet and a crocodile farm; boating stops around 5 pm.

name: Kalpathy (Palakkad)
tagline: Four agraharam streets by a river, Kerala's first heritage village
festival: Nov: Kalpathy Ratholsavam, three wooden chariots pulled through the streets

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season for the agraharam rows: 21 C mornings, filter coffee at the corner shop and the Kalpathy river running low and clear under the weir.
why.summer: March warms fast and Apr-May push past 40 C through the Palakkad gap; the lanes empty between 11 am and 4 pm, so this is a dawn and dusk town.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the rain is heavy but the tiled roofs and deep verandahs were built for it; the river fills and the streets are at their greenest and quietest.
why.autumn: October cools things off and mid November brings Ratholsavam, when chariots too big for the lanes are hauled through them. Book a bed weeks ahead.

vibe: Heritage houses taking guests on the agraharam streets, temple mess meals, shutters down by 9 pm; town traffic stays 2 km away
hub: Palakkad Junction railhead 5 km by autorickshaw, Coimbatore airport 55 km east through the gap

name: Kannur
tagline: Theyyam heartland, Asia's longest drive-in beach
festival: Dec-Mar: Theyyam ritual season at village shrines

why.winter: Peak season - heart of Theyyam ritual season with trance performances most nights, plus calm beach weather
why.summer: Increasingly hot and humid, Theyyam season winding down by April-May, though the beach still works
why.monsoon: Heavy rain and rough surf shut down the drive-in beach; Theyyam performances pause almost entirely
why.autumn: October-November is when Theyyam season restarts - fewer tourists than winter but rituals already underway

vibe: Few backpackers make it this far north - you meet devotees and locals more than travellers
hub: Fly to Kannur airport or train to Kannur, auto/taxi to Muzhappilangad

spots.name: Muzhappilangad Drive-in Beach
spots.note: Four km of hard sand you can drive a car onto, the longest such beach in Asia; only at low tide, and not in the monsoon.

spots.name: Parassinikkadavu Sri Muthappan Temple
spots.note: The one temple where theyyam is performed every day, not just in season; the Muthappan ritual runs at dawn and again at dusk.

spots.name: St Angelo Fort
spots.note: Portuguese laterite fort of 1505 over the fishing bay; free, open till 6 pm, go late for the light on the Mappila Bay boats.

spots.name: Arakkal Museum
spots.note: The durbar wing of Kerala's only Muslim royal house, kept as it was left; closed Mondays, an hour is plenty.

spots.name: Payyambalam Beach
spots.note: The town's own evening beach, past the memorials of Kerala's leaders and a giant mother and child sculpture; wade only.

name: Kanthalloor
tagline: Rain-shadow orchard village of apples, dolmens and sandalwood

why.winter: Dec-Feb nights dip toward 5°C while days stay sunny: orange and strawberry season, and clear walks to the Muniyara dolmens.
why.summer: March-May stays mild at 1,500 m while the plains roast; the rain-shadow air stays dry and homestay porches catch a cool breeze.
why.monsoon: The rain shadow keeps Jun-Sep to drizzle while the rest of Kerala floods; apples ripen mid-monsoon and the valley glows green.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the sweet spot: washed skies, harvest stalls along the Marayoor road and cool nights before the December trickle.

vibe: Farm homestays amid apple, orange and garlic terraces; Malayali weekenders, few foreigners, early quiet nights
hub: Bus Munnar-Marayoor (40 km through sandal forest), then 12 km jeep or bus climb; Kochi airport is 5 h out

spots.name: Marayoor Muniyara Dolmens
spots.note: Megalithic granite burial chambers standing in the sugarcane fields, roughly 3000 years old; ask in Marayoor for the caretaker.

spots.name: Marayoor Sandalwood Forest
spots.note: India's only natural sandal reserve, guarded day and night; the forest office arranges the escorted walk, no entry alone.

spots.name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Thorn scrub rain shadow park on the Tamil Nadu road, grizzled giant squirrels; treks are booked at the checkpost, guide compulsory.

spots.name: Thoovanam Waterfalls
spots.note: Falls on the Pambar inside Chinnar, an hour's walk from Alampetty with a compulsory guide; thin by March, best after October.

spots.name: Vattavada
spots.note: Terraced vegetable and strawberry village over the ridge, the coldest nights in Kerala; the link road is rough, take a jeep.

name: Kovalam
tagline: Crescent lighthouse beach, Kerala's original resort town

why.winter: Peak season - calm sea, sunny days, Lighthouse and Eve's beach busy with a mixed domestic/foreign crowd
why.summer: Hot and humid; sea still swimmable in early March but conditions worsen through April-May
why.monsoon: Rough surf and strong rip currents make swimming genuinely dangerous on red-flag days; quieter and cheaper
why.autumn: October-November sees the sea calm back down while prices stay below peak-season rates

vibe: More resort-y than backpacker-dense, but promenade cafes are an easy spot to meet people
hub: Fly to Trivandrum airport, 20min taxi to Kovalam

spots.name: Vizhinjam Lighthouse
spots.note: Striped tower on the headland at the south end of the beach; about 140 steps up the spiral for the view over the crescent.

spots.name: Vizhinjam Rock Cut Cave Temple
spots.note: Eighth century Ay dynasty shrine cut into one boulder, the carvings inside left unfinished; free, ask at the house next door.

spots.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
spots.note: The gold vault temple in Trivandrum, reclining Vishnu seen through three doors; mundu or sari required, Hindus only, no phones.

spots.name: Vizhinjam Fishing Harbour
spots.note: The working fishing harbour a bay south of Kovalam; the auction runs as the boats land soon after dawn, wear old shoes.

spots.name: Poovar Island
spots.note: Sand bar where the Neyyar meets the sea, reached only by boat from Poovar jetty; agree the fare first, two hours is enough.

spots.name: Azhimala Siva Temple
spots.note: Clifftop shrine south of Kovalam under a 58 foot Gangadhareswara statue; come for sunset, steep steps down to the rocks.

spots.name: Napier Museum
spots.note: Indo Saracenic 1880 building in Trivandrum's museum park, old bronzes and a Kathakali gallery; shut Mondays and Wednesday mornings.

name: Kumarakom
tagline: Vembanad Lake birding village and backwater resort belt

why.winter: Peak season - migratory birds fill the sanctuary, cool mornings for canoe rides through the backwaters
why.summer: Hot and still by April-May; the bird sanctuary empties out as migratory species leave
why.monsoon: June-July downpours are heavy and the lake turns choppy; by August it calms into a quieter green window
why.autumn: October is a good transition - migratory birds start arriving back as monsoon humidity fades

vibe: Skews toward couples and resorts - peaceful for birding, not a place to meet backpackers
hub: Fly to Cochin, 1.5h taxi to Kumarakom via Kottayam

spots.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
spots.note: Fourteen acres of old rubber and mangrove on the lake edge; opens at 6 am, migrants November to February, carry repellent.

spots.name: Pathiramanal Island
spots.note: Uninhabited islet out in Vembanad, herons and darters, reached only by boat; hire at the jetty, allow three hours return.

spots.name: Bay Island Driftwood Museum
spots.note: One woman's collection of sea worn driftwood read as figures and animals; closed Mondays, half an hour and you are done.

spots.name: Thazhathangady Juma Masjid
spots.note: One of India's oldest mosques, all carved teak, on the Meenachil at Kottayam; men only inside, ask before you photograph.

spots.name: Aruvikkuzhi Waterfall
spots.note: Small cascade in a rubber estate up the hill behind the resorts, a short walk in; only worth it during and just after rain.

spots.name: Vaikom Mahadeva Temple
spots.note: Ancient Shiva temple, site of the 1924 Vaikom Satyagraha; dress code applies, Hindus only, go in the morning before 11.

name: Marari Beach (Mararikulam)
tagline: Shore-seine fishing beach with coir villages and no promenade

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the whole point: 24-32°C, a calm sea you can actually swim in, and shore-seine crews hauling nets at dawn.
why.summer: Mar-May is 34°C, humid and airless, the sea turns choppy from May and the sand is too hot to cross before five in the evening.
why.monsoon: June-Aug is a write-off for swimming, with red flags, heavy swell and 700 mm months, though the coir villages keep working.
why.autumn: Oct is still stormy off this coast; November settles down and is the quietest month before the Christmas and New Year rush.

vibe: Homestays and low-rise resorts scattered through coir-making hamlets; you meet couples and Europeans, not backpackers
hub: Cherthala station 10 km on the Ernakulam-Alappuzha line, then an auto; Kochi airport 70 km, Alappuzha 12 km

spots.name: Arthunkal St Andrew's Basilica
spots.note: Sixteenth century Portuguese shore church; the January feast pulls lakhs of walkers, any other week it is silent and cool.

spots.name: Andhakaranazhi Beach
spots.note: Where the Vembanad backwater cuts through to the sea, a lighthouse and a working harbour; vicious rip, do not swim here.

spots.name: Thanneermukkom Bund
spots.note: The salt water barrier across Vembanad, shutters closed through the dry months; walk the causeway for the width of the lake.

spots.name: Cherthala Karthyayani Devi Temple
spots.note: The town's own Bhagavathy temple, a short auto from Cherthala station; dress code applies, opens early and shuts by noon.

name: Munnar
tagline: Tea-carpeted hill station, Kerala's iconic highland escape

why.winter: Peak season - crisp mountain air, clear tea-garden views, book stays weeks ahead
why.summer: Cool at altitude (18-28C) even as plains bake; April-May turns hazy and more crowded
why.monsoon: Landslide-prone roads and thick fog cut visibility to metres; waterfalls roar but views vanish
why.autumn: Best window: monsoon just ended, hillsides impossibly green, clear skies before winter crowds

vibe: Hostels draw a steady trickle of solo travellers for tea-garden treks and campfires
hub: Fly to Cochin, 4h taxi/bus via Munnar ghat road

spots.name: Eravikulam National Park
spots.note: Rajamalai grassland where Nilgiri tahr walk up to the bus track; book the slot online, shut February and March for calving.

spots.name: KDHP Tata Tea Museum
spots.note: Working demo of the old rolling and drying machines with the estate's history; ticketed, closed Mondays, an hour at most.

spots.name: Mattupetty Dam
spots.note: Reservoir on the Top Station road with speedboats and the Indo Swiss cattle farm beside it; boat queues build after 11 am.

spots.name: Top Station
spots.note: Old ropeway point looking down into the Theni plains from 1700 m; be there before 9 am or cloud fills the whole valley.

spots.name: Pothamedu Viewpoint
spots.note: First proper tea slope view above town on the Kochi road; free, best in the hour after sunrise before the buses arrive.

spots.name: Attukad Waterfalls
spots.note: Broad falls on the Pallivasal road seen from a footbridge; only worth the stop in and just after the monsoon, rocks stay slippery.

spots.name: Kundala Lake
spots.note: Dam lake in the shola on the way to Top Station, pedal boats and one shikara; the cherry blossom along it flowers in November.

name: Munroe Island (Munroe Thuruthu)
tagline: Canoe canals through eight islets where Kallada meets Ashtamudi

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: still canals, three-hour dawn canoe rides through coir retting pools, herons everywhere and 24-31°C.
why.summer: Mar-May is hot and glaring on open water, so go at six in the morning or five in the evening and expect the retting pools to reek.
why.monsoon: June-July floods the low wards and canoe trips stop in the worst weeks; these islands sit barely above the tide as it is.
why.autumn: Oct still brings evening thunderstorms off the lake; November is clear, empty and the cheapest time to book a homestay.

vibe: A dozen family homestays on a quiet island, canoe punters rather than guides, and nowhere to eat after eight at night
hub: Munroe Turuttu halt takes passenger trains only; Kollam 30 min by bus, Trivandrum airport 90 km

spots.name: Ashtamudi Lake
spots.note: The lake the island's canals drain into; the canoe tours push off about 6 am and 2 pm to catch the low tide under the bridges.

spots.name: Kallada River
spots.note: The river feeding the canals, coir retting racks along its banks; the Kallada boat race is held four days after Thiruvonam.

spots.name: Sasthamcotta Lake
spots.note: Kerala's largest freshwater lake, a Ramsar site with a hilltop Sastha temple and its monkeys; buses from Kollam, half a day out.

spots.name: Thangassery Lighthouse
spots.note: A 1902 tower on the Kollam headland with Portuguese fort ruins beside it; afternoon hours only, climb it near closing.

name: Muziris Heritage (Kodungallur)
tagline: Lost Roman spice port with the Cheraman mosque and synagogues
festival: Mar/Apr: Kodungallur Bharani

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry and flat calm, the right window to ride the Muziris ferries between Paliam Palace, Chendamangalam and Kottappuram.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is 35°C and humid but it brings the raucous Bharani at the Bhagavathy temple, which is not a quiet sightseeing day.
why.monsoon: June-Aug the backwater boat links get patchy and the small museums empty out; 700 mm months make village walking grim.
why.autumn: Oct is still wet from the retreating monsoon; by November it is dry, green and you will have most of the sites to yourself.

vibe: A quiet, under-visited museum circuit where you sleep in small Kodungallur or North Paravur hotels, never resorts
hub: Aluva station 35 km, Kochi airport 40 km; buses run to Kodungallur, then autos and ferries between sites

spots.name: Cheraman Juma Masjid
spots.note: Held to be India's first mosque, 629 AD, a brass lamp always burning; the old wooden core survives behind, small museum.

spots.name: Kodungallur Bhagavathy Temple
spots.note: Kali temple at the heart of the old port town; the Bharani festival falls in March or April, other mornings it is nearly empty.

spots.name: North Paravur Synagogue
spots.note: Best restored of the Muziris Jewish sites, now a museum of Kerala's Jews; closed Mondays, one ticket covers the circuit.

spots.name: Paliam Palace, Chendamangalam
spots.note: The Paliath Achan family's Dutch built house and nalukettu, with a synagogue and a church inside a short walk; shut Mondays.

spots.name: Mar Thoma Pontifical Shrine
spots.note: At Azhikode, where St Thomas is said to have landed in 52 AD; a bone relic in the chapel, ferry across from Munambam.

name: Nelliyampathy
tagline: Orange-and-tea hills above Palakkad with the Seetharkundu drop

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the sweet spot at 12-25°C, with orange groves in fruit and clear views out over the Palakkad plains from Seetharkundu.
why.summer: Mar-May stays in the twenties up here while Palakkad below hits 40°C, which makes this the region's obvious hot-weather escape.
why.monsoon: June-Aug is landslide season on the ten-hairpin ghat road: buses get cancelled for days and the viewpoints show only cloud.
why.autumn: Oct clears slowly with north-east showers; November is green, cold after dark and almost empty of other visitors.

vibe: Estate bungalows and a couple of homestays, no market and no nightlife; you come for cold mornings and nothing else
hub: Bus from Palakkad to Nenmara, then a limited ghat bus 22 km up; Palakkad Junction 60 km, last bus down early

spots.name: Seetharkundu Viewpoint
spots.note: The edge of the plateau with a stream dropping off it and all of Palakkad below; cloud usually closes the view by noon.

spots.name: Poabs Organic Estate
spots.note: Organic tea, coffee and orange plantation you can walk through; ask at the office for the factory visit, oranges by December.

spots.name: Kesavanpara
spots.note: Bare rock shoulder you scramble up for the valley, far less visited than Seetharkundu; no railing, skip it in the wet.

spots.name: Pothundy Dam
spots.note: Reservoir at the foot of the ghat with a garden and pedal boats, the last stop before the climb; gates close about 5 pm.

name: Nilambur
tagline: World's oldest teak plantation and the Nedumkayam rainforest

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry at 20-33°C and made for it: Conolly's Plot of 1846, the teak museum and the Nedumkayam forest road at first light.
why.summer: Mar-May hits 37°C down in the Nilambur valley, so it is shaded plantations and the Chaliyar river only, and you are out by ten.
why.monsoon: June-Aug is one of Kerala's wettest pockets; the Nedumkayam road washes out and the tribal hamlets beyond it get cut off.
why.autumn: Oct still rains hard some evenings, but by November the Chaliyar runs clear and the teak forest is at its absolute best.

vibe: A small teak-trade town with basic lodges and no traveller scene at all; the forest office decides what you can enter
hub: Nilambur Road is the end of the branch line from Shoranur, 2 h; Calicut airport 55 km, buses from Kozhikode

spots.name: Conolly's Plot
spots.note: The world's oldest teak plantation, sown in 1846 on the Chaliyar bank; small ticket, half an hour under 40 m trees.

spots.name: Nilambur Teak Museum
spots.note: The only teak museum anywhere, at Chandakunnu on the Gudalur road, run by the forest institute; closed Mondays, small fee.

spots.name: Nedumkayam Rainforest
spots.note: Evergreen forest with a colonial timber rest house and an old elephant kraal; the forest office decides entry, jeep only.

spots.name: Adyanpara Waterfalls
spots.note: Falls and rock pools on the Kurumbalangode stream; ticket at the gate, staff stop entry in heavy rain, rocks stay slippery.

spots.name: Nilambur Vettakorumakan Temple
spots.note: The Kovilakam family's temple in town; the week long Nilambur Pattu in January or February is the one time it fills up.

name: Paithalmala
tagline: Grassland summit on the Kodagu border, Kannur's rooftop

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the clean window: cool grassland, a firm trail and the watchtower's 360° sweep into Coorg's blue ranges.
why.summer: March is the last good month; through April-May the grass browns and haze flattens the Coorg views, so start at first light.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug is hard rain on an exposed ridge, slippery laterite and zero visibility; admire the mist from the valley instead.
why.autumn: Sep is mist-and-drizzle roulette; Oct-Nov the hills turn deep green with streams still running, the prettiest weeks up here.

vibe: A locals' sunrise trek with Kannur weekenders and a trailhead chai shack; sleep in Kannur or a rare village homestay
hub: Pottenplave trailhead, 65 km from Kannur, 45 km from Kannur airport; bus to Kudiyanmala, auto on, 3 km walk

spots.name: Alakode
spots.note: The nearest real town, a settler farming bazaar for cash, food and buses; last shops before the Kudiyanmala trailhead road.

spots.name: Palakkayam Thattu
spots.note: Grass topped ridge above Kolayad that sits in cloud; a jeep runs the last steep stretch on a ticket, shuts in heavy rain.

name: Parambikulam Tiger Reserve
tagline: Teak-and-tiger reserve reached through Tamil Nadu, shut in monsoon

why.winter: Nov-Feb is the season at 15-30°C: the reserve is fully open and the odds are best on gaur, elephant and the giant Kannimara teak.
why.summer: Mar-May concentrates animals at the reservoir but fire-risk closures can bite without warning, and Pollachi below sits at 38°C.
why.monsoon: Tourism shuts for roughly June to September; the Pollachi-Top Slip ghat road is landslide-prone and all bookings stop.
why.autumn: Reopening comes in October, still damp and leech-heavy; by November the trails dry out and the tented niche books up early.

vibe: Forest-department tree houses, island nests and a tented niche; you share a jeep with strangers or walk with a guide
hub: Approach via Pollachi in Tamil Nadu, 55 km through Top Slip; Coimbatore airport 100 km, book stays online

spots.name: Kannimara Teak
spots.note: One of the oldest living teak trees on earth, roughly 450 years; reached by guided jeep and a short walk, fix it at the forest office.

spots.name: Parambikulam Dam
spots.note: The reservoir the reserve wraps around; forest run boating and bamboo rafting leave early, life jackets on, no private boats.

spots.name: Cochin Forest Tramway trail
spots.note: Rotting sleepers of the 1907 timber tramway to Chalakudy, walked as a guided forest trail; half a day, a guide is compulsory.

spots.name: Karian Shola
spots.note: Dense evergreen shola where lion tailed macaques feed; a short guided trail off the road, thick with leeches in and after rain.

spots.name: Karimala Gopuram
spots.note: The reserve's highest peak, a hard two day guided trek with a night camped in forest; fixed dates only, book weeks ahead.

name: Ponmudi
tagline: Trivandrum's easy-reach hairpin-bend hill station

why.winter: Peak season - cool air after the 22-hairpin drive up, clear Western Ghats views towards the coast
why.summer: Warm but tolerable at 1100m; April-May turns hazy and the trails get dustier
why.monsoon: Frequent landslides and fog close in on the hairpin road; waterfalls are spectacular but the drive is risky
why.autumn: October onward the monsoon eases into a solid, uncrowded weekend escape from Trivandrum

vibe: A Trivandrum weekender day trip more than a backpacker stop - come for the drive
hub: Fly to Trivandrum, 1.5h taxi up the 22-hairpin ghat road

spots.name: Golden Valley (Kallar)
spots.note: The Kallar running over smooth rock slabs at the foot of the ghat; safe pools in dry months, deadly current after rain.

spots.name: Meenmutty Falls
spots.note: Forest falls two kilometres in on foot from Kallar with a guide; closed in heavy monsoon, carry salt for the leeches.

spots.name: Agasthyakoodam
spots.note: 1868 m peak climbed from Bonacaud over two days; the season runs mid January to March and permits are booked online, they sell out.

spots.name: Peppara Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Reservoir and forest below the hill with elephants near the water at dusk; entry only through the forest check post, no walking in alone.

spots.name: Bonacaud
spots.note: Abandoned tea estate and bungalow at the end of the road, the Agasthyakoodam trailhead; buses are rare, come with your own ride.

name: Ranipuram
tagline: Grassland and shola ridge above Kasaragod, reached only on foot

why.winter: Dec-Feb brings mist in the sholas and 14 C on top; the 6 km climb from the forest gate is dry underfoot and the view runs west to the sea haze.
why.summer: March still gives long clear views before the heat haze; by Apr-May the grass is burnt yellow, so start the climb by 7 am and carry all your water.
why.monsoon: Jun-Jul the gate closes on the heaviest rain and leeches own the grass; September reopens to green slopes, full streams and cloud on the ridge.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the green window: waist-high grass, cloud shadow crossing the ridge and almost nobody on the trail on a weekday.

vibe: A DTPC cottage and a forest rest house at the gate, homestays down in Panathady; evenings are frogs, stars and patchy phone signal
hub: Kanhangad railhead 48 km, then bus or shared taxi via Panathady to the forest gate, about 2h

name: Silent Valley National Park (Mukkali)
tagline: Untouched rainforest saved from a dam, entered only by permit

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the clear window at 15-30°C, permits are easier to secure and the forest bus runs the 23 km up to Sairandhri.
why.summer: March and April are warm but still workable at this altitude, and lion-tailed macaques drop lower; by May it is close and hazy.
why.monsoon: June-Sep brings 2,800-3,400 mm of rain, leeches on every trail and repeated closures, so do not plan a Silent Valley trip then.
why.autumn: Oct is still dripping and trips restart slowly; November is green, cool and the best month before the December permit rush.

vibe: Almost nobody here: a forest office, a couple of Mukkali homestays and a permit queue at eight with a few naturalists
hub: Mukkali is 40 km from Mannarkkad by bus; entry only on a Forest Department permit, applied for 24-48 h ahead

spots.name: Sairandhri
spots.note: The one point inside the core zone, a watchtower over unbroken rainforest; forest jeep from Mukkali on your permit, back by afternoon.

spots.name: Kunthipuzha hanging bridge
spots.note: Suspension bridge over clear water at Sairandhri, the way into the core forest walk; the guide leads, and swimming is not allowed.

spots.name: Agali
spots.note: Attappady's market town among tribal hamlets, with the only ATMs and pharmacies for miles; buses from Mukkali stop by early evening.

spots.name: Kanjirapuzha Dam
spots.note: Earth dam with a garden and boating below Mannarkkad, an easy stop on the way out; ticketed, packed on Sunday evenings.

name: Thalassery (Tellicherry)
tagline: Biryani, a British fort and Kerala's only drive-in beach

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season at 23-32°C, with theyyam nights at the village kavus and sand firm enough to drive at Muzhappilangad.
why.summer: Mar-May is 35°C and sticky; the biryani, the kalthappam and the cheap bars over in Mahe survive it, the midday beach does not.
why.monsoon: June-Aug closes the drive-in beach completely, with 900 mm months, high tides washing over the sand and no swimming anywhere.
why.autumn: Oct still gets thundery evenings but the theyyam season opens mid-month; November is dry, green and the best value of the year.

vibe: A food-and-cricket town of Muslim tea shops and old spice godowns; small hotels, no hostels and very few outsiders
hub: Thalassery station on the Mangaluru-Kozhikode line; Kannur airport 25 km, Muzhappilangad beach 8 km north

spots.name: Thalassery Fort
spots.note: 1708 East India Company fort of laterite walls and tunnels above the sea; open through the day, best in the last hour of light.

spots.name: Muzhappilangad Drive-in Beach
spots.note: Four kilometres of hard sand you can drive or ride along; go at low tide, and stay out of the water, the current is strong.

spots.name: Dharmadam Island
spots.note: Wooded islet you can wade across to at low tide; landing needs permission from the tourism office, check the tide before you cross.

spots.name: Odathil Palli
spots.note: Eighteenth century mosque with no minaret, teak inside and a copper roof, built by a spice merchant; ask before entering at prayer time.

spots.name: Mambally's Royal Biscuit Factory
spots.note: The bakery that baked India's first Christmas cake in 1883; still selling plum cake and biscuits from a lane off the main road.

name: Thattekad (Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary)
tagline: Salim Ali's richest peninsular birding forest on the Periyar

why.winter: Nov-Feb is prime: winter migrants are in, mornings start near 20°C and the dawn trails turn up frogmouth, trogon and hornbills.
why.summer: March still delivers with the leaf litter dry and birds pinned to water, but by May it is 37°C and walks have to end by nine.
why.monsoon: June-July is relentless rain and leeches; the birds are breeding and loud but you will barely see through the wet canopy.
why.autumn: Oct is wet and quiet because the migrants have not arrived; November flips it and the guide-run homestays start filling up.

vibe: Serious birders in a handful of guide-run homestays; you are up at half past five and asleep by nine, alone or paired up
hub: Kothamangalam 12 km by bus, Aluva station 50 km, Kochi airport 55 km; hire a local bird guide, it is worth it

spots.name: Bhoothathankettu
spots.note: Barrage where the Periyar squeezes through a rock gorge, with a forest park and boating; ticketed, gates shut in the late afternoon.

spots.name: Idamalayar Dam
spots.note: Reservoir dam deep in the forest upstream; the road runs through elephant country, go early and do not stop in the ghat section.

spots.name: Malayattoor Kurisumudi
spots.note: St Thomas hill shrine, a 3 km climb of rock steps to the summit chapel; enormous crowds in the week after Easter, dawn is coolest.

spots.name: Kothamangalam Cheriapally
spots.note: Old Syrian Christian church holding the tomb of Mar Abo, a working parish rather than a monument; cover shoulders, quiet by afternoon.

name: Thekkady (Periyar)
tagline: Periyar Tiger Reserve - boat safaris around a forest lake

why.winter: Peak season - cool mornings, best wildlife visibility as animals gather at waterholes, scenic boat safaris
why.summer: Increasingly hot and humid; April can still bring decent waterhole sightings but treks are sweatier
why.monsoon: Leech-heavy treks and rain-hampered boat safaris; animals scatter into cover so sightings drop off
why.autumn: October-November is a good reset - monsoon clears, forest is lush, wildlife viewing starts improving

vibe: Kumily's guesthouses organise group treks and rafting - an easy way for solos to team up
hub: Fly to Cochin or Madurai, 4-5h taxi/bus to Kumily/Thekkady

spots.name: Periyar Lake
spots.note: The flooded valley you cross by boat for elephants and gaur on the shore; forest boats sell out, queue at the ticket office by 7 am.

spots.name: Periyar Tiger Trail
spots.note: One or two day guided trek camping inside the reserve, led by reformed poachers; five people per group, book well ahead.

spots.name: Periyar Bamboo Rafting
spots.note: Full day forest programme, a long walk then rafting on the lake with lunch; starts at eight, seats are few, book a day early.

spots.name: Mangala Devi Kannagi Temple
spots.note: Ruined stone temple on the Tamil Nadu border, gates opened only on Chithra Pournami in April; forest jeep and pass, no walking up.

spots.name: Chellarkovil
spots.note: Village on a cliff edge with the Cumbum plains a kilometre below and a step waterfall in the rains; go late afternoon for the light.

spots.name: Kadathanadan Kalari Centre
spots.note: Evening kalaripayattu show in a sunken pit theatre, an hour of fire and swords; buy the ticket earlier in the day, it fills up.

name: Thenmala
tagline: India's first planned ecotourism site, built round a dam reservoir

why.winter: Dec-Feb is dry at 20-32°C and everything runs: the canopy walk, the swinging bridge, reservoir boating and dry forest trails.
why.summer: Mar-May climbs to 36°C in the Shencottah gap, the reservoir drops, the trails bake and the deer rehabilitation area is the only shade.
why.monsoon: June-July brings hard rain and leeches on every trail, and the nearby Palaruvi falls gets closed off when the river rises.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov catch the north-east monsoon in short evening bursts, but the forest is at its greenest and virtually empty.

vibe: A forest-department set-up rather than a village scene: KTDC and small lodges, school groups by day and silence at night
hub: Thenmala has a station on the Kollam-Shencottah line; buses from Kollam cover the 65 km in about two hours

spots.name: Palaruvi Falls
spots.note: A 300 foot fall on the Shencottah road with a bathing pool below; ticket plus a forest bus from the gate, shut in heavy rain.

spots.name: Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Evergreen forest around the reservoir, with boat safaris and guided trails; book at the eco office in the morning, guides are few.

spots.name: Parappar Dam
spots.note: The Kallada irrigation dam that holds back Thenmala's reservoir; short climb up from the ecotourism gate, best light early morning.

spots.name: Thenmala Adventure Zone
spots.note: Rope bridges, rock climbing and mountain biking run by the ecotourism board; pay per activity at the counter, school groups by day.

spots.name: Aryankavu Sastha Temple
spots.note: One of the old Sastha shrines on the Ayyappa route, busiest in the Mandala season; dress code applies, men bare chested inside.

name: Thirunelli (Brahmagiri)
tagline: Old Vishnu temple alone inside the Brahmagiri forest
festival: Jul/Aug: Karkidaka Vavu Bali, ancestral rites on the Papanasini

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the clean window: 15 C dawns on the Papanasini steps, dry forest paths and Pakshipathalam trek permits actually being issued at the gate.
why.summer: Mar-May the Brahmagiri slopes turn brown and midday reaches 32 C, but the 860 m temple yard stays cool and close to empty on weekdays.
