spots.note: The 60 foot Awadhi gateway of 1784, two minutes from Bara Imambara; nothing to enter, shoot it early or floodlit at night

spots.name: Tunday Kababi
spots.note: Aminabad original for the galouti kebab everyone comes to Lucknow for; cash only, no frills, queues build from 8 pm

spots.name: Hazratganj
spots.note: Cream colonnaded shopping street and the evening walk locals call ganjing; Ram Asrey for sweets, many shops shut Sunday

name: Mahoba (Chandela Lakes)
tagline: Chandela lakes cut into granite hills, temple ruins standing in the water
festival: Aug: Kajli Mela at Kirat Sagar

why.winter: Nov to Feb runs 7C to 26C, right for walking the Madan Sagar bund to the half sunken Shiva temple and climbing Gokhar hill at dawn
why.summer: Bundelkhand bakes: April past 42C, May and June near 47C with the granite throwing heat back and the tanks dropping. Sit it out
why.monsoon: July and August refill the Chandela tanks and green the hills; Kajli Mela packs the town for a week around Raksha Bandhan
why.autumn: October and November are the clean weeks: full lakes, cool mornings, the Rahila sun temple and the Jain rock carvings to yourself

vibe: A small Bundelkhand town with plain hotels near the junction; evenings are chai stalls, paan shops and the lake bund
hub: Mahoba Junction sits on the Jhansi to Khajuraho line, 3h from Jhansi and 2h from Khajuraho; autos reach every lake

name: Naimisharanya (Nimsar)
tagline: Forest where the Puranas were told: Chakra Tirth and Gomti

why.winter: Peak at 8-25 °C for the circular Chakra Tirth tank, the Vyas Gaddi and a stretch of Gomti bank that is quiet.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is 44 °C in central UP: the tank drops, the parikrama road shimmers and rooms have no real cooling.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is humid and the 84-kos parikrama road turns to slush; pilgrim numbers fall and so do bus services.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the best window: harvested fields, cool mornings and amavasya bathing crowds you can easily dodge.

vibe: A pure pilgrim town of dharamshalas and Sanskrit chanting; no cafes, no travellers, food is thali or nothing
hub: Naimisharanya halt on the Balamau-Sitapur branch; buses from Lucknow (90 km) take 2.5 h via Sandila

spots.name: Chakra Tirth
spots.note: Round kund where Vishnu's chakra is said to have fallen, the centre of town; pilgrims bathe at dawn, fullest after the rains

spots.name: Lalita Devi Temple
spots.note: Shakti Peeth a short walk from Chakra Tirth and the busiest shrine here; queues are short on weekdays, shoes off at the gate

spots.name: Vyas Gaddi
spots.note: Seat under a banyan where Vyasa is said to have dictated the Puranas; a priest recites at dusk and expects a small offering

spots.name: Hanuman Garhi
spots.note: Large seated Hanuman in a walled compound on the Sitapur road; Tuesday brings the crowds and the free prasad line

spots.name: Misrikh (Dadhichi Kund)
spots.note: Sage Dadhichi's tank west of town, part of the same pilgrim circuit; shared autos run from Nimsar until about 6 pm

name: Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary (Unnao)
tagline: Shallow migratory-bird lake halfway between Lucknow and Kanpur

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the whole point: pintail, shoveller and greylag on the water, sarus cranes in the fields, 8 C dawns.
why.summer: Apr-Jun the lake shrinks and shimmers at 45 C, the migrants are long gone and the tower is an oven by 9 am.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the lake is brim full and empty of birds, the walking bund floods and the boats stop running.
why.autumn: November is the build-up month as the first flocks drop in: warm days, and the paths finally dry underfoot.

vibe: A watchtower, a bund walk and a small state tourist complex; birders with scopes at dawn, nobody else
hub: On the Lucknow-Kanpur highway, 45 km from either; any bus between the two drops you at the sanctuary gate

spots.name: Nawabganj Watch Tower
spots.note: Two storey tower over the shallow jheel, the only real vantage for sarus cranes and winter duck; go within an hour of sunrise

spots.name: Nawabganj Deer Park
spots.note: Fenced chital and blackbuck enclosure by the entry gate, worth ten minutes while the light comes up; same sanctuary ticket

name: Pilibhit Tiger Reserve (Chuka)
tagline: Terai tiger forest with tree huts on the Sharda Sagar water

why.winter: Peak: cold gypsy safaris through sal and grassland, 60-plus tigers in a narrow reserve, huts near empty.
why.summer: April at the waterholes gives the best tiger odds of the year; by May it is 43 °C and gates shut on 15 June.
why.monsoon: Closed 16 Jun to 14 Nov: the Sharda floods, forest roads dissolve and safaris simply do not run at all.
why.autumn: October is shut. The reserve reopens 15 November and that first fortnight is green, cool and uncrowded.

vibe: Forest department huts by the Chuka water, no private resorts; book ahead online and expect to share a jeep
hub: Pilibhit Jn railhead, then about 55 km by road via Puranpur to the Chuka gate; Bareilly is the bigger hub

spots.name: Chuka Beach
spots.note: Sand shelf where the Sharda Sagar water meets the sal forest, the reason people come; forest gates shut at dusk, no shops

spots.name: Sharda Sagar Dam
spots.note: Long earthen bund holding the reservoir back, open water on one side and grassland on the other; drive it at first light

spots.name: Mahof Gate
spots.note: Safari gate near Pilibhit town for the reserve's sal blocks and grassland; morning jeeps leave at first light, book a day ahead

spots.name: Gomti Udgam (Fulhar Jheel)
spots.note: Marshy pool near Madho Tanda taken as the Gomti's source, a small temple beside it; a puddle in summer, full after the rains

name: Piprahwa (Kapilavastu)
tagline: Brick stupa in mango orchards where the Buddha's relics were dug up
festival: Apr/May: Buddha Purnima prayers at the stupa

why.winter: Dec to Feb brings 8C mornings and mustard fields around the mound; Thai and Sri Lankan bus groups stop for an hour and are gone
why.summer: March still walks well, April climbs past 40C and May and June bake an open mound with no shade at all; the museum shuts by 5 pm
why.monsoon: Jul to Sep means mud lanes, heavy air and standing water, but the Ganwaria monastery ruins sit green and completely empty
why.autumn: October and November are the best weeks here: dry paths, clear light on the old brick courses and paddy being cut all around

vibe: One monastery guest house and basic rooms at Birdpur; nights are village quiet and dinner is dal and roti at a roadside dhaba
hub: Naugarh in Siddharthnagar is the railhead 20 km away with the nearest hotels; shared autos run via Birdpur to the site

name: Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam)
tagline: Ganga-Yamuna Sangam, Magh Mela sands and Anand Bhavan
festival: Jan/Feb: Magh Mela on the Sangam sands

why.winter: Peak: the Magh Mela tent city rises on the sand from mid-Jan, 8 °C dawns, rowboats to the Sangam all day.
why.summer: Apr-Jun runs to 45 °C with hot loo winds off the dry riverbed and the Sangam is a glare pit by 9 am.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the Ganga and Yamuna swallow the mela ground and lower ghats; boats stop and lanes waterlog.
why.autumn: October drains the flood and Kartik bathers return: warm clear days, cheap boats and the ghats near empty.

vibe: Pilgrim families, university students and mela sadhus; cheap dharamshalas, traveller crowds only in mela season
hub: Prayagraj Jn on the Delhi-Howrah main line; airport 15 km, shared autos to the Sangam ghat in 20 min

spots.name: Anand Bhavan
spots.note: The Nehru family mansion kept as it was, Congress history room by room; shut Mondays, the planetarium next door is separate

spots.name: Allahabad Fort
spots.note: Akbar's riverside fort, still army held; only the underground Patalpuri temple and the Akshayavat tree are open, carry ID

spots.name: Bade Hanuman Mandir
spots.note: Twenty foot reclining Hanuman set below ground near the Sangam; the Ganga floods it every monsoon, Tuesday queues are long

spots.name: Khusro Bagh
spots.note: Walled Mughal garden with three sandstone tombs including Prince Khusrau's; free, empty at dusk, guava sellers at the gate

spots.name: Loknath Gali
spots.note: Old city lane for kachori sabzi, dahi jalebi and thick lassi; go before 10 am or after 7 pm, cash only, eat standing

spots.name: All Saints Cathedral
spots.note: 1887 gothic cathedral in white and red sandstone at Civil Lines, locals call it Patthar Girja; open around services

spots.name: Chandrashekhar Azad Park
spots.note: Big colonial park where Azad shot himself in 1931; the Allahabad Museum and public library sit inside, museum shut Mondays

name: Rajdari & Devdari Falls (Chandraprabha)
tagline: Two forest waterfalls inside Chandraprabha sanctuary on the Kaimur scarp

why.winter: Dec and Jan still carry water over both lips, mornings sit near 10C, and the picnic buses from Varanasi arrive by noon, so start early
why.summer: March thins the falls to a trickle and Apr to Jun is 44C on bare rock with dry channels; there is nothing to see then
why.monsoon: July fills the Chandraprabha and Aug to Sep is the reason to come, both falls in full roar, though the last stretch of track turns to mud
why.autumn: October pairs strong flow with clear light, November is cooler and near empty; the sal forest is green and chinkara come to the water

vibe: A forest rest house and a few plain rooms in Chakia; weekend picnickers from Varanasi, nobody at all on a weekday
hub: Varanasi to Chakia is 2h by bus, then 15 km by auto or shared taxi on the Naugarh road to the sanctuary gate

name: Salkhan Fossils Park (Sonbhadra)
tagline: Stromatolite fossils 1400 million years old on the Kaimur scarp

why.winter: Cool dry months to wander the open hillside where 1400-million-year stromatolite rings stripe the rock, usually alone.
why.summer: April-June the bare Kaimur scarp bakes past 43 °C with zero shade on the fossil beds; dawn visits only, if at all.
why.monsoon: Rain greens the scarp and nearby Kaimur falls start running, but the fossil beds turn slick and buses crawl.
why.autumn: October-November is the sweet spot: rinsed air, green cliffs and easy walking weather across the fossil beds.

vibe: A geology pilgrimage, not a scene: you, a caretaker and school groups; sleep in Robertsganj's plain hotels
hub: Robertsganj railhead 12 km, autos to Salkhan village; Varanasi 90 km, an honest day trip by car

spots.name: Vijaygarh Fort
spots.note: Ruined hill fort above Robertsganj with rock cut tanks and old inscriptions; a 20 minute climb, no signage, go with someone

spots.name: Mukkha Falls
spots.note: Fall off the Kaimur scarp that runs hard from July to October; the last stretch is a rough track and it is dry by March

spots.name: Agori Fort
spots.note: Twelfth century Kharwar fort on a spur above the Son near Chopan; reached by boat and a short walk, nothing but ruins

name: Shakumbhari Devi (Behat)
tagline: Shakti Peeth in a Shivalik riverbed with sal forest on three sides
festival: Mar/Apr: Chaitra Navratri fair, again in Sep/Oct

why.winter: Dec and Jan drop to 4C at night with the Shivalik ridgelines standing clear; weekdays are quiet and the forest track is dry
why.summer: March is the best month, green and mild after the winter rain; April warms quickly and May and June push 40C on the plains below
why.monsoon: July and August the seasonal nala the approach road crosses runs hard and washes out, and the last few km are regularly cut
why.autumn: October and November are cool and washed clean, the riverbed walkable, and the Ashwin Navratri fair fills the valley for nine days

vibe: Temple dharamshalas and a row of dhabas at the gate, nothing else; pilgrims by day, then only forest noise and bells
hub: Saharanpur is the railhead 40 km south, buses and shared jeeps run up via Behat, last one back leaves mid afternoon

name: Shravasti (Sahet-Mahet)
tagline: Jetavana ruins where the Buddha spent 25 rain retreats

why.winter: Peak at 7-25 °C over Jetavana's brick foundations; Sri Lankan and Korean pilgrim groups, otherwise silence.
why.summer: Apr-Jun runs to 43 °C on treeless excavation mounds, with no cafes, thin buses and long waits in the sun.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the Rapti floods this belt, the mud tracks out to Mahet get bad and the ruins feel abandoned.
why.autumn: October is green and warm with the fields cut: the best light on the Anandabodhi tree and Angulimala stupa.

vibe: Sri Lankan, Thai and Korean monastery guesthouses plus one state lodge; you will meet almost no Indian tourists
hub: Balrampur railhead 18 km or Gonda 50 km; buses from Lucknow (170 km) take 4-5 h and the last one back is early

spots.name: Gandhakuti
spots.note: Brick plinth of the hut the Buddha used through 19 rain retreats in Jetavana; pilgrims circle it with candles at dusk

spots.name: Anandabodhi Tree
spots.note: Peepal in the Jetavana grove grown from a Bodh Gaya cutting; Sri Lankan groups chant under it in the evening, shoes off

spots.name: Angulimala Stupa
spots.note: Bare brick mound inside the old city ramparts at Maheth, with Anathapindika's stupa nearby; open field, carry water

spots.name: Sobhnath Temple
spots.note: Jain shrine in the Maheth ruins marking Sambhavanatha's birthplace; a stone platform and a small hall, quiet all day

spots.name: Wat Thai Shravasti
spots.note: Thai monastery on the Balrampur road, gilded hall and swept gardens; open through the day, one of a dozen foreign viharas

name: Varanasi
tagline: Ancient Ganges ghats, India's chaotic spiritual heart
festival: Nov: Dev Deepawali

why.winter: Peak season: cool mornings for sunrise boat rides, and Dev Deepawali in November is unmissable
why.summer: Brutal 45C+ heat with high humidity by May-June; the ghats are near-empty for good reason
why.monsoon: The Ganges rises and can submerge lower ghat steps; muggy but atmospheric if you handle the heat
why.autumn: Pleasant temperatures return by late October, building to the spectacular Dev Deepawali festival

vibe: Long-term travelers linger for weeks on the ghats; boat-sharing makes solo mixing easy
hub: Flights/trains from Delhi 12h; airport 25km from the ghats

spots.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
spots.note: The main ghat and the 7 pm Ganga aarti; arrive by 6 for a step, or hire a boat and watch from the water for less crush

spots.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
spots.note: Shiva's jyotirlinga at the end of the new corridor; phones and bags go into lockers, the queue is shortest before 6 am

spots.name: Manikarnika Ghat
spots.note: The main burning ghat, fires going day and night; watch quietly from the upper steps, no photos, ignore the wood touts

spots.name: Sarnath
spots.note: Where the Buddha first taught, Dhamek Stupa in lawns and the museum holding the Ashokan lion capital; museum shut Fridays

spots.name: Assi Ghat
spots.note: Southern ghat with the 5.30 am Subah e Banaras aarti and yoga on the steps; cafes behind it, easiest place to sit alone

spots.name: Kachori Gali
spots.note: Lane behind the Vishwanath corridor for kachori sabzi and jalebi from 7 am; gone by 11, eat standing, cash only

spots.name: Ramnagar Fort
spots.note: The Kashi Naresh's crumbling 18th century fort across the river, vintage cars and clocks inside; last entry about 5 pm

spots.name: Banaras Hindu University
spots.note: Vast campus with the marble New Vishwanath temple and the Bharat Kala Bhavan museum; rickshaws inside, museum shut Sunday

name: Vrindavan-Mathura
tagline: Krishna's birthplace and playground of temple towns
festival: Mar: Holi, incl. Barsana's Lathmar Holi

why.winter: Peak season: cool enough for long temple-hopping days across Vrindavan's 1000+ temples
why.summer: Severe heat by April-May; only the devout brave the midday sun for temple visits
why.monsoon: Humid and quieter: a good off-peak window if the spiritual pull outweighs sticky weather
why.autumn: Excellent weather resumes by late October, with Diwali on Krishna's home turf drawing crowds

vibe: ISKCON's international devotees give this temple town a surprisingly easy-to-meet vibe
hub: Train Delhi to Mathura 2-3h, then auto to Vrindavan 15km

spots.name: Banke Bihari Temple
spots.note: Vrindavan's busiest shrine, the curtain drawn open in glimpses; take the 8 am darshan on a weekday, leave phones outside

spots.name: Prem Mandir
spots.note: Marble temple lit up after dark with Radha Krishna dioramas and fountains; free, evening gates from about 4.30 pm, big crowd

spots.name: ISKCON Krishna Balaram Mandir
spots.note: The international temple, 4.30 am mangala aarti and Govinda's canteen; the guesthouse books out through Kartik

spots.name: Nidhivan
spots.note: Tangled tulsi grove that empties at dusk because of the story told about it; small, eerie, best in the first hour of day

spots.name: Krishna Janmabhoomi
spots.note: Krishna's birth prison beside the mosque in Mathura; heavy security, no phones, bags or pens past the gate, slow line

spots.name: Vishram Ghat
spots.note: Mathura's main Yamuna ghat, evening aarti about 7 and turtles in the water; boatmen quote high, agree a price first

spots.name: Kusum Sarovar
spots.note: Sandstone pavilions on a tank at Govardhan, the pretty stop on the 21 km parikrama; go at sunset, monkeys take glasses

name: Abbott Mount (Lohaghat)
tagline: Forgotten colonial hilltop of 1920s cottages, oaks and silence

why.winter: Dec-Feb is frosty and utterly quiet; clear spells show the snow line, but cottages run on bukharis, so pack for cold nights.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is fresh and green with rhododendron on the walk up; May stays far cooler than the plains though the views haze over.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug wraps the hill in fog and the Tanakpur road in slips; atmospheric for a day, tedious beyond, and the paths get leechy.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the pick: sharp air, long Himalayan views and empty lanes past the dozen-odd colonial cottages and the old church.

vibe: You, a caretaker-run heritage cottage, a derelict church and deodar silence; Lohaghat 8 km away for dhabas
hub: Road only: buses from Haldwani or Pithoragarh to Lohaghat, then 8 km taxi climb; Tanakpur rail 75 km (3 h)

spots.name: St John's Church
spots.note: Small stone church at the top of the spur, long disused and half roofless; the caretaker holds the key, oaks all round

spots.name: Abbott Mount cricket ground
spots.note: Flat green ledge cut for colonial cricket, still the only open ground here; walk its rim at sunset for the Panchachuli line

spots.name: Mayawati Advaita Ashram
spots.note: Ramakrishna Mission ashram of 1899 on an old tea estate, a library and museum; visitors 9 to 5, silence kept, no photos

spots.name: Banasur ka Kila
spots.note: Ruined hill fort above Lohaghat, about 20 minutes up from the road head; nothing but walls at the top and a wide view

spots.name: Baleshwar Temple
spots.note: Carved stone temple group in Champawat built by the Chand kings; free, open all day, the outer walls are the reason to go

name: Almora
tagline: Understated Kumaoni market town with Himalayan views

why.winter: Cold, clear mornings and snow-dusted peaks from Bright End Corner, but cafes shut early
why.summer: Warm days, cool nights: a calmer, cheaper alternative to Nainital's summer crowds
why.monsoon: Landslide-prone hill roads and low visibility erase the Himalayan views that are the point
why.autumn: Best light of the year. Crisp air, snow-capped Trishul and Nanda Devi visible from town

vibe: Quiet old bazaar; the real traveler scene is a short ride away in Kasar Devi's hostels
hub: Rail Kathgodam 90km, 3h shared taxi; or overnight Delhi bus 9-10h

spots.name: Kasar Devi Temple
spots.note: Ridge temple where Vivekananda sat and the old hippie trail settled; the cafes along Crank's Ridge below are the real draw

spots.name: Chitai Golu Devta Temple
spots.note: Shrine of the justice god hung with thousands of handwritten petitions and bells; buy a bell at the gate if you have a case

spots.name: Katarmal Sun Temple
spots.note: Ninth century sun temple above the Kosi, a 2 km climb from the road; ruined but the carved doorframe is intact, nobody there

spots.name: Nanda Devi Temple
spots.note: Chand era stone temple in the bazaar with carved panels; the September Nanda Devi fair takes over the whole lane

spots.name: Lala Bazaar
spots.note: Flagstoned bazaar of carved wooden shopfronts through the old town; buy bal mithai and singori, shops shut Sunday afternoon

spots.name: Bright End Corner
spots.note: Sunset ledge past the Vivekananda ashram on the ridge, the standard evening walk from town; 30 minutes each way on foot

name: Asan Conservation Reserve (Dakpathar)
tagline: Uttarakhand's Ramsar wetland where the Asan meets the Yamuna

why.winter: Dec to Feb is the whole point: ruddy shelduck, red crested pochard and 50 odd species on the water, cold still mornings at 4 to 20 C.
why.summer: March still holds late migrants; by May the Doon floor passes 40 C, the birds have gone north and the reserve is a hot mudflat.
why.monsoon: Jun to Aug the Yamuna runs high and brown, the barrage gates open and there is little to watch beyond egrets in sticky 35 C heat.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov the first waders and ducks drop in and the air clears; boating restarts and the Dakpathar canal walk is at its best.

vibe: A GMVN rest house and a few lodges at Dakpathar; birders with scopes at dawn, canal-side chai stalls, nothing after 9 pm
hub: Dehradun to Dakpathar 45 km by bus, about 1.5 h, then 4 km to the barrage; Jolly Grant airport 75 km

name: Auli
tagline: Uttarakhand's top ski slopes with Nanda Devi views
festival: Jan: Auli Winter Games

why.winter: Peak season: Uttarakhand's best skiing, snow slopes backed by views of Nanda Devi
why.summer: Green meadows and cable car views without snow. Pleasant, but skiing, the main draw, is gone
why.monsoon: The Joshimath approach road is landslide-prone and views fog out completely. Skip it
why.autumn: Clear and quiet before the snow arrives. Good for the cable car, no skiing yet though

vibe: Ski instructors and Delhi weekenders; here for slopes and cable car, not nightlife
hub: Fly Dehradun 280km or train Rishikesh, then 9-10h via Joshimath

spots.name: Auli Ropeway
spots.note: The 4 km gondola down to Joshimath, the quickest way in or out; runs about 9 to 5, shuts in wind, buy tickets early in season

spots.name: Gorson Bugyal
spots.note: Open meadow 3 km above the slopes, two hours return on a clear trail; Nanda Devi fills the skyline from the top ridge

spots.name: Auli Artificial Lake
spots.note: Man made tank that feeds the snow guns, with a path right round it; a 20 minute walk from the slopes, best in first light

spots.name: Chattrakund
spots.note: Small lake in oak and rhododendron past Gorson, about 4 km on from the meadow; carry water and food, nothing sold up there

spots.name: Narsingh Temple
spots.note: Badrinath's winter seat down in Joshimath, the deity's arm said to be thinning; morning aarti around 7, easy to combine

name: Badrinath & Mana
tagline: Char Dham shrine at 3100 m with Mana village 3 km on
festival: Apr/May: Badrinath kapat opening, date fixed at Basant Panchami

why.winter: December-March the portals are shut, the deity moves down to Joshimath, and the road above Hanumanchatti is closed by snow.
why.summer: May-June after the spring kapat opening is peak yatra: 5-18C, long darshan queues and every shop in Mana open for business.
why.monsoon: July-August the Alaknanda valley slides; the highway above Joshimath closes for hours or days and the yatra thins right out.
why.autumn: September-October is the best of it: clear Neelkanth peak, short queues, and the portals closing in the second half of November.

vibe: Pilgrim town with GMVN and dharamshala beds; walk 3 km to Mana for Bhotia weavers and the Saraswati gorge
hub: 295 km from Rishikesh, 12 h by bus via Joshimath; online Char Dham yatra registration is mandatory

spots.name: Badrinath Temple
spots.note: Char Dham shrine to Vishnu below Neelkanth peak; the 4.30 am maha abhishek needs a paid booking, doors shut November to April

spots.name: Tapt Kund
spots.note: Sulphur spring at about 45C on the steps below the temple; pilgrims bathe before darshan, separate hours for women

spots.name: Vyas Gufa
spots.note: Rock cave at Mana where the Mahabharata was dictated; the flaking roof looks like manuscript pages, small entry donation

spots.name: Bhim Pul
spots.note: Boulder slab bridging the Saraswati where it roars out of a slot at Mana; go before 10 am, yatra jeeps fill the lane

spots.name: Vasudhara Falls
spots.note: About 120 m fall reached by a 6 km walk past Mana over open moraine; no shade or water on the way, start by 7 am

spots.name: Brahma Kapal
spots.note: Flat rock on the Alaknanda where pandits perform pind daan for ancestors; rites run from first light, fix rates first

spots.name: Charanpaduka
spots.note: Boulder with a footprint of Vishnu, a steep 3 km climb from town; allow two hours return, the air at 3380 m is thin

name: Bageshwar
tagline: Saryu-Gomti confluence town and gateway to Pindari glacier
festival: Jan: Uttarayani Mela at the Bagnath temple

why.winter: December-February is 4-19C, and the week-long Uttarayani mela around 14 January turns the dry riverbed into a trading fair.
why.summer: March-April is warm and clear at 15-28C; May is hazier at 30C but is the other good window for the Pindari trek.
why.monsoon: June-August the Saryu runs dangerous and the Kapkot road to the Pindari trailhead slips; leave the glacier trek alone.
why.autumn: October-November is the classic Pindari and Kafni window, dry and cool, with the town itself pleasantly empty of pilgrims.

vibe: A working Kumaoni market town rather than a hill station: KMVN rest house, Pindari porters, cheap lodges by the Saryu
hub: Kathgodam railhead 165 km, 6 h by bus via Almora; Pindari trailhead at Loharkhet 40 km on by shared jeep

spots.name: Bagnath Temple
spots.note: Stone Shiva temple of 1450 at the Saryu and Gomti meeting point; the ghats below fill at dawn, shoes off at the gate

spots.name: Saryu Gomti Sangam
spots.note: Confluence ghats in the middle of town where the January Uttarayani fair sets up; the steps stay slippery all year

spots.name: Gauri Udyar
spots.note: Wide limestone cave on the Almora road holding Shiva idols; a caretaker unlocks the grille, carry your own torch

spots.name: Baijnath Temple
spots.note: Katyuri stone temples of the 12th century on the Gomti bank; shared jeeps to Kausani drop you at the gate, free entry

spots.name: Chandika Temple
spots.note: Kali shrine on the slope above town, busiest through Navratri; a ten minute climb from the bazaar opens the valley up

spots.name: Loharkhet
spots.note: Last road village on the Pindari trail with a KMVN hut and porters; shared jeeps leave Bageshwar in the morning only

name: Binsar
tagline: Quiet oak sanctuary with 200km Himalayan views

why.winter: Cold and occasionally snowy, oak forest is stark and beautiful, but interior roads can be tricky
why.summer: Pleasant and cool, good birdwatching season before the rains, moderate crowds
why.monsoon: Leeches, mud, and landslide-prone approach roads make this best avoided in the rains
why.autumn: Clearest views of the year, dry trails, peak season for the 200km Himalayan panorama

vibe: Near-silent forest: you'll likely have the trails and rest house to yourself
hub: Rail Kathgodam 120km, 4h taxi via Almora; no public bus inside

spots.name: Zero Point
spots.note: Wooden deck at the end of a 2 km forest walk with Nanda Devi to Kedarnath in one line; clearest at sunrise in winter

spots.name: Bineshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Chand era stone Shiva temple that gave Binsar its name; quiet all day, the road stops short so you walk the last bit

spots.name: Khali Estate
spots.note: Colonial commissioner's house on the ridge, later Uday Shankar's dance retreat; ask at reception to walk the gardens

name: Chakrata
tagline: Restricted cantonment near Delhi, untouched forest and falls

why.winter: Cold and often snowy above 2000m, roads to higher points like Deoban can close after heavy snow
why.summer: Pleasant, forested, and still nearly empty of tourists. A genuine off-the-radar escape
why.monsoon: Landslide-prone forest roads and a dangerously slippery Tiger Falls trail
why.autumn: Clear, dry, and the best time for the Tiger Falls hike and Deoban forest walks

vibe: Barely visited even by Indian tourists. Likely the only outsider at Tiger Falls
hub: Train Dehradun 90km, 3h taxi; foreigners need prior permission

spots.name: Tiger Falls
spots.note: Roughly 50 m fall in deodar forest, a 1.5 km walk down from the road head; the last stretch of track needs a jeep

spots.name: Deoban
spots.note: Dense deodar ridge at 2800 m looking at Swargarohini and the Bandarpunch wall; forest rest house, carry your own food

spots.name: Chilmiri Neck
spots.note: Grassy knoll above the cantonment for sunset over the Yamuna valley; walk up from the bazaar in about half an hour

spots.name: Budher Caves
spots.note: Limestone chambers on Moila Danda past Deoban, reached on foot through the forest; take a torch and a local guide

spots.name: Lakhamandal
spots.note: Old Shiva temple and stone sculpture yard above the Yamuna, tied to the Mahabharata lac house story; ASI site, free

name: Chaukori
tagline: Tea-garden ridge staring straight at the Panchachuli wall

why.winter: Dec-Feb is cold, often near freezing at night with occasional snow, but the Panchachuli sunrise is at its sharpest all year.
why.summer: Mar-Apr reddens the oaks with rhododendron and keeps the peaks clear most mornings; by May the haze slowly eats the massif.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is a washout: the Berinag and Thal roads slip, cloud sits on the ridge and the rest-house verandah stares at grey.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the reason to come: rinsed skies, gold light on terraced fields and the five Panchachuli summits burning at dawn.

vibe: KMVN rest-house verandah scene: chai, families on Kumaon circuits and photographers setting 5 am alarms
hub: Road only: Kathgodam rail is 170 km, 7-8 h via Almora and Berinag; KMOU buses and shared jeeps do it in hops

spots.name: Chaukori Tea Estate
spots.note: Small hillside garden below the rest house, plucking from April; the shop sells the leaf, ask before walking the rows

spots.name: Berinag
spots.note: Ridge town 10 km on that gave its name to a colonial era tea; the bazaar has the nearest ATM and the shared jeeps out

spots.name: Haat Kalika Temple
spots.note: Kali shrine at Gangolihat held as a shakti peeth and revered by the Kumaon Regiment; no photography in the inner hall

name: Chopta
tagline: Basecamp for the Tungnath-Chandrashila alpine trek

why.winter: Snow trekking to Chandrashila draws a niche crowd, but it's bitterly cold with tricky footing
why.summer: Prime trekking season: wildflower meadows, clear alpine views, good trail conditions
why.monsoon: Leeches, slippery trails, and landslide-hit approach roads make this the worst window to trek
why.autumn: Post-monsoon skies are clearest of the year. Arguably the best trekking weather here

vibe: Trekkers swap trail stories in tiny dhabas. Small but genuine traveler community
hub: Taxi/bus from Rishikesh or Haridwar 7-8h via Rudraprayag

spots.name: Tungnath Temple
spots.note: Highest Shiva temple in the world at 3680 m, a paved 3.5 km climb; the priest closes it and moves down in November

spots.name: Chandrashila
spots.note: Summit an hour above Tungnath at 4000 m with Nanda Devi and Trishul out front; leave Chopta by 5 am for clear air

spots.name: Deoria Tal
spots.note: Still lake that mirrors Chaukhamba, a 2.5 km climb from Sari village; camping is regulated, a day walk is simpler

spots.name: Kanchula Korak Musk Deer Sanctuary
spots.note: Mossy rhododendron forest on the Ukhimath road with a musk deer breeding enclosure; tickets at the gate hut

spots.name: Omkareshwar Temple
spots.note: Winter seat of Kedarnath and Madmaheshwar at Ukhimath; the idols arrive with a procession each November

name: Devprayag
tagline: Stone town stacked over the confluence where the Ganga begins

why.winter: Dec to Feb the gorge sits at 5 to 18 C, both rivers run clear and low, and the ghat steps under Raghunath temple stay empty.
why.summer: March is warm and clear; by May the rock gorge holds 38 C past noon, so walk down to the sangam at dawn and hide indoors after.
why.monsoon: Jun to Aug the Alaknanda runs brown and violent, the bathing steps are roped off and NH58 slides shut for hours; September clears.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov are the best weeks: the water turns green again, the air is clean enough for snow peaks, and buses run to time.

vibe: A handful of dharamshalas and river-view guest houses; pilgrim buses pass through and evenings belong to the priests and you
hub: Rishikesh 74 km along NH58 by bus or shared jeep, about 2.5 h; Rishikesh railhead, Dehradun airport 100 km

name: Dwarahat (Dunagiri)
tagline: Fifty odd Katyuri stone temples in a quiet Kumaon bazaar
festival: Apr: Syalde Bikhauti fair, drums through the bazaar

why.winter: Dec to Feb run 2 to 16 C with frost on the temple plinths, clear enough for Trishul from the Dunagiri ridge and nobody else about.
why.summer: March to May give the best light on the carved stone, 18 to 28 C, and the Syalde Bikhauti drums fill the bazaar in mid April.
why.monsoon: Jul and Aug soak the temple courtyards and put slides on the Ranikhet road; the moss and green are lovely if you can sit them out.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov are ideal: cold clean mornings, the Nanda Devi wall from Dunagiri and the eight temple groups completely empty.

vibe: A one street bazaar with two basic hotels and a KMVN; pilgrims bound for Dunagiri, students, no tourist scene at all
hub: Kathgodam railhead to Dwarahat about 5 h by bus via Ranikhet, or a 1 h shared jeep from Ranikhet

name: Ghuttu (Khatling Glacier)
tagline: Road end in the Bhilangana valley below Khatling glacier

why.winter: Dec to Feb the village is cold but open at 1540 m; the Sahastra Tal and Khatling routes above are under snow, so keep the walks low.
why.summer: May and June are the season: 12 to 24 C, the Bhilangana loud with melt and the five day walk to the Khatling snout finally clear.
why.monsoon: July and August close the Ghansali road with slides for days and make the stream crossings dangerous; September usually settles.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov bring the clearest air of the year over Thalaysagar and Jogin, cold nights and the homestays almost to yourself.

vibe: Two lodges, a forest rest house and a few homestays; porters, shepherds and no phone signal past the last shop
hub: Rishikesh to New Tehri by bus 4 h, then shared jeep through Ghansali to Ghuttu, 3 h more on a single lane road

name: Hanol (Mahasu Devta)
tagline: Ninth century Huna-style stone temple on the Tons river
festival: Aug/Sep: Jagra, a night of drums for Mahasu Devta

why.winter: Dec to Feb the Tons gorge runs 2 to 14 C, but the road up from Tyuni stays open and the deodar temple courtyard is yours alone.
why.summer: April and May are the pick: 18 to 28 C, deep deodar shade, the Tons still clear and Jaunsari villages busy with the wheat harvest.
why.monsoon: July and August cut the Chakrata to Tyuni road with slides for days at a stretch; June and September are green and usually passable.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov put clean light on the wooden village roofs and give the coldest, clearest river of the year, with almost no visitors.

vibe: One temple guest house, a dharamshala and two tea shops; you eat what the temple kitchen cooks and sleep to the river
hub: Dehradun to Tyuni by bus 7 h via Chakrata, then 8 km shared jeep to Hanol; the last jeep goes by mid afternoon

name: Haridwar
tagline: Har Ki Pauri, the ghat where the Ganga leaves the hills

why.winter: December-February is 6-22C with river fog at dawn; the 6 pm aarti is packed but the ghats empty out again by nine.
why.summer: March is fine at 20-32C, but by May-June it is 42C on open stone and the evening aarti crush becomes genuinely unpleasant.
why.monsoon: July-August the Ganga runs brown and dangerous, and the Kanwar Yatra puts millions of walking pilgrims on every road in.
why.autumn: October-November is the sweet spot: clean green water, 15-30C, and Rajaji's Chilla gate reopening for safaris mid-November.

vibe: Pilgrim-town intensity: dharamshalas, ashrams, a few hostels, sadhus, and Rishikesh backpackers passing through
hub: Haridwar Junction takes direct Delhi trains in 4-5 h; Jolly Grant airport 35 km; Rishikesh buses every 15 min

spots.name: Har Ki Pauri
spots.note: The main bathing ghat and Brahma Kund; the Ganga aarti fills it at dusk, come 45 minutes early for a step to sit on

spots.name: Mansa Devi Temple
spots.note: Hill shrine above the ghats by cable car or a 1.5 km paved climb; the queue is shortest before 8 am on weekdays

spots.name: Chandi Devi Temple
spots.note: Shrine on Neel Parvat across the river, a 3 km climb or a ropeway from Gauri Shankar; quieter than Mansa Devi

spots.name: Daksha Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Kankhal temple on the ground where Sati's father held his yagna; huge at Shivratri, a cheap autorickshaw from town

spots.name: Moti Bazaar
spots.note: Lane of brass puja pots, rudraksha and dried fruit running back from Har Ki Pauri; bargain hard, it shuts around 9 pm

spots.name: Chilla Range, Rajaji National Park
spots.note: Elephant forest on the far bank of the Ganga; morning jeep safaris book at the Chilla gate, shut through the monsoon

spots.name: Hoshiyar Puri
spots.note: Bara Bazaar counter serving puri with aloo and pumpkin since 1937; go before noon, they sell out and there is no menu

name: Harsil
tagline: Deodar and apple village on the Bhagirathi below Gangotri
festival: Apr/May: Gangotri portals open on Akshaya Tritiya

why.winter: December-March the highway above Harsil is snow-blocked, the Gangotri temple is shut and the village all but hibernates.
why.summer: May-June is Harsil at its best, 5-22C, apple orchards leafing out, with Gangotri 25 km on and the Char Dham rush in full flow.
why.monsoon: July-August is the Bhagirathi valley's landslide season; the highway above Uttarkashi has stranded pilgrims for days on end.
why.autumn: September-October is dry, gold and quiet after the yatra, with Gangotri's portals closing around Diwali in early November.

vibe: GMVN huts and a few homestays in an army-adjacent apple village; trekkers bound for Gaumukh, and very little else
hub: 73 km beyond Uttarkashi on the Gangotri highway, 3 h by bus or jeep; Dehradun railhead 250 km, 10 h in all

spots.name: Gangotri Temple
spots.note: Char Dham shrine on the Bhagirathi an hour up the highway; open Akshaya Tritiya to Diwali, shared jeeps go early

spots.name: Bagori
spots.note: Bhotia village of wooden houses across the river, home to Jadh traders of the old Tibet route; carpets woven at home

spots.name: Mukhwa
spots.note: Winter home of the Ganga idol, carried down from Gangotri each Diwali; a short walk from Harsil over the bridge

spots.name: Gartang Gali
spots.note: Wooden staircase pinned to a cliff on the old Tibet trade route past Lanka; forest office permit, limited daily slots

spots.name: Nelong Valley
spots.note: Cold desert beyond the Bhagirathi gorge, Indian nationals only on a day permit; no overnight stay, no fuel or food

name: Jageshwar
tagline: Over a hundred stone Shiva temples in a deodar gorge
festival: Feb/Mar: Maha Shivratri Mela at Jageshwar Dham

why.winter: December-February is 0-14C and the deodars drip; the Shivratri mela in February or March is the one time the gorge fills up.
why.summer: April-May is the best walking weather at 12-26C, with the whole 124-temple cluster to yourself on a weekday morning.
why.monsoon: July-August the Jataganga runs hard and the Almora road slips; the temples are atmospheric but the buses are unreliable.
why.autumn: October-November is dry and gold at 8-22C, and the KMVN rest house beside the temple wall is easy to get a bed in.

vibe: A single lane of dharamshalas and one KMVN rest house in a deodar gorge: pilgrims by day, total silence by night
hub: 36 km from Almora by bus or shared taxi, 1.5 h; Kathgodam railhead 125 km, Pantnagar airport 150 km

spots.name: Mrityunjaya Temple
spots.note: Oldest shrine in the deodar cluster, its lingam carved with an eye; the abhishek queue is longest through Shravan

spots.name: Jageshwar Archaeological Museum
spots.note: ASI room of Katyuri stone figures lifted from the temple yard; small ticket, shut Mondays, an hour is plenty

spots.name: Dandeshwar Temple
spots.note: Largest temple of the group, standing alone downstream among the deodars; usually empty, the caretaker opens on ask

spots.name: Vriddha Jageshwar
spots.note: Old Jageshwar on the ridge above, a 3 km climb through oak; the Himalayan line shows on clear mornings, carry water

name: Jim Corbett (Ramnagar)
tagline: India's oldest tiger reserve, entered from Ramnagar town

why.winter: December-February is 5-24C with fog until nine; Dhikala's grasslands are open and elephant sightings are close to certain.
why.summer: April-June gives the best tiger odds at the shrinking water holes, but it is 40-43C by noon and Dhikala shuts around 15 June.
why.monsoon: July-September the core zones close for breeding and the Ramganga floods; only the Jhirna and Dhela buffers stay open.
why.autumn: Bijrani reopens on 15 October and Dhikala on 15 November, and the sal forest is at its greenest and cleanest after the rains.

vibe: Safari-lodge country where a solo traveller must share a gypsy; Ramnagar has cheap hotels and the booking office
hub: Ramnagar takes overnight Delhi trains in 6 h and buses from Haldwani 65 km; book Dhikala permits online early

spots.name: Dhikala Zone
spots.note: Core grassland zone with the best tiger odds; day visitors only on the canter tour, forest rest house beds go months out

spots.name: Bijrani Zone
spots.note: Sal forest zone entered at Amdanda near town, the easy morning jeep out of Ramnagar; shut through the monsoon months

spots.name: Garjiya Devi Temple
spots.note: Shrine on a rock island in the Kosi, up steep steps from the bank; evening aarti, the river runs high in monsoon

spots.name: Jhirna Zone
spots.note: The zone that stays open all year, sloth bear and deer more than tiger; the fallback when the core is shut in rains

spots.name: Sitabani Forest Reserve
spots.note: Buffer forest outside the reserve booking system, good for birds and an old Ram temple; tracks are rough after rain

spots.name: Corbett Falls
spots.note: Small fall in sal forest off the Kaladhungi road, five minutes from the gate; thin outside monsoon, small ticket

spots.name: Corbett Museum
spots.note: Jim Corbett's winter bungalow at Kaladhungi, now a museum of his guns, letters and photographs; small ticket, an hour

name: Kanatal
tagline: Deodar ridge of apple orchards and campfires above the Tehri valley
festival: May/Jun: Ganga Dussehra mela at Surkanda Devi (dates shift)

why.winter: Dec-Feb brings real snowfalls at 2400 m; many tent camps shut, so book a cottage, carry chains for icy bends and enjoy the quiet.
why.summer: Apr-May is the sweet spot: 12-25 °C, orchard bloom and buzzing weekend campsites while the plains cook 2000 m below.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is fog, leeches and slips on the Chamba road and most camps close; Jun and Sep are usable between showers.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is peak-clear: Bandarpunch and the Gangotri peaks line the horizon from Surkanda Devi and nights dip near freezing.

vibe: Delhi weekenders around bonfires, one small backpacker hostel, and quiet orchard homestays a lane off the road
hub: Dehradun (Jolly Grant) airport 80 km, about 2.5 h; buses Rishikesh to Chamba then 12 km taxi; rail is 3 h out

spots.name: Surkanda Devi Temple
spots.note: Shakti peeth at 2757 m above Kaddukhal, a 1.5 km climb or the ropeway; the Himalayan line clears right after rain

spots.name: Dhanaulti Eco Park
spots.note: Deodar and oak park at Amber and Deolsari with rope walks and benches; small ticket, weekends fill with families

spots.name: Tehri Lake at Koti Colony
spots.note: Reservoir jetty for boats and jet skis under the dam; an hour down by taxi, rates are fixed at the counter

spots.name: Kaudia Forest
spots.note: Pine and deodar range below the road with a jungle trail and a mountain bike track; no signage, take someone local

spots.name: Chamba
spots.note: Junction bazaar where the Mussoorie and Rishikesh roads meet; nearest ATMs, chemist and shared jeeps, busy till 8 pm

name: Kartik Swami (Kanakchauri)
tagline: Knife-edge ridge shrine with 360 degree Garhwal snow peaks
festival: Nov: Kartik Purnima all-night vigil at the shrine

why.winter: Dec to Feb the ridge runs 0 to 12 C with snow on the last kilometre now and then; the payoff is the cleanest Chaukhamba view of the year.
why.summer: March and April are mild and clear; by late May haze off the plains softens the peaks, so start the 3 km climb well before sunrise.
why.monsoon: Jul and Aug wrap the ridge in cloud, the stone path turns slick and the Rudraprayag road slides; September usually gives the view back.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov are the best: sunrise from the shrine picks out Trishul, Nanda Devi and the Kedar dome, and Kanakchauri homestays stay warm.

vibe: Six or seven homestays in Kanakchauri and one tea stall at the top; most people walk up at 5 am and are gone by nine
hub: Rudraprayag to Kanakchauri 38 km by shared jeep, 1.5 h, then a 3 km stone path; Rishikesh railhead about 5 h

name: Kausani
tagline: 300km Himalayan skyline view, Gandhi's hill retreat

why.winter: Clearest Himalayan panorama of the year. Snow peaks framed against clear skies, cold but worth it
why.summer: Pleasant and green in March-April; May warms up but stays a calmer escape than Nainital
why.monsoon: Clouds hide the entire reason to visit, the mountain view, plus landslide risk en route
why.autumn: Post-monsoon clarity makes this peak season for the panoramic view Kausani is famous for

vibe: Mostly honeymooners chasing sunrise views; solo travelers may find few peers here
hub: Rail Kathgodam 135km, then 4-5h taxi via Almora; no direct air/rail

spots.name: Anasakti Ashram
spots.note: The 1929 house where Gandhi wrote his Gita commentary, now a small museum and ashram; prayers at 6 pm, entry free

spots.name: Kausani Tea Estate
spots.note: Organic garden on the Baijnath road with a tasting counter and shop; plucking April to October, free to walk in

spots.name: Baijnath Temple
spots.note: Katyuri stone temples of about 1150 beside the Gomti with a fine Parvati image; Bageshwar buses stop at the gate

spots.name: Sumitranandan Pant Museum
spots.note: The poet's birth house in the old village, kept with his manuscripts and glasses; small ticket, twenty minutes

spots.name: Rudradhari Falls
spots.note: Fall and cave shrine in the pines past Kausani, a 2 km walk in from the road; slippery in monsoon, no shop en route

name: Kedarnath
tagline: Himalayan Shiva shrine at 3583m, open just 6 months
festival: Apr/May: Kapat opening ceremony

why.winter: Closed entirely: the temple shuts around early November and the deity moves to Ukhimath
why.summer: May-June is prime pilgrimage season before the monsoon; trails are clear, temple newly reopened
why.monsoon: Technically open but this is landslide and flash-flood country. The 2013 disaster hit in this window
why.autumn: September-October is the second great window. Thinning crowds, temple closes by early November

vibe: Shoulder-to-shoulder with pilgrims on the climb. Devotion, not a party circuit
hub: Bus/taxi to Sonprayag 9-10h, jeep to Gaurikund, 16km trek or heli

spots.name: Adi Shankaracharya Samadhi
spots.note: Rebuilt shrine and 12 ft statue right behind the main temple where Shankara is said to have died; free, open all day.

spots.name: Bhairavnath Temple
spots.note: Half hour climb on the ridge south of the shrine, guardian of Kedarnath and the best view of the valley; go at first light.

spots.name: Bhim Shila
spots.note: The house sized boulder that split the 2013 flood and saved the temple behind it; five minutes on foot, always open.

spots.name: Chorabari Tal (Gandhi Sarovar)
spots.note: Glacial lake about 3 km above town, two hours up; ask at the police post first, the 2013 breach still closes the trail.

spots.name: Vasuki Tal
spots.note: High lake at 4135 m, a hard six hour round trip from town; only for acclimatised walkers, start by 6 am with a guide.

spots.name: Gaurikund
spots.note: Trailhead village at the foot of the 16 km climb, with the Gauri temple and a sulphur spring; jeeps shuttle to Sonprayag.

spots.name: Triyuginarayan Temple
spots.note: Village temple where Shiva married Parvati, its fire pit still burning; 12 km up from Sonprayag, an easy taxi detour.

name: Khati (Pindari Glacier)
tagline: Last village on the Pindari trail, 6 km past the road head

why.winter: Dec to Feb the Dhakuri pass above Khati fills with snow and the Pindari trail closes; the village lives on but there is no walking.
why.summer: May and June are the season: rhododendron below Dhakuri, 10 to 22 C, and the walk on towards the glacier snout is clear of snow.
why.monsoon: July and August wash out the Bageshwar to Kharkiya road and put leeches on every step; June is fine and September dries quickly.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov give the hardest, clearest views of Nanda Kot from Dhakuri, cold nights and near empty rest houses all the way up.

vibe: Homestays and a KMVN rest house in a slate-roof village; porters, a school and no road noise because there is no road
hub: Bageshwar to Kharkiya 36 km by shared jeep, 2 h, then 6 km on foot to Khati; Kathgodam railhead is 8 h back

name: Khirsu
tagline: Hushed oak and deodar ridge facing a wall of Garhwal snow peaks

why.winter: Dec-Feb is cold, crisp and empty: frosty mornings, the sharpest Chaukhamba views of the year, and a GMVN rest house that barely fills.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is peak: rhododendron flares through the oak forest and the snow wall stays clear at dawn before May haze blurs it.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug means landslide-prone bends on the Pauri road and a fog bank where the panorama should be; give the ridge a miss.
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the classic window: rinsed post-monsoon skies, warm walking days and the full Garhwal snow line from the sunset point.

vibe: A sleepy GMVN-and-homestay hamlet of birdsong and apple orchards; expect two other guests, not a scene
hub: Road only: buses Rishikesh to Srinagar or Pauri (4-5 h), then 19 km shared jeep; Dehradun airport 150 km

spots.name: Ghandiyal Devta Temple
spots.note: Small stone shrine to the local guardian god in the deodar grove at the edge of the village; five minutes on foot, no fee.

spots.name: Kandoliya Temple
spots.note: Pine forest shrine on the ridge above Pauri with an open air theatre and a snow skyline; catch the last shared jeep back.

spots.name: Kyunkaleshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Old Shiva temple below Pauri linked to Adi Shankara, quiet stone courtyard; pair it with a run into the Pauri bazaar.

spots.name: Dhari Devi Temple
spots.note: Riverside Kali shrine now raised on pillars over the Alaknanda past Srinagar; go early, the afternoon buses fill up.

name: Lansdowne
tagline: Sleepy Garhwal Rifles cantonment, refreshingly untouristy

why.winter: Cold, foggy mornings, occasional light snow: quiet and atmospheric, some cafes shut
why.summer: Cool pine-forest air, a favorite quick escape from Delhi's heat without Mussoorie's crowds
why.monsoon: June still works; Jul-Sep brings 200-425mm a month and Garhwal's landslide season cuts the Kotdwar ghat road - don't come.
why.autumn: Clear skies and comfortable temperatures. The best weather window of the year

vibe: Empty pine roads and military-town hush. Solitude more than social mixing
hub: Train to Kotdwar 40km, then 1.5h taxi or shared jeep up

spots.name: Tip-in-Top
spots.note: Ridge lookout ten minutes above the Mall with a tea stall and a Himalayan line on clear mornings; walk up, do not drive.

spots.name: Darwan Singh Sangrahalaya
spots.note: Garhwal Rifles regimental museum of 1887 uniforms, medals and captured kit; small ticket at the gate, no photos inside.

spots.name: Bhulla Tal
spots.note: Little army built lake with pedal boats and a cafe, named for the regiment's younger brothers; ticketed, shuts at dusk.

spots.name: St. Mary's Church
spots.note: Deconsecrated 1896 garrison church on a spur, now a small war gallery with a light and sound show; ticket at the door.

spots.name: Tarkeshwar Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple in a deodar forest at 2100 m, a cold quiet drive of about 90 minutes; carry cash, no shops past Jaiharikhal.

name: Madhyamaheshwar (Ransi)
tagline: Panch Kedar shrine at 3450 m, 16 km on foot above Ransi
festival: May: the doli walks up from Ukhimath to open the shrine

why.winter: Dec to Mar the shrine is shut, the deity sits down in Ukhimath and the last 8 km hold deep snow; there is nothing open to walk to.
why.summer: March and April the shrine is still shut and the upper trail snowbound; May opens it, rhododendron above Gaundar, 12 to 20 C and freezing nights at 3450 m.
why.monsoon: June is green and fine. July and August bring leeches, slides on the Ukhimath road and cloud over Chaukhamba; September dries out.
why.autumn: October is the sharpest month here, cold clear air and half empty huts; the shrine closes around Bhai Dooj in Nov, so check the date.

vibe: Homestays at Ransi and Gaundar, then dharamshalas and a GMVN hut at the temple; a dozen walkers a day in season
hub: Ukhimath to Ransi 25 km by shared jeep, 1.5 h, then 16 km on foot via Bantoli and Gaundar, 6 to 7 h

name: Malari (Niti Valley)
tagline: Last open Bhotia village on the road up to the Niti pass

why.winter: Dec to Mar the families move down to Ghat and Joshimath, the stone houses are padlocked and the road above Tapovan closes with snow.
why.summer: May and June are the season: 8 to 20 C, barley in the terraces, Bhotia families back home and the Dhauli valley road open to Malari.
why.monsoon: June stays clear. July and August bring the worst slides on the Joshimath to Malari road and army convoys go first; September clears.
why.autumn: October is the best month, cold nights, gold willows and hard blue sky over the Niti ridge; by mid November the village empties again.

vibe: A dozen homestays and a rest house among stone and slate houses; army trucks, shepherds and long silent evenings
hub: Joshimath to Malari 62 km by shared jeep, about 3 h; carry ID, the checkpost logs everyone past Tapovan

name: Mukteshwar
tagline: Laid-back orchard town with cliff views and paragliding

why.winter: Cold, clear, occasional snow: great for cozy homestays and unbroken Himalayan views
why.summer: Pleasant weather and the peak season for paragliding and rock climbing here
why.monsoon: Green and dramatic cloud views, but slippery cliffs raise the risk for outdoor activities
why.autumn: Crisp, clear, and quieter than summer: arguably the best all-round window

vibe: Weekend paragliders from Delhi/Bengaluru; friendly, not much of a hostel scene
hub: Rail Kathgodam 50km, 2h taxi; easy day trip from Nainital

spots.name: Mukteshwar Dham
spots.note: The 350 year old Shiva temple the town is named for, on the cliff top at 2315 m; a short flight of steps, best at sunrise.

spots.name: Chauli Ki Jali
spots.note: Sheer rock ledge right behind the temple, also used for rappelling and rock climbing; the railings are thin, mind the edge.

spots.name: Bhalu Gaad Waterfall
spots.note: Forest waterfall past Dhanachuli, about a 1 km walk down from the road; small entry fee, slippery after rain.

spots.name: Indian Veterinary Research Institute
spots.note: Colonial 1893 research campus of stone buildings, lawns and a small museum; sign in at the gate, weekday mornings only.

spots.name: Dhanachuli
spots.note: Quiet orchard village 20 minutes on, terraced fields and a long snow line; the onward road to Peora is the pretty one.

name: Munsiyari
tagline: Remote gateway to Panchachuli peaks and glacier treks

why.winter: Snowbound and beautiful in December, but January-February often cuts off roads and shuts guesthouses
why.summer: April-May is prime trekking season; March is still cold as roads reopen after winter
why.monsoon: June is calm before the storm; July-September bring landslides that regularly cut the remote road
why.autumn: October is prime: post-monsoon clarity gives the best Panchachuli views; November turns cold fast

vibe: A trekking basecamp of serious hikers; guesthouse owners become your main company
hub: Fly Kathgodam, then 8-9h drive via Almora; shared jeeps run

spots.name: Khaliya Top
spots.note: Meadow at 3500 m facing the Panchachuli wall, 6 km of road to Balati then a 3 km climb; snow shuts it December to March.

spots.name: Tribal Heritage Museum
spots.note: One man's collection of Johar valley Bhotia tools, wool and trade relics at Nanasem; knock at the house, small donation.

spots.name: Thamri Kund
spots.note: Small forest lake above town where musk deer drink at dawn; take a local guide, the last 2 km is a walking track only.

spots.name: Nanda Devi Temple
spots.note: Stone temple on the spur above the bazaar, the best free spot for the Panchachuli sunrise; ten minutes uphill on foot.

spots.name: Birthi Falls
spots.note: 126 m fall beside the Thal road, worth a stop on the way in or out; 5 minutes from the tea stall, heaviest after the rains.

name: Mussoorie
tagline: Colonial 'Queen of the Hills', Delhi's easiest escape

why.winter: Cold and foggy, occasional snow draws a niche crowd, but many cafes shut for the season
why.summer: Peak season: Delhi's classic heat escape, great weather but Mall Road gets packed
why.monsoon: Heavy rain and landslide-prone roads from Dehradun make the hillside genuinely risky
why.autumn: Best all-round window: clear skies, comfortable temperatures, fewer crowds than summer

vibe: Honeymooners throng Mall Road; solo travelers drift to quieter Landour nearby
hub: Fly/train Dehradun 35km, then 1h taxi up the hill

spots.name: Char Dukan, Landour
spots.note: Four tea shops at the top of Landour doing pancakes and ginger lemon honey; walk up from Picture Palace, about 45 minutes.

spots.name: Camel's Back Road
spots.note: Flat 3 km walk from Kulri bazaar to the Library round the ridge, past a rock camel and the old cemetery; go at sunset.

spots.name: Gun Hill
spots.note: Second highest point in town, reached by a short ropeway off the Mall or a 20 minute path; hazy by noon, so go early.

spots.name: Lal Tibba
spots.note: Highest point at Landour with a paid telescope deck facing Bandarpunch; clearest in the hour after sunrise, then it hazes.

spots.name: George Everest House
spots.note: The Surveyor General's estate on a windy spur, restored as a museum; 6 km past the Library, last stretch better on foot.

spots.name: Kempty Falls
spots.note: The famous roadside fall, commercial and packed but a cold plunge pool; get there before 10 am or skip it in season.

spots.name: Company Garden
spots.note: Municipal garden with a boating pond and an aviary, family heavy; ticketed, 20 minutes by shared taxi from the Mall.

name: Nag Tibba
tagline: Weekend snow summit at 3020 m above Pantwari village

why.winter: December-March is the point of this trek: knee-deep snow on the ridge, -5C at camp, and Bandarpoonch clear to the north.
why.summer: April-May still works at 10-22C, but haze off the plains flattens the summit view and the water sources start running low.
why.monsoon: July-August is a leech-ridden slog with real lightning risk on the open ridge and slides on the Dehradun-Pantwari road.
why.autumn: October-November is the other good window: dry ground, cold nights and a completely uncluttered Gangotri-group skyline.

vibe: The easiest real Himalayan snow trek out of Delhi; weekend groups from Dehradun, homestays and camps at Pantwari
hub: Pantwari trailhead 90 km, 3.5 h from Dehradun by bus or jeep; 4 km climb to base camp, 3 km more to the summit

spots.name: Nag Tibba Temple
spots.note: Serpent god shrine in the clearing below the summit ridge that gives the peak its name; shepherds still leave offerings.

spots.name: Pantwari
spots.note: Trailhead village of homestays and the last shop for supplies; the 4 km climb to base camp starts behind the school.

spots.name: Devalsari
spots.note: Deodar forest hamlet on the Thatyur side with an old Mahadev temple and a butterfly count each June; the quieter way up.

spots.name: Nainbagh
spots.note: Highway junction where the Dehradun buses drop you, with shared jeeps for the last climb to Pantwari; go before dark.

name: Nainital
tagline: Colonial lake town, Kumaon's biggest tourist magnet
festival: Sep: Nanda Devi Mela

why.winter: Cold, sometimes snowy: pretty around the lake but many hotels half-shut, mornings misty
why.summer: Peak crowds fleeing plains heat; book ahead, expect queues for the boat ride
why.monsoon: Frequent landslides on the approach roads and leeches on trails. Best skipped
why.autumn: Post-monsoon air clears for the climb to Naina Peak at 2,615 m; days hold 19C but November nights hit 6C and shops shut early.

vibe: Boating families crowd the lake; solo travelers escape to quieter Naina Peak trails
hub: Rail Kathgodam 35km or overnight Delhi bus 7-8h to town

spots.name: Naina Devi Temple
spots.note: Shakti peeth on the north shore where the goddess's eyes are said to have fallen; aarti at dusk, shoes off at the gate.

spots.name: Naina Peak
spots.note: Highest point above the lake at 2615 m, a 6 km climb through oak from Mallital, two hours up; ponies wait at the start.

spots.name: Tiffin Top
spots.note: Also called Dorothy's Seat, a rock terrace over the lake reached by a 4 km walk or pony from Mallital; go for sunset.

spots.name: Snow View Point
spots.note: Ropeway from Mallital to a 2270 m deck facing Nanda Devi; book the return slot, the queue gets long after 11 am.

spots.name: Hanuman Garhi
spots.note: Hilltop temple on the Kaladhungi road known for its sunset view; open from dawn to about 9 pm, ten minutes by shared taxi.

spots.name: Pangot
spots.note: Birding hamlet past Kilbury where the road runs through oak and the koklass pheasant lives; hire a guide for the dawn walk.

spots.name: Nainital Raj Bhavan
spots.note: The Governor's gothic house and golf course, open to visitors on ticket; carry ID and check the day, it shuts for VIPs.

name: Patal Bhuvaneshwar
tagline: Torchlit limestone cave shrine sunk 90 ft into a Kumaon ridge

why.winter: Dec-Feb is cold and pin-quiet: the cave stays open outside the monsoon shutdown, queues vanish and ridge views sharpen towards the snows.
why.summer: Mar-Apr pairs the cave with rhododendron ridge walks; even May works since the 90 ft descent stays cool while the valleys bake.
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep is a write-off: authorities shut the cave for much of the monsoon (low oxygen, slick rock) and the Gangolihat road slips.
why.autumn: The cave reopens by mid Oct after the monsoon closure: dry rock, clear snow-peak views from the ridge and short queues into Nov.

vibe: Priest-led torch descents past stone serpent formations; sleep at the KMVN rest house or a village homestay
hub: Road only: Kathgodam rail 190 km, about 8 h via Almora and Gangolihat; shared jeeps cover the last 14 km

spots.name: Haat Kalika Temple
spots.note: Gangolihat's Mahakali peeth in a cedar grove, kuldevi of the Kumaon Regiment; a bed is made up for the goddess nightly.

spots.name: Gangolihat
spots.note: Nearest bazaar and jeep junction for cash, a chemist and a hot meal; the last jeep back to the cave leaves by evening.

spots.name: Kotgari Devi Temple
spots.note: Justice goddess near Thal where people file written appeals on stamped paper; a long shared jeep ride out via Berinag.

name: Raithal (Dayara Bugyal)
tagline: Slate-roof village under the Dayara meadow and Bandarpunch

why.winter: Dec to Feb Raithal sits in snow above the Bhagirathi and the 8 km climb to Dayara becomes a snow walk; homestays run stoves and quilts.
why.summer: April and May clear the meadow and fill it with primula and shepherds moving up; days 15 to 22 C, nights still close to freezing.
why.monsoon: Jul and Aug bring leeches, cloud and slides on the Uttarkashi road and the bugyal stays hidden; June and September are walkable.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov are the sharpest weeks of the year: Bandarpunch and Srikanth stand clear above the meadow and the village is quiet.

vibe: About twenty homestays in a stone village; trek groups pass through, and after 8 pm it is dogs, woodsmoke and the ridge
hub: Dehradun to Uttarkashi by bus 7 h, then 45 km shared jeep via Bhatwari to Raithal, about 2 h

name: Ranikhet
tagline: Kumaon Regiment cantonment with pine golf links and Nanda Devi

why.winter: December-February is 1-15C with the occasional snowfall; the Chaubatia orchards are bare but the high peaks are clearest.
why.summer: April-May is 12-27C under deodar and oak, a real escape from Haldwani's 40C, and still far quieter than Nainital.
why.monsoon: July-August brings 400 mm months, leeches on the Jhula Devi walk and cloud that hides the range for a week at a stretch.
why.autumn: October-November is the peak: dry, 8-22C, and Nanda Devi and Trishul standing up clean on the skyline every morning.

vibe: An army town that stayed low-key: KMVN rest houses, orchard homestays, walkers rather than a lakeside boating crowd
hub: Kathgodam railhead 75 km, 3 h by bus or shared taxi; Pantnagar airport 110 km; buses from Almora 50 km

spots.name: Jhula Devi Temple
spots.note: Bell covered Durga shrine on the Chaubatia road where a granted wish is repaid with a new bell; buy one at the stalls.

spots.name: Chaubatia Gardens
spots.note: Government fruit orchards of apple, apricot and peach with a snow line behind; ticketed, blossom in April, fruit in July.

spots.name: Kumaon Regimental Centre Museum
spots.note: Regimental weapons, uniforms and Param Vir stories from 1813 on; small ticket, carry ID, shut on gazetted holidays.

spots.name: Upat Kalika Golf Course
spots.note: Nine hole course at 1800 m ringed by pines, clubs on hire for a day green fee; walkers can use the road along it.

spots.name: Haidakhan Babaji Temple
spots.note: Hillside ashram at Chilianaula with a quiet white temple and long views; visitors welcome, keep silence at the fire puja.

spots.name: Bhalu Dam
spots.note: Small stone dam past Chaubatia with a still green pool and pines around it; 10 minutes in from the road, carry water.

name: Rishikesh
tagline: Yoga capital and rafting hub on the Ganges
festival: Mar: International Yoga Festival

why.winter: Cool crisp days, clear Himalayan views from Kunjapuri, yoga ashrams at their calmest
why.summer: March is pleasant, but April-May heat climbs fast and the ghats fill with day-trippers
why.monsoon: Ganges swells brown and dangerous, rafting suspended, landslide risk on the Badrinath road
why.autumn: Best window of the year. Rafting resumes, skies clear, the whole backpacker scene wakes up

vibe: Zostel dorms full of backpackers doing yoga by day, riverside chai by night
hub: Fly Dehradun 35km or overnight Delhi bus 6-7h; local auto-rickshaw

spots.name: Triveni Ghat
spots.note: The main bathing steps in town where the Ganga aarti is sung at dusk; free, get there by 6 pm for a place on the steps.

spots.name: Parmarth Niketan
spots.note: Ashram ghat at Swarg Ashram with the big Shiva statue and a lamp lit aarti sung by resident boys; free, sit down early.

spots.name: Beatles Ashram
spots.note: Maharishi's abandoned Chaurasi Kutia, graffiti covered domes inside Rajaji forest; ticketed, gates about 10 am to 4 pm.

spots.name: Lakshman Jhula
spots.note: The 1929 suspension bridge, shut to walkers since 2019; cross on Ram Jhula or the newer Janki Setu and shoot it from there.

spots.name: Shivpuri
spots.note: Put in point for the standard 16 km raft back to town, grade 3 in season; agencies bus you up, closed in the monsoon.

spots.name: Neer Garh Waterfall
spots.note: Three tiered fall above Lakshman Jhula, 20 minutes uphill from the road; small ticket, the pools are best after rain.

spots.name: Vashishta Gufa
spots.note: Meditation cave by the Ganga on the Badrinath road, silence inside and a sand beach below; buses drop you at the gate.

spots.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
spots.note: Shiva temple at 1330 m in the hills behind town, 32 km by road or a 12 km forest walk; Mondays and Shivratri are mobbed.

name: Sankri (Har Ki Dun)
tagline: Govind park trailhead for Har Ki Dun and Kedarkantha

why.winter: December-February Sankri is the Kedarkantha base: snow from the village up, -5C nights, and every homestay booked out.
why.summer: May-June is Har Ki Dun season at 8-22C, rhododendron on the lower ridges and the Swargarohini wall closing the valley head.
why.monsoon: July-August the Tons valley road from Purola slips badly and the Har Ki Dun trail turns into leech-ridden mud all the way.
why.autumn: October-November is the cleanest trekking window of the year: dry trail, cold nights, and no fresh snow above 3000 m yet.

vibe: A one-street trailhead village of homestays and trek outfitters; you will find a group to join within a day of arriving
hub: 200 km and 9-10 h by bus from Dehradun via Purola; Govind sanctuary permit issued at the Sankri forest office

spots.name: Kedarkantha
spots.note: 3810 m summit, the classic two night snow climb from Sankri via Juda ka Talab; December to April for snow, guides in village.

spots.name: Juda Ka Talab
spots.note: Forest lake and campground a 4 km climb above the village, fine as a half day walk; it freezes over in January.

spots.name: Taluka
spots.note: Road head for the Har Ki Dun trail, shared jeeps grind the rough 12 km from Sankri; the last one back leaves by mid day.

spots.name: Osla
spots.note: Old wooden village above the Supin with the Someshwar Mahadev temple; on the trail, homestays but no shop, carry cash.

spots.name: Mori
spots.note: Tons river rafting base downstream, grade 3 to 4 water in May and June; the drive out to Dehradun passes through it.

name: Sattal
tagline: Seven linked lakes hidden in an oak and pine bowl full of birds

why.winter: Dec-Feb is birding prime: 200-plus species around the lakes, mist lifting off Garud Tal at dawn and mild 5-20 °C days.
why.summer: Mar still delivers birds; by Apr-May the water turns picnic-green and warm, with kayaks out and Bhimtal day-trippers at the main ghat.
why.monsoon: Jul-Aug is leech-and-landslide season on the Bhimtal approach and the lakeside trails turn to slick clay; sit it out.
why.autumn: Oct rinses the forest and Nov opens the winter bird season; weekdays are properly quiet before the Christmas holiday rush.

vibe: Dawn birders with scopes, 1930s church-camp lawns, students kayaking; evenings go properly silent
hub: Kathgodam rail 23 km (1 h), Pantnagar airport 60 km (1.5 h); bus to Bhimtal then 4 km taxi or walk in

spots.name: Sattal Christian Ashram
spots.note: Stone cottages and lawns of a 1930s mission camp beside the lakes; day visitors can walk the grounds, rooms book direct.

spots.name: Nal Damayanti Tal
spots.note: Small oak ringed pool up a 30 minute climb from the Sattal road; empty on weekdays and no shops at all, carry water.

spots.name: Naukuchiatal
spots.note: Nine cornered lake with kayaks and a paragliding landing field; quieter than Bhimtal, boats are charged by the hour.

spots.name: Butterfly Research Centre, Bhimtal
spots.note: Peter Smetacek's Himalayan butterfly collection at Jones Estate; small fee, call ahead because the hours are erratic.

spots.name: Bhimtal Lake
spots.note: Biggest lake of the group, with an island aquarium and cafe; pedal boats from the ghat, busiest 11 am to 4 pm.

spots.name: Ghorakhal Golu Devta Temple
spots.note: Hill shrine hung with thousands of brass bells and written petitions; open dawn to dusk, shared taxis run from Bhowali.

name: Valley of Flowers
tagline: UNESCO alpine meadow of rare flora, open Jul-Sep only

why.winter: Completely closed: the park and trek route are buried under snow from October to May
why.summer: Still closed; snowmelt is only beginning and the trail isn't passable until June at earliest
why.monsoon: The only real window: park opens in June but flowers aren't out yet; peak bloom is Jul-Aug, fading by mid-Sep
why.autumn: Closes by early October as snow returns. At most the first days are viable, don't risk it

vibe: Trekkers and Hemkund Sahib pilgrims share the trail. Good camaraderie in Ghangaria
hub: Drive Rishikesh to Govindghat 10h, trek 14km to Ghangaria (permit)

spots.name: Hemkund Sahib
spots.note: Sikh shrine at 4300 m by a glacial lake, 6 km of steep steps above Ghangaria; start by 6 am, it shuts in early October.

spots.name: Pulna
spots.note: Shared jeeps from Govindghat stop here and the walk up begins; last mule hire and last cheap tea before the climb.

spots.name: Bhyundar Village
spots.note: Last hamlet on the trail with tea and maggi in season only; it is the last shade before the steep pull to Ghangaria.

spots.name: Govindghat Gurudwara
spots.note: Roadhead gurudwara on the Alaknanda with free langar and dorm beds; leave surplus luggage here before walking up.

name: Wan (Bedni Bugyal)
tagline: Road-end village below the Ali and Bedni meadows
festival: Apr/May: the Latu Devta temple opens for its one day

why.winter: Dec to Feb snow reaches the village and the meadow walk turns into a snow trek; homestays keep going but the last jeep is unreliable.
why.summer: April and May melt the bugyal clear, shepherds bring the flocks up and the 6 km climb to Ali puts Trishul and Nanda Ghunti head on.
why.monsoon: July and August mean leeches, cloud and slides on the Tharali road; June is green and fine and September dries into good walking.
why.autumn: Oct and Nov are the classic weeks: the grass goes gold, nights drop below zero and the peaks stay out from dawn to dusk.

vibe: Stone houses, a few homestays and the Latu Devta temple; trek groups in season, otherwise farmers, sheep and dogs
hub: Rishikesh to Debal or Tharali by bus 9 h, then shared jeep via Lohajung to Wan, about 2 h more

name: Ajodhya Hills (Purulia)
tagline: Purulia plateau of palash red, Chhau masks and stone falls

why.winter: Cold enough for a jacket at 575 m; clear plateau air, Bamni and Turga falls low but walkable, and very few outsiders.
why.summer: March is the palash bloom that turns whole hillsides orange-red; from April Purulia bakes past 44 C and is unsafe.
why.monsoon: June sits at 44 C before the break; Jul-Sep the falls finally run but plateau roads wash out and leeches own the trails.
why.autumn: October is the green-and-clear month once the rains go; November onward it keeps improving into the winter peak.

vibe: Cyclists, climbers on the Matha rock faces and mask buyers at Charida; homestays and eco-huts only, no hostels.
hub: Purulia station (5 h from Howrah), then 45 km by bus or shared jeep to Ajodhya Hilltop; nothing after dark.

spots.name: Charida Mask Village
spots.note: Chhau mask makers' street near Baghmundi; watch the clay and paper layers dry and buy straight from the workshops.

spots.name: Bamni Falls
spots.note: Falls in a rock gorge below the hilltop, roughly 450 steps down and a hard climb back; only worth it after the rains.

spots.name: Turga Falls
spots.note: Stream falls and a small dam under the plateau, best July to October; the last stretch is a rough walk from the road.

spots.name: Marble Lake
spots.note: Flooded quarry of green water and pale cut walls, five minutes off the Ajodhya road; no railing, the sides drop fast.

spots.name: Khairabera Dam
spots.note: Quiet reservoir under the Matha rock faces where climbers camp; one eco resort and no shops, carry food for the day.

name: Bakkhali & Henry Island
tagline: Quiet mudflat beach and a mangrove watchtower island

why.winter: The one good window: 14-26 C, hard flat sand you can walk for kilometres, red crabs at low tide and Henry Island.
why.summer: March is warm but usable; April-May is 38 C and humid, and the pre-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclone risk starts up.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the sea is rough and grey, hotels are half shut and the beach is a wind-blown mudflat; no swimming at all.
why.autumn: October and early November still carry post-monsoon cyclone risk, but late November is clean, cool and near empty.

vibe: Bengali families on cheap weekend packages; simple beachfront hotels, fish thali shacks, no bar or backpacker scene.
hub: Namkhana is about 3.5 h from Kolkata by Sealdah South local or bus, then an hour by bus or auto to Bakkhali.

spots.name: Frasergunj Fishing Harbour
spots.note: Trawlers unload at dawn and the catch is auctioned on the jetty; 6 km on by toto, go early or it is all over.

spots.name: Mousuni Island
spots.note: Tent camps on an eroding beach across the Chinai river; boat from Namkhana then a toto, power and food are basic.

spots.name: Kapil Muni Temple (Gangasagar)
spots.note: The Gangasagar mela shrine at the mouth of the Ganga; take the Chemaguri ferry from Namkhana and start early.

spots.name: Jambudwip
spots.note: Uninhabited forest island offshore once used by fishing crews to dry the catch; landing is barred, boats pass it only.

name: Belpahari (Kankrajhore)
tagline: Sal forest on the Jharkhand edge: Ghagra rapids, Gadrasini, Kankrajhore
festival: mid-Jan: Tusu Parab, the Makar Sankranti harvest fair

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the window: 10 C nights around a fire, dry tracks out to Kankrajhore and Gadrasini, and Tusu songs through the hamlets in mid-January
why.summer: March still works before 10 am, then April to June turn the Jangalmahal into 44 C of bare sal, dry stream beds and water shortages in the villages
why.monsoon: July mud makes the forest roads a gamble, but by late August the Tarafeni is loud over the rocks at Ghagra and September is green and almost empty
why.autumn: October and November are the best of it: clear water in the Kangsabati, kash grass on the banks, and forest rest houses you book a month ahead

vibe: Santhal and Kurmi hamlets, a forest rest house and a few homestays; no nightlife, and staff want you off the roads after dark
hub: Jhargram is the railhead 40 km out, buses reach Belpahari in about 90 minutes, then a hired bike or jeep for the forest

name: Bishnupur (Terracotta Temples)
tagline: Laterite and terracotta temples of the Malla kings
festival: Dec: Bishnupur Mela (23-27 Dec)

why.winter: Dec-Feb is the season: 12-25 C, low clear light on the terracotta panels, and Bishnupur Mela fills late December.
why.summer: March is still walkable at 33 C; by April-May the laterite radiates 40 C heat and the temple town empties out.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug is the write-off: 38 C before the break, then 1000 mm of rain on open laterite courtyards; September dries out.
why.autumn: October stays humid until the rains pull out around the 10th, then November turns crisp and rivals winter.

vibe: Weekend Bengali families and craft buyers; you walk or rickshaw between temples and Baluchari weavers let you watch.
hub: Bishnupur has its own railhead, 4 h from Howrah; the temple circuit is walkable or a half-day by rickshaw.

spots.name: Rasmancha
spots.note: Laterite pyramid of 1600 where every Krishna idol in town gathered at Ras; one ASI ticket covers it and the temples.

spots.name: Shyam Rai Temple (Pancha Ratna)
spots.note: Five pinnacle temple of 1643 carrying the finest terracotta panels here; the south face gets the morning light.

spots.name: Jorbangla Temple (Keshta Rai)
spots.note: Twin hut roof temple of 1655 with Ramayana battles cut into brick; five minutes on foot from Rasmancha.

spots.name: Madan Mohan Temple
spots.note: Single tower temple of 1694 still in daily worship and free to enter; the front wall carving is the deepest in town.
