spots.name: Dalmadal Cannon
spots.note: The Malla kings' huge iron cannon sitting in the open near the fort gate; two minutes to see, worth the walk over.

spots.name: Panchmura
spots.note: Potters' village that makes the Bankura terracotta horse; kilns are open to visitors, the bus takes about an hour.

name: Buxa Tiger Reserve (Jayanti)
tagline: River-bed village under Bhutan hills with a limestone cave

why.winter: Prime: the dry white Jayanti riverbed to walk, the Mahakal cave trail and the Buxa Fort climb from Santalabari.
why.summer: April-May is 36 C and humid in the foothills; birding is still strong but the riverbed reflects heat by mid-morning.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Jayanti river becomes uncrossable, the reserve shuts on 16 June and landslides cut the Alipurduar road.
why.autumn: The reserve reopens mid-September but the river runs high into October; November is when Jayanti properly comes back.

vibe: A few homestays and a forest bungalow on the riverbank; birders and Bengali offbeat travellers, and nothing else here.
hub: Alipurduar Junction is 30 km out; shared jeep to Jayanti, permits at Rajabhatkhawa, nothing moves after dusk.

spots.name: Mahakal Cave (Jayanti)
spots.note: Limestone cave shrine reached along the river bed and a forest path; take a local guide and skip it in heavy rain.

spots.name: Buxa Fort
spots.note: Ruined hill fort the British used as a jail, a 4 km climb from Santalabari; carry water, one tea shack at the top.

spots.name: Lepchakha
spots.note: Drukpa hamlet on a shelf above the fort with homestays and Dooars views; another hour up on foot, no vehicles at all.

spots.name: Sikiajhora
spots.note: Shallow forest stream where a boatman poles you under the canopy; go at first light for birds, book at Rajabhatkhawa.

spots.name: Rajabhatkhawa
spots.note: Reserve checkpost with the interpretation centre and the vulture breeding centre; forest permits are issued here.

name: Chandannagar
tagline: French Hooghly riverfront and Bengal's best festival lighting
festival: Nov: Jagaddhatri Puja (Chandannagar lighting)

why.winter: Cool and clear for the Strand promenade, the Sacred Heart church and the Dupleix house museum; an easy day out.
why.summer: April-May is 39 C and humid off the river; the Strand only works after 5 pm and the museum has already shut by then.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep the Hooghly runs high and brown and the Strand floods in spells; only the small museum stays worth the trip.
why.autumn: November is the whole point: four nights of Jagaddhatri Puja when the lighting artisans turn streets into a gallery.

vibe: Bengali day-trippers and photographers; eat jolbhora sandesh on the Strand and take the last local train back.
hub: Local trains from Howrah reach Chandannagar in about an hour, or cross by Hooghly ferry; the town is walkable.

spots.name: The Strand
spots.note: A kilometre of paved riverbank with iron benches and French facades; best in the last hour of light, busy after 5 pm.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Church
spots.note: 1884 church a minute behind the Strand, with a rose window and marble floor; quiet on weekdays, cover shoulders.

spots.name: Chandannagar Museum (Dupleix House)
spots.note: French period furniture, cannon and papers in Dupleix's riverside house; closed Thursdays, the entry fee is small.

spots.name: Patal Bari
spots.note: River house whose lowest floor sits under the Hooghly, where Tagore stayed; you can only see it from the Strand side.

spots.name: Surja Kumar Modak
spots.note: Sweet shop known for jolbhora sandesh with liquid palm jaggery inside; sells out by evening, buy a box for the train.

spots.name: Bandel Church
spots.note: Portuguese basilica of 1599 with a ship's mast in the courtyard; the local train from Chandannagar takes 20 minutes.

spots.name: Hangseshwari Temple
spots.note: Blue thirteen spired temple at Bansberia with terracotta Ananta Basudeba beside it; toto from Bansberia station.

name: Darjeeling
tagline: Queen of the Hills - tea, toy train, Kanchenjunga views

why.winter: Crisp, clear Kanchenjunga views most mornings; cold nights near freezing, pack real layers.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is peak: rhododendrons bloom and skies are clearest, but it's crowded, book ahead.
why.monsoon: Landslide season on the hill roads. The town itself is wet and foggy, views vanish for days.
why.autumn: Best window of the year: post-monsoon clarity, Kanchenjunga visible daily, Puja-season crowds.

vibe: Backpacker cafés on Nehru Road; easy to link a Sikkim loop or Sandakphu trek.
hub: Fly Bagdogra, 3hr jeep up; or NJP rail for the toy train.

spots.name: Tiger Hill
spots.note: Sunrise over Kanchenjunga from a crowded terrace; jeeps leave about 4 am and seats are arranged the evening before.

spots.name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park
spots.note: Red pandas and snow leopards in hillside enclosures; one ticket also covers the Mountaineering Institute, shut Thursdays.

spots.name: Happy Valley Tea Estate
spots.note: Working garden twenty minutes downhill from Chowrasta; a worker walks you round the factory in plucking season, tip him.

spots.name: Batasia Loop
spots.note: Spiral where the toy train turns above the Gorkha war memorial garden; small entry fee, time it for a steam run.

spots.name: Yiga Choeling (Ghum Monastery)
spots.note: Oldest Tibetan gompa here, 1850, with a fifteen foot Maitreya; a donation is expected, five minutes from Ghum station.

spots.name: Tibetan Refugee Self Help Centre
spots.note: Settlement from 1959 where weavers and carpet makers still work; workshops and shop open on weekdays, not Sunday.

spots.name: Glenary's
spots.note: Old bakery and restaurant on Nehru Road, the default warm room in town; the ground floor counter is the cheap way in.

name: Gangasagar (Sagar Island)
tagline: Ganga meets the sea at a wide empty beach and the Kapil Muni temple
festival: mid-Jan: Gangasagar Mela on Makar Sankranti

why.winter: Dec and Feb give cool crossings and sand you can walk alone for an hour; around 14 Jan the Makar Sankranti mela packs a few million pilgrims onto the island
why.summer: March is still easy on the sand, but from late April the flats bake and May is cyclone month on this coast, when vessel timings turn unreliable
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep squalls make the Muriganga crossing rough and launches stop on bad-weather days; the sea runs grey and the lodges shut, so skip it
why.autumn: October clears after the rains and November is the quiet sweet spot: warm water, empty beach, the pilgrim lanes still shuttered for the season

vibe: Pilgrim dharamshalas, a youth hostel and a few beach lodges; outside mela week you share the sand with fishing crews and dogs
hub: Sealdah local to Kakdwip (3 h), the Lot 8 vessel across the Muriganga to Kachuberia, then a 30 km bus down the island

name: Garh Panchkot
tagline: Ruined Panchkot fort under a hill, an hour from Asansol

why.winter: Best here: 10-26 C, empty temple ruins in the sal forest and the Panchet Hill climb finished before the sun bites.
why.summer: By April the Damodar valley sits at 43 C with the ruins in open scrub; only March is still tolerable for the climb.
why.monsoon: June is 43 C and rainless until the break; Jul-Sep greens the hill but the forest track in turns slippery and leechy.
why.autumn: October dries out and November is near peak; weekends fill with Asansol and Durgapur day-trippers, midweek is yours.

vibe: Ruins of a raja's fort at the foot of Panchet Hill; a state forest resort plus a few lodges, mostly local weekenders.
hub: Asansol junction is 33 km out; local bus to Neturia then a toto, or hire a car for the day from Asansol.

spots.name: Panchet Dam
spots.note: DVC dam holding back the Damodar under Panchet Hill; walk the embankment at sunset, and do not swim below the gates.

spots.name: Panchet Hill
spots.note: The hill behind the ruins, about two hours up a rough path from the fort side; no water on the way and no shade on top.

spots.name: Baranti Lake
spots.note: Small irrigation lake ringed by hills with a few resorts; palash reddens the shore in March, no food outside the lodges.

spots.name: Joychandi Pahar
spots.note: Stepped granite hill with a temple on top, filmed in Hirak Rajar Deshe; about 500 steps, climb before the rock heats.

spots.name: Maithon Dam
spots.note: Big lake dam on the Barakar with boat rides and Kalyaneshwari temple close by; a half day out and back from the fort.

name: Gaur (Malda)
tagline: Sultanate capital in ruins among Malda mango orchards

why.winter: The season to walk it: 10-25 C past Dakhil Darwaza, Firoz Minar, the Baisgazi wall and Lattan Masjid, with no crowd.
why.summer: Malda pushes 42 C through April-May with zero shade between monuments spread across 10 km of open field; do not try.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the field paths turn to mud and the brick ruins go slick; September drains slowly and only the last week works.
why.autumn: The rains leave in early October and the light gets good; November is as fine as winter and the orchards are bare.

vibe: Almost no tourists; hire a toto in Malda for a day of Gaur plus Adina Masjid at Pandua, often alone with a caretaker.
hub: Malda Town station on the Kolkata-NJP line, then 12-16 km by toto or auto to the Gaur ruins; sleep in Malda.

spots.name: Bara Sona Masjid (Baroduari)
spots.note: The great golden mosque of 1526, a long facade of stone arches with the roof gone; open sunrise to sunset, no ticket.

spots.name: Dakhil Darwaza
spots.note: Tall brick gateway into the old fort, patterned all over in moulded terracotta; the caretaker points out the guard rooms.

spots.name: Firoz Minar
spots.note: Five storey victory tower of the 1480s, about 26 m and leaning slightly; the inside stair is usually locked, ask first.

spots.name: Qadam Rasul Mosque
spots.note: Small domed mosque built to hold a footprint relic and still in use; Fateh Khan's tomb stands in the same yard.

spots.name: Adina Masjid (Pandua)
spots.note: Ruined 1373 mosque, once the largest in the subcontinent; pair it with the Eklakhi tomb, toto from Malda Town.

name: Gorumara National Park (Lataguri)
tagline: Dooars grassland park for one-horned rhino and gaur

why.winter: Peak: gates open, 8-25 C, dawn jeep safaris and the Jatraprasad and Chandrachur watchtowers over rhino in the grass.
why.summer: April-May is 35 C and sticky, but the grass is short and animals crowd the waterholes so sightings are actually better.
why.monsoon: Closed 16 June to 15 September for breeding and about 3000 mm of Dooars rain; the gates simply shut, so do not plan it.
why.autumn: It reopens mid-September into tall wet grass and poor visibility; from late October the grass drops and viewing lifts.

vibe: Resorts and homestays along Lataguri bazaar; safaris book at the forest counter and jeeps are shared with strangers.
hub: New Mal Junction is 30 min from Lataguri and NJP about 1.5 h; Bagdogra airport is roughly 2 h away.

spots.name: Jatraprasad Watchtower
spots.note: Tower over a grassland salt lick where rhino and gaur come out late afternoon; slots sell at the Lataguri counter early.

spots.name: Medla Watchtower
spots.note: Reached by a hand pulled canoe over the Murti and then a short walk; best at dawn, booked with your safari slot.

spots.name: Chapramari Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Denser forest north of Gorumara with a tower above the Murti; elephants cross here, permits from the Lataguri office.

spots.name: Murti River
spots.note: Shallow boulder river lined with resorts where people picnic on the stones; quiet on weekday mornings, do not swim.

spots.name: Samsing and Suntalekhola
spots.note: Tea and orange village at the Neora Valley edge with a hanging bridge; shared jeeps go up from Chalsa, none after dark.

name: Jaldapara National Park (Madarihat)
tagline: Torsa riverine grassland with Bengal's densest rhino count

why.winter: Best window: 8-25 C, elephant-back and jeep safaris out of Madarihat, and rhino in the tall Torsa grass at first light.
why.summer: April-May runs 36 C and humid; the grass is burnt back so rhino and bison are easier to find, but afternoons are brutal.
why.monsoon: Shut 16 June to 15 September; the Torsa floods, Madarihat takes the full Dooars rain and every safari counter closes.
why.autumn: Reopens mid-September into head-high wet grass; wait for late October when it is burnt back and visibility returns.

vibe: Hollong bungalow inside the park books out months ahead; Madarihat itself has plain lodges and one small bazaar.
hub: Madarihat has its own halt on the Siliguri-Alipurduar line; NJP is 3.5 h by road and Bagdogra about 4 h.

spots.name: Hollong Forest Bungalow
spots.note: Bungalow deep inside the park where the kunki elephant rides start; the ride is balloted the evening before at Madarihat.

spots.name: Chilapata Forest
spots.note: Old elephant corridor of thick sal with the ruined Nalraja Garh inside; jeep safaris start from Kodalbasti gate.

spots.name: Totopara
spots.note: The only Toto village, under the Bhutan hills; the road is rough and beds are scarce, so most people return the same day.

spots.name: South Khayerbari Rescue Centre
spots.note: Leopards taken from circuses live out their years in big enclosures; small ticket, no bus, so hire a car at Madarihat.

spots.name: Bhutan Gate, Phuentsholing
spots.note: Painted border gate where Jaigaon ends; Indians can walk into the town for the day, going further needs a permit.

name: Jhalong & Bindu (Jaldhaka Valley)
tagline: Riverside cardamom hamlets where the road ends at Bhutan

why.winter: Nov-Feb is crisp and clear, 6-22 C; the Jaldhaka runs teal below wooded ridges and Bindu's cardamom yards dry in the sun.
why.summer: March-April stays fresh at 450 m with citrus and cardamom blossom on the slopes; by May afternoon cloud sits on the valley.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep catches the full Dooars monsoon: the river turns brown and violent and the Gorubathan road slips regularly.
why.autumn: October is the reward, washed air and a full river; homestay courtyards fill with drying cardamom through November.

vibe: Family homestays in Jhalong, Paren and Bindu facing the river; birders and the odd angler, no traveller scene at all.
hub: New Mal Jn 45 km, NJP 90 km; Malbazar shared jeeps thin out by mid-afternoon and the last stretch is one lane.

spots.name: Bindu Dam
spots.note: Barrage where the Jaldhaka crosses into Bhutan and the road ends; carry photo ID, the check post logs visitors and shuts by dusk

spots.name: Jaldhaka Hydel Project
spots.note: 1960s power works on the river at Jhalong itself; the still water above the weir is where the morning birding starts

spots.name: Paren
spots.note: Cardamom hamlet on the ridge above Jhalong with wide valley views; a few homestays, and the access road is one lane throughout

spots.name: Todey Tangta
spots.note: Twin border hamlets high above the Jaldhaka, cold even in May; the last stretch is rough, so hire a car for the whole day

spots.name: Suntalekhola
spots.note: Forest camp of huts reached by a hanging bridge over the stream below Samsing; sign in at the checkgate, phone signal dies here

name: Jhargram
tagline: Sal-forest Rajbari town on the Jangalmahal edge

why.winter: The good months: 12-27 C, sal forest tracks out to Chilkigarh and its sacred grove, and the 1930s Rajbari to sleep in.
why.summer: April-May crosses 42 C in the Jangalmahal and the thin sal canopy gives no relief; March is the last easy month.
why.monsoon: June is a 42 C dead zone before the rains; Jul-Sep the sal woods drip, the Dulung runs hard and forest tracks go to mud.
why.autumn: October clears once the rains pull back, but Dalma elephant herds also move in, so keep off forest tracks after dark.

vibe: Quiet district town with a heritage Rajbari, forest lodges and homestays; Santhal haats nearby, no traveller scene.
hub: Jhargram sits on the Howrah-Mumbai main line, 3 h from Kolkata; totos in town, hired car for forest trips.

spots.name: Jhargram Rajbari
spots.note: The Malla Deb family's 1930s palace, part of it now a heritage hotel; the facade and lawns are open, rooms only if you stay

spots.name: Chilkigarh Kanak Durga Temple
spots.note: Durga shrine inside a protected sacred grove above the Dulung river; totos run out from town, allow half a day for the trip

spots.name: Jhargram Zoological Park
spots.note: Small state zoo and deer enclosure on the town edge, a first look at Jangalmahal fauna; cheap ticket, closed on Thursdays

spots.name: Ghagra Falls
spots.note: The Tarafeni breaking over rock ledges in the Belpahari hills; only worth the hired car after the rains, dry by February

spots.name: Khandarani Lake
spots.note: Quiet reservoir under sal forest near Belpahari with seasonal boating; pair it with Ghagra on one car, no food stalls there

name: Kalimpong
tagline: Quiet hill town near Darjeeling - monasteries, nurseries

why.winter: Cold and clear like Darjeeling but a fraction of the tourists. Good for quiet monastery walks.
why.summer: Mar-Apr flower nurseries (Kalimpong supplies orchids nationwide) are in full, fragrant bloom.
why.monsoon: Same landslide risk as the rest of the Darjeeling hills. Teesta valley roads can shut suddenly.
why.autumn: Clear skies, cool air: the easiest month to combine with a Darjeeling or Sikkim loop.

vibe: Slower than Darjeeling, fewer backpackers - good for a quiet reset.
hub: Bagdogra airport or NJP rail, then 1.5-2hr taxi/jeep.

spots.name: Deolo Hill
spots.note: Highest point above town at 1704 m, a park with Teesta and Relli views; small entry fee, and the wind picks up after noon

spots.name: Zang Dhok Palri Phodang (Durpin)
spots.note: Hilltop gompa consecrated in 1976, holding rare Tibetan texts brought from Tibet; the ridge behind it frames the Teesta bend

spots.name: Thongsa Gompa
spots.note: Bhutanese monastery of 1692, the oldest here, rebuilt after the Gorkha raids; a short climb up from the Tenth Mile bazaar

spots.name: Dr Graham's Homes
spots.note: 1900 hillside school with a stone chapel and cricket field; ask at the gate before walking the grounds, term time is busier

spots.name: Kalimpong Haat Bazaar
spots.note: Tenth Mile market that fills on Wednesday and Saturday with hill greens, dalle chillies and churpi; get there before 10 am

spots.name: Pineview Nursery
spots.note: Glasshouses of cactus and succulents, with orchid growers on the same lane; small ticket, an hour covers it

name: Kalna (Ambika Kalna)
tagline: 108 Shiva temples in a double ring, and a Rajbari of terracotta walls

why.winter: Dec-Feb mornings come up misty off the Bhagirathi, the best light of the year on the terracotta panels; day trippers land at 10 and leave by four
why.summer: March is the last comfortable month. From April the laterite courtyards throw the heat back past 41 C and the temple ring has no shade at all
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep rain darkens the brick and lifts the carving out of the wall, and the Bhagirathi runs full at the ghats; wet lanes, sudden afternoon downpours
why.autumn: October stays humid but green; by November the Kali Puja lighting and the pandals along the ghat road give the old town its best evenings

vibe: A river town of cycle rickshaws and sweet shops, a couple of plain lodges, and evenings spent on the Bhagirathi ghats
hub: Howrah to Ambika Kalna local train (2 h), then a 15 minute rickshaw to the Rajbari temple complex

name: Kolkata
tagline: India's cultural capital - colonial streets, great food
festival: Oct: Durga Puja

why.winter: Best months in the city. Cool, dry, Puja afterglow still in the air, easy all-day sightseeing.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is genuinely brutal: 40C+ with punishing humidity before the rains break. Indoor days.
why.monsoon: Waterlogged streets after heavy downpours and high humidity throughout, though the food never stops.
why.autumn: Durga Puja (Oct) is the city's single best reason to visit. Pandal-hopping, all-night energy.

vibe: Hostel common rooms, street-food crawls, easy to meet fellow backpackers.
hub: Major air/rail hub; direct flights and trains nationwide.

spots.name: Victoria Memorial
spots.note: Marble 1921 memorial and museum in the Maidan; gardens open at dawn, galleries from 10 and closed Monday, separate tickets

spots.name: College Street (Boi Para)
spots.note: A kilometre of second hand bookstalls around Presidency; haggle, ask for what you want by name, most stalls shut on Sunday

spots.name: Mullick Ghat Flower Market
spots.note: Wholesale flower market under Howrah Bridge, going from before dawn; be there by 6 am, and do not photograph the bridge

spots.name: Kumartuli
spots.note: North Kolkata lanes where the Durga idols are built in straw and clay; best from August, ask before photographing anyone

spots.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
spots.note: Ramakrishna's riverside Kali temple of 1855 with twelve Shiva shrines; metro to Dakshineswar, phones and shoes stay outside

spots.name: Marble Palace
spots.note: 1835 Mullick mansion, still lived in, stuffed with statuary and paintings; free permit from the tourism office, shut Mon and Thu

spots.name: South Park Street Cemetery
spots.note: Overgrown 1767 colonial burial ground of pyramids and obelisks; free, sign the register at the gate, closes around 5 pm

spots.name: Indian Coffee House (College Street)
spots.note: Coffee House in Albert Hall since 1942, ceiling fans, infusion and adda over shared tables; cheap, cash only, shuts by 9 pm

name: Lava & Rishop (Neora Valley)
tagline: Pine-and-cardamom ridge above Neora Valley's cloud forest

why.winter: Dec-Feb drops near 2 C with a real chance of snow at Rishop; rooms are unheated and the Neora tracks can be iced up.
why.summer: March-May is the best walking: rhododendron and orchids in the Neora forest, 10-20 C, Kanchenjunga out most mornings.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is out: the park shuts on 16 June, the Gorubathan road slides and leeches own the forest floor completely.
why.autumn: October-November gives the clearest air of the year for Kanchenjunga from Tiffin Dara, and the park is open again.

vibe: Homestays in Lava and a scatter of huts at Rishop; birders after satyr tragopan, plus Bengali families in season.
hub: New Mal Junction is 2.5 h by hired car, NJP about 3.5 h; Neora day permits come from the Lava range office.

spots.name: Lava Monastery
spots.note: Kagyu Thekchen Ling gompa on the ridge above Lava bazaar, red and gold; morning prayers around 6, shoes off at the hall

spots.name: Neora Valley National Park
spots.note: Cloud forest with red panda and satyr tragopan; day permit, guide and vehicle are booked at the Lava range office, not online

spots.name: Tiffin Dara
spots.note: Ridge lookout half an hour on foot above Rishop, straight at Kanchenjunga; leave by 5 am, cloud closes it in most mornings

spots.name: Changey Falls
spots.note: Waterfall dropping into a gorge on the Kolakham road, viewed from a rail; steep steps down, slippery for weeks after rain

spots.name: Kolakham
spots.note: Handful of homestays on a shelf below the Neora forest, quieter than Lava; the last 4 km of road is broken, go by jeep

spots.name: Lolegaon
spots.note: Lepcha village in a heritage forest with a canopy walkway; the hanging bridge has been shut on and off, check in Lava first

name: Mandarmani-Tajpur
tagline: Bengal's 'drive-on' beach: long flat sand, low-key escape

why.winter: Prime beach weather: dry and breezy, good for the famous bike-on-the-sand rides.
why.summer: Hot and increasingly humid through May as the Bay of Bengal builds toward monsoon.
why.monsoon: Rough surf, frequent rain and real cyclone risk off the Bay of Bengal. Not a beach window.
why.autumn: Oct is still a bit unsettled post-monsoon; by Nov sea and weather have properly calmed.

vibe: Weekend crowd of Kolkata twenty-somethings, beach shacks and bonfires.
hub: 3hr drive/bus from Kolkata via Digha Road.

spots.name: Tajpur Beach
spots.note: Quieter sand than Mandarmani with red crabs at low tide; the approach road is bad, and nothing stays open past dark

spots.name: Mandarmani Mohana
spots.note: Creek mouth at the end of the beach where the fishing boats land; walk or cycle at low tide, the sand is soft by noon

spots.name: Shankarpur Fishing Harbour
spots.note: Trawler harbour where the catch is landed and auctioned in the afternoon; wear shoes you can rinse, the jetty is slippery

spots.name: Marine Aquarium and Regional Centre
spots.note: ZSI aquarium at Digha holding Bay of Bengal species; small ticket, an hour is plenty, mornings before the bus groups

spots.name: Chandaneswar Shiv Temple
spots.note: Border shrine just inside Odisha, packed for the Chaitra Sankranti mela in mid April; shoes and phones stay at the counter

spots.name: Talsari Beach
spots.note: Casuarina beach in Odisha where the Subarnarekha meets the sea; cross the creek by boat at low tide, carry your own water

name: Mayapur (Nabadwip)
tagline: Chaitanya's river country: Nabadwip's old lanes and Mayapur's temples
festival: Mar: Gaura Purnima, Chaitanya's birth anniversary

why.winter: Dec-Feb is cool and dry for walking Nabadwip's old lanes, crossing to Mayapur by ferry and sitting out the evening kirtan on the Jalangi bank
why.summer: Gaura Purnima in March fills every room in both towns, then April to June bake the Nadia plain past 41 C with river humidity and little shade
why.monsoon: Jul-Sep the Bhagirathi runs high and brown, ferries are cancelled on rough days and the ghat steps go under; temples stay open but everything is wet
why.autumn: October is warm and clear after the rains, and November brings the Nabadwip Rash Yatra, a week of night processions through the old town

vibe: Pilgrim guest houses on both banks and cheap rooms on the temple campus; evenings are kirtan, prasad canteens and ferry horns
hub: Sealdah to Nabadwip Dham by train (3 h) then a ferry across, or a direct bus from Kolkata to Mayapur in 4 h

name: Mirik
tagline: Lake town below Darjeeling with orange orchards and tea

why.winter: Dec-Feb is 3-13 C with the lake often under mist; quiet and cheap, but Kanchenjunga hides more mornings than it shows.
why.summer: March-April is the pick: 12-22 C, the Sumendu lake loop and tea garden paths; May greys out as pre-monsoon showers build.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep dumps over 2500 mm; the Mirik-Darjeeling road slips regularly and the lake bowl sits inside cloud for days.
why.autumn: October-November is the best air of the year here, with the orange orchards on the Pashupati road heading to harvest.

vibe: Day-trippers from Siliguri clear out by evening and the lake goes quiet; small hotels, momo shops, no backpackers.
hub: Bagdogra and NJP are both about 2 h by shared jeep; onward jeeps to Darjeeling take another 2 h.

spots.name: Sumendu Lake
spots.note: The town's lake with a walking path and the Indreni footbridge; boats and ponies work till about 5, walk it early instead

spots.name: Bokar Ngedon Chokhor Ling
spots.note: Working Kagyu monastery on the ridge above the lake, murals and young monks; prayers at dawn, visitors welcome, shoes off

spots.name: Pashupati Nagar Market
spots.note: Border bazaar on the Nepal side for cheap blankets, crockery and liquor; carry ID, keep purchases small for the way back

spots.name: Thurbo Tea Estate
spots.note: Goodricke garden on the slopes below Mirik, plucking from March to November; walk the roads freely, factory needs a request

spots.name: Rameetey Dara
spots.note: Bend on the Darjeeling road looking down the ridges to the plains; best after rain when the haze clears, no stalls up there

spots.name: Bunkulung
spots.note: Riverside farming hamlet below Mirik with fish ponds and homestays; a rough 40 minute descent by car, arrange the ride back

name: Mukutmanipur
tagline: Kangsabati reservoir ringed by low Bankura hills

why.winter: The reason to come: 11-26 C, boats out onto the reservoir and a long dam embankment walk with almost nobody on it.
why.summer: March is warm but fine; April-June pushes past 42 C in the Bankura interior and the reservoir shrinks to mudflats.
why.monsoon: June is a 42 C furnace until the rains break; Jul-Sep fills the lake but the Khatra road floods and boatmen stop.
why.autumn: By late October the water is high, the air is clear and the state lodge is bookable without a month of notice.

vibe: Bengali picnic parties at weekends, near-empty midweek; a state youth hostel and a few guesthouses, no traveller scene.
hub: Bankura railhead (4 h from Howrah), then 55 km by bus via Khatra; the last bus back leaves mid-afternoon.

spots.name: Kangsabati Dam
spots.note: Long earth dam holding back two rivers, walkable end to end at sunset; the reservoir side has boats, the far side is empty

spots.name: Musafirana
spots.note: Hillock above the reservoir with the widest view of the water and islands; a short climb, go for the last hour of light

spots.name: Pareshnath Temple
spots.note: Old Jain stone images gathered under a shelter near Ambikanagar; boat or a road loop to get there, nobody selling anything

spots.name: Bonpukuria Deer Park
spots.note: Fenced spotted deer park in the forest across the dam; small ticket, best early morning, half an hour is enough

name: Murshidabad (Hazarduari)
tagline: Nawabi capital of Bengal in ruins along the Bhagirathi

why.winter: Best window: 10-26 C for the Hazarduari, Katra Masjid and Khoshbagh circuit, with river mist on the Bhagirathi at dawn.
why.summer: April-June is a 41 C Gangetic oven with no shade between monuments; only workable if you start at 6 am and quit by 10.
why.monsoon: Jun-Sep is out: airless at 39 C in June, then the Bhagirathi runs high and the open monument circuit turns to mud.
why.autumn: October dries out fast once the rains leave, and November is close to winter quality with the palace grounds quiet.

vibe: Bengali history buffs and school groups; cheap lodges in Lalbagh, and tonga or toto drivers double as guides for a day.
hub: Murshidabad station on the Sealdah-Lalgola line is about 4 h out; Hazarduari and Lalbagh are 2 km by toto.

spots.name: Katra Masjid
spots.note: 1724 brick mosque where Murshid Quli Khan lies buried under the entrance steps, as he asked; no ticket, go before the heat

spots.name: Khoshbagh
spots.note: Walled Nawabi burial garden across the Bhagirathi holding Siraj ud Daulah; country boat from Lalbagh ghat, almost no shade

spots.name: Kathgola Palace
spots.note: The Dugar family's 1873 garden mansion with an Adinath Jain temple behind; ticketed, and a guide comes with it either way

spots.name: Nizamat Imambara
spots.note: The largest imambara in India, built 1847 inside the palace compound; the hall opens only around Muharram, courtyard daily

spots.name: Motijheel
spots.note: Horseshoe lake with Nawab-era ruins and a mosque on its rim; small park ticket, evening light show, totos wait at the gate

spots.name: Jahan Kosha Cannon
spots.note: Seventeenth century Mughal siege gun lying under a tree at Topkhana; free, five minutes by toto from Katra Masjid

name: Sandakphu
tagline: West Bengal's highest point - sunrise over 4 of 5 top peaks

why.winter: Doable with proper gear: sub-zero nights and snow underfoot, but the clearest sunrise of the year.
why.summer: Apr rhododendrons carpet the ridge red and pink; by May haze builds as monsoon approaches.
why.monsoon: Leech-and-landslide trail with zero summit visibility. Operators won't run departures.
why.autumn: Peak window: driest air of the year, both Everest and Kanchenjunga visible from one ridge.

vibe: Teahouse trek, trekkers worldwide; a mandatory guide means you're never truly alone.
hub: Base in Darjeeling; jeep to Manebhanjan, guide compulsory.

spots.name: Singalila National Park
spots.note: The park the whole ridge sits inside, red panda country; entry and guide fees are paid at Manebhanjan, shut in the monsoon

spots.name: Phalut
spots.note: Next high point 21 km along the ridge, closer to Kanchenjunga and emptier; a full day on foot, no shops or signal en route

spots.name: Kalapokhri
spots.note: Small dark pond the locals hold sacred, on the trail below the last climb; teahouse lunch stop, the water is said never to freeze

spots.name: Tumling
spots.note: Overnight stop just inside Nepal with the first clean Kanchenjunga view; Indian notes work, rooms are basic and very cold

spots.name: Manebhanjan
spots.note: Roadhead below the ridge where permits, guides and the old Land Rovers are arranged; last place to buy anything you forgot

name: Shantiniketan (Bolpur)
tagline: Tagore's university town of open-air classes and Baul song
festival: Dec: Poush Mela (starts 7 Poush, about 22-25 Dec)

why.winter: Peak: Poush Mela in late December turns the mela ground into a Baul and craft fair, and Bolpur rooms sell out weeks ahead.
why.summer: Basanta Utsav at Holi in March is lovely and mobbed; after that Birbhum hits 42 C and the red earth is a furnace.
why.monsoon: June bakes at 41 C until the rains break; Jul-Sep is wet and sticky, but the Sonajhuri haat still runs every Saturday.
why.autumn: From late October the humidity drops and you get the campus, the murals and the Saturday haat without Mela crowds.

vibe: Students, Baul singers and Kolkata weekenders; cycles are easy to hire and Sonajhuri haat is where solo travellers land.
hub: Bolpur Shantiniketan station is 2.5 h from Howrah by express; everything else is toto-rickshaw distance.

spots.name: Sonajhuri Haat
spots.note: Saturday afternoon craft haat under sonajhuri trees by the Khoai, Bauls singing between stalls; cash only, over by dusk

spots.name: Rabindra Bhavana
spots.note: Tagore's five houses in the Uttarayan complex plus his manuscripts and paintings; ticketed, closed Wednesday, no phones in

spots.name: Chhatimtala and Upasana Griha
spots.note: Debendranath's meditation seat under chhatim trees and the 1891 glass prayer hall; the Wednesday service is open to all

spots.name: Kala Bhavana
spots.note: The art school where Ramkinkar Baij's concrete figures stand in the open; walk the campus, the Nandan gallery keeps the rest

spots.name: Kopai River
spots.note: The shallow river of Tagore's song, best at dusk from the Goalpara side; cycle out, and it only runs deep during the rains

spots.name: Ballavpur Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.note: Reclaimed forest with spotted deer and a bird lake, 20 minutes by toto; ticket at the gate, go early, no canteen inside

name: Sittong (Orange Village)
tagline: Lepcha orange orchards in a warm river valley below Darjeeling

why.winter: Dec-Jan the orchards hang heavy over homestay roofs and the valley stays a mild 8-22 C while Darjeeling shivers above.
why.summer: March-April is for birds: hornbill nests and minivets up at Latpanchar in Mahananda WLS, though haze builds by midday.
why.monsoon: Jun-Aug the Riyang roars under Jogighat bridge and the steep concrete lanes run with rain; landslips cut the Mongpu road.
why.autumn: October is washed and green with Kanchenjunga out from Ahaldara at dawn; the oranges start turning by late November.

vibe: Bamboo-and-tin Lepcha homestays scattered up the hillside; birders, Bengali weekenders, Sunday bells at the old church.
hub: NJP 40 km, Bagdogra 55 km, 2 h via the Sevoke-Kalijhora climb; shared cars rare, ask your homestay for pickup.

spots.name: Ahaldara
spots.note: Ridge lookout over the Teesta bends with Kanchenjunga behind on a clear dawn; a rough climb by car, tea shack at the top

spots.name: Sittong Church
spots.note: Century old stone Catholic church on the hillside, the village landmark; Sunday morning service is when it is actually open

spots.name: Namthing Pokhri
spots.note: Forest pond above Latpanchar known for Himalayan salamanders; they show after the first rains, keep to the bank, no swimming

spots.name: Latpanchar
spots.note: Cinchona plantation village in the Mahananda sanctuary, birders come for the hornbills; take a local guide, roads are steep

spots.name: Riyang
spots.note: River hamlet at the bottom of the orange terraces on the Kalijhora road; walking down is easy, arrange a lift back up

name: Sundarbans
tagline: World's largest mangrove forest: tiger territory by boat

why.winter: The real season here: calm water, cool air, best odds of spotting a tiger on the riverbanks.
why.summer: Apr-May heat and humidity in the delta are punishing, and tiger activity near the banks drops.
why.monsoon: Core-zone tourism effectively shuts: swollen rivers and unsafe boat conditions.
why.autumn: Oct is a reasonable early option as the water calms; Nov onward is noticeably better.

vibe: Little solo scene - most join a shared boat tour and bond over 3 days.
hub: 2hr drive from Kolkata to Godkhali jetty, then boat in.

spots.name: Sudhanyakhali Watch Tower
spots.note: Sweet water pond in the core zone with the best tiger odds here; boats crowd it mid-morning, take the first trip out.

spots.name: Sajnekhali Watch Tower
spots.note: Forest office with a mangrove interpretation centre and crocodile pond; permits are checked here so every boat stops first.

spots.name: Dobanki Watch Tower
spots.note: Caged canopy walkway about 500 m long over the forest floor; deer and boar pass below, allow 20 minutes end to end.

spots.name: Pakhiralay
spots.note: Riverside village across the water from Sajnekhali where nearly all the lodges are; walk the embankment at dusk for herons.

spots.name: Gosaba
spots.note: Island village laid out as a 1903 cooperative estate; Hamilton's bungalow, where Tagore stayed in 1932, opens on request.

spots.name: Netidhopani Watch Tower
spots.note: Ruined 400 year old temple deep in the core forest; needs a separate permit and a full day on the boat, so arrange it early.

name: Susunia Hill (Bankura)
tagline: Bengal's rock-climbing hill, with a 4th century royal inscription
festival: mid-Jan: Makar Sankranti fair at the Narasimha stone spring

why.winter: Dec-Feb is climbing season: Kolkata clubs rope up on the north face at dawn, the stone spring runs cold and the summit walk takes about an hour
why.summer: Palash and simul redden the slope through March, then April and May sit past 43 C on open rock with no shade until you reach the tree line
why.monsoon: Jul and Aug make the granite slick and bring leeches into the sal, but the whole hill greens over and September walks are fine again
why.autumn: October and November give clear air across the Bankura plain, cool nights at the eco centre and the quietest weekdays of the year

vibe: A youth hostel and an eco centre at the base, stone carvers chipping bowls by the road, climbers in tents on winter weekends
hub: Bankura town is 20 km off by bus or toto, and Bankura is 4 h from Howrah on the Adra line
